speaker: Leonardo
en: Salaì? Is that you? Ezio! I must be getting lazy in my old age. I did not know you had returned to Roma.

speaker: Ezio
en: Unfortunately, I cannot stay. I am here to charter a ship.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Let me assist you! I know a captain, he is very discreet. Hang on, I have the name recorded somewhere.

speaker: Ezio
en: What are you working on?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Oh this? A hobby of mine. Of course you are familiar with Pythagoras!

speaker: Ezio
en: Remind me.

speaker: Leonardo
en: The brilliant scholar from Grecia (Greece) who discovered many secrets about the heavenly spheres and our cosmos.

speaker: Ezio
en: These symbols come from him?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Ever since my exploration of that strange Apple, they have been stamped on my mind. I found symbols like them in the writings of the Pythagorean disciples. I am afraid the captain's name escapes me.

speaker: Ezio
en: The Apple has been put to rest. Perhaps it would do you good to focus on painting. You seem to be doing decent work on this one.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Ha! You are kind, however even I can see that she is badly drawn. And that smile? Overdone. Meaningless. But forget painting, I made a breakthrough in my research several days ago. A huge discovery. Salaì! Can you bring the—Oh, he is not back! I intended to accompany you to the docks, but we cannot leave my workshop without my assistant.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene. (Good.) An easy task.

speaker: Leonardo
en: I am afraid you underestimate Salaì!

speaker: Ezio
en: Hehe. Wait and see.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Suit yourself. You will likely find him at La Volpe Addormentata (The Sleeping Fox).

speaker: Salaì
en: Di nuovo! (Again!)

speaker: Hermeticist
en: I told you those dice were lucky.

speaker: Salaì
en: Fortuna wishes she were as good as me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Gian Giacomo?

speaker: Salaì
en: I do not answer to that name.

speaker: Ezio
en: Salaì.

speaker: Salaì
en: Better. But not good enough.

speaker: Salaì
en: Yes! Di nuovo! (Again!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Leonardo, your master, requests your presence.

speaker: Salaì
en: Let him wait.

speaker: Ezio
en: No.

speaker: Salaì
en: Nice hood. Are you one of Julius's monks?

speaker: Ezio
en: My church is not of God.

speaker: Salaì
en: Outside the kingdom of God is the realm of men. You worship there, Messere (Sir)?

speaker: Ezio
en: Come with me and find out.

speaker: Salaì
en: It has been fun, but I must go.

speaker: Hermeticist
en: Please, do not depart. The game is not finished.

speaker: Salaì
en: Sorry, but a better offer has arisen.

speaker: Salaì
en: Lead on, Messere (Sir).

speaker: Ezio
en: The three men from the dice game follow us. Stay quiet

speaker: Salaì
en: Why?

speaker: Salaì
en: Sentite! (Listen!) I am done playing.

speaker: Hermeticist
en: So are we!

speaker: Salaì
en: There is only one man in Roma who can put on a show like that. You must be Ezio Auditore.

speaker: Ezio
en: Come. We need to return to Leonardo right away.

speaker: Salaì
en: You do not talk much, do you? Fine. I will run ahead. You catch up.

speaker: Salaì
en: These strangers do not quit.

speaker: Ezio
en: Disciples wearing similar robes appeared once before. They sought an... object I had in my possession.

speaker: Salaì
en: You mean, the Piece of Eden?

speaker: Ezio
en: Leonardo told you?

speaker: Salaì
en: He tells me everything.

speaker: Ezio
en: I fear his indiscretion has cost us greatly. We must warn him.

speaker: Salaì
en: Say no more. I know the best route home. I take it every morning after the taverns close. Follow me.

speaker: Salaì
en: I am going around. How about some fun on the rooftops?

speaker: Ezio
en: Leonardo told me that he had discovered something important.

speaker: Salaì
en: He has been exploring a hidden catacomb for years now. I think he came to Roma to find it. You have no idea what he is like. He works on this all the time, he never takes me out. And he is so cheap! I have to beg him for money.

speaker: Ezio
en: He actually gives coins to you?

speaker: Salaì
en: More or less. What he does not know will not hurt him. Allora (So), you are from Firenze? Tell me more.

speaker: Salaì
en: Fine, I will use my imagination.

speaker: Salaì
en: It is too early in the day for fighting. Follow me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Leonardo discovered something in the catacombs?

speaker: Salaì
en: He found the entrance to a temple, something he read about in his books. I have not seen him that excited in years.

speaker: Ezio
en: Did he say anything else?

speaker: Salaì
en: That the temple contains the perfect number, something discovered by some scholar from Grecia.

speaker: Ezio
en: Pythagoras.

speaker: Salaì
en: Get them! Attack! Taste my blade! Try this on for size! You want to get back quickly? Avoid their swords.

speaker: Ezio
en: Knowing Leonardo, I suppose he spoke of his discovery to whomever would listen. Did you notice any robed men around him?

speaker: Salaì
en: Why would I spend my time at the workshop when I can go out and have fun? Ask the master himself when you get there.

speaker: Salaì
en: Maestro!

speaker: Ezio
en: They took him.

speaker: Salaì
en: No. He must be here.

speaker: Ezio
en: The temple he discovered. Where is it?

speaker: Salaì
en: Leonardo!

speaker: Ezio
en: Salaì. If you want to save him, tell me where the temple is.

speaker: Salaì
en: I do not know.

speaker: Ezio
en: Cazzo. (Fuck.)

speaker: Salaì
en: Ezio... something is written on the floor.

speaker: Ezio
en: What does it say?

speaker: Salaì
en: I cannot read. Leonardo promised to teach me. But now...

speaker: Ezio
en: "Villa. Paintings." He wants us to examine art?

speaker: Salaì
en: I remember when Leonardo lived at your villa, he was researching the location of the catacombs.

speaker: Ezio
en: Several of his paintings hung in the gallery there. What do they have to do with the temple?

speaker: Salaì
en: Perhaps the pages of his research are hidden in one of the frames?

speaker: Ezio
en: The paintings are gone. They all burned in the attack.

speaker: Salaì
en: No, they did not—only "" and "". The Borgia took the rest.

speaker: Ezio
en: Six paintings.

speaker: Salaì
en: Five. I told the art merchant that "" was by Leonardo. I needed the money for a doublet. Of course, now it has gone out of fashion.

speaker: Ezio
en: Who has the paintings now?

speaker: Salaì
en: Lucrezia Borgia, in her husband's palazzo outside Ferrara.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then it is time I took back what was stolen.

speaker: Federico
en: What about that one?

speaker: Ezio
en: Oh! She is beautiful...

speaker: Federico
en: Okay! Then go talk to her?

speaker: Ezio
en: Just like that? Talk about what?

speaker: Federico
en: It doesn't matter. See, little brother, most men are so afraid of beautiful girls that, anyone who actually talks to them has an advantage! Just make it up as you go.

speaker: Cristina
en: What.

speaker: Ezio
en: What?

speaker: Cristina
en: Why are you just standing there?

speaker: Ezio
en: Oh. Um... Because I... wanted to ask you something. Which is... What's your name?

speaker: Cristina
en: Pft! Not one you'll ever need to make use of.

speaker: Ezio
en: Aspetta! (Wait!) I wasn't ready. I was planning on being really charming. And funny! Can I just have a second chance?

speaker: Ezio
en: Oh well...

speaker: Federico
en: Ezio, all is not lost. You made her smile! She will remember you now.

speaker: Ezio
en: No, I can still fix this. I'll follow her a ways, see where she lives.

speaker: Cristina
en: I told you. I'm not interested.

speaker: Vieri
en: Sì. (Yes.) But I am.

speaker: Cristina
en: Get in line.

speaker: Vieri
en: I think not, amore mio (my love). I've decided I'm tired of waiting for you to open your legs on your own.

speaker: Vieri
en: Cane rognoso! (Shabby dog!) What do you want here? This has nothing to do with you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Nice to see you too, Vieri. I think you're disturbing this young lady's day.

speaker: Vieri
en: Finally, father will be forced to notice. To give me respect!

speaker: Ezio
en: Is that the best you can do?

speaker: Vieri
en: Shut your mouth. I'll kill you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Why am I not surprised to find you forcing yourself on a nice girl? Just like your father's banks treat Firenze.

speaker: Vieri
en: Fool. Your father is the one who needs to be taught a lesson.

speaker: Ezio
en: You Pazzi are all mouth and no fist. You've been slandering my family's name around this town for too long.

speaker: Vieri
en: No more than they deserve.

speaker: Ezio
en: Come on then, hit me! Give me a reason to break your neck!

speaker: Vieri
en: You will pay for interfering. Your whole family will!

speaker: Cristina
en: Thank you. That was very kind of you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Are you alright?

speaker: Cristina
en: I am now... You asked for my name earlier. It's Cristina.

speaker: Ezio
en: Piacere, (A pleasure) Cristina! I'm Ezio.

speaker: Cristina
en: Well, Ezio. Looks like you got yourself a second chance.

speaker: A Seed
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore's genetic memories that was relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus 2.01.

speaker: Caterina
en: Well, well, look who it is.

speaker: Ezio
en: Madonna.

speaker: Caterina
en: I thought when we met you were a bit special. But, an Assassin, hmmm?

speaker: Caterina
en: Walk with me, caro (darling.) You're going to love Forlì! The cannons in our cittadella alone go back a hundred years. The artifact will be quite safe there.

speaker: Ezio
en: Forgive me, but I've never heard of a woman ruling her own city before. It's very impressive.

speaker: Caterina
en: Well... It was my husband's before, of course. He died.

speaker: Ezio
en: Oh. I'm sorry.

speaker: Caterina
en: Don't be. I had him killed.

speaker: Ezio
en: Oh...

speaker: Niccolò
en: We discovered Girolamo Riario was working for the Templars. Making a map of the locations of the remaining Codex pages.

speaker: Caterina
en: I never liked the goddamned son of a bitch anyway. He was a lousy father, boring in bed, and a pain in my ass

speaker: Niccolò
en: Look

speaker: Caterina
en: Oh no...

speaker: Caterina
en: Aspetta! (Wait.) What's happening?

speaker: Civilian
en: They came as soon as you left the city walls, Signora. The city is under attack.

speaker: Caterina
en: What!? By who—!?

speaker: Civilian
en: The Orsi brothers, Signora.

speaker: Caterina
en: Aw, sangue di Giuda! (God damn it!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Who are the Orsi?

speaker: Caterina
en: The same canaglie (rascals) I hired to kill my husband!

speaker: Niccolò
en: It's the Spaniard, of course. The Orsi have no world view bigger than their purse.

speaker: Ezio
en: But how could he know where we were taking the Apple—before we even knew!?

speaker: Niccolò
en: Because they're not here for the Apple, Ezio. They're after Riario's map.

speaker: Caterina
en: Basta (Stop) with your map, Niccolò! My children are inside! Oh, porco demonio! (Oh, fucking hell!)

speaker: Caterina
en: They're already inside! Double-crossing bastards...

speaker: Ezio
en: Is there another way into this place?

speaker: Caterina
en: Aspetta... (Wait...) Perhaps, yes. There's an old tunnel under the western wall from the canal.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene (Got it)—I'll be right back.

speaker: Caterina
en: Hey! You! Yeah, I'm talking to you, you spineless dogs! You occupy MY city!? MY home!? You think I'm going to stand here and do nothing about it!? How about I come up there and rip your balle (balls) off? What kind of men are you? Doing the bidding of your masters for loose change! You're not afraid of me? You will be when I come up there and cut your head off, piss down your necks, and shove your faces up my fica! I'll stick your balle (balls) with a fork, and roast them over my kitchen fire! How's that sound?

speaker: Caterina
en: You laugh? You wouldn't if I was a man. You think I won't do it, just because of THESE—!? Le tette!! Le mie tette! (Tits! My tits!) I bet you want to touch them, don't you? You wish you could touch them, you wish you could lick them. Don't you? Well, come down here and give it a try, like a real man... And I'll kick your balls so hard they'll fly out your nostrils! Lurido branco di cani bastardi! Tornatevene a casa, se non volete finìre impalati sulle mura della mia cittadella. Ahhh! Ma forse è per questo che non vi decidete a uscire. Già, scommetto che lo gradireste assai un bel palo di quercia su per il culo! Sanguediddio! Ma dove vi hanno pescato? In un convento di monache? Non ho mai visto in vita mia un'accozzaglia di codardi peggio assortita di voi. Che vista penosa! Dopo che vi avrò fatto castrare, non sarete meno uomini di quanto siete ora! (Vile pack of bastard dogs! Go back to your kennel, or I'll have you all impaled along my citadel walls. Ahhh! But maybe this is the reason you are not leaving. Yes, I guess you'd really enjoy a long oaken pole up your asses. God almighty! Where did they find you? In a nunnery? Never in all my days have I laid eyes on such an abject, motley crew of cowards. What a pathetic sight! Even after I've had you castrated, you'll not be less men than you are now!)

speaker: Caterina
en: Ezio! You did it! Seguimi! (Follow me!)

speaker: Ezio
en: A magnificent sight.

speaker: Suleiman
en: It is a work in progress.

speaker: Ezio
en: No city in Europa has a skyline quite like this.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Well, to be precise, that is Europa...

speaker: Suleiman
en: ...that is Asia.

speaker: Ezio
en: Ah... some borders even the Ottomans cannot move.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Very few. You are Italian by the sound of it, but your outfit is not. Have you been traveling long?

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì, da molto tempo. (Yes, a very long time.) I left Roma twelve months ago, looking for... inspiration. And that search brought me here. When I was a child, my father told me stories about the fall of Costantinopoli.

speaker: Suleiman
en: You must mean the conquest of Konstantiniyye. I suppose the moral of any story matches the temper of the man telling it.

speaker: Ezio
en: That we can agree on.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Guzel. (I am glad.) Konstantiniyye is a city for all kinds and creeds. Students like me or... travelers such as yourself.

speaker: Suleiman
en: I have so much work to return to, but it is good to be home.

speaker: Ezio
en: Work? When I was your age, my interests were... were mainly...

speaker: Ezio
en: Salve. (Hello.)

speaker: Suleiman
en: Incredible. I am surprised you got anything done.

speaker: Ezio
en: As was my mother.

speaker: Suleiman
en: It was a pleasure speaking with you. Beyefendi, (Sir). I hope you find something to hold your interest here.

speaker: Ezio
en: I have faith I will.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Yardim edebiir miyim Effindim? (May I, my lady?)

speaker: Lady
en: Grazie (Thank you), dear boy.

speaker: Ezio
en: A scholar and a gentleman, you are full of surprises.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Very few, my friend. Eksik Olmayin! (May God bless you!)

speaker: Yusuf
en: Hoshgeldin﻿ Kardeshim! (Welcome, brother!) Unless the legend is a lie, you are the man I long to meet. Renowned Master and Mentor, Ezio Auditore de la la la!

speaker: Ezio
en: Prego? (Excuse me?)

speaker: Yusuf
en: Forgive me. I have a hard time remembering that Italian gibberish.

speaker: Ezio
en: Da Firenze. The city where I was born.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Ah yes! So by your custom, I would be... Yusuf Tazim da Istanbul! I like that.

speaker: Ezio
en: Istanbul? Yet another name for this city?

speaker: Yusuf
en: Evet (Yes), it's a local favorite. Come, Mentor da Firenze. I will show you around.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Welcome to Galata district. For centuries it has been a home to orphans from Europe and Asia alike. You won't find more diversity anywhere else in the city. And for that reason, Assassins make it their home.

speaker: Ezio
en: I would like to see where.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Kesinlikle. (Absolutely.) The Brotherhood is always eager to meet the man who put the Borgias out to pasture.

speaker: Ezio
en: Oh. Does everyone in this city know I'm here already?

speaker: Yusuf
en: Well, your holy land tussle with the Templars did not go unnoticed.

speaker: Ezio
en: When I first set out, violence was so far from my mind. I sought wisdom. The contents of Altaïr's library.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Not realizing it has been sealed for three centuries?

speaker: Ezio
en: No, I assumed as much. But I never expected to find Templars guarding it.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Very troubling, no? Five years ago, Templar influence here was minimal. A small faction with dreams of restoring the Byzantine throne. But they're growing in number, day by day. And with Sultan Bayezid on his way out, they may try something dramatic.

speaker: Ezio
en: Is there no heir to the Ottoman throne?

speaker: Yusuf
en: Not just one—two angry sons. It's a familiar pattern with these . When the Sultan coughs—ahem!—the Princes draw their swords.

speaker: Ezio
en: Between the Templars and the Ottomans, you must stay busy.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Ezio, I barely have time to polish my blade!

speaker: Yusuf
en: Inanilmaz. (Incredible.) A master at work! Leave some for me, eh? I must remember that. Ezio, there! Another wave. More Templars. Look sharp!

speaker: Yusuf
en: No, no. Watch.

speaker: Ottoman Guard
en: Byzantium is dead, as are you!

speaker: Yusuf
en: The whole city wakens to welcome you, Ezio! First the regents, now the rats! Ottoman soldiers have a special loathing for these Byzantine thugs. That gives us some breathing room.

speaker: Ezio
en: How much?

speaker: Yusuf
en: Eh, just a little. They'll still kill you if you look at them wrong, but they will feel bad about it later.

speaker: Ezio
en: Touching.

speaker: Yusuf
en: It's not so bad really. For the first time in many decades, the Assassins have a strong presence here. It wasn't always that way. Under the Byzantine Emperor, the Assassins were hunted down and killed on the spot. We're almost there. This way.

speaker: Vagrant
en: Did you see that white knight?

speaker: Priest
en: Benedicat vos omnipotens Deus, Pater, et Filius, et Spìritus Sanctus, Amen. Ite, missa est. Deo gratias. (Almighty God bless you, Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, Amen. Go, the dismissal is made. Thanks be to God.)

speaker: Cardinal 1
en: Did you hear? The Baron de Valois is dead. Now Bartolomeo d'Alviano will surely rise up against the Pope.

speaker: Cardinal 2
en: Cesare's campaign will be in trouble.

speaker: Cardinal 1
en: Is that such a bad thing?

speaker: Cardinal 2
en: Perhaps not.

speaker: Cardinal 3
en: Some say the Papal funds lie in disarray.

speaker: Cardinal 4
en: Sul serio? (Seriously?) The Pope's treasury is never empty. His Holiness will simply kill another wealthy cardinal if he requires funds.

speaker: Cardinal 3
en: Disgusting.

speaker: Cardinal 5
en: His name is Ezio Auditore.

speaker: Cardinal 6
en: Who?

speaker: Cardinal 5
en: The Assassin. He killed the Banker. Some say he walks the halls of Il Vaticano with no one able to stop him.

speaker: Cardinal 6
en: Perhaps Cesare's rule will come to an end, and the Church will be restored to its former glory.

speaker: Borgia cardinal
en: I will write the sermons, then leave them for you within the shrine. Make sure you deliver them convincingly... with passion.

speaker: Follower of Romulus
en: The followers will do anything we tell them to, padrone (master). They believe their god commands them.

speaker: Borgia cardinal
en: Bene. (Good.) Do you have the key?

speaker: Follower of Romulus
en: Yes, padrone (master).

speaker: Borgia cardinal
en: May the Lord be with you.

speaker: Follower of Romulus
en: And also with you, padrone (master).

speaker: Borgia cardinal
en: Assassino! (Assassin!) You will not get me!

speaker: Borgia Cardinal
en: My ascension takes me closer to God, and away from you, Assassino (Assassin)!

speaker: Borgia cardinal
en: Sanctuary denied!

speaker: Borgia cardinal
en: It seems God is on my side, Assassino (Assassin)!

speaker: Borgia cardinal
en: What do you want, Assassino (Assassin)?

speaker: Ezio
en: The Followers of Romulus work for the Pope's gain.

speaker: Borgia cardinal
en: Of course. They are ignorant, we are enlightened. Their savagery will lead the people to the light of the Church.

speaker: Borgia cardinal
en: Godspeed!

speaker: Ezio
en: You have nowhere to run.

speaker: Borgia cardinal
en: What a fool. You wage war against the very instrument that prevents the people from overthrowing order.

speaker: Ezio
en: Your order is no order at all!

speaker: Borgia cardinal
en: You saved me! Praise God!

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in pace. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Vagrant
en: There he goes again.

speaker: Wife
en: That faithless husband of mine is cheating! I know it! As do all the neighbours... please, teach him a lesson for me.

speaker: Husband
en: Dannato! (Goddamn!) She wins! I give up! That bitch, I mean, wonderful wife of mine! I'll go home!

speaker: Paola
en: You can go now, girls.

speaker: Courtesans
en: Do we have to? So innocent... He's cute...

speaker: Paola
en: Now that you've learned how to approach the enemy, we need to find you a suitable weapon.

speaker: Ezio
en: What would you have me use?

speaker: Paola
en: Ah, but you already have the answer...

speaker: Ezio
en: Hey! My father's blade and bracer... How did you get them?

speaker: Paola
en: By using the same skills I've just taught you.

speaker: Ezio
en: It's not exactly in working condition.

speaker: Paola
en: I assume you are familiar with Leonardo da Vinci?

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì. (Yes.) But how does a painter factor into this?

speaker: Paola
en: He's far more than that. Bring him the pieces. You'll see.

speaker: Ezio
en: Before I go, one last question—if I may?

speaker: Paola
en: Of course.

speaker: Ezio
en: Why have you given your aid so readily to me, a stranger?

speaker: Paola
en: I, too, know betrayal.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Oh! Ezio Auditore! I... I didn't expect to see you again. What with all that's happened... Ah! Where are my manners! Welcome back! Now, how can I be of service?

speaker: Ezio
en: I was hoping you could repair something of mine.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Of course! Come! This way.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Ah, che pasticcio... Tutto il santo giorno che cerco... (Oh, what a mess.. I've spent the whole day looking for...) Let me clear a space. All right, lets see it!

speaker: Leonardo
en: Fascinating... I don't know, Ezio. Despite its age, the construction is rather advanced. I've never seen anything quite like it. I'm afraid, there's not much I can do without the original plans. Mi dispiace. (I'm sorry.)

speaker: Leonardo
en: Wait, wait, wait!

speaker: Ezio
en: What are you doing?

speaker: Leonardo
en: The contents of this page are encrypted! But if my theory is correct... Based on these sketches it may very well...

speaker: Ezio
en: It may very well what?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Please, sit!

speaker: Ezio
en: Leonardo?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Shhhh!

speaker: Leonardo
en: Remarkable! If we transpose the letters and then select every third...

speaker: Leonardo
en: There. It's finished!

speaker: Ezio
en: Hmm? What's finished?

speaker: Leonardo
en: The blade! I managed to decode that parchment of yours. It showed me exactly what to do.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Now all that's left is to remove your ring finger.

speaker: Ezio
en: Really?

speaker: Leonardo
en: I'm sorry, but this is how it must be done. The blade is designed to ensure the commitment of whoever wields it.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene. (Fine.) Do it quickly.

speaker: Leonardo
en: I was only having fun, Ezio! Though the blade once required a sacrifice, it's been modified. You can keep your finger.

speaker: Ezio
en: Incredible...

speaker: Leonardo
en: Yes it is! Tell me: Do you have other pages like this?

speaker: Ezio
en: I'm sorry, only the one.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Listen, if you ever do happen across another one of these, please bring it to me.

speaker: Ezio
en: You have my word. And thank you for fixing this. It–

speaker: Guard
en: By order of the Florentine guard: Open this door!

speaker: Leonardo
en: Eh, just a moment.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Wait here!

speaker: Guard
en: Are you Leonardo da Vinci?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Sì. (Yes.) How may I be of service?

speaker: Guard
en: I need you to answer some questions.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Certainly.

speaker: Leonardo
en: What seems to be the trouble?

speaker: Guard
en: A witness claims to have seen you consorting with an enemy of the city.

speaker: Leonardo
en: What? Me? Consorting? Prepostorous!

speaker: Guard
en: When was the last time you saw or spoke with Ezio Auditore?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Who?

speaker: Guard
en: Non fare il finto tonto. (Don't play dumb with me.) We know you were close with the family. Hmm.

speaker: Guard
en: Perhaps this will help to clear your head? Ready to talk? What about now? Tell me what I want to know and we will end this. Had enough yet?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Grazie, (Thank you,) Ezio!

speaker: Ezio
en: Sorry about that.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Eh, I've grown accustomed to their abuses.

speaker: Ezio
en: What of the body?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Bring it inside and put it with the others.

speaker: Ezio
en: Others?

speaker: Leonardo
en: The city gives them to me. For research.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Over there. See? Like it never happened!

speaker: Ezio
en: Thank you, Leonardo—for everything.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Any time! And remember, if you find more of those strange pages, bring them to me. Should they contain new designs, I will upgrade your blade as well!

speaker: Ezio
en: Of course. Now I really should be getting back to Paola...

speaker: Leonardo
en: Porgile i miei omaggi! (Send her my regards!)

speaker: Acrobat
en: A curse on you, thieves! You have ruined me! I hope the Janissaries pluck out your eyes and cut off your hands!

speaker: Ezio
en: Signora (Lady), what is troubling you?

speaker: Acrobat
en: Those brutes there. They attacked me in my home and robbed me of my possessions! Please help.

speaker: Acrobat
en: I owe you my life already, effendi (sir), but I must ask another favor. Will you follow?

speaker: Ezio
en: Where to?

speaker: Acrobat
en: Back to my shop where these men first set upon me. I fear they have taken or destroyed everything I own.

speaker: Ezio
en: Lead on.

speaker: Acrobat
en: They are still here! Out you damn thieves! Get out of my shop!

speaker: Acrobat
en: You have done a great good, effendi (sir). I am sorry I have nothing but my respect to offer you in return.

speaker: Ezio
en: You do not owe me anything, but consider lending your skills to the Assassins. You are a skilled climber, and could learn so much more.

speaker: Acrobat
en: Ah. I am grateful for the offer. Truly.

speaker: Ezio
en: I am impressed, Yusuf. My brothers in Roma would like this.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Just give credit where it is due.

speaker: Kasim
en: Yusuf, cabuk buraya gel! (Yusuf, come quickly!)

speaker: Yusuf
en: Eh?

speaker: Kasim
en: An attack on two fronts! Galata and the Grand Bazaar.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Every day, the same bad news.

speaker: Yusuf
en: How is your appetite for swordplay?

speaker: Ezio
en: I do what I must.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Good man.

speaker: Yusuf
en: When he tires of running, an Assassin must take to the air. Watch.

speaker: Yusuf
en: A Templar scout. And another one there. Watch this.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Assassin! Help!

speaker: Yusuf
en: Time to part company. I'll head to the Bazaar, you stay here. Do you see that tower?

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì. (Yes.) The Galata den?

speaker: Yusuf
en: Evet. (Yes.) I can't be in two places at once... but with you here, I don't have to be. Haydi rastgele. (Good luck.)

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: My men tell me Cesare rallies his best soldiers in front of the main gate into Roma (Rome).

speaker: Ezio
en: Gather the Assassins. We'll face him together.

speaker: Cesare
en: All of Italia (Italy) shall be united, and you will rule beside me.

speaker: Cesare
en: Come to watch my triumph? Soon Micheletto and his army will arrive. But you shall be dead before then.

speaker: Ezio
en: Insieme per la vittoria! (We stand together!)

speaker: Assassins
en: Vittoria agli Assassini! (Victory to the Assassins!)

speaker: Cesare
en: My men will never fail me. They know what awaits them if they do. Kill him. Soon you will pass from this Earth and my dominions will be returned to me. Rip the Assassin's throat out. I want the Assassin name to die today. Your uncle fought back. Look what happened to him.

speaker: Ezio
en: Throw down your arms, Cesare Borgia.

speaker: Cesare
en: Micheletto's troops mass behind me. We will take back my city once and for all.

speaker: Ezio
en: This is not your city anymore.

speaker: Fabio Orsini
en: By order of Pope Julius II, I arrest you, Cesare Borgia, for the crimes of murder, betrayal and incest.

speaker: Cesare
en: No! No! No! No! This is not how it ends! Chains will not hold me! I will not die by the hand of man!

speaker: Ezio
en: It was the manner in which he said it, "Chains will not hold me."

speaker: Leonardo
en: If you are so worried, there is a way to find out.

speaker: Ezio
en: No, it is too powerful. It must be hidden outside the domain of men.

speaker: Leonardo
en: What a shame, hiding a masterpiece where no one will ever see it.

speaker: Ezio
en: And yet... what if he meant what he said? I cannot risk it.

speaker: Ezio
en: Cesare was right. I have to leave.

speaker: Leonardo
en: What about your friends?

speaker: Ezio
en: I built this Brotherhood to last, with or without me.

speaker: Leonardo
en: What do you intend to do?

speaker: Ezio
en: Plant a seed. Here. A gift.

speaker: Leonardo
en: If this is goodbye, then keep your money. I do not want it.

speaker: Ezio
en: We will see each other again, you have my word. Buona fortuna, (good luck) my oldest friend. And take the money. On your meager salary you will need it.

speaker: Leonardo
en: My patron has been arrested after all.

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Rosa
en: There you are, Ezio. Why so serious?

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Ezio
en: It's my birthday.

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Rosa
en: Davvero? (Really)? Cento di questi giorni (Happy birthday). That's wonderful!

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Ezio
en: Is it? It's been over ten years since I watched my father and brothers die. Ten years hunting the men responsible. I'm so close to the end now, but....no closer to understand what any of it was for.

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Rosa
en: You may not see it, Ezio, but it's better here now because of the things you've done. Basta (Enough). Look, here. I have a birthday present for you. It's L'Arsenale's shipping manifest, from the day the boat left.

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Ezio
en: The boat to Cyprus? You're serious?

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Rosa
en: And guess when it's scheduled to return? Tomorrow.

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Leonardo
en: Ezio!

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Ezio
en: Leonardo?! When did you get back?

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Leonardo
en: Just now. I need to talk to you. Right away.

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Rosa
en: Go on. Have fun, boys.

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Ezio
en: This better be good.

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Leonardo
en: Oh, it is! It is! Walk with me. Stay close.

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Leonardo
en: These last two codex pages...I was studying the copies. I don't know why I never saw it before! But when put together, I realized the markings on the back clarify into words. Here: "The Prophet will appear when the second piece is brought to the floating city."

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Ezio
en: Prophet...? "Only the prophet may open it... two Pieces of Eden..."

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Leonardo
en: What are you saying? Ezio, what is this?

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Ezio
en: We've known each other a long time, Leonardo. If I can't trust you, there is nobody. My uncle Mario spoke of it long ago. A prophecy hidden in the Codex.... leading to an ancient vault that holds something... very powerful.

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Leonardo
en: Grandioso (How grand). But, if you took these pages from the Barbarigo, then maybe they know about this vault too. That's not good.

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Ezio
en: Wait...what if that's why they sent the ship to Cyprus? To find this...Piece of Eden...and bring it back to Venezia.

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Leonardo
en: "When the second piece is brought to the floating city..."

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Ezio
en: "...The Prophet will appear...only the prophet can open the vault..." My God! When my uncle told me about the Codex I was too young, too brash to imagine it was anything but an old man's fantasy! But now I see....the killing of Mocenigo....even the Medici....my father and brothers....it was all part of his plan! To find the vault...the Spaniard!

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Leonardo
en: Rodrigo Borgia.

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Ezio
en: The boat from Cyprus arrives tomorrow. I plan to be there to meet it.

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Leonardo
en: Good luck, my friend.

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Ezio
en: Uncle Mario...? Where are they taking it?

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Guard
en: The Maestro awaits. He will not suffer mistakes. Package it correctly. Do it now.

scene: All Things Come to He Who Waits
speaker: Ezio
en: The Spaniard's here?! That changes things. If I can infiltrate this group...take the place of the courier....they'll lead me right to the figlio di puttana (son of a bitch).

speaker: Host
en: Welcome, benvenuti (Welcome)! Are you ready to test yourselves with a game of speed and endurance? Many challenges lie in your path. The game is simple, but finishing it, near impossible! Start when you're ready. The first contestant to beat the course record is one step closer to the Golden Mask!

speaker: Host
en: The winner! You've proven yourself the fastest and strongest in Venezia! You are now one step closer to the grand prize!

speaker: Cesare
en: What has happened here?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: I do not know what you mean?

speaker: Cesare
en: My funds, my troops. Gone.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Financial difficulties strike all of us, even those with an army.

speaker: Cesare
en: You intend to give me money?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: No, I do not.

speaker: Cesare
en: Then I will use the Piece of Eden to get what I want. Your help is not necessary.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: That has been made abundantly clear to me. Are you aware that the Baron de Valois is dead?

speaker: Cesare
en: No. Did you

speaker: Rodrigo
en: What reason could I possibly have to kill him? Was he plotting against me with my "brilliant," traitorous, Captain General?

speaker: Cesare
en: I do not have to stand for this.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: The Assassins murdered him.

speaker: Cesare
en: Why did you not stop them?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: As if I could. It was not my decision to attack Monteriggioni, it was yours! It is high time you took responsibility for your actions.

speaker: Cesare
en: My accomplishments. Despite the constant interference of failures like you.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: You are not going anywhere. I have the Piece of Eden.

speaker: Cesare
en: Get out of my way, old man.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: I gave you everything and yet it's never enough!

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Cesare! He intends to poison you!

speaker: Rodrigo
en: You would not listen to reason.

speaker: Cesare
en: Father. Do you not see? I control all of this. If I want to live, I live. If I want to take, I take. If I want you to die, you die!

speaker: Cesare
en: Where is the Piece of Eden?

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Stop! I know where it is.

speaker: Cesare
en: And you did not tell me he had taken it?

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Cesare... It's me... your queen.

speaker: Cesare
en: You are my sister. Nothing more. Where is it?

speaker: Lucrezia
en: You... never loved me?

speaker: Cesare
en: Where is the Apple? Tell me.

speaker: Cesare
en: Tell me!

speaker: Ezio
en: All right, Cesare. I am coming through that window.

speaker: Cesare
en: I want the Apple!

speaker: Cesare
en: Am I hurting you? Give me the Apple! It is mine, not yours. Where is the Apple?

speaker: Cesare
en: Smart decision, little sister.

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in pace. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Lucrezia
en: I know... I know where that bastard is going. San Pietro (Saint Peter's)... The pavilion in the courtyard.

speaker: Ezio
en: Thank you.

speaker: Cesare
en: Assassino! (Assassin!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Cazzo. (Fuck.)

speaker: Cesare
en: I will come for you later.

speaker: Cesare
en: You?!

speaker: Ezio
en: Looking for this?

speaker: Cesare
en: It ends now, Assassino. My sword will take your life.

speaker: Cesare
en: GUARDS! GUARDS!

speaker: Arch Enemies
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus 2.0.

speaker: Condottiero
en: Non si passa! (None shall pass!) Do you hear me? Until you've all submitted and given yourself over to the prophet, Savonarola—this bridge will remain closed to you! I hear you moaning and complaining. You say you have things to do. Places to go. Obligations to fulfill. Hah! You have but ONE obligation—TO SUBMIT! Why fight us? Why resist us? The city is ours. Your precious Medici have abandoned you! Fled into the wastes to wallow in self pity! Savonarola wants only the best for you. A city free of vice and temptation. A people united by faith. All men are equal in the eyes of the Lord—and so they shall be in Firenze! This is a chance for us to turn over a new leaf! To leave behind our miserable past—and return to simpler times. I am here to help. To lead you into a new future. Only accept our gift. Continue to refuse, and I fear you'll have to contend with more than just a shattered bridge. Understand my intention is not to threaten! I merely seek to open your eyes to a greater truth—that times are changing. No... that times HAVE changed. And nothing good will come of resisting...

speaker: Ezio
en: You wear a noble's clothes. How is it Savonarola charmed you?

speaker: Condottiero
en: Wealth and power do not ensure contentment. I wanted even more...

speaker: Ezio
en: And now, instead, you have nothing. Questo non è che un atto dovuto (This is something that must be done)... Requiescat in pace (Rest in peace).

speaker: Paola
en: Bentornato (Welcome back) Ezio. Were you successful?

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes.

speaker: Ezio
en: Madre? (Mother?)

speaker: Claudia
en: Ezio! Where have you been?! They wouldn't let us leave. And mother... Uch! She hasn't spoken a single word since we left the house. Father will need to sort things out... Where is father? And Federico? And Petruccio? Hmmm?

speaker: Ezio
en: Something's happened.

speaker: Claudia
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Claudia
en: No. It's impossible!

speaker: Ezio
en: Claudia...

speaker: Claudia
en: No, no, no, no.

speaker: Ezio
en: I did everything I could, piccina (little one)...

speaker: Ezio
en: Listen, right now what matters is getting us all someplace safe. But to do that, I need you to stay focused. Do you understand?

speaker: Ezio
en: Good. Will you watch over mother for me?

speaker: Ezio
en: Then we are ready. Thank you again, for everything.

speaker: Paola
en: Stay safe, Ezio. Stay vigilant. I suspect the road ahead is yet long.

speaker: Claudia
en: How could this have happened to us?

speaker: Ezio
en: I don't know.

speaker: Claudia
en: Will we ever be back?

speaker: Ezio
en: I don't know.

speaker: Claudia
en: What will happen to our house?

speaker: Ezio
en: I don't know!

speaker: Claudia
en: Were they... Were they given a proper burial?

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes. They were...

speaker: Manuel
en: You may verify the amount, Tarik, but the money stays with me until I have seen the cargo for myself and assayed its quality.

speaker: Tarik
en: Understood. You are a shrewd man, Manuel.

speaker: Manuel
en: Trust without cynicism is hollow.

speaker: Janissary
en: The count is good, Tarik. It's all here.

speaker: Manuel
en: So what now?

speaker: Tarik
en: You will have access to the arsenal. When you are satisfied, the cargo will be delivered to a location of your choosing.

speaker: Manuel
en: Are your men prepared to travel?

speaker: Tarik
en: Not a problem.

speaker: Manuel
en: Poli Kalà. (Very good.) I will have a map drawn up for you within the week.

speaker: Ezio
en: Are we here for the same reason?

speaker: Yusuf
en: One of my men claims he saw a shipment of weapons enter the arsenal. So I got curious.

speaker: Ezio
en: Weapons. I would like to see them for myself.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Short of killing everyone, I'm not sure how you will get inside.

speaker: Janissary
en: You have been warned twice! No merchants near the arsenal wall. Take this away!

speaker: Merchant
en: Hypocrites! If your men did not buy my produce, I wouldn't sell it here! You are worse than the Byzantines, you traitor!

speaker: Janissary
en: Hold your tongue, parasite!

speaker: Yusuf
en: Even in times of peace, the poor are always under siege.

speaker: Ezio
en: If we inspire them to vent their anger, perhaps that will help our cause.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Feigning solidarity to push your own agenda. What a gentleman. No?

speaker: Ezio
en: It is not pretty, I know. But it will work.

speaker: Herald 1
en: The Janissaries are corrupted, good people of Konstantiniyye! They have surrendered their loyalties to the devil, and do injury to our Sultan's image!

speaker: Herald 2
en: Men and women of the city! Hear me now! You have broken no laws, and thus deserve no abuse. Fight back against these men who belittle you!

speaker: Herald 3
en: Good citizens of Istanbul! The Janissaries collude against you! Do not suffer their injuries! Return them!

speaker: Ezio
en: That gate will not stay closed for long.

speaker: Yusuf
en: The people are doing you a favor, Ezio. Return it, and keep them safe from harm.

speaker: Citizens
en: Justice or death!

speaker: Guards
en: Hold them back!

speaker: Citizens
en: Down, you bastard!

speaker: Guards
en: Sound the alert!

speaker: Citizens
en: Push through! Go! Go! Justice or death! Forward!

speaker: Manuel
en: Twenty years in this city, living like a cipher... and finally, everything is falling into place.

speaker: Shahkulu
en: When the Palaiologos line is restored, Manuel, do not forget who helped you bring it back.

speaker: Manuel
en: Of course not, my friend! I would not dream of betraying a man of your influence. But you must be patient. Nova Roma wasn't built in a day. I am satisfied. Take me to my ship. If a single one is damaged, the money stays with me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Merda! (shit!)

speaker: Margherita
en: Calmatevi (Calm down). The pain will end soon.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where have you brought me?

speaker: Margherita
en: Nowhere, Messere (Mister). A man left you here.

speaker: Ezio
en: Did he say anything?

speaker: Margherita
en: Only this. You are to meet Messer (Mister) Machiavelli in front of the Mausoleo di Augusto. Let me help you get dressed.

speaker: Ezio
en: The same man who brought me here gave me these clothes?

speaker: Margherita
en: Sì, Messere. (Yes, Mister).

speaker: Ezio
en: Ah. Roma.

speaker: Margherita
en: Yes, or what is left of it since the Borgia came to power.

speaker: Ezio
en: And the Mausoleo?

speaker: Margherita
en: Unfortunately, you cannot see it from here.

speaker: Ezio
en: How about from the top of that church?

speaker: Margherita
en: Yes, but the stairs up are closed.

speaker: Ezio
en: That should not be a problem. Vi ringrazio di tutto quello che avete fatto per me, buona donna. Addio. (Thank you very much for everything you have done for me. Farewell, good woman).

speaker: Ezio
en: I need to find a doctor. My arm! Merda! (Shit!) My back...

speaker: Ezio
en: Salute (Hello). I require medicine.

speaker: Doctor
en: Let me look. Someone your age cannot recover from a wound like this with medicine. Here is something to dull the pain; you will heal over time.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie. (Thank you).

speaker: Doctor
en: Four out of five doctors would suggest leeches, but they have not proven effective against such things. However, I can recommend several good colleagues around the city. Do you need anything else?

speaker: Ezio
en: "Someone my age." Imbecille... (Jerk...)

speaker: Borgia Soldier
en: Word has gone out that a peasant is resisting arrest. We will show him how things operate under the Borgia.

speaker: Ezio
en: Machiavelli can wait.

speaker: Ezio
en: Volpe, how goes Roma?

speaker: La Volpe
en: Very well Ezio. The French and the Papal forces are in disarray.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then it is almost time. Call the Assassins together and... bring Claudia.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Now?

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Laa shay'a waqi'un moutlaq bale kouloun moumkine. The wisdom of our Creed is revealed through these words. We work in the dark, to serve the light. We are Assassins.

speaker: Ezio
en: Claudia. We here dedicate our lives to protecting the freedom of humanity. Mario, our father and our brother once stood around this fire, fighting off the darkness. Now, I offer the choice to you. Join us.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: You and I have not seen eye-to-eye on many issues.

speaker: Ezio
en: Niccolò

speaker: Machiavelli
en: But you are exactly what the Order needed. You have led the charge against the Templars and rebuilt this Brotherhood. Now, we must put Ezio where he belongs, at the head of the Assassins. Ezio Auditore da Firenze. You will now be known as il Mentore (The Mentor), the guardian of our Order and our secrets.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where other men blindly follow the truth, remember...

speaker: All
en: Nothing is true.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where other men are limited by morality or law, remember...

speaker: All
en: Everything is permitted.

speaker: Ezio
en: Why the sudden change of heart?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: I have always stood by you. I was the one who brought you to Roma, and the one who caused the explosion as you fled the Castello. The mercenari who protected you at il Colosseo (The Colosseum) were mine as well. You just did not know it.

speaker: Informant
en: Maestro Machiavelli. Cesare has returned to Roma alone. He rides for the Castel Sant'Angelo.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Grazie. (Thank you.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Well?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: The decision is yours, not mine.

speaker: Ezio
en: Niccolò. You'd better not stop telling me what you think. Why else would I seek the opinion of my most trusted advisor?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Go kill them, Mentore. Finish what you started.

speaker: Ezio
en: Good advice.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: I intend to write a book about you one day.

speaker: Ezio
en: If you do, make it short.

speaker: Ezio
en: I hope we can speak without interruption, Gaspar. Who gave you the names of the imprisoned Assassins?

speaker: Gaspar
en: What do you mean "Assassins"? Our dungeons are for heretics, not medieval phantoms.

speaker: Ezio
en: No... your purge was too systematic to be a coincidence.

speaker: Gaspar
en: Whoever those men claim to be, it won't matter after today. A public burning is about to commence for one of them. A wilful young man.

speaker: Ezio
en: If he dies, I will keep that fire burning until this town is a cinder. What's this? A list? Six names... they may be Assassins too... when Sánchez and I cross paths again, I will ask him.

speaker: Ezio
en: I must not be seen anywhere near this man's body... patience.

speaker: Torquemada
en: The Queen let the Moor King live? Isabella's heart is not hard enough to do lasting good for España (Spain). When the time is right, I will give her counsel. España (Spain) must be unified. One people, one faith.

speaker: Juan
en: Until then, Tomás...?

speaker: Torquemada
en: Round up all who do not profess allegiance to the Pope and expel them. If they resist, you are free to do as you will.

speaker: Juan
en: Yes Tomás. God be with you.

speaker: Torquemada
en: And you, Juan de Marillo. May he guide your every step.

speaker: Juan
en: Round up your best men and prepare for a sweep of the city.

speaker: Sánchez
en: Ezio, the shadows of my city are moving again! How many of our brothers were you able to find?

speaker: Ezio
en: Five of six. An inquisitor named Torquemada murdered one before I could reach him.

speaker: Sánchez
en: That would be Tomás Torquemada, the King's Grand Inquisitor... he must be here to speak with Pedro Llorente.

speaker: Ezio
en: I saw them together. It appears their orders to arrest the Assassins came directly from Rodrigo Borgia himself.

speaker: Sánchez
en: Just as we suspected: contact between the Templars and the Inquisitors. Both these men must be stopped. Pedro will be easy to find here in Zaragoza. But locating Torquemada may take some time.

speaker: Ezio
en: I'm a patient man, Sánchez.

speaker: Pedro
en: What's this? You're not allowed in here!

speaker: Ezio
en: Excuse my intrusion, but I was told you might know how to get me in contact with the Templars.

speaker: Pedro
en: The Templars? Surely you're joking, young man. The Templars were disgraced and disbanded two centuries ago. Rumors of their continued activities are as reliable as fairy tales.

speaker: Ezio
en: That's a shame, Padre... if they don't exist, they won't be able to save you.

speaker: Guard 1
en: You there. Open the gate to the catacombs.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Off to counsel King Muhammad, are you? I don't understand that fool. Why does he keep us fighting this pointless war?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Are you being insubordinate, soldier? Just open the damn gates!

speaker: Guard 2
en: Yes, sir.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Ha ha. The poor lad's got no idea does he?

speaker: Guard 1
en: And it had better stay that way. If anyone knew we were prolonging this war deliberately, it would alter the Queen's tactics.

speaker: Guard 3
en: By God, you Templars convolute even the simplest plans.

speaker: Ezio
en: You are a vile and pitiful man, Torquemada. And your alliance with the Spaniard has disqualified you from your God's love.

speaker: Torquemada
en: You dare to lecture me? I am the hammer of heretics, the light of España (Spain), the honor of my order. I follow none but God's command.

speaker: Ezio
en: All lies. Rodrigo Borgia is an unbeliever like me, and yet you lavish him with favors.

speaker: Torquemada
en: A fantastic tale, and a spurious one. Borgia is one of three Papal candidates this year. And he is as devoted to God as I am.

speaker: Ezio
en: There's no better hiding place than in the shadow of virtue. You are as blind to his evil as you are to yours.

speaker: Torquemada
en: So what will you do with me, heathen? Murder me? Slit my throat and bathe in my blood?

speaker: Ezio
en: No... I prefer a quick, clean kill.

speaker: Torquemada
en: Guards!

speaker: Ezio
en: You will discover the truth about Rodrigo Borgia in time. But by then it will be too late.

speaker: Ezio
en: Forgive me, my friends. Torquemada escaped. But not before enlightening me on one or two points. He is a petty man, consumed by self-deception.

speaker: Luis
en: What of his connection to the Spaniard?

speaker: Ezio
en: He admires Rodrigo Borgia, but I do not believe Torquemada is a Templar himself. Merely a credulous old sycophant. Perhaps this is for the best. Torquemada's death would have caused more turmoil than it ended.

speaker: Luis
en: We will work hard to distance him from the Queen, while we protect ourselves from the Inquisitors.

speaker: Ezio
en: Best of luck, my new friends. And send me word when Christoffa .

speaker: Sanchez
en: He has promised to write me the moment he arrives. I will forward a copy of any letter he sends.

speaker: Ezio
en: I look forward to it...

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Salute, Ezio. Welcome back. And well done. My host is restored to its former glory. Now Silvio will see just how grave a mistake he's made.

speaker: Ezio
en: How should we proceed? A direct assault against the Arsenale?

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: No. We'd be massacred at the gates. I have something else in mind. Take my men and plant them throughout the district. The trouble they cause will force Silvio to dispatch most of his guards.

speaker: Ezio
en: And with the Arsenale drained of mercenaries, I can move in for the kill.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Esatto! (Exactly!) You'll be virtually unopposed.

speaker: Ezio
en: Let's hope he takes the bait.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Oh, don't worry. He will.

speaker: Ezio
en: Wait here for my signal.

speaker: Mercenary
en: As you wish.

speaker: Ezio
en: Hold your ground here.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Consider it done.

speaker: Ezio
en: Here. This is where you'll wait.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Send word when it's time to strike.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Ezio. You have to save my wife. Take the rooftops.

speaker: Octavian
en: I only wanted respect.

speaker: Ezio
en: Respect is earned, not inherited or purchased.

speaker: Octavian
en: Perhaps you are right... I need more time...

speaker: Ezio
en: Che tu sia pari nella morte. (May you be equal in death.) Requiescat in pace. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Pantasilea!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Don't ever disappear again. I was lost without you.

speaker: Pantasilea
en: Really? But you rescued me.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Ezio came up with a brilliant plan.

speaker: Ezio
en: I did not. It was all your husband's idea.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: It was?

speaker: Pantasilea
en: You are my prince.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Now I better earn that title.

speaker: Pantasilea
en: You will.

speaker: Pantasilea
en: Thank you.

speaker: Avenger
en: Please... please help. Find the man who did this to me.

speaker: Ezio
en: I should get you to a hekim (healer).

speaker: Avenger
en: No, there is no time. The man who did this, he is looking for my wife and my daughter. If he finds them, God knows what he will do! If you value justice, arkadashim (my friend), please... do not let that monster harm my family.

speaker: Ezio
en: It is done. How are you feeling?

speaker: Avenger
en: My wounds will heal, and my heart is lifted knowing that my family is safe. How can I repay you?

speaker: Ezio
en: Join us when you are feeling well, brother. We could use men with a sense of honor.

speaker: Avenger
en: Evet (Yes), I will. Most certainly.

speaker: Courtesan
en: The Senator and I have uncovered the planned meeting place of the Borgia and the foreign ambassadors. You have killed ambassadors, now those who plotted with them must be stopped. I can show you where, but I leave the rest to you. We must ride.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Grazie (Thank you), Ezio! I will return to the Rosa in Fiore. The others will know of your bravery.

speaker: Ezio
en: Tarik was no traitor, Suleiman. He too was tracking the Byzantines.

speaker: Suleiman
en: What? So did you...?

speaker: Ezio
en: I am sorry.

speaker: Suleiman
en: God forgive me. I should not have been so quick to judge.

speaker: Ezio
en: He was loyal to your grandfather to the end, and through his efforts we have the means to save your city.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Ah, Tarik. He should not have been so secretive. What a terrible way to do a good thing.

speaker: Ezio
en: The weapons were taken to Cappadocia. Can you get me there?

speaker: Suleiman
en: Yes, of course. I will arrange a ship to take you

speaker: Ahmet
en: Suleiman! Suleiman, I have been set up, and made to look a traitor! Do you remember Tarik, the Janissary?

speaker: Suleiman
en: The man you quarreled with?

speaker: Ahmet
en: He has been murdered. It is no secret that he and I were at odds. Now the Janissaries will accuse me of this crime.

speaker: Suleiman
en: This is terrible news, uncle.

speaker: Ahmet
en: When word gets back to my father, he will banish me from the city!

speaker: Ahmet
en: Ah. Forgive me, nephew. I was not aware that you had a guest.

speaker: Suleiman
en: This is Marcello, one of my European advisers in Kefe.

speaker: Ezio
en: Buonasera. (Good evening.)

speaker: Ahmet
en: Marcello, my nephew and I have a private matter to discuss.

speaker: Suleiman
en: As I said, there will be a ship waiting for you when you wish to leave.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie, mio principe. (Thank you, my Prince.)

speaker: Suleiman
en: We will track down the perpetrator of this crime, uncle. Have patience.

speaker: Bearers of Bad News
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Ezio
en: Ehi Claudia. (Hey Claudia.) How are you?

speaker: Claudia
en: Bene... (Okay...)

speaker: Ezio
en: You shouldn't keep things from me.

speaker: Claudia
en: It's Duccio.

speaker: Ezio
en: What of him?

speaker: Claudia
en: I think he's been... unfaithful.

speaker: Ezio
en: Who told you this?

speaker: Claudia
en: The other girls. I thought they were my friends.

speaker: Ezio
en: Harpies! You're better off without them.

speaker: Claudia
en: I loved him.

speaker: Ezio
en: No, Claudia. You only thought you did.

speaker: Claudia
en: He should suffer for what he's done.

speaker: Ezio
en: Wait here. I'll go have a word with him.

speaker: Woman
en: Oh, Duccio! It's beautiful!

speaker: Duccio
en: Nothing but the best for you, amore mio. (my love)

speaker: Woman
en: But... what of Claudia? I thought you'd been promised to her?

speaker: Duccio
en: Father said I could do much better than an Auditore.

speaker: Woman
en: Birbante! (Naughty!) Come, let us walk a bit.

speaker: Duccio
en: Walk? I had something else in mind...

speaker: Woman
en: Oh Duccio...

speaker: Ezio
en: Ehi, lurido porco! (Hey, dirty pig!)

speaker: Duccio
en: Ezio, my friend!

speaker: Duccio
en: Ma che ti piglia?! (What the hell?!)

speaker: Ezio
en: You insult my sister, parading around with this puttana. (whore)

speaker: Duccio
en: Wh-what are you talking about?!

speaker: Ezio
en: I saw the gift you gave her. Heard the things you said.

speaker: Duccio
en: Maybe your sister shouldn't be so stingy with her virtù... (virtue...)

speaker: Ezio
en: You broke her heart.

speaker: Duccio
en: And now I'm going to break your face!

speaker: Duccio
en: You Auditores all talk big—but when it comes time for action? Hah!

speaker: Ezio
en: You'll regret ever opening your mouth!

speaker: Duccio
en: I could have taught your sister a great many things! She's lucky to have had someone like me!

speaker: Ezio
en: Bastardo! (Bastard!)

speaker: Duccio
en: Basta! Mi arrendo! (Stop! I yield!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Stay away from my sister!

speaker: Man
en: You there! Hello! Can you help me?

speaker: Ezio
en: What is troubling you, amico (friend)?

speaker: Man
en: There is a madwoman in this district putting curses on people with little silver coins!

speaker: Ezio
en: Curses?

speaker: Man
en: Well, not curses exactly... but old Byzantine coins. She is sneaking them into our pockets while our heads are turned, and I do not find it funny!

speaker: Ezio
en: Keep your leggings on. I will have a look.

speaker: Ezio
en: Ferma! (Stop!) Stop!

speaker: Ezio
en: Quite a trick you have there. Slipping worthless coins into men's pockets. Have you ever been caught?

speaker: Thief
en: Not once! Although I have, on occasion, TAKEN money as well. But only to feed myself.

speaker: Ezio
en: Why do you not put that trick to better use. Fight with the Assassins. Work for a just cause.

speaker: Thief
en: Hm. Well it would be nice to be a part of something larger than myself. Evet (Yes), I will fight with you.

speaker: Beginnings of a Conspiracy
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus 2.0.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Over here, Ezio! We've found Archbishop Salvati! He's barricaded himself inside that villa... Take some of my men. Use them to clear the fields. Then find a way over the walls so you can open the gates.

speaker: Ezio
en: Hmmm... Command over my own army? A nice change of pace from the usual sneaking and stabbing. I like it.

speaker: Salviati
en: I see you there, Assassin! These walls have stood for a hundred years and will stand for a hundred more! Stop wasting the lives of your men! Vattene! Vattene via! (Go away!) All that awaits you here is death! Turn back!

speaker: Salviati
en: Men prepare yourself, the Assassin has arrived!

speaker: Ezio
en: I need to find a way to open the gates...

speaker: Salviati
en: I warned you to stay away, Assassin! You should have listened!! You're finished, Assassin! Do you hear me?! Finished!

speaker: Ezio
en: You Templars, always singing the same song...

speaker: Salviati
en: Do you think a few mercenari (mercenaries) scare me? Hah!

speaker: Ezio
en: They should.

speaker: Salviati
en: Shall I send your remains to that ubriacone (drunkard), Mario? Hah! What's the point? There won't be anything left of you to recognize!

speaker: Ezio
en: It's quite a plan you have: Spouting nonsense while you send these other men to die.

speaker: Salviati
en: I am a reasonable man. What say you to this: turn back now and I'll call off my men.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sorry, friend. You are on my list. Your fate is sealed.

speaker: Salviati
en: Tear him limb from limb! Let us paint the walls with his blood!

speaker: Ezio
en: That is no way to treat a guest!

speaker: Salviati
en: What is this?! Guards! To me!

speaker: Ezio
en: Where is Jacopo?

speaker: Salviati
en: He knows you come for him... emerging only in darkness to meet with the others...

speaker: Ezio
en: That answers when... Now tell me where?

speaker: Ezio
en: La fede dovrebbe dare conforto, non pena. (Faith should bring comfort, not pain.) Requiescat in Pace. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Alvise
en: Messer da Vinci?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Yes?

speaker: Alvise
en: Buongiorno e ben arrivato! I am Alvise. Il Signor Dona has asked that I escort you to the workshop. Are you ready?

speaker: Alvise
en: Ah, Venezia! What other place is as beautiful, as stable, as perfect? Come, I will show you her wonders! Our first stop, the Rialto bridge! Behold the elegance with which she spans the Grand Canal; a symbol of Venetian unity and pride! Let us continue. Here we are: San Giacomo di Rialto. Oldest church in Venezia. Isn't she beautiful? And her clock tower? Magnifico! Come, come! There's more to see! No other city can match the size of Venezia's markets. Be it spices or silk, from near and far, there is... there is...

speaker: Guard
en: You were told to stay home!

speaker: Merchant
en: But the rent is paid! I have every right to sell here!

speaker: Guard
en: Emilio disagrees!

speaker: Merchant
en: No, stop! Stop!

speaker: Alvise
en: Let us continue the tour... elsewhere.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Look! Isn't it amazing? Would you mind buying it for me? I... uh... I left my money with my bags.

speaker: Ezio
en: Hey! Mind your step, coglione (jerk)!

speaker: Alvise
en: And here we have the Palazzo della Seta, home to Emilio Barbarigo. Normally, I'd suggest a closer look, but... with the way things are now...

speaker: Ezio
en: Why? What's happened?

speaker: Alvise
en: He is attempting to unify the merchants beneath a single banner. There's been resistance, some of it violent.

speaker: Ezio
en: What kind of resistance?

speaker: Alvise
en: They say they're fighting for the people; for freedom or some such nonsense. Baggianate (Nonsense), if you ask me.

speaker: Merchant
en: They destroyed my stand. I demand compensation!

speaker: Guard 1
en: Here you are, then.

speaker: Merchant
en: The Doge will know about this! I'll report you to the Council!

speaker: Guard 2
en: Good luck with that, my friend.

speaker: Merchant
en: What are you doing?!

speaker: Guard 3
en: You're under arrest for disrupting commerce.

speaker: Merchant
en: What?! You just invented that! There's no such law!

speaker: Guard 3
en: There is now.

speaker: Merchant
en: No! Stop!

speaker: Alvise
en: And now, I present to you, your workshop, Ser da Vinci! We spared no expense in its design! You'll see it is perfect; as if you never left Firenze! I wish you great success and hope you enjoy Venezia as much as she enjoys having you.

speaker: Leonardo
en: So, here we are! Exciting, isn't it? Care to come in?

speaker: Ezio
en: Maybe later. I need to visit the Palazzo della Seta; try and gain an audience with Emilio.

speaker: Leonardo
en: As you wish, but should you find yourself with free time or another Codex page, don't hesitate to visit. My door is always open.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie (Thank you), my friend.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Di nulla. (It's nothing.)

speaker: Cristina
en: Ezio! What are you doing here?

speaker: Ezio
en: I only just came back to Firenze... Look at you! As beautiful as ever.

speaker: Cristina
en: But... Oh, Ezio... I... It's been two years!

speaker: Ezio
en: And I've thought of nothing but you.

speaker: Cristina
en: Oh, but, Ezio...

speaker: Ezio
en: What is it?

speaker: Cristina
en: I'm engaged to be married! My father kept asking me to choose... I thought I would never see you again!

speaker: Woman
en: It's Manfredo! He's going to kill him!

speaker: Cristina
en: What!?

speaker: Man
en: Un tale (Some guy) he lost money to! He's dragged him out to the end of the new bridge!

speaker: Ezio
en: Who the hell is Manfredo?

speaker: Cristina
en: My fiancé...

speaker: Manfredo
en: I'll pay you back, I swear!

speaker: Guard
en: It's too late for that now.

speaker: Manfredo
en: It wasn't my fault. I was going to have the money for you today... But a payment came in late!

speaker: Guard
en: I do not care about you troubles. Only my money.

speaker: Manfredo
en: But I can pay you!

speaker: Guard
en: Now?

speaker: Manfredo
en: Tomorrow!

speaker: Guard
en: You'll be dead tomorrow.

speaker: Manfredo
en: Wait. Please. I'm about to be married tomorrow.

speaker: Guard
en: You should've thought of that before you started gambling.

speaker: Manfredo
en: Grazie, Messere! You don't know how close–

speaker: Manfredo
en: Whoa! Hey! Aspetta! (Wait!) What are you doing!?

speaker: Ezio
en: Do you love her?

speaker: Manfredo
en: What!?

speaker: Ezio
en: DO YOU LOVE HER? Cristina! The woman you're about to marry!

speaker: Manfredo
en: Yes, I do! I swear, I do. Kill me here and I will die still loving her.

speaker: Ezio
en: You are never going to gamble again.

speaker: Manfredo
en: Never, Messere.

speaker: Ezio
en: You will be a good husband to her. Or I will hunt you down and kill you myself.

speaker: Ezio
en: He's fine. He'll make a good husband. I made sure of it.

speaker: Cristina
en: What– What!?

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Ezio Auditore! Come in, come in. I'll kill you if you don't.

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Ezio
en: Bartolomeo!

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Wait here. You have to meet my wife. Pantasilea! Pantasilea! Where is she?

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Ezio
en: Did you check behind the table?

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Ahhh. Here she is!

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Pantasilea
en: Lieta di conoscervi. (Nice to meet you.)

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Ezio
en: Charmed. Truly.

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Now, we talk about war.

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Ezio
en: How goes the fight against the French?

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Bene. (Good.) My men are holding their own.

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Ezio
en: Machiavelli seemed to think things were more difficult.

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Bartolomeo
en: You know Machiavelli. He

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Mercenary
en: Abbiamo bisogno del vostro aiuto! (We need your help!)

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Scusatemi. (Excuse me.) Throw me Bianca!

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Pantasilea
en: Ezio. Let me get straight to the point. The fight is not going well. We have been attacked on both sides. Borgia on one, French on the other. But know this; the Borgia position is weak. If you can defeat them, we can concentrate our forces on the French front.

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Ezio
en: I think I know a way to help. Thank you for disclosing this to me Madonna (Madame) d'Alviano.

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Pantasilea
en: It is the least a wife can do to help her husband.

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Mercenary
en: Someone! Stop their leader before he gets to the tower!

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Ezio. We sent those luridi codardi (fucking cowards) running for the hills!

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Ezio
en: Yes, we did.

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Now that the Pope's dogs have fled, I will be able to draw more men to the fight. But first, I want to reinforce our barracks.

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Ezio
en: Who will take care of this?

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Bartolomeo
en: I'm no good with these things. You are the educated one, you approve the plans!

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Ezio
en: Va bene (Okay), but in return I need to know Cesare and Rodrigo's every move. Can your men track them for me?

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Of course!

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Isn't she a thing of beauty?

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Ezio
en: Very impressive.

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Bartolomeo
en: More men join us everyday. It has become very competitive, which is just the way I like it. As you can see, this board shows the ranks of our top warriors. Prove your skills and you will move up the list.

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Ezio
en: Shouldn't I already be at the top?

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Mercenary
en: Gian's fighting downstairs!

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Bartolomeo
en: If you are looking to show off, we also have fights. Now, if you'll excuse me, I've got money on this match.

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Pantasilea
en: Where is Bartolomeo?

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Ezio
en: At the fight downstairs.

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Pantasilea
en: He has such an aggressive view of the world. However, strategy is equally important. Take these carrier pigeons for example: Each one sent from Machiavelli bears the name of an important Templar in Roma. Eliminate them and you will have more of an impact than a battle ever could.

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Ezio
en: Thank you, Madonna (Madame). Can you ask Bartolomeo to come see me at Isola Tiberina (Tiber Island) with a report about Cesare and Rodrigo's whereabouts?

scene: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
speaker: Pantasilea
en: He will be there.

speaker: Silvio
en: Where is Emilio?

speaker: Carlo
en: I told him to be here.

speaker: Silvio
en: You told him yourself? In person?

speaker: Carlo
en: Yes, myself, in person. I'm concerned that you don't trust me.

speaker: Silvio
en: As am I. Perhaps he'll arrive with the others. Walk with me.

speaker: Silvio
en: So, how goes things at the palace?

speaker: Carlo
en: Honestly, it's difficult. Mocenigo keeps his circle close. I have tried to lay the groundwork, making suggestions, but he has other voices at his ears.

speaker: Silvio
en: Then you must work harder. You must become part of his inner circle.

speaker: Carlo
en: Sì (Yes). I understand. But it's harder than I expected.

speaker: Silvio
en: And why is that, Carlo?

speaker: Carlo
en: I don't know! He's just a... the Doge doesn't like me.

speaker: Silvio
en: I wonder why.

speaker: Carlo
en: It's not my fault! I keep trying to please him. I learn what he craves, and I have it delivered. The finest jams from the orchards of Sardinia, the latest fashions from Milano

speaker: Silvio
en: Yes, and that's called being a sycophant.

speaker: Carlo
en: A what? What did you call me?!

speaker: Silvio
en: A doormat, a flatterer, a bootlicker. Need I go on?

speaker: Carlo
en: Bastardo (Bastard)! You don't know what it's like; you don't understand the pressure in there.

speaker: Silvio
en: Oh, I don't understand pressure?!

speaker: Carlo
en: No, you have no idea! You are a government official! I am two steps from the Doge himself. I am beside him day and night! You WISH you could be where I am!

speaker: Silvio
en: Are you done?

speaker: Carlo
en: Hardly. You listen to me now! I am close. The Doge can be recruited to our cause, I'm sure of it. I just... I need a little more time.

speaker: Silvio
en: Time is not a thing we have in great supply. Keep moving.

speaker: Carlo
en: Is it much further?

speaker: Silvio
en: Don't be such a little girl!

speaker: Marco
en: Buon giorno (Good day), cousin. Signor Carlo.

speaker: Silvio
en: We thought Emilio would be with you.

speaker: Marco
en: Emilio is dead.

speaker: Silvio
en: What? How?

speaker: Carlo
en: The Assassin! The same one who hunted down the Pazzi! He's here, in Venezia.

speaker: Marco
en: È così (It is so). Silvio, did you not know? He could be anywhere. He could be here right now and we might not even know. He struck Emilio inside his own palazzo!

speaker: Silvio
en: And so, what of our plans?

speaker: Marco
en: There is no longer time for subtlety, my brothers. We must act now.

speaker: Carlo
en: But Marco, I'm so close! A few more days. If I can just

speaker: Marco
en: No. It happens this week.

speaker: Dante
en: We should keep moving.

speaker: Marco
en: My feet are killing me. Can't we sit down inside somewhere?

speaker: Emilio
en: Do you know anywhere truly safe to discuss things such as these?

speaker: Silvio
en: And what does the Spaniard have to say of this change of plan?

speaker: Marco
en: You can ask him yourself soon enough.

speaker: Carlo
en: He's here? From Roma?

speaker: Marco
en: So I've heard.

speaker: Silvio
en: Good! Then perhaps he's made a decision.

speaker: Marco
en: About what, cousin?

speaker: Silvio
en: About which of us shall step into the robes of the Doge, "cousin."

speaker: Marco
en: I didn't know there was a decision to be made. Surely the choice is obvious to all.

speaker: Silvio
en: Obvious, indeed. It should be the one who organized the entire operation; the one who came up with the idea of how to save this city.

speaker: Marco
en: There is no lack of value in tactical intelligence, good Silvio. But it is wisdom one needs to rule. Do not think otherwise.

speaker: Carlo
en: Calma, calma amici (Calm, calm friends), please. There is no need for this. You know, it's not up to either of you. For all we know, he might not even choose a Barbarigo.

speaker: Carlo
en: And why not me? I'm the one who's done all the hard work!

speaker: Marco
en: Basta (Enough)! We wait for his arrival.

speaker: Carlo
en: Are you sure he's coming?

speaker: Marco
en: Yes.

speaker: Dante
en: Signori (Gentlemen), we should move a little faster. I feel eyes on us.

speaker: Marco
en: Thank you, Dante. We will move at your pace.

speaker: Silvio
en: This guard's a good find, cousin. How much did you pay for him?

speaker: Marco
en: Perhaps not as much as he deserves. He's saved my life on two occasions, though he's not much of a conversationalist.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Enough with your inane prattle! The choice of Doge was never up to any of you, and you were never given permission to make plans.

speaker: Marco
en: Forgive us, Maestro. We wish only to serve.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: The plan is this. Doge Mocenigo will die tonight. And once the deed's been done, Marco shall take his place.

speaker: Marco
en: Vi ringrazio umilmente, Maestro. (I humbly thank you, Master).

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Good. Messer Grimaldi, you are closest to Mocenigo, your work, the most vital. Serve us well, and it won't be forgotten. Walk with me.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: I don't want any blood spilled, you understand? It must appear to all that he goes quietly.

speaker: Carlo
en: Certo, Maestro.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: When are you closest to him?

speaker: Carlo
en: I have full run of the palace. He may not care to hear what I have to say, but he trusts me by now as one of his own.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Bravo. Then I want you to infiltrate the kitchen and poison his meal.

speaker: Carlo
en: So be it.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Marco, can you furnish us with a suitable toxin on short notice?

speaker: Marco
en: I defer to my cousin. That is really his area of expertise.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Ah, Silvio...

speaker: Silvio
en: I am at your service, Maestro.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: What can you bring to get this done?

speaker: Silvio
en: I will confer with my associates in the streets, but chances are good that I can procure some Cantarella.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Yes, and what is that?

speaker: Silvio
en: It is a most effective form of arsenic and difficult to trace.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Ah, va bene, va bene (Good, good). Then it's decided.

speaker: Marco
en: Forgive me, Maestro, but is this not a tad dangerous for you, involving yourself so intimately with the minutiae of our plans?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: I feel the need to involve myself more directly. The Pazzi disappointed us in Firenze. I pray you will not do the same.

speaker: Silvio
en: Do not worry this time. The Pazzi were a bunch of foolish

speaker: Rodrigo
en: The Pazzi were a potent and venerable family, reduced to rubble by one young Assassin. Do not underestimate this troublesome foe who now haunts your city, or the same fate will befall the Barbarigo. I want this done promptly. Bene (Good), I must return to Roma (Rome). Time is of the essence. Do not fail us.

speaker: Ezio
en: Che idiota sono (What an idiot I am)! I should have kept my eyes on them! I need to go and see Antonio if I've any hope of salvaging this mess I've made.

speaker: Blade in the Crowd
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus 2.0.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Ezio! Thank God you're all right! This madness with the Medici and the Pazzi, is this why you pursued Francesco?

speaker: Ezio
en: Not exactly...

speaker: Leonardo
en: Well, whatever your reasons, the city's safe again thanks to you! Now tell me: how may I be of service?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Ah! Another page! Aha! It's a similar cipher to the last one. This won't take long. Interesting... oh... indeed... I see... It's another blade design—for delivering poison!

speaker: Ezio
en: Can you build it?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Sì. (Yes.) It won't take very long. I just need to find a way to hollow out the blade without sacrificing the–

speaker: Ezio
