en: It's alright, Leonardo. Just do what you need to do.

speaker: Leonardo
en: All done! I've filled your blade with a bit of poison to start with. Should you run out, just visit a doctor.

speaker: Ezio
en: Poison? From a doctor?

speaker: Leonardo
en: In high enough doses, that which cures, can kill.

speaker: Ezio
en: I am in your debt once more, my friend.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Anytime, Ezio! Anytime!

speaker: Thief
en: Ezio, La Volpe tells me you are a skilled horseman. I have discovered that the leaders of the Cento Occhi (Hundred Eyes) train on horseback at the Circo Massimo. This grants us an opportunity to cut down several of them in once place.

speaker: Ezio
en: Speed will not save you. This is not over yet!

speaker: Leaders
en: Faster! Stay back! Attack him! Do not let him leave alive!

speaker: Caterina
en: Aprite la porta! Aprite la porta! Presto! (Open the door! Open the door! Hurry!)

speaker: Machiavelli
en: It's an ambush!

speaker: Caterina
en: Ezio! Niccolò! In here! Now!!! Get your chiappe (asses) in here! Into the Cittadella!

speaker: Ezio
en: Any damage?

speaker: Yusuf
en: Not that I can see. Byzantine Templars may be bad hosts, but are decent tenants. Once they capture a location, they like to keep it intact.

speaker: Ezio
en: Because they intend to stay.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Kesinlikle. (Exactly.) Well, as promised. If you want to craft your own bombs, I can show you.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Ah ah ah! Don't touch that! One wrong move and BANG! The building comes down.

speaker: Ezio
en: Are you serious?

speaker: Yusuf
en: The look on your face. Here, I'll show you. We craft our bombs from a combination of three parts: the shell, the gunpowder, and the primary ingredient. Sometimes we add a few extras too, for fun. But we'll come to that later. For now, focus on these elements.

speaker: Yusuf
en: You'll find many ingredients for bomb recipes scattered throughout the city. So keep your eyes open and your nose to the ground as you move about.

speaker: Ezio
en: That should keep me busy. Grazie (Thank you), Yusuf.

speaker: Ezio
en: Have you ever seen this book?

speaker: Yusuf
en: No. It's a journal?

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì. (Yes.)

speaker: Yusuf
en: "The Secret Crusade". By Niccolò Polo. Marco's father?

speaker: Ezio
en: I found this on a Templar in Masyaf. It mentions the five keys to Altaïr's library. Niccolò brought them here and hid them.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Ah. And the Templars know this, so it's a race against time.

speaker: Ezio
en: They found one already. Beneath Topkapı. I want to recover it, and find the other four.

speaker: Yusuf
en: So where will you begin?

speaker: Ezio
en: The old Polo trading post, I think. They ran a business in this area, no?

speaker: Yusuf
en: I believe so. Speak with a man named Piri Reis in the Bazaar. He can point you in the right direction. And teach you a few more bomb recipes, if you are so inclined.

speaker: Ezio
en: Piri Reis? I think I have seen some of your earliest work.

speaker: Piri Reis
en: Reis? Did Yusuf Tazim send you? That sounds like one of his exaggerations.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì (Yes). He said you could show me the location of Niccolò Polo's former trading post.

speaker: Piri Reis
en: Ah. You must be that Floransali (Florentine) he's been yammering on about. Lothario?

speaker: Ezio
en: Ezio.

speaker: Piri Reis
en: I don't hear the difference. Yes, the old Polo shop, it's just west of the Ayasofya. Here.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie. (Thank you). Yusuf also mentioned that you were the man to talk to about specialty bombs.

speaker: Piri Reis
en: Ach, that man. He is a talker. Evet (Yes), I am a navigator in the Sultan's navy, currently on leave to study cartography. But through my soldiering, I have also gained an appreciation for artillery and explosives. And it has served the Assassins well. It gives us a... an edge. I carry many kinds of bombs. For Assassins only, of course. Lethal, tactical, diversionary, and a few... peculiar casings. Everything you see here is for sale... if you can prove you know how to use it first.

speaker: Ezio
en: I am eager to learn.

speaker: Piri Reis
en: Well, no one is stopping you. Just let me know.

speaker: Ezio
en: Buongiorno (Good day). Is this the home of Francesco Colonna?

speaker: Woman
en: It was, but now the banks own everything. We have lost it all.

speaker: Ezio
en: Even the Da Vinci paintings?

speaker: Woman
en: A lesser part of Signore's (Sir's) collection.

speaker: Ezio
en: I have an interest in them nonetheless.

speaker: Woman
en: The three paintings were put up for auction and purchased by a merchant of Firenze. He prepares to set sail from the harbor immediately.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie mille. (Thank you very much.)

speaker: Duccio
en: Ezio Auditore.

speaker: Duccio
en: Come back down to the harbor when I return to Roma. I will show you the inside of my ship.

speaker: Duccio
en: Living in this third rate city, instead of beautiful Firenze? How low you have sunk.

speaker: Ezio
en: Duccio. We are not children anymore.

speaker: Duccio
en: Look around. I have help this time. And you are all alone.

speaker: Ezio
en: I am warning you...

speaker: Duccio
en: We are only talking, are we not? I see this place has worked its magic on your sister. She did not want to open her legs in Firenze, but now she is the Madame of Roma.

speaker: Duccio
en: Cazzo! (Fuck!) Why are you just standing there? Hit him!

speaker: Duccio
en: You can hit me, but that does not mean that Firenze will take you back! Dirty Roman! Your father pretended to be one of us, but we all knew you were outsiders. Get him!

speaker: Ezio
en: You are going to shut your mouth, and give me what I want. The three Da Vinci paintings.

speaker: Duccio
en: One is on the boat. The other two were sold to a cardinal, he is displaying them for high ranking members of the Church.

speaker: Ezio
en: How do I get in?

speaker: Duccio
en: How should I know? Go ask your whore of a sister, I am sure she has slept with a couple of cardinals.

speaker: Disciple 1
en: Where is Marco? He was to come here after examining another Da Vinci painting near Il Vaticano.

speaker: Disciple 2
en: Imagine. Once we open the temple, the true Renaissance will be upon us and the teachings of Hermes will be known to all men.

speaker: Disciple 1
en: Patience, brothers. Soon we will reveal the secrets of this painting.

speaker: Ezio
en: Insieme per la vittoria! (We stand together!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Silenzio (Silence), my friends. Silenzio! (Silence!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie. (Thank you.) Do you know what brings us here tonight? HONOR! Vieri de' Pazzi slanders my family's name and forces his own miseries upon us. If w

speaker: Vieri
en: Enough of your nonsense, grullo! (idiot!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Buona sera (Good evening), Vieri! We were just talking about you. I'm surprised to see you here. I thought the Pazzi hired others to do their dirty work.

speaker: Vieri
en: It's your family that cries for guards when there's trouble, codardo! (coward!) Afraid to handle things yourself?

speaker: Ezio
en: Your sister seemed quite satisfied with the 'handling' I gave her earlier.

speaker: Vieri
en: Uccidetelo! (Kill him!)

speaker: Federico
en: Ehi! (Hey!) Behind you!

speaker: Ezio
en: Federico? What are you doing here?!

speaker: Federico
en: I wanted to see if baby brother had finally learned how to fight.

speaker: Ezio
en: And?

speaker: Federico
en: You have style, but endurance is what counts. Let's see how many of them you can ruin before they get the best of you.

speaker: Vieri
en: Fall back! Fall back!

speaker: Federico
en: Hold on...

speaker: Ezio
en: What? We've almost won this!

speaker: Federico
en: Your lip...

speaker: Ezio
en: Just a scratch.

speaker: Federico
en: Let the doctor decide.

speaker: Ezio
en: It's not necessary. Besides, I've no money for this doctor of yours.

speaker: Federico
en: Wasted it on women and wine, huh?

speaker: Ezio
en: I'd hardly call it wasted. Lend me some florins then...Or have you done the same?

speaker: Federico
en: Search them. There's bound to be something in their pockets.

speaker: Federico
en: Va bene. (Alright.) That should be enough. Let's get out of here before the guards arrive...

speaker: Brawler
en: You there! You have the bearing of a man who thinks rather highly of himself. But I find you a rather pathetic specimen. What do you have to say about THAT, alchak (lowlife)?

speaker: Ezio
en: If I had a message for you, amico (friend), I would give it to your mother.

speaker: Brawler
en: How dare you! We settle this NOW!

speaker: Ezio
en: Stay down, and do not pester anyone again.

speaker: Brawler
en: Ah ha! Surprise attack!

speaker: Ezio
en: Are you serious?

speaker: Brawler
en: You fell for my ruse, old man!

speaker: Ezio
en: Do not embarrass yourself further.

speaker: Brawler
en: I am the cudgel of Konstaniniyye!

speaker: Ezio
en: Have you not had enough?

speaker: Brawler
en: Never!

speaker: Brawler
en: Ah... we will call it a draw, alright? You are quite a fighter.

speaker: Ezio
en: As are you, if a little reckless. How would you like to put those fists to better use with the Assassins?

speaker: Brawler
en: You mean... fight for a cause, and not only for amusement?

speaker: Ezio
en: I am sure you would still find some joy in it.

speaker: Brawler
en: Evet (Yes), I believe you, efendim (sir). Alright.

speaker: Ezio
en: Ben trovato (Good to see you), Ugo. What's the trouble?

speaker: Ugo
en: You and Rosa managed to escape from Seta, but the others were not so lucky. Emilio's captured them and now they await execution.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do you know where they're being held?

speaker: Ugo
en: I know they're still in the district, but beyond that, no. You'll have to look for them.

speaker: Ezio
en: I'll have your brothers back in no time.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Hah! Listen to them squeal.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Pathetic. It's no wonder their master hides.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Where is Emilio? I'd like to be rid of this trash.

speaker: Thieves
en: The markets belong to the people! Emilio says he seeks unity, but all he really wants is control! Your crimes cannot continue! The people won't allow it!

speaker: Guard 3
en: Where's your master now?

speaker: Guard 4
en: Perhaps we'll mount your heads on pikes.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Better to hang their corpses from the palazzo windows.

speaker: Ugo
en: I'm impressed. I didn't expect you to succeed so quickly.

speaker: Ezio
en: I aim to please.

speaker: Ugo
en: I'll let Antonio know of our progress. Come find me later. I've got another job for you.

speaker: Ezio
en: What sort of job?

speaker: Ugo
en: Meet me near the docks and I'll explain.

speaker: Ezio
en: Molto bene. (Very well.)

scene: Bring the Atlas to the Harbor
speaker: Christoffa
en: Ah, there he is! Do you have the Atlas! Show it!

scene: Bring the Atlas to the Harbor
speaker: Ezio
en: Take it and go. Borgia's soldiers are combing the streets.

scene: Bring the Atlas to the Harbor
speaker: Luis
en: A few maps are missing... but the Piri Reis map remains. We are satisfied.

scene: Bring the Atlas to the Harbor
speaker: Ezio
en: Gentlemen, if you return to Italia in the future, bring your own protection.

scene: Bring the Atlas to the Harbor
speaker: Luis
en: We would have done so, but there are no more men in España of your skill. Not since a group of Assassins were imprisoned by Tomás Torquemada's inquisitors.

scene: Bring the Atlas to the Harbor
speaker: Ezio
en: Wait! What do you know of the Assassins?

scene: Bring the Atlas to the Harbor
speaker: Luis
en: I am a well connected man, Ezio, with a great number of friends. Sadly the Inquisition has made a recent habit of arresting them.

scene: Bring the Atlas to the Harbor
speaker: Christoffa
en: Luis, our ship is waiting!

scene: Bring the Atlas to the Harbor
speaker: Luis
en: Be well, Ezio, May you find everything you seek.

scene: Bring the Atlas to the Harbor
speaker: Ezio
en: Distressing news, Antonio. My search for the Apple of Eden will have to be postponed. I'm going to Barcelona.

scene: Bring the Atlas to the Harbor
speaker: Antonio
en: I've heard rumors of some turmoil there. What's wrong?

scene: Bring the Atlas to the Harbor
speaker: Ezio
en: Santángel claims that a number of Assassins have been jailed. I feel it is my duty to help them.

scene: Bring the Atlas to the Harbor
speaker: Antonio
en: A noble cause, I will put you in contact with my people there. They should be of some help.

speaker: Brutes and Brutality
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Antonio
en: Avanti, Ezio (Come in, Ezio). Prego (Welcome). Can I offer you something? ? Un caffè (A coffee)?

speaker: Ezio
en: What's caffè (coffee)?

speaker: Antonio
en: An interesting concoction, brought to me by a Turk merchant. Here, have a taste.

speaker: Ezio
en: A little bitter if you ask me. It just seems lacking somehow....I don't know. Have you considered adding sugar, maybe? Or latte? (milk)?

speaker: Antonio
en: I suppose it is something of an acquired taste. Enough about that. Now where were we? Our failure at the palazzo cost us dearly. It will take time to recover. No doubt Emilio will use this pause to strengthen his defenses and continue his oppression of the district. You may not share our motive, but I know you share our goal.

speaker: Ezio
en: Why not gather your forces and try again?

speaker: Antonio
en: To act in haste would only bring more losses. No. We must resupply and draw new plans.

speaker: Ezio
en: I can ill afford to sit around and wait.

speaker: Antonio
en: Nor would I want you to. Work with us instead. Already my men begin to mend today's wounds. Seek them out; they'll put you to work. The sooner you aid them, the sooner we can strike.

speaker: Ezio
en: Molto bene, Messere. (Very well, sir). I accept.

speaker: Antonio
en: It is the right decision.

speaker: Caterina
en: Salute Lucrezia! How I've missed you.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Vai a farti fottere, troia. (Go fuck yourself, whore.)

speaker: Caterina
en: Always a pleasure. Bring her here. I'll take the key.

speaker: Caterina
en: Oh, classy.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: GUARDS! GUARDS!

speaker: Caterina
en: That's enough out of you!

speaker: Ezio
en: Can you walk?

speaker: Caterina
en: No.

speaker: Ezio
en: I guess we are going out the front.

speaker: Ezio
en: Wait here.

speaker: Caterina
en: As if I have a choice. What are you doing, Ezio? Come, Ezio, this way. Ezio, this way, per favore.

speaker: Caterina
en: Why save me, Ezio? With Forlì taken, I am useless to you.

speaker: Ezio
en: You have a family.

speaker: Caterina
en: It is not your family. That night at the Villa. I had to ensure our allegiance to protect Forlì. Do you understand, Ezio?

speaker: Ezio
en: È la politica. (Politics.) Of course. I knew it. You need not explain. Caterina. Did they...? Did Cesare...?

speaker: Caterina
en: No. My name must still have some small value. I was left... unspoiled.

speaker: Caterina
en: Don't you dare.

speaker: Caterina
en: Figlio di puttana (Son of a whore). Never do that to me again.

speaker: Caterina
en: It seems to open from over there.

speaker: Rosa
en: Climbing a bit of scaffolding is all well and good, but let's see how you do out in the open.

speaker: Ezio
en: Top of that tower, then? Torno fra un attimo (I'll be right back).

speaker: Ezio
en: So?

speaker: Rosa
en: Looks like you've learned all I have to teach. I'll let Antonio know about your progress. Finish your other tasks. We're almost there.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Please... help...

speaker: Ezio
en: You must be one of Bartolomeo's men. What's happened here? Where is he?

speaker: Mercenary
en: Silvio's thugs... attacked. Took him deeper into the district... north of here...

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in pace (Rest in peace).

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Luridi cordardi (Fucking cowards)! I'll take you all on! At the same time! With one arm – no – BOTH arms tied behind my back! You must be wondering how this is EVEN POSSIBLE! Only release me and I'LL GLADLY DEMONSTRATE, miserabili pezzi di merda (you spineless pieces of shit)! You have no honor! No valor! No VIRTUE! And people wonder why it is Venezia's star has begun to fade! I'll show mercy to whoever here has the COURAGE to release me! All the rest of you are GOING TO DIE! By MY HAND! I swear it! What sort of man sells his honor and dignity for a bit of coin? You realize you are in service to a TRAITOR and a COWARD! Oh ho! Do you think I don't know WHY you've chained me up?! Do you think I don't know WHO pulls Silvio's puppet strings?! I've been fighting his weasel of a master since before most of you were even GLIMMERS in your fathers' eyes! Let me out! Let me out!!! Giuro che quando usciró da questa gabbia il mio unico pensiero sará spiccarvi dal tronco quelle teste di cazzo e ficcarvele su per il CULO! (I swear, once I'm free of this cage I'm going to make it my mission to sever EACH AND EVERY ONE of your FUCKING heads and SHOVE them up your FUCKING asses!) And I've no intention of matching ass to head either! Oh and what a grand display it will be! The likes of which shall be sung of for YEARS to come.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: About goddamn time! I don't know if I should kiss you or slap you. Maybe both, just to be safe.

speaker: Ezio
en: That's quite alright.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Who are you?

speaker: Ezio
en: I am Ezio Auditore da Firenze. I'm here to rescue you.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Ha! Let's see who winds up rescuing who.

speaker: Ezio
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Guard
en: Down there! Stop them!

speaker: Ezio
en: We should go.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Agreed! There are still more heads to be smashed!

speaker: Ezio
en: Perhaps we should try and avoid conflict?

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Why?! Are you afraid?

speaker: Ezio
en: No, just practical, given that they outnumber us 100 to 1.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: As you wish, bella mia (my lady)! Watch for the large one. Dante, he's called. Most of Silvio's men are useless, but that one is trouble.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Where to, Madonna? Don't overextend yourself, now! Hmm... What... Oh, sorry. I'd fallen asleep! Find me a face to put my fist in! Must. Break. Bones. About time! Are we there yet? Ah, sweet freedom, how I have missed you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Silvio's set his men to ransacking your place. Prepare yourself for a fight.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: No need! Bartolomeo is ALWAYS prepared for a fight!

speaker: Guard Captain
en: If you value your life, you'll stand down.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Never! What good is a man's life if it's not lived free, eh? I'll not go back into a cage!

speaker: Guard Captain
en: Then you'll go into the ground! Kill them!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: What a mess they've made... Bianca! I hope she's unharmed!

speaker: La Volpe
en: Where is Pietro?

speaker: Spy
en: I cannot tell you. But Micheletto waits at the city gates east of the Terme di Traiano (Baths of Trajan). He intends to disguise his men to make the killing look like an accident.

speaker: Ezio
en: He will lead me to Lucrezia's lover.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Ezio, Machiavelli has betrayed us. We would both wish to deny it, but the truth is now clear. Do what needs to be done. If you don't, I will.

speaker: Ezio
en: Without Volpe's thieves, I may require the help of my recruits.

speaker: Francesco
en: Please, I have done nothing.

speaker: Cesare
en: Francesco Troche, dear friend. Would I lie to you? You told your brother about my war plan in Romagna, who contacted the ambassador of Venezia.

speaker: Francesco
en: It was an accident. I am still your servant and ally.

speaker: Cesare
en: Are you demanding that I discount your actions and rely on friendship?

speaker: Francesco
en: I am asking... not demanding.

speaker: Cesare
en: To unite Italia, I must have every institution under my control. And if the Church does not fall in the line, I will eliminate it entirely.

speaker: Francesco
en: You know that I really work for you, not the Pope.

speaker: Cesare
en: Ah. But do I, Troche? There's only one way I can know that unconditionally now.

speaker: Francesco
en: You intend to kill me? Your most loyal friend?

speaker: Cesare
en: Of course not.

speaker: Francesco
en: Are you letting me go? Thank you, Cesare. You will not regret–

speaker: Cesare
en: Guards! Give Micheletto the costumes for the play. Lucrezia is mine. No one else shall have her.

speaker: Cesare
en: Make doubly sure it is done correctly.

speaker: Micheletto
en: I obey, Cesare.

speaker: Cesare
en: Oh yes. Dump Francesco's body in the Tevere (Tiber).

speaker: Micheletto
en: Once you get dressed, you follow me to the play. Capito? (Understand?) Tieni. (Here.) This is for you. Il tuo costume (Your costume.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Il Colosseo (The Colosseum).

speaker: Micheletto
en: I seek Pietro.

speaker: Guard
en: He acts on stage, Signore (Sir). One of my men will take you to him.

speaker: Micheletto
en: Don't forget, I wear the black shirt. Protect me and wait for Pilate's call to the Centurion to strike.

speaker: Cardinal Sin
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Mario
en: So, tell me everything!

speaker: Ezio
en: They executed father for treason. Federico and Petruccio too. Then they came for me.

speaker: Mario
en: Do you know why?

speaker: Ezio
en: I have no answers, uncle... Only a list of names taken from a man who wished me dead. I still can't believe they are gone...

speaker: Mario
en: Don't worry. We will make sense of this.

speaker: Ezio
en: I wish I shared your optimism.

speaker: Mario
en: Come on, keep pace! We're almost there. I think you will find much to like in Monteriggioni.

speaker: Ezio
en: I thought Monteriggioni was an enemy of Firenze...

speaker: Mario
en: For now. Next year it will be its friend. The year after, its enemy again. And on and on. I cannot keep track. So I have stopped trying. These are honest, hardworking people. Our shops may only carry simple goods, but they're well made and dependable. There is a chapel here too. The prete (priest) seems a nice enough fellow, but I've never been much of a believer. Did you know the Villa Auditore is almost 200 years old? It was built by my great-grandfather, a strange man, who carried all kinds of secrets. Keep your eyes open, and you might discover a few of them yourself... With all the fighting that's been going on, this place has started to get a bit rough around the edges. I wish I could do something about it, but I just don't have the time or money to fix things up. Guess that's life, eh? Here we are, Casa dolce casa! (Home sweet home.) So? What do you think?

speaker: Ezio
en: It's most impressive, uncle.

speaker: Mario
en: She's seen better days, I suppose. Believe me, I'd have her shining again... if only I had the time. Now that you have had the tour, nipote (nephew), you should go and outfit yourself. My men in the market are expecting you. Return here when you are finished and we'll begin.

speaker: Ezio
en: Begin? Begin what?

speaker: Mario
en: I thought you'd come here to train?

speaker: Ezio
en: No, uncle. I came here to escape Firenze – and intend to take my family further still.

speaker: Mario
en: But what about your father? He'd want you to finish his work.

speaker: Ezio
en: What work? My father was a banker.

speaker: Mario
en: Wait... He did not tell you?

speaker: Ezio
en: I have no idea what you're talking about...

speaker: Mario
en: Ma che mi combini, Giovanni?! (What were you thinking, Giovanni?!) Where to even begin... Go and fetch the gear in the market. It will give me time to think.

speaker: Ezio
en: But–

speaker: Mario
en: But that's that. We'll talk more later. Some spending money, should you need it. And if you find yourself in need of rest, I've prepared a room for you on the top floor of the Villa.

speaker: Ezio
en: Don't worry, we're only staying here for a little while.

speaker: Claudia
en: I don't like it here. I want to go home.

speaker: Ezio
en: I know.

speaker: Contact
en: Get this to its destination fast. Really fast. I'll pay you well.

speaker: Recipient 1
en: Oh grazie! (Thank you!)

speaker: Recipient 2
en: Oh, grazie. (Thank you.)

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Salve cittadini di Roma! (Hail citizens of Rome!) Behold a sight most splendid! Caterina Sforza, she-whore of Forlì—has at last been brought to heel!

speaker: Caterina
en: Ha! No one kneels as low as Lucrezia Borgia! Who put you up to this? Was it your brother or your father? Perhaps a bit of both? Perhaps at the same time!

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Chiudi la bocca! (Shut your mouth!) None speak ill of the Borgia!

speaker: Lucrezia
en: The same will happen to any who defy us!

speaker: Caterina
en: Good people of Roma, stay strong! You will be free, your time will come, I swear it!

speaker: Ezio
en: They are going to torture her.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: You are here for Cesare and Rodrigo.

speaker: Ezio
en: Caterina is a powerful ally, if we help her now while she is weak, she will aid us in return.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Perhaps. But kill Cesare and Rodrigo first.

speaker: Cesare
en: Forget the Pope, you answer only to me. Roma is the pillar that holds our entire enterprise aloft. She cannot waver. Which means neither can you.

speaker: Octavian
en: What of il Vaticano (The Vatican)?

speaker: Cesare
en: That tired old men's club? Play along for now, but soon we will have no need of them.

speaker: Juan
en: He's left us Roma.

speaker: Micheletto
en: She'll be in good hands.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Cesare.

speaker: Cesare
en: Lucrezia.

speaker: Cesare
en: I hope you have treated our guest with kindness.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: That mouth on her... How I'd love to sew it shut.

speaker: Cesare
en: I rather like it open, myself.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Oh?

speaker: Cesare
en: Have you talked to the Pope about the funds requested by my banker?

speaker: Lucrezia
en: He is away from the Castello, and he might need some convincing when he returns.

speaker: Cesare
en: That shouldn't be a problem, should it?

speaker: Lucrezia
en: No. Only... it gets quite lonely here. You and I spend so little time together these days, busy as you are with your OTHER conquests.

speaker: Cesare
en: Soon, once I have secured the throne of Italia, you are going to be my queen, and your loneliness will be a thing of the past.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: I cannot wait.

speaker: Cesare
en: Behave yourself while I am gone.

speaker: Guard
en: Open the gate! The Captain General is leaving for Urbino! Buona fortuna, (Good fortune) Padron Cesare!

speaker: Ezio
en: Machiavelli is going to be very disappointed.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Open her cell!

speaker: Lucrezia
en: How was the journey to Roma? Did you sit in Cesare's private carriage?

speaker: Caterina
en: You're pathetic, Lucrezia.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: What did he talk about? His plans for Napoli? Did you like it?

speaker: Caterina
en: I can't remember.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Perhaps you will remember this.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: That put you in your place.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Lock it and give me the key.

speaker: Caterina
en: Oh. My back. Please, can you reach this water jug for me? I cannot get it myself.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Anything else I can reach, Princess?

speaker: Guard 2
en: Why not move closer to us, Principessa (Princess)? We will help you.

speaker: Caterina
en: No. You must come closer. You boys are being so good to me.

speaker: Caterina
en: Thanks.

speaker: Caveat Emptor
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Cesare Borgia
en: Well, well. My tormentor has finally shown himself.

speaker: Ezio
en: You are one to speak of torment.

speaker: Cesare Borgia
en: And you are one to preach! We are the same, you and I. Two men carrying out the dying wishes of their fathers.

speaker: Ezio
en: Only one of ours fathers died by the hand of their son.

speaker: Cesare Borgia
en: A slanderous lie.

speaker: Ezio
en: I was there. I saw it with my own eyes.

speaker: Cesare Borgia
en: So you admit to both hallucinations and trespassing!

speaker: Ezio
en: Nothing of the sort.

speaker: Cesare Borgia
en: You continue to delude yourself. I suppose it's no greater delusion than believing you could best me in combat.

speaker: Ezio
en: Only one of us shall live through this day, Cesare, and it will not be you.

speaker: Cesare Borgia
en: Ha! If you insist upon death, I will not deny you. I will await your challenge.

speaker: Cesare Borgia
en: You fool, Ezio! You should have known better!

speaker: Ezio
en: You will die by my hand, Cesare. Not today, it seems, but soon.

speaker: Cesare Borgia
en: I am the greatest fighter to have ever lived! No one can murder me!

speaker: Ezio
en: That arrogance will be your undoing.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Mentor, do you have a moment? I have a request.

speaker: Ezio
en: I am eager to hear it.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Today a local printer received a death threat I feel we must take seriously. I believe the Templars are trying to silence him. I would like to draw his enemies out into the open by pretending to escort him to a new location.

speaker: Ezio
en: And what do you need from me?

speaker: Apprentice
en: I want you to stalk the stalkers. We will walk in the open, while you remain undetected.

speaker: Ezio
en: Molto bene. (Very good.)

speaker: Apprentice
en: Stay close, and kill any Templars you find. They could be anywhere.

speaker: Champion
en: Stand down, Assassin. There is a contract on this man's head!

speaker: Printer
en: I will not be silenced! I will not! Do not kill me, efendim (sir)! Please! God help me!

speaker: Ezio
en: I am trying to save you!

speaker: Ezio
en: Stay here and stay hidden. My Assassin needs help.

speaker: Ezio
en: What happened? Who was that fighter?

speaker: Apprentice
en: Quite an animal, no? I have never seen the Templars attack with such brute strength. Today I bested him, but not by much.

speaker: Ezio
en: Be on your guard. He will be back.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Ezio, do you remember the printer we sent into hiding?

speaker: Ezio
en: I do. And I remember the Templar brute who nearly killed him.

speaker: Apprentice
en: That same brute has now set his sights on the printer's father, a local herald.

speaker: Ezio
en: A cruel way to draw his real target out into the open, no? We should warn the father... and get rid of this Templar.

speaker: Ezio
en: Mi scusi, signore (Excuse me, sir). Your son has stirred up some trouble... enough that the men looking for him, may come for you now.

speaker: Herald
en: My son? But he is a humble printer. And I, a simple herald. Why would anybody want to hurt us?

speaker: Ezio
en: Words can wound like any blade, amico (friend).

speaker: Apprentice
en: Ezio! I think we are being watched. Can you see anything?

speaker: Ezio
en: Templars! Do you see them?

speaker: Apprentice
en: Evet (Yes), Mentor!

speaker: Herald
en: Ah!

speaker: Georgios
en: If you draw your weapon, this man dies! Now, bring me the printer! Bring me this man's son! What is this man's life worth, Assassin?

speaker: Ezio
en: More than you can afford.

speaker: Georgios
en: Are you proud of your kill, Assassin? Do you expect praise for murdering a better and braver man? You have taken my life, but you cannot erase my legend, my power, my influence. Men feared me, even as they did my bidding... that is the mark of a true leader.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Leave this life in peace.

speaker: Mario
en: And here he is! Our campione (champion), Ezio!

speaker: Mercenaries
en: All Hail, Ezio!

speaker: Ezio
en: I see you wasted no time starting the celebrations.

speaker: Mario
en: And why not?! You've done us a great service, nipote (nephew)! With Vieri dead, la Toscana (Tuscany) will grow quiet once more. Do you know what that means?

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Basta lavorare! (No more work!)

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Si passa tutto il giorno a bere! (We can drink all day!)

speaker: Mercenary 3
en: E a puttane! (And with whores!)

speaker: Mercenary 3
en: What?! It's true!

speaker: Mario
en: Come, Ezio. Walk with me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes, uncle?

speaker: Ezio
en: The Pazzi answer to another; a Spaniard.

speaker: Mario
en: He is Rodrigo Borgia, one of the most powerful men in all of Europe and leader of the Templar Order.

speaker: Ezio
en: Which makes him responsible for the murder of my father and brothers.

speaker: Mario
en: Yes. And he will kill you too, given the chance.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then I must stand against him if I wish to be free... But not until every other Templar has fallen to my blade. Father's list will guide me.

speaker: Mario
en: Where will you go next?

speaker: Ezio
en: Firenze. Francesco de' Pazzi will share the fate of his son.

speaker: Mario
en: A sensible next step. No doubt he intends evil for the city. Alright. That's enough grim talk for one night, I'll be in my study if you need me.

speaker: Ezio
en: I should read the letter my uncle gave me...

speaker: Mario
en: Look familiar?

speaker: Ezio
en: Other Codex pages.

speaker: Mario
en: Yes. Your father managed to find and translate a few before he...

speaker: Ezio
en: Here.

speaker: Mario
en: This is not your father's work. Someone else has translated it.

speaker: Ezio
en: Leonardo da Vinci. A friend.

speaker: Mario
en: Do you see the way the words cross from one page to the next?

speaker: Ezio
en: There is something underneath it all. Some kind of map. Where is it supposed to lead?

speaker: Mario
en: Your father and I managed to make out bits of a prophecy scrawled across these pages. It was written by an Assassin like us, who long ago held a "Piece of Eden." His name was Altaïr... He spoke of something powerful and ancient hidden beneath the land.

speaker: Ezio
en: What is it?

speaker: Mario
en: What indeed. Solving that little mystery is exactly why we collected these pages.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then let me help. It's time I take on my father's work. All of it. I'll start with the page I took from Vieri. Leonardo will decode it for us.

speaker: Mario
en: Bene (Good). Return here when time permits and we'll add it to the wall.

speaker: Francesco
en: Mentor, I must kill a man.

speaker: Ezio
en: Who?

speaker: Francesco
en: The Marquis, Charles de la Motte.

speaker: Ezio
en: I see.

speaker: Francesco
en: I ask your blessing, Mentor. And I apologize, for I will go after him even if you tell me not to.

speaker: Ezio
en: The Brotherhood is not about revenge, Francesco. But there are times when revenge can motivate a man to do important things.

speaker: Francesco
en: Then you approve?

speaker: Ezio
en: You are still in training, Francesco. I fear your anger will undermine your ability. You must have control of both in order to face a man such as the Marquis.

speaker: Francesco
en: But!

speaker: Ezio
en: But I agree that he must be dealt with. I will track him down personally. Can you direct me to where he is?

speaker: Francesco
en: Yes. Cesare has given de la Motte control of a guard tower in the Campagna District.

speaker: Ezio
en: Thank you. I shall return.

speaker: Charles
en: Is this the best you can muster, Assassin?

speaker: Ezio
en: You may escaped, Marquis, but your time will come soon enough.

speaker: Charles
en: I doubt it. I have seen nothing that shows you have even the slightest chance against me.

speaker: Ezio
en: You will.

speaker: Charles
en: Hmph! Save your gloating; this means nothing.

speaker: Ezio
en: I did not come here to gloat. I came here to put an end to you.

speaker: Charles
en: As you have done, so why linger? Be off with you.

speaker: Ezio
en: A word, first.

speaker: Charles
en: No. I'll not dally long enough to listen to the likes of you.

speaker: Ezio
en: So be it.

speaker: Helene
en: You're a long way from home, traveler.

speaker: Ezio
en: From the sound of your accent, I'd guess you were too.

speaker: Helene
en: Not exactly. I haven't called any place home for a very long time.

speaker: Ezio
en: What brings you here?

speaker: Helene
en: Rumor of war. Upheavals. Miseries from which I hope to extract a modest profit.

speaker: Ezio
en: Charming.

speaker: Guard
en: She went this way! Hurry!

speaker: Helene
en: If you'll excuse me... I have some business in the city. It was a pleasure meeting you, Assassin...

speaker: Ezio
en: Wait! Who are you?

speaker: Helene
en: Watch your back!

speaker: Ezio
en: She took my blade!

speaker: Helene
en: That shook them!

speaker: Ezio
en: I'll have my sword...

speaker: Helene
en: You're skilled stranger. As proficient as any Assassin, yet half as wise.

speaker: Ezio
en: Don't patronize me. If you have information about the Assassins then speak.

speaker: Helene
en: I'm not in España (Spain) to make friends, sir. Just a reputation, and a little money.

speaker: Host
en: Benvenuti, lottatori (Welcome, fighters)! The game is simple. There's only one rule: no weapons. Fight until you are the last man left standing. Will it be you? O tu (Or you)? Hmm? Who will win the Golden Mask?

speaker: Host
en: Let's bring out the next contender!

speaker: Host
en: Who else wishes to compete?!

speaker: Host
en: Do we have another challenger?

speaker: Silvio
en: Looks like this one thinks himself some kind of campione (champion). Go on, Dante. Show him how sadly mistaken he is.

speaker: Host
en: Is there nobody else to challenge our man in the ring? Do we have a winner?

speaker: Host
en: Ah! We have combatants!

speaker: Ezio
en: So that's how it's going to be, eh?

speaker: Host
en: Signore e Signori (Ladies and gentlemen)! The games of Carnevale have come to a glorious conclusion. Come see our winner claim his Golden Mask! Our winner has proven himself the fleetest of foot, the strongest of champions, the wisest strategist, and clearly a favorite of the ladies! With four games won lealmente (fair and square), the winner of the Golden Mask is

speaker: Host
en: The winner of the Golden Mask is... Dante Moro!

speaker: Silvio
en: Congratulations. We'll see you this evening.

speaker: Ezio
en: What are you doing out here?

speaker: Caterina
en: I'm so sorry, Ezio. I'm so sorry.

speaker: Ezio
en: What happened?

speaker: Caterina
en: It was a trick. To lower our defenses.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: As soon as you left, they attacked again. Checco Orsi—he has the Apple!

speaker: Ezio
en: WHAT!? No! Where is he!?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: We chased him out here. But the bastard's escaped to the mountains

speaker: Ezio
en: I'm going!

speaker: Checco
en: So... you have your prize again.

speaker: Ezio
en: Was it worth it? So much bloodshed?

speaker: Checco
en: A prize of such value, it will not remain yours for long.

speaker: Ezio
en: We shall see.

speaker: Ezio
en: Che miserie nascono dall'avidità. (What wretched things are borne of greed.) Requiescat in pace. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Wait.. Don't... Who are you? Stop... Don't open it...

speaker: Caterina
en: Ezio! Thank God, you're back with us. Are you all right? What happened to you?

speaker: Ezio
en: I... I don't know...

speaker: Caterina
en: One of my guards had the luck to find you in the hills, next to Checco Orsi's dead body.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì (Yes)... I remember... Wait... There was a third man... He took the Apple!

speaker: Caterina
en: Who?

speaker: Ezio
en: He wore a black robe. Like a monk... And I think... a missing finger? Sì! (Yes) Caterina, I have to go - right away!

speaker: Caterina
en: Of course. Then you will need this as well.

speaker: Ezio
en: The map Niccolò spoke of. Your husband's

speaker: Caterina
en: EX-husband, mio caro (my darling). He swore he'd uncovered the locations of all the Codex pages. You will recover the Apple, but you'll never find the Vault without this. You know, there is an Abbey here, where I've seen monks wearing black robes. I'd start there. Now, go. Find us a stramaledetto (fucking) monk.

speaker: Ezio
en: I think I'm going to miss you, Caterina.

speaker: Caterina
en: Oh, I know you will.

speaker: Thief
en: Ezio! They said you were coming but I did not believe it, the Cento Occhi have challenged us to a brawl. Little risk for them since they have greater numbers, but they will not be expecting to see you! Ready yourself!

speaker: Thief
en: We have an unspoken agreement with the poor in Roma. We do not steal from them and in turn they do not see us. But the Cento Occhi (Hundred Eyes) prey upon these people. Their banditi (bandits) patrol Roma's rooftops today. If they were to... disappear, no one would miss them.

speaker: Antonio
en: Ah, Ezio. I was hoping you might return. I want your advice on something.

speaker: Ezio
en: Of course. Tell me what troubles you.

speaker: Antonio
en: Emilio has turned some of my own men against me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bribery and blackmail, is it?

speaker: Antonio
en: Yes, and we cannot strike until the traitors are dealt with. They're still somewhere in this district; keeping tabs on us and reporting back to Emilio.

speaker: Ezio
en: Not for much longer, they're not.

speaker: Ezio
en: Something's wrong here. Where is everyone...?

speaker: Guard captain
en: Ah! Another challenger! Excellent! Savonarola warned me that some would oppose our rule, and so I devised this little trap – to ferret out those foolish enough to play at hero. It's proven to be both entertaining and effective. Incominciamo! (Let us begin!)

speaker: Guard captain
en: What a spectacle! I wonder how long you'll survive. Another – a few days back – he made it through over three dozen of my men – before he was finally put down. It's interesting. Every day, without fail, another of you approaches. Nonconformists. Malcontents. Revolutionaries. Ribelli. (Rebels.) I've seen – and heard – it all. Just excuses. Am I to believe you're a champion of the downtrodden, then? A hero come to free the city? A rebel leader intent on ushering in a new age? One who fights for justice? Liberty? Hmmmm? Which lie do you tell yourself!? And do not be mistaken. These are lies. No matter what any of you say – you're all here for the same reason. The same selfish reason: You seek something. Glory. Distinction. Fame. Rewards either physical, spiritual – or both! So which are you? Is it validation you desire? Or perhaps penance for some old ill? Did your father abuse you? Did other children tease you? Did a lover spurn you? If I had to guess, I would suspect a form of insecurity. Why else do you wear the hood? Why do you hide your face from the world? From yourself? I see these words are wasted, serving only to send you further into frenzy. As you wish. Fight on. You can't hold out forever...

speaker: Guard captain
en: You're making a very big mistake. You seek to challenge me? You've just signed your death warrant, boy! Approach at your peril, Assassino! I was born for battle boy. Come on then! Let's see what you're made of!

speaker: Guard captain
en: Is this truly who I was? So proud and cruel...

speaker: Ezio
en: No. Savonarola bewitched you.

speaker: Guard captain
en: Did he? Or was it that I tasted power and found myself intoxicated? I wish I had been stronger.

speaker: Ezio
en: As do I. Mi rincresce, ma non c'è altro modo (I am truly sorry, but there is no other way). Requiescat in pace (Rest in peace).

speaker: Ezio
en: You were right. The Master intends to kill you.

speaker: Copernicus
en: I will not let his bullying stop my research. Tonight there is an eclipse. I intend to chronicle it.

speaker: Ezio
en: But the Master hunts for you.

speaker: Copernicus
en: Better to die enlightened, than to live in ignorance.

speaker: Ezio
en: His end will come much sooner than yours.

speaker: Ezio
en: Silencing the truth will not stop its spread.

speaker: Master
en: People are lazy, they will believe what we tell them to believe. I have sent my best man to find Copernico. You are already too late.

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in pace. (Rest in Peace.)

speaker: Copernicus
en: Is the world not marvelous?

speaker: Ezio
en: Some of it.

speaker: Copernicus
en: You should not be so emotional. You will find it all makes more sense that way.

speaker: Ezio
en: Perhaps.

speaker: Copernicus
en: Cesare thinks himself the center of it all, but he circles the periphery with the rest of us. Did you know that the sun is most likely the midpoint of the universe, not the Earth? I see the movements of the moon and stars, and yet I can only observe. So much is unknown to me. This age of reason is but the beginning of an end I will never see. Someday we will be able to influence this world, to exploit the power of the human will to harness light and perhaps even travel into the heavens. But I am getting ahead of myself, first we must see the sun spinning at the center.

speaker: Ezio
en: I believe what you say is possible.

speaker: Copernicus
en: You should not accept my word. Not until I have proof. Soon. Buona Notte (Good night), Ezio, and thank you.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Ezio, my loyalty to your family has left me in a precarious situation. Rodrigo is trading favors with his foreign ambassadors. He wishes to gain information that will lead him to you. I go to meet with one of these ambassadors. He will demand my help and I will provide none. He may try to respond with violence, which is why you will be watching.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Ezio! Aiutatemi (Help me)!

speaker: Courtesan
en: Grazie (Thank you), Ezio. My faith in you is well placed.

speaker: Ugo
en: Rescuing my brothers was more than just an act of charity, Ezio. The men you freed will play a vital role in the weeks to come. Just ask for their help, and they'll join you.

speaker: Ezio
en: And once I have my little band of thieves?

speaker: Ugo
en: Send them towards a group of guards and they'll create a distraction....

speaker: Ezio
en: ...opening the way for me.

speaker: Ugo
en: Exactly.

speaker: Ezio
en: Saves me from having to bloody my sword. I like it.

speaker: Ugo
en: Exactly. Now I'll tell you what to do with them. Antonio's plan calls for a bit of deception. We're to imitate his archers, which means we'll need the armor that they wear. A shipment of the stuff has just been loaded into chests and now awaits delivery to Seta. Loot the chests and retrieve the outfits. When that's finished, I'll need you to fetch me a boat as well and bring it back here. We'll use it to move our men into the Palazzo undetected.

speaker: Ezio
en: Consider it done.

speaker: Ugo
en: Molto bene (Very good), Ezio. This is exactly what we needed. I'll let Antonio know you've finished the job.

speaker: Ezio
en: Machiavelli. We must talk.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Yes. I secured something of great worth from one of my contacts. We now have the names of several Templar agents Cesare has recruited to terrorize Roma.

speaker: Ezio
en: How do I find them?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: I can give you a general location. I suggest looking for signs of distress nearby. Perhaps you will uncover citizens who can point you in the right direction. My contact will continue searching for more names.

speaker: Ezio
en: This information came from a city guard?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Yes. How did you know?

speaker: Ezio
en: Lucky guess. Grazie (Thank you).

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Claudia, Bartolomeo and La Volpe are waiting for you inside. I can't imagine how you did it.

speaker: Ezio
en: , Machiavelli.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Virtú? (Virtue?)

speaker: Ezio
en: What have you discovered?

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: That bastardo (bastard) Cesare is in the Castel Sant'Angelo with the Pope.

speaker: La Volpe
en: My spies tell me that the Apple has been secreted to someone for study. I am working on determining his identity.

speaker: Claudia
en: Caterina will be moved to the prison within the Castello next week.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Bene. (Good). So the Castello it is. Roma will heal quickly with Cesare and Rodrigo gone.

speaker: Ezio
en: Only if the opportunity to assassinate them arises will I take it.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Do not repeat your mistake in the Vault. You must kill them now.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: I'm with Machiavelli, Ezio. We should not wait.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Bartolomeo is right.

speaker: Claudia
en: They must pay for Mario's death.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do not worry. They will die. You have my word.

speaker: Architect
en: Ser Ezio, I represent the combined resources of Bartolomeo d'Alviano, Claudia Auditore and La Volpe. Through my associates spread across the city you can channel your florins to any part of the underground you desire. You may have seen notices posted around Roma which allow you to purchase buildings. Income from your new tenants will be deposited with bookkeepers as well as additional profit from renovations. Bookkeepers can be found throughout the city.

speaker: Ezio
en: Molto bene. (Very good.)

speaker: Mercenary
en: Ezio! About time you got here. We've found Bernardo Baroncelli.

speaker: Ezio
en: Ottima notizia! (This is good news!) Tell me where he is and I'll see that he's dealt with.

speaker: Mercenary
en: That's the trouble. Lorenzo actually had him arrested days ago, after being returned to us from Constantinople. But he escaped! We believe him to be somewhere inside San Gimignano.

speaker: Ezio
en: Va bene. (Okay.) I'll see if I can't pin him down.

speaker: Mercenary
en: How do you expect to succeed where the rest of us have failed?

speaker: Ezio
en: I have my ways...

speaker: Bernardo
en: ...I just need to take things one day at a time... He'll get bored... Lost... Confused... Distracted... Killed... It'll be okay... And if he does come... If it happens... I keep moving... Never in one place for long... Only... Only how to sleep... When to sleep... Where to sleep... The guard tower perhaps... They'll think me mad... They don't know... I'll pay them, yes... Then what will it matter... All they care about is coin... All anyone cares about is coin... Good for the brotherhood... Good for me... Safer this way... Yes... Yes.. I'll ask ... And then... And then I will be protected... We'll meet when it's time... And I'll leave this place... Free.. In time... In time... Wait! What is that... I saw something... Another mercenario (mercenary) come to SPY on me... No... No... Just my nerves... Hard to stay calm knowing that he seeks me... I must stay focused... And soon this will be done... Soon...

speaker: Bernardo
en: He's here! Help! Assassin! No! Guards! Guards! Where are the god-damned guards? Get away from me, Assassin! Away! Away! Away!! I won't give you the satisfaction! HELP! Why do you all just stand around and gawk!? DO SOMETHING! HELP ME!

speaker: Bernardo
en: I knew you would come...

speaker: Ezio
en: Where is Jacopo?

speaker: Bernardo
en: So you can do to him what you've done to me?

speaker: Ezio
en: There is still time for you to clear your conscience.

speaker: Bernardo
en: We gather at the church when a meeting is called...

speaker: Ezio
en: Mi duole dover giungere a tanto. (I am sorry that it came to this.) Requiescat in Pace. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Madonna...

speaker: Woman
en: Don't! Hasn't he hurt me enough?

speaker: Ezio
en: I will not touch you. What happened here?

speaker: Woman
en: Auguste. My beloved husband. He believes he owns this neighborhood.

speaker: Ezio
en: The Borgia have given it to him.

speaker: Woman
en: He once made signs for the shops in the district, but now he posts lies for the Borgia and hurts those who stand in his way.

speaker: Ezio
en: Like you. Where is he?

speaker: Woman
en: He spends his days locked in his workshop, but I may know how to goad him out...

speaker: Ezio
en: How?

speaker: Woman
en: Tear down the signs he has posted throughout the district. His pride won't stand for it!

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie (Thank you).

speaker: Auguste
en: Who has been tearing down my signs? I want him dead.

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in pace (Rest in peace).

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Mercenary
en: Ah! There you are! Listen, we've found Stefano da Bagnone. Just follow this road and it'll bring you to the abbey where he's taken refuge. Wait, before you go... Take these. You can create a distraction.

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Ezio
en: My thanks, friend.

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Monk
en: Let us pray brother.

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Stefano
en: Pray? Pray for what?

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Monk
en: The Lord's protection!

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Stefano
en: If you think the Lord has any interest in our affairs, you've another thing coming. But please, by all means, continue to delude yourself if it helps to pass the time.

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Monk
en: You speak blasphemy.

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Stefano
en: No. I speak truth.

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Monk
en: But to deny His most exalted existence...

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Stefano
en: ...Is the only rational response when faced with the declaration that there exists some invisible madman in the sky. And believe me, if your precious is anything to go by, he's completely lost his mind.

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Monk
en: How can you speak as such? You wear His vestments...

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Stefano
en: Only because they afforded me the opportunity to get close to the Medici. But you're right, I should look into replacing them – after the Assassin is dealt with.

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Monk
en: Ah! That unholy demon!

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Stefano
en: At least on this we agree.

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Monk
en: They say the devil has gifted him with unnatural speed and strength.

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Stefano
en: The devil? No. These are gifts he gave himself, through training. It is disturbing how unwilling you are to credit people for their circumstances. I think you'd make victims out of the entire world if you could.

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Monk
en: I forgive your lack of faith and forked tongue. You are still one of His children.

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Stefano
en: I told you... Oh, what's the use? Enough of this! It's like speaking to the wind.

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Monk
en: I will pray for you.

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Stefano
en: As you wish. But do so quietly. I must keep watch.

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Stefano
en: Now I will see who was right...

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Ezio
en: Where is Jacopo?

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Stefano
en: Nothing to fear I suppose... They meet in the shadows of the Roman Gods...

scene: The Cowl Does Not Make the Monk
speaker: Ezio
en: Ora sei libero dalla paura. Requiescat in pace. (Be free of your fear now. Rest in peace.)

speaker: Crash a Party
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where did these murderers come from?

speaker: Ezio
en: They must have come from in here.

speaker: Host
en: Welcome, welcome! The rules of this game are simple: out run your opponents, take the flag from the middle of the field, and bring it back to your starting position to score. If the opposition holds the flag, you must knock them down to steal it! Be the first to capture the flag three times, and the Golden Mask may yet be yours!

speaker: Host
en: We have a winner! You've protected your flag, and captured the enemy's. You've proven yourself a warrior without peer and inch ever closer to victory!

speaker: Cult of Hermes Reborn
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore's genetic memories stored in the Abstergo Cloud and relived by an Assassin hacker in 2023 through the Animus.

speaker: Ezio
en: I have seen happier men at the gallows.

speaker: Romani
en: Crack wise elsewhere, efendim (sir). Today the Byzantines stole half a year's worth of coin from us.

speaker: Ezio
en: Mi dispiace (I am sorry). Can I help?

speaker: Romani
en: Perhaps. For centuries my people have been slandered and insulted, labeled witches and warlocks. Well, so be it. We will not run from these lies any more, but embrace them. Encourage these rumors, for it is better to be infamous than ignored.

speaker: Ezio
en: I like the sound of that.

speaker: Romani
en: Here is my plan. Every man who touched that chest of coins must die, but discreetly... as if cursed by a pagan hex. The Romani curse becomes our blessing. Perhaps then people will leave us be.

speaker: Almogavar 1
en: God, I cannot believe how heavy this is.

speaker: Almogavar 2
en: You want me to carry it? They probably stole this money from someone else. It serves them right.

speaker: Almogavar 3
en: What would you spend the money on?

speaker: Almogavar 4
en: A hot meal, maybe a bath.

speaker: Almogavar 2
en: So much money, I cannot believe it.

speaker: Almogavar 3
en: Let me see.

speaker: Almogavar 4
en: Later!

speaker: Almogavar 3
en: What is happening? Is he ill?

speaker: Almogavar 2
en: Leave him! We cannot stay!

speaker: Almogavar 3
en: What the hell is going on here?

speaker: Almogavar 4
en: Is it a Romani curse? God help us. This is a bad idea.

speaker: Almogavar 4
en: God preserve me! I was a fool!

speaker: Romani
en: Ah, the old tricks are always the best. Do be careful, Ezio. I hear that chest is cursed.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where to, bella donna (lovely lady)?

speaker: Romani
en: This way. And stay alert.

speaker: Romani
en: Have you heard the term "gypsy"?

speaker: Ezio
en: Quite often, sì (yes).

speaker: Romani
en: Did you know that this word was born from the misapprehension that my people are from Egypt?

speaker: Ezio
en: You find it offensive?

speaker: Romani
en: I find it funny. My people are from eastern Persia and beyond. Yet, somehow we have become citizens of a land we have never seen.

speaker: Ezio
en: People are quick to judge and slow to correct themselves.

speaker: Romani
en: Psh... People are stupid.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sometimes.

speaker: Romani
en: Ezio, the simplest answer is always the best.

speaker: Ezio
en: You should count it. Make sure everything is there.

speaker: Romani
en: You have our thanks, Ezio. And you can count on us from here on out. For anything, at any time.

speaker: Ezio
en: Good to know. If I need, say... to borrow some money, I will ask you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Antonio, we need to talk.

speaker: Antonio
en: Ezio! Ezio Auditore! Teodora, meet the most... ahem... talented man in all of Venezia!

speaker: Ezio
en: Madonna. Ah! "Sister" Teodora... (to Antonio) I never imagined you as a religious type.

speaker: Teodora
en: It depends how you understand religion, my son. It's not just men's souls that call for soothing.

speaker: Antonio
en: Come! Join us, Ezio! Have a drink! Meet the ladies!

speaker: Courtesan
en: Murderer! Butcher! He sliced Lucia and stole her money!

speaker: Teodora
en: So, Messer (Sir) Ezio, let's see just how talented you are. After him!

speaker: Murderer
en: Don't come any closer, or I will carve up another one! Don't make me kill again!

speaker: Day at the Market
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Mentor, I have heard some troubling rumors.

speaker: Ezio
en: Tell me.

speaker: Apprentice
en: We have reason to believe a rogue Orthodox Deacon is planning to murder the Patriarch of Konstantiniyye.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do we know who this Deacon is?

speaker: Apprentice
en: Not yet. Clues have been sparse.

speaker: Ezio
en: We need a name first. It would not serve our cause to eliminate every holy man between Bursa and . Vieni (Come), and we will ask around to see what we can learn.

speaker: Apprentice
en: What is our plan, Mentor?

speaker: Ezio
en: The Orthodox millet in the city is too small to hide big secrets. We will ask the clergy some questions, and if necessary, make them answer.

speaker: Ezio
en: There are rumors that the Patriarch is in danger from a rogue Deacon. Does that stir any ideas?

speaker: Official
en: Ah yes. We have heard those rumors too. And the name behind them is always Cyril of Rhodes. The Patriarch cast him out some years ago for gross misdeeds. He is banished. . If you see him in the city, you can be sure he intends to do harm.

speaker: Apprentice
en: What did you learn?

speaker: Ezio
en: Our target is Cyril of Rhodes. A banished Deacon.

speaker: Ezio
en: Hold fast. There are a number of holy men here.

speaker: Apprentice
en: I know what to do, Mentor. And if I see an opportunity to eliminate him, I will take it.

speaker: Apprentice
en: I have him, Mentor.

speaker: Ezio
en: Stop! That is not our target!

speaker: Ezio
en: Brash fool! You killed an innocent man!

speaker: Apprentice
en: I have no excuse, Mentor. Forgive me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Even if I do, many others will not.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Nor should they.

speaker: Ezio
en: Take up his body and bring him to the shore. This is your burden to bear.

speaker: Ezio
en: Commit this poor man to the sea, then meditate on your mistake.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Evet (Yes), Mentor. May the shame I feel never fade.

speaker: Ezio
en: Cyril of Rhodes remains a danger to this city. Do you understand why?

speaker: Apprentice
en: I was overeager, Mentor.

speaker: Ezio
en: You were hasty, thinking only of the kill, and not the approach.

speaker: Apprentice
en: I can correct my mistake, Mentor. Cyril was spotted this morning, not far from here.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene (Good). We will find his trail together.

speaker: Apprentice
en: What is all this?

speaker: Ezio
en: That is the body of the man who gave me Cyril's name.

speaker: Apprentice
en: The Deacon is trying to clear his trail.

speaker: Ezio
en: But not quickly enough. We can still find him.

speaker: Ezio
en: There. The Deacon. It is unwise to kill a man in plain sight. What do you propose?

speaker: Apprentice
en: I will create a diversion. If he gives chase, you follow.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene (Good). Do it.

speaker: Cyril
en: Thief! You'll not get away! Guard! You cannot escape!

speaker: Cyril
en: Assassin! I should have known you brutes were behind this.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Who else, Deacon?

speaker: Cyril
en: You are meddling in affairs far outside your understanding. Go hide in your haystack! A pity you Assassins work alone. It will take longer to kill you all. So what happens now, Assassin?

speaker: Cyril
en: What do you hope to hear, Assassin? That I regret my associations? Never. Rome abandoned us in our time of need. The west turned a blind eye to the Ottoman juggernaut. Is it any wonder that I should turn to man with more honor, more courage, and more vision? I regret nothing...

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in pace.

speaker: Dead on Arrival
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Ezio
en: Have you found anything?

speaker: Salaì
en: Nothing is there, no pages, nothing.

speaker: Ezio
en: That cannot be. Something must be special about them. Think.

speaker: Salaì
en: I am done thinking. These paintings are a blank slate.

speaker: Ezio
en: Salaì, doesn't Leonardo conceal his research?

speaker: Salaì
en: He frequently writes backwards... Ezio, he also experimented with inks, including an ink that vanishes! But we can't see invisible ink... can we? Ezio, use your gift!

speaker: Ezio
en: You know about that too?

speaker: Ezio
en: I am going to solve this.

speaker: Salaì
en: I hope so. I cannot take much more.

speaker: Salaì
en: Do you think they would hurt him? Leonardo is terrified of violence.

speaker: Ezio
en: Unfortunately, this world is a violent place.

speaker: Salaì
en: Don't look at me, I cannot see them.

speaker: Ezio
en: There are drawings on the paintings!

speaker: Salaì
en: We were right!

speaker: Ezio
en: Found another! This one has been searched entirely. I see a drawing. Everything found. I found one. I found two drawings. There were two in this one as well. Got one!

speaker: Salaì
en: You have finished with that one, I see.

speaker: Ezio
en: I've found all the images. They seem to fit together.

speaker: Salaì
en: Draw them already!

speaker: Ezio
en: Bring me paper and ink.

speaker: Salaì
en: Is that a map? Show me the entrance.

speaker: Ezio
en: I must first position its pieces.

speaker: Salaì
en: Wait! What about the burned paintings?

speaker: Ezio
en: It is likely the missing parts will not be needed.

speaker: Salaì
en: Care to bet on that?

speaker: Ezio
en: No.

speaker: Ezio
en: Here! The entrance to the catacombs!

speaker: Salaì
en: Go. Bring him back to me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Hang on, old friend. I am coming.

speaker: Worker 1
en: Sigà! Sigà! (Steady! Steady!) This is gunpowder, not millet!

speaker: Worker 2
en: I got it!

speaker: Ezio
en: Rodrigo Borgia is dead.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: And Cesare?

speaker: Ezio
en: Poisoned, but alive.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: We must not allow him to assemble his remaining supporters. The coming weeks are critical.

speaker: Ezio
en: With your aid I will hunt him down.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: My men will patrol the city, but we might need an army.

speaker: Ezio
en: We have one.

speaker: Cesare
en: You must find them.

speaker: Guard Captain
en: They are everywhere and nowhere at once.

speaker: Cesare
en: I do not care how you do it.

speaker: Guard Captain
en: We cannot on our own, Signore (Sir). You must help us.

speaker: Cesare
en: I am ill, you idioti (idiots). Micheletto will soon be here with my armies and then you will see how quickly the Assassini (Assassins) fall.

speaker: Ezio
en: You delude yourself, Cesare.

speaker: Cesare
en: Guards!

speaker: Bystanders
en: What sorcery is this? He has God on his side! Please Lord, do not smite me! How is this possible? Il Diavolo (The Devil)!

speaker: Ezio
en: You have earned your rest, brother. Requiescat in pace (Rest in peace).

speaker: Ezio
en: Brothers. Sisters. The whole city rises against us while Yusuf's murderer waits and watches from the arsenal, laughing. Fight with me, and show him what it means to cross the Assassins.

speaker: Ahmet
en: You double it again. But the pieces are far beyond your grasp. You suppose the next Sultan will be an easy kill? Your time has come, Assassin! You have been a thorn in my side long enough, Assassin!

speaker: Ezio
en: Where is she?

speaker: Ahmet
en: Such fury!

speaker: Ezio
en: Where is she!

speaker: Ahmet
en: If you think you are in a position to negotiate, kill me and be done with it!

speaker: Ahmet
en: I am sorry it had to come to this. Two men who should be friends, quarreling over the keys to a library. We both strive for the same end, Ezio. Only our methods differ. Do you not see that? Peace. Stability. A world where men live without fear. People desire the truth, yes, but even when they have it, they refuse to look. How do we fight this kind of ignorance?

speaker: Ezio
en: Liberty can be messy, Ahmet. But it is priceless.

speaker: Ahmet
en: Of course. And when things fall apart, and the lights of civilization dim, Ezio Auditore can stand above the darkness and say proudly, "I stayed true to my Creed." I will open that library, and I will find the Grand Temple. And with the power that is hidden there, I will destroy the superstitions that keep men divided.

speaker: Ezio
en: Not in this life, Ahmet.

speaker: Ahmet
en: Bring the seals to Galata Tower when you are ready. Do this and Sofia will be spared.

speaker: Ahmet
en: My brother's army will be here soon, Ezio. After that, everything changes.

speaker: Ezio
en: How long have you been here?

speaker: Suleiman
en: Long enough. I had Ahmet tailed as soon as he returned, but I never expected to hear... all this.

speaker: Ezio
en: And what do you think?

speaker: Suleiman
en: He is a sincere man. But this Templar fantasy of his is dangerous. It flies in the face of reality. The world is a tapestry of many colors and patterns. A just leader would celebrate this, not seek to unravel it.

speaker: Ezio
en: He fears the disorder that comes from difference.

speaker: Suleiman
en: That is why we make laws to live by, a kanun (set of laws) that applies to all in equal measure.

speaker: Janissary
en: Shehzadem (Prince), stand back!

speaker: Suleiman
en: Hold, soldier. This man is not our enemy.

speaker: Ezio
en: What a challenge it would be to have a son like you.

speaker: Suleiman
en: You are not dead yet, old friend. Ezio... Spare my uncle, if you can.

speaker: Ezio
en: Would your father?

speaker: Suleiman
en: No.

speaker: Preacher
en: People of Firenze! Come! Gather round. Listen well to what I say! The end approaches! Now is the time to repent! To beg God's forgiveness.

speaker: Preacher
en: Don't you see?! The SIGNS are all around us: Unrest! Famine! Disease! Corruption! These are the harbingers of DARKNESS! We must stand firm in our devotion lest they CONSUME US ALL! I see you doubt; that you think me mad. Ahhhh... but did the Romans not say the same of Gesù? (Jesus?) Know that I, too, once shared your uncertainty. Your fear. But that was before Savonarola came to me. He showed me the TRUTH! At last, my eyes were OPENED. And so I stand before you today in the hope that I might open yours as well! Understand that we teeter upon a precipice. On one side, the shining, glorious KINGDOM OF GOD. On the other - a bottomless pit of DESPAIR! Will you turn back to the Lord? Or will you cast yourself into DARKNESS?! Already you stand precariously on the edge... Men like the Medici - and the other families you once called MASTERS sought earthly goods and gains. They abandoned their beliefs in favor of material pleasures. And they would have seen you all do the same! Our wise prophet once said: "The only good thing that we owe to Plato and Aristotle is that they brought forward many arguments which we can use against the heretics. Yet they and other philosophers are now in hell." If you value your immortal souls you'll turn back from this unholy course and embrace the words of our prophet, Savonarola. You will sanctify your bodies and spirits - you will discover the glory of God! You will, at last, become what our creator intended: loyal and obedient servants!

speaker: Ezio
en: Your mind... I sense it is your own.

speaker: Preacher
en: Not all of us required deception to be convinced. I already believed. All I said is true!

speaker: Ezio
en: Nothing is true. Non è un compito facile il mio... Requiescat in pace. (This is not an easy thing I do... Rest in peace.)

speaker: La Volpe
en: Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: La Volpe. I am surprised to see you.

speaker: La Volpe
en: And why have you appeared at my door? Wait, I know the answer.

speaker: Ezio
en: You always do.

speaker: La Volpe
en: You want to put my spies to work.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then, join me.

speaker: La Volpe
en: In aiding Machiavelli? No thank you. That man is a traitor to our Order.

speaker: Ezio
en: A serious allegation, coming from a thief. What is your proof?

speaker: La Volpe
en: He was an ambassador to the Papal court and traveled as the personal guest of Cesare himself. I also know he abandoned you right before the Villa attack.

speaker: Ezio
en: Machiavelli may not please all tastes, but he is an Assassin, not a traitor.

speaker: La Volpe
en: I am not convinced.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Ah. He is meeting someone in the Trastevere right now. Care to accompany me?

speaker: Ezio
en: I will follow...

speaker: La Volpe
en: What do you make of that?

speaker: Claudio
en: Help!

speaker: Trimalchio
en: Volpe, my son Claudio has been injured!

speaker: Ezio
en: They are going to shoot him.

speaker: La Volpe
en: I will kill these. Go! Get the others.

speaker: Ezio
en: Quick! Hide from the guards.

speaker: Claudio
en: I cannot. They are going to kill me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Pay attention. Do what I do.

speaker: Trimalchio
en: Claudio! Molte grazie, Messere. (Thank you very much, Mister.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Keep out of sight for a while, intesi (understood)?

speaker: La Volpe
en: The guards are looking for you.

speaker: Ezio
en: I see they have posters up.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Then rip them down. You can pay the heralds a few florins to silence them.

speaker: Ezio
en: Or I can eliminate witnesses.

speaker: La Volpe
en: You know how to disappear.

speaker: La Volpe
en: What a night this has been.

speaker: Ezio
en: Volpe, listen to me. I know what we saw, but you have nothing to fear from Machiavelli, I am sure of it.

speaker: La Volpe
en: I have you to thank for saving Claudio's life. If you believe Machiavelli remains loyal to the order, I trust you.

speaker: Ezio
en: So what of the thieves?

speaker: La Volpe
en: We had plans to repair this old building but, now that you and I are working together, I would like to know what you think.

speaker: Ezio
en: We need to make sure the Borgia stay away. Perhaps it could look like an inn.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Yes. Hmm, I like that idea.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then I will make it so.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Welcome, Ezio, to La Volpe Addormentata (The Sleeping Fox).

speaker: Ezio
en: The inn looks perfect. No one will ever suspect its real purpose.

speaker: La Volpe
en: The guild will be run from here. Visit me whenever you like. There might be objectives to pursue that will help our cause in the city.

speaker: Ezio
en: I see you thieves compete against each other.

speaker: La Volpe
en: You can participate, if you wish. Perhaps you will show them a thing or two. Ah yes, I forgot. We have gambling. It is a great source of income, especially since we ensure that the Borgia guards always lose.

speaker: Ezio
en: One last thing, I need your spies to find the Apple. It has been taken from me.

speaker: La Volpe
en: We are searching the city for it already.

speaker: Ezio
en: Molto bene (Very good). Come to Isola Tiberina (Tiber Island) with your findings.

speaker: La Volpe
en: I shall.

speaker: Ezio
en: Careful... I have fallen from my share of rooftops.

speaker: Woman
en: I'm waiting for my Lanz.

speaker: Ezio
en: Up here?

speaker: Woman
en: He left me after our baby died. Joined up with the Cento Occhi gang. They say he kills now... Pushes men from buildings. I tell them I don't believe it...

speaker: Ezio
en: But you do.

speaker: Woman
en: I do.

speaker: Ezio
en: What will you say to him if he comes?

speaker: Woman
en: I will jump.

speaker: Ezio
en: Why should you pay for his crimes?

speaker: Woman
en: My death will remind him of the man he once was.

speaker: Ezio
en: He does not deserve your sacrifice. Where is Lanz?

speaker: Woman
en: Up here... Somewhere...

speaker: Ezio
en: He will trouble you no more Madonna.

speaker: Lanz
en: Merda (Shit)!

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in pace (Rest in peace).

speaker: Thief
en: Ezio, one of the Cento Occhi (Hundred Eyes) leaders has worked his way into our own guild! He is an accomplished liar, responsible for the deaths of many of our brothers. Come, I will lead you to him.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: You excel at opening wounds, Ezio, but can you also close them?

speaker: Ezio
en: I intend to heal the sickness, not treat its symptoms.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Stop sparring with me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Fine. Let us talk openly then. Rodrigo Borgia's death would not have solved anything.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: I am inclined to disagree.

speaker: Ezio
en: Look at this city, the center of Borgia and Templar rule. Killing one man will not change things. We need to take away the source of their power.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Are you suggesting we appeal to the people?

speaker: Ezio
en: Maybe.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Relying on the people is like building on the sand.

speaker: Ezio
en: You are wrong. Our belief in humanity rests at the heart of the Assassin Brotherhood.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: He must be from your inner circle. Go. Get back what he has stolen.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: I will wait at the Campidoglio (Capitoline Hill). I am meeting a contact there.

speaker: Ezio
en: Give me back my money! Come back here! You are making a big mistake.

speaker: Ezio
en: Get out of here before I regret sparing your life.

speaker: Sánchez
en: ... and so, spurred by their desire to see the kingdom of España (Spain) united by a single faith, the Inquisitors convinced the Queen and King to drive out the remaining Moors. This is why war rages here in Granada. The palace of Alhambra and the city surrounding it are the last Moorish strongholds on the continent.

speaker: Ezio
en: It sounds like the battle is already won.

speaker: Sánchez
en: One would think... but for some reason the Moors continue to fight. Perhaps King Muhammad XII has a death wish. Hold... we have reached the outskirts of the city. It is a disputed territory and still quite dangerous.

speaker: Ezio
en: What is our course?

speaker: Sánchez
en: We'll do a sweep of the area, and eliminate all threats. We must make it safe for the civilians to move about.

speaker: Ezio
en: Basta! (Enough!) I can walk.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Look out! They are coming! Everyone retreat to the Villa!

speaker: Ezio
en: I cannot fight like this. Stand with me!

speaker: Claudia
en: Ezio!

speaker: Ezio
en: Get inside the Sanctuary.

speaker: Claudia
en: Follow me!

speaker: Mercenary
en: I will hold them back!

speaker: Ezio
en: Stop! Wait for us!

speaker: Paganino
en: We thought you had been killed, Ser Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: Not yet.

speaker: Paganino
en: Where does this passage lead?

speaker: Ezio
en: To the north, outside the walls.

speaker: Paganino
en: I'm surprised it exists.

speaker: Paganino
en: Let me through, I must go help the troops.

speaker: Claudia
en: Hurry Ezio!

speaker: Ezio
en: Where's mother? Is she all right?

speaker: Maria
en: I am here Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie a Dio. (Thank God).

speaker: Claudia
en: We could not leave without you.

speaker: Ezio
en: The way out will be dangerous. Protect our mother.

speaker: Claudia
en: Where is Mario? I thought he would be waiting for us.

speaker: Man
en: The Borgia infantry are circling the town!

speaker: Ezio
en: Mario is dead. You must leave this place. Take mother to Firenze.

speaker: Ezio
en: Get me a horse!

speaker: Claudia
en: You are not coming with us? Where are you riding?

speaker: Ezio
en: To Roma.

speaker: Maria
en: Go, my son, destroy them... but remember for whom we Assassins fight.

speaker: Ezio
en: Emilio! Your life ends now!

speaker: Emilio
en: For what reason? I've done nothing to you.

speaker: Ezio
en: You didn't need to.

speaker: Emilio
en: You have no reason then? You sabotage my business, you kill my men, you free criminals that the authorities have rightfully imprisoned... All on a whim?

speaker: Ezio
en: There are plenty who can vouch for your cruelties.

speaker: Emilio
en: Who? Thieves? People who rely on deceit and trickery to feed themselves?

speaker: Ezio
en: They are thrustworthy.

speaker: Emilio
en: Says a man who sneaks about in the dark with a hood covering his face.
