speaker: Ezio
en: We all have our methods.

speaker: Emilio
en: You can sneak around outside all you want. You'll never find a way inside here!

speaker: Ezio
en: We shall see.

speaker: Ezio
en: Emilio! Come back here!

speaker: Emilio
en: I think not. Really, why would I do that? You are obviously in a killing mood.

speaker: Ezio
en: Wherever you are going, I will track you down.

speaker: Emilio
en: We shall see of that.

speaker: Emilio
en: You go to such great lengths... and for what?

speaker: Ezio
en: To see men like you removed from power.

speaker: Emilio
en: It seems you are taking more than just power from me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Let me ask you, then. Was there another way?

speaker: Emilio
en: No. I would have done the same if I were you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then we understand one another.

speaker: Ezio
en: We are close! Keep steady!

speaker: Ahmet
en: Well, well! You have come to see me off!

speaker: Ezio
en: Hold on.

speaker: Sofia
en: Ah!

speaker: Ezio
en: Hang on, Sofia!

speaker: Sofia
en: Look out!

speaker: Ezio
en: Argh!

speaker: Sofia
en: Ezio!

speaker: Sofia
en: Help!

speaker: Ezio
en: Are you hurt, Sofia?

speaker: Sofia
en: I don't think so!

speaker: Ezio
en: Hold on!

speaker: Sofia
en: Obviously!

speaker: Sofia
en: Oh no!

speaker: Sofia
en: Va bene (okay) I am all right.

speaker: Ezio
en: Soldiers, up ahead!

speaker: Sofia
en: I see them! Forgive me!

speaker: Ezio
en: Sofia! You must be careful!

speaker: Sofia
en: I know, I know!

speaker: Ezio
en: Steel yourself, Sofia. More soldiers!

speaker: Ahmet
en: Faster! Out of the road!

speaker: Ezio
en: What are you doing?

speaker: Sofia
en: Keeping us on track! Oh my! Please move!

speaker: Ahmet
en: Your determination would be charming if it was not so infuriating! Incompetent children! Where did you learn to fight?

speaker: Sofia
en: Ezio, Look!

speaker: Sofia
en: Whoa! Go, Ezio! I am fine!

speaker: Ahmet
en: So what now, Ezio? How does this end?

speaker: Ezio
en: I am wondering that myself.

speaker: Selim
en: Hold!

speaker: Ahmet
en: Soldiers! Selim is not your master! You serve the Sultan! You carry out his command alone! Where is he? Where is our Sultan?

speaker: Selim
en: He stands before you, brother. Father made his choice.

speaker: Ahmet
en: Selim! Stop! Please!

speaker: Selim
en: So, you are the Assassin, Ezio Auditore? I am Selim, Suleiman's father. He speaks quite highly of you.

speaker: Ezio
en: He is a remarkable boy with a magnificent mind.

speaker: Selim
en: Were it not for his endorsement, I would have you killed where you stand. Leave this place, and do not return.

speaker: Sofia
en: You did the right thing, Ezio. This is not your fight.

speaker: Ezio
en: But where does one end, and the next begin?

speaker: Ezio
en: Explosions from above... has the siege started again?

speaker: Ahmet
en: Poor Manuel, last of the Palaiologi. I should not have put him in charge of our Masyaf expedition. He was an arrogant man, impossible to keep in line.

speaker: Ezio
en: You disappoint me Ahmet. Why the Templars?

speaker: Ahmet
en: Because I am tired of all these pointless blood feuds that pit father against son, brother against brother. To achieve true peace, mankind must think and move as one body, with one master mind. The secrets in the Grand Temple will give us just that. And Altaïr will lead us there.

speaker: Ezio
en: Delusions. Altaïr's secrets are not for you.

speaker: Ahmet
en: I am not interested in arguing, Ezio. I am here for the Masyaf keys.

speaker: Ezio
en: Keys? Are there more than this one?

speaker: Ahmet
en: So I have heard. Perhaps I should ask someone who knows better. Sofia Sartor? Is that her name?

speaker: Ezio
en: She knows nothing! Leave her be!

speaker: Ahmet
en: We shall see.

speaker: Ezio
en: I will kill you if you touch her!

speaker: Ahmet
en: I know you'll try.

speaker: Claudia
en: What do you want?

speaker: Ezio
en: You spoke of a Senator at the meeting.

speaker: Claudia
en: Find him on the Campidoglio, you do not need me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Once I kill the Banker, your girls must take his money back to the underground.

speaker: Claudia
en: Fine.

speaker: Ezio
en: Stay alert.

speaker: Ezio
en: Now, where is that Senator?

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Why would we give our money to Egidio? We know what he intends to do with it.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Egidio's been asking for money again.

speaker: Civilian 3
en: What is it for this time?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Some proposal to diminish the frequency of public executions.

speaker: Civilian 4
en: Did you hear? Egidio wants to get rid of the exemption licenses.

speaker: Civilian 5
en: Please! Every citizen who feels mistreated by our laws should be allowed to pay for an exemption to those laws. Such is our duty. As Jesu Cristo said, 'blessed are the messengers'.

speaker: Civilian 6
en: Egidio's petitioning for an end to witness torture in the criminal courts.

speaker: Civilian 7
en: Like that's going to happen. He just wants the money to pay off his debts.

speaker: Guard 1
en: No more arguing.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Your bill has come due.

speaker: Egidio
en: Make an exception for an old man.

speaker: Guard 1
en: No.

speaker: Guard 3
en: The Banker sent us to collect.

speaker: Egidio
en: I will have his money momentarily.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Not good enough.

speaker: Egidio
en: A good Samaritan in Roma? I thought they were a dying breed.

speaker: Ezio
en: Senator Egidio Troche.

speaker: Egidio
en: I don't owe you money too, do I?

speaker: Ezio
en: I'm looking for Cesare's banker.

speaker: Egidio
en: Ha. Cesare Borgia. And you are?

speaker: Ezio
en: A friend of the family.

speaker: Egidio
en: Cesare has a lot of friends these days. Unfortunately, I am not one of them.

speaker: Ezio
en: I can pay.

speaker: Egidio
en: Ma che meraviglia! (Well, isn't that something!) He fights guards and gives away money. Where have you been all my life?

speaker: Ezio
en: We'd better get out of here.

speaker: Egidio
en: I know a place.

speaker: Egidio
en: You're going to have to protect me though. The guards aren't being very friendly, if you know what I mean.

speaker: Ezio
en: Someone really wants you dead.

speaker: Egidio
en: A few months ago my brother Francesco, the Pope's Chamberlain—I know, I know, don't get me started—he told me of Cesare's plans for Romagna. I wrote to the ambassador of Venezia, warning him. One of my letters must have been intercepted. The Senate has nothing to do these days, the Borgia have taken all the power. You know what it's like to not have un cazzo (fuck) to do? It changes a man. I admit I've been gambling, drinking...

speaker: Ezio
en: And whoring.

speaker: Egidio
en: Oh, you're good. Was it the perfume on my sleeve?

speaker: Ezio
en: Something like that.

speaker: Egidio
en: Senators used to petition about real issues, like unlawful cruelty, abandoned children. Now we write up legislation on the appropriate width of women's sleeves.

speaker: Ezio
en: Not you. You raise money for false causes to pay back your gambling debts.

speaker: Egidio
en: False causes! I am interested in pursuing them as soon as I am financially able to do so. You ever look at a grave and think "This is the most significant thing I will ever do?"

speaker: Ezio
en: It is not safe here. We must keep moving.

speaker: Ezio
en: We cannot stop here. Too many guards.

speaker: Egidio
en: Maledette (Fucking) letters. I should never have sent them to the ambassador. Now Cesare will murder me. Benvenuto (Welcome) to the home of my brother, Francesco. Thank God he's not here, we haven't talked since he found out about the letters. What did you want again?

speaker: Ezio
en: Cesare's banker.

speaker: Egidio
en: Right. I need to arrive with the money. Problem is, there is no money.

speaker: Ezio
en: You are meeting the Banker? Where?

speaker: Egidio
en: I never know until I'm there. I go to one of three places. Then his friends take me to him.

speaker: Ezio
en: I will bring you all the money you owe.

speaker: Egidio
en: Sul serio? (Seriously?) You need to stop this. You might actually give me hope!

speaker: Sánchez
en: How strange to meet a gentleman leaping through these sewers. Are you on the run, or just recreating?

speaker: Ezio
en: Step aside, stranger.

speaker: Sánchez
en: You bear the mark of the Assassins... and from the cut of your outfit I'd say you were... Venetian?

speaker: Ezio
en: No, Florentine. What do you know of the Assassins?

speaker: Sánchez
en: Only that I am one of them, sir. My name is Raphael Sánchez. I arrived here this morning, bound to the same errand as you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do you know who betrayed us to the Inquisitors?

speaker: Sánchez
en: Not yet, but we know the name of the Inquisitor Prosecutor responsible for their arrests. Gaspar Martínez.

speaker: Ezio
en: I'd like to meet this Prosecutor.

speaker: Sánchez
en: Good. Find me again when you're finished with him.

speaker: Escape the Tower
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus 2.0.

speaker: Mario
en: Ezio! Haha, Come in, come in! To what do we owe the honor?

speaker: Ezio
en: I've been sent from Firenze by Il Magnifico to attend to some unfinished business. I'm looking for Jacopo de' Pazzi.

speaker: Mario
en: Ha... Who isn't? We've been at it for days.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then perhaps what I carry will help us both: a list of his co-conspirators. One of them WILL talk before he dies.

speaker: Mario
en: Excellent! These men are sure to lack Jacopo's resources, which means they will be easier to find. I will put my scouts to it at once.

speaker: Ezio
en: I appreciate the help, uncle. I've got something else for you as well: more Codex pages.

speaker: Mario
en: Ah! Let's see what we can learn. What is this...? What Prophet...?

speaker: Ezio
en: What did you find, uncle?

speaker: Mario
en: Just another damn mystery! The text here roughly translates to: "Only the prophet may open it..." There's reference to two "Pieces of Eden." But these pages offer no answers, nipote (nephew). At least not on their own. You must find more.

speaker: Ezio
en: We'll have to save it for another day, uncle. I have a mission to attend to.

speaker: Mario
en: As you wish. Now, if you hope to defeat these bastardi (bastards), I will need to teach you a few things. Meet me on the practice field.

speaker: Mario
en: Alright, Ezio. You're familiar with counter-attacking - but what happens when your enemy is as well?

speaker: Ezio
en: I don't usually give them the opportunity.

speaker: Mario
en: Tough talk offers little protection against Templar steel.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then by all means, maestro (master) - teach me what to do!

speaker: Mario
en: Now dodge! Bravo!

speaker: Mario
en: Magnifico! (Magnificent!) Once again you exceed my expectations!

speaker: Mercenary
en: Signore! (Sir!) We've found Jacopo's men, and await your word to strike!

speaker: Mario
en: Relay the following: no man moves until they have spoken with Ezio. Intesi? (Understand?)

speaker: Mercenary
en: It will be done!

speaker: Mario
en: Go, Ezio! Visit with my mercenaries in the countryside. See if Jacopo's lackeys won't lead you to him. But be careful. They will be expecting you!

speaker: Ugo
en: Please, enter!

speaker: Antonio
en: Your good work has restored us to our former strength, Ezio. We are ready to strike.

speaker: Ezio
en: Just tell me what needs to be done, and I'll see that it is.

speaker: Antonio
en: You'll approach from above, under the cover of night. Emilio has posted archers around the Palazzo. Kill them, but do so quietly. As they fall, my men shall replace them.

speaker: Ezio
en: What about the guards?

speaker: Antonio
en: When you've finished with the archers, we'll regroup in front of this building here, and discuss next steps.

speaker: Ezio
en: Nessun problema (Not a problem). I'll take care of the archers and return to you.

speaker: Antonio
en: Then it's settled. In bocca al lupo. (Into the wolf's mouth.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Crepi il lupo! (May the wolf die!)

speaker: Ugo
en: Hurry!

speaker: Antonio
en: Well done, Ezio. Everything is going according to plan. As we speak, my men are replacing the archers you removed. The way to the Palazzo is clear now.

speaker: Ezio
en: But not the building itself. Emilio's guards still patrol its border.

speaker: Ugo
en: Use my men. They can distract the guards; save you from having to fight.

speaker: Rosa
en: And when it comes time to storm the place, remember what I've taught you.

speaker: Antonio
en: Sii cauto (Take care), Ezio. We await word of your success.

speaker: Carlo Grimaldi
en: Your little house of cards is crumbling, Emilio.

speaker: Emilio
en: A minor setback. It will be dealt with. This povero scemo (poor fool) Antonio and his thieves...

speaker: Carlo
en: Never mind them! It's the Assassin you should be worried about!

speaker: Emilio
en: Why? Is... is he in Venezia?

speaker: Carlo
en: He's been here for weeks! How could you be so blind?!

speaker: Emilio
en: Unlike you, I've been busy! Someone had to provide weapons to our brothers in Firenze!

speaker: Carlo
en: Yes, and we all saw what good that did...

speaker: Emilio
en: Enough with the barbs! What is it you want, Carlo?

speaker: Carlo
en: Maestro has called a meeting; three days from now at Santo Stefano.

speaker: Emilio
en: Very well. I'll be there.

speaker: Carlo
en: Assuming you still live. If you want my advice, I'd find a less conspicuous place to wait. Seta is a target now.

speaker: Emilio
en: Seta is a fortress!

speaker: Carlo
en: If you say so. Goodbye, Emilio.

speaker: Emilio
en: Cazzo (Fuck), what if he's right?

speaker: Emilio
en: You! Call my boat, it should be close. When it arrives, load these crates and prepare to sail. I'll be right back. If Carlo speaks true, I must find a place to hide—just until the meeting. Then we'll deal with the Assassin. He must be working with Antonio. That means the attacks... No! I've worked too hard for this! Don't they understand... There is so much less crime... The people have better lives... So some must leave... It is the price of progress... Why must the Assassins always interfere... Like Giovanni... If he had just left well enough alone... Is the ship loaded? Are you ready?

speaker: Guard
en: It is done. Let us go.

speaker: Emilio
en: Yes. And quickly.

speaker: Emilio
en: Guardia! Guardia! (Guards! Guards!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Do not be afraid.

speaker: Emilio
en: I feel no fear, assassin. Only regret. I sought unity... stability... order.

speaker: Ezio
en: At too great a cost.

speaker: Emilio
en: Progress demands sacrifice.

speaker: Ezio
en: Non trovo alcuna gioia in questo, ma non c'e altro modo. Requiescat in pace. (I take no joy in this, but I see no other way Rest in peace).

speaker: Rosa
en: Sorry! We couldn't resist.

speaker: Rosa
en: Come! Let's open the gate for Antonio.

speaker: Antonio
en: Seta is fallen and Emilio is no more! All thanks to you, Ezio!

speaker: Antonio
en: Go! Tear down Emilio's banners! Return what he has stolen from the people.

speaker: Antonio
en: Tell me, Ezio. How can I repay you for your service?

speaker: Ezio
en: Money's always nice.

speaker: Antonio
en: Easy enough.

speaker: Antonio
en: What else?

speaker: Ezio
en: Emilio was meeting with a man named Carlo. He looked to be a government official. Do you know him?

speaker: Antonio
en: Carlo Grimaldi. He sits on the Council of Ten. Why do you ask? What are you up to?

speaker: Ezio
en: I have a meeting to attend.

speaker: Assassin
en: Mentor.

speaker: Ezio
en: Now should be a time for remembrance and mourning, I know... but our enemies do not permit us that luxury. Yusuf thought highly of you, Assassin. And I find no reason to second-guess this judgment. Do you have it in your heart to lead these men and women, and to maintain the dignity of our Order as Yusuf did with such passion?

speaker: Dogan
en: It would be an honor.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene. (Good.) I am glad. Our enemy is close. Take positions around the tower. Then wait for my command.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where is she?

speaker: Ahmet
en: I admire you, Ezio. But your bloodlust makes it hard to call you a friend.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bloodlust? A strange insult from the man who ordered an attack on his own nephew.

speaker: Ahmet
en: He was to be kidnapped, Ezio, not killed.

speaker: Ezio
en: I see. Kidnapped by the Byzantines, so that his uncle could rescue him and be heralded a hero?

speaker: Ahmet
en: More or less. Now... the keys.

speaker: Ezio
en: First the girl.

speaker: Ahmet
en: She's all yours.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sofia!

speaker: Ahmet
en: Tell your men to back off.

speaker: Ahmet
en: She's all yours.

speaker: Ezio
en: Dannazione! (Dammit!)

speaker: Azize
en: Teshekkurler efendim, chock teshekkurier. (Thank you, sir, oh thank you.)

speaker: Sofia
en: Help!

speaker: Ezio
en: Are you hurt?

speaker: Sofia
en: No, not hurt. But very confused.

speaker: Ezio
en: I did not mean to drag you into this. I am sorry.

speaker: Sofia
en: You are not responsible for the actions of other men.

speaker: Ezio
en: All this will be over soon. But I need to recover what they have taken.

speaker: Sofia
en: I do not understand what is happening, Ezio. Who are these men?

speaker: Ezio
en: Run!

speaker: Monk
en: Give, and it shall be given to you. For whatever measure you deal out to others, it will be dealt to you in return. These are insightful words... words to live by, yet Brother Ristoro spits at them! Deus omnia videt. We Minims require your donations to survive. In return, we offer you knowledge. A fair trade, but one of us takes advantage! He abuses the trust we have worked so hard to establish! Come and see where your donations have gone! Two of our order slain by their own teacher! Ristoro's innocence bought from the Borgia! God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble. Ristoro is far from humble! He has broken his vow of poverty! Soiled every promise of purity! He must be held accountable! Deus omnes vel absolvit vel judicat!

speaker: Ezio
en: How were these men killed?

speaker: Monk
en: They questioned Brother Ristoro's habits, and now here they are, poisoned.

speaker: Ezio
en: You question him as well, why do you not fear his wrath?

speaker: Monk
en: A man with nothing fears nothing. I have remained true to my vows. I put my fate in the hands of the divine. Deus asculti.

speaker: Ezio
en: Your vows keep you from acting, so you seek another to do what you will not.

speaker: Monk
en: Please understand. I cannot kill.

speaker: Ezio
en: But I can. Where is Ristoro?

speaker: Monk
en: He will be at the church. But guards always accompany him.

speaker: Ezio
en: The Borgia cannot protect him from me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in pace (Rest in peace).

speaker: Ezio
en: I must get to Pietro before he does.

speaker: Pietro
en: My god, my god, why hast thou thus forsaken me?

speaker: Ezio
en: Merda (shit.) Which cross is Pietro's?

speaker: Legionary 1
en: Hark, hark how he cryeth upon Elijah to deliver him.

speaker: Legionary 2
en: Wait and we shall see whether Elijah dare come here or not.

speaker: Pietro
en: My thirst is great, my thirst is great.

speaker: Legionary 2
en: Yea, thou shall drink no more.

speaker: Pietro
en: Mighty God in majesty, to work thy will I will never cease. My spirit I betake to thee; receive it, lord, into thy hands. 'Consummatum est.

speaker: Centurion
en: Lords, I say you, this was God's son almighty. I know it must be so. I know by manner of his cry he has fulfilled the prophecy and godhead showed in him.

speaker: Bishop
en: Centurion, as God gives me speed, thou must be daft; thou cannot read. When thou seest his heart bleed, let us see what thou will say. Now, Longyus, take this spear in hand.

speaker: Legionary 3
en: Yes, have this spear and take good heed. Thou must do, as the bishop bade thee, a thing that is full of great need.

speaker: Longyus
en: I will do as he bade me, but on your peril it shall be. What I do I may not see, whether it be evil or good. High king of heaven, I see thee here. On my hand and on my spear running water throw; and on my eyes some can fall that I may see both one and all. Lord, where does this water come from? Alas, alas, and woe is me! What deed have I done? A man I see, sooth to say, I have slain in this stead. Of mercy, lord, I thee now pray, for I was not what I did. Jesus, much have I heard spake of thee, that sick and blind through thy pity thou has healed before in this city as thee has healed me today. Thee will I serve and with thee be, for well I leave in days three thou will rise. Lord, I thee pray.

speaker: Ezio
en: I need to get onstage.

Ah, lord God, what heart have ye to slay this man that I here see dead, hanging, that never yet did amiss? For, surely, God's son is he. Therefore a tomb is made for me therein his buried shall be, for he is king of bliss.
Sir Joseph, I say surely this is God's son almighty. Go ask for his body and buried shall he be. I shall help thee to take him down devotedly.

speaker: Joseph
en: Sir Pilate, special I thee pray a boon thou grant me as thou may. This prophet that is dead today, thou grant me his body.

speaker: Pilate
en: Joseph, all ready, in good faith! If that Centurion says that he is dead, him will I not deny. Centurion, is Jesus dead?

speaker: Micheletto
en: Hah. You cannot save Pietro. The wine he drank was poisoned. As I promised Cesare, I made doubly sure.

speaker: Micheletto
en: I am not yet dead.

speaker: Ezio
en: I did not come here to kill you. He who is the cause of someone else becoming powerful is the agent of his own destruction.

speaker: Ezio
en: The Borgia are after you.

speaker: Scholar 1
en: Then I will hide. Thank you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Read this and get to safety.

speaker: Scholar 2
en: I will. Grazie (Thank you).

speaker: Ezio
en: Take this. It is from Copernico.

speaker: Scholar 3
en: Grazie (Thank you).

speaker: Thief
en: Ezio, La Volpe has uncovered an opportunity too golden to ignore, a gift from the Borgia to the Cento Occhi (Hundred Eyes). It is filled with pardons, promises, and payoffs. Needless to say, it holds great value to our guild if you manage to steal it.

speaker: Thief
en: Grazie (Thank you), Ezio. I will take this to La Volpe.

speaker: Ezio
en: Come with me. Once we get inside, I will mark the paintings for you to steal. Bring them to Leonardo's workshop. Capito? (Understand?)

speaker: Guard 1
en: Invitation?

speaker: Ezio
en: Here.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Oh my. Come back soon... I hope.

speaker: Cardinal 1
en: How daring! I have not seen an annunciation from this angle before.

speaker: Cardinal 2
en: The composition suffers I feel. The light of God is not properly expressed. It does not move me.

speaker: Cardinal 1
en: You are truly stuck in your ways, my friend.

speaker: Guard 2
en: The upper floors are now open to the cardinals who wish to see additional expressions of devotion.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Two of the paintings are missing! Be on the lookout for a thief!

speaker: Fallen Archers
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Copernicus
en: The world itself is unchanging, WE must change to understand it. Its secrets will only be revealed through a careful study of the truth, but we have been taught incorrectly. Theories by great men who were limited by archaic tools and beliefs! We live in a time of progress. Art, medicine, philosophy... everyday new breakthroughs are made. But when we look to the sky, we do not question. We remain in the past. It is time to remand our schooling, to explore the world as it truly is! My colleagues and I have set up workshops throughout Roma. Please, visit us. We have much to share. Anyone who wishes to be enlightened step forward. I have much to share. A new world awaits you. The truth comes to those who seek it out.

speaker: Ezio
en: Who is this man?

speaker: Citizen
en: He comes from Prussia. I hear he studies at Il Vaticano (the Vatican), but his words are unlike any that issue from that place.

speaker: Copernicus
en: Some may tell you to be content with Ptolemy's explanation of the heavens. His mathematical contortions of the spheres dancing around the Earth. But why are such complicated numbers required? Perhaps, to disguise a myriad of contradictions? You must question bad logic. It is why we live, to ask questions.

speaker: Guard
en: Kill him quickly. The Master wants all scholars silenced by nightfall.

speaker: Ezio
en: If the Borgia are involved, then so am I.

speaker: False Legacy
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Sofia
en: Buon Giorno! (Good day!) Merhaba! (Hello!) Please come in. Ah! Excuse the clutter. I have not had time to tidy up since my trip.

speaker: Ezio
en: You sailed from Rhodes, no?

speaker: Sofia
en: Sì. (Yes.) How did you know?

speaker: Ezio
en: We were on the same ship. I am Ezio Auditore.

speaker: Sofia
en: Sofia Sartor. Have we met?

speaker: Ezio
en: We have now. May I have a look around?

speaker: Sofia
en: Prego. (Please.) Most of my best tomes are in the back.

speaker: Sofia
en: It is nice to meet another Italian in this district. Most keep to the Venetian quarter and Galata.

speaker: Ezio
en: Altrettanto. (Likewise.) I assumed the Ottoman war with Venezia would have driven most of you away.

speaker: Sofia
en: I lived here with my parents when I was a girl. The war pushed us out, but I always knew I would return.

speaker: Sofia
en: Have you found anything interesting?

speaker: Sofia
en: Mio Dio! (My God!) Who put that there? Incredibile. (This is incredible.) Where does it lead?

speaker: Ezio
en: Why don't we find out?

speaker: Sofia
en: Who are you, messere (sir)?

speaker: Ezio
en: Only the most interesting man in your life.

speaker: Sofia
en: Ah, che presuntuoso! (Ah, go bury your head!)

speaker: Ezio
en: A presto (Goodbye), Sofia. I will return in a moment.

speaker: Ezio
en: Father said there was a door here...

speaker: Ezio
en: I need to bring this to Messer Uberto.

speaker: Guard
en: Traditore. (Traitor.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Hey! What's with the swords? Aren't you supposed to arrest me?

speaker: Guard
en: No.

speaker: Ezio
en: What do you want, then?

speaker: Guard
en: For you to die.

speaker: Ezio
en: Well, that's not going to happen. So why don't we explore other options?

speaker: Guard
en: There are no other options.

speaker: Uberto
en: Ezio Auditore? What are you doing here at this hour?

speaker: Ezio
en: It... I don't...

speaker: Uberto
en: Wait, child. Take a breath. Collect your thoughts.

speaker: Ezio
en: My father and brothers have been imprisoned. I was told to bring you this.

speaker: Uberto
en: Ahh. I see now. It's a misunderstanding Ezio. I'll clear everything up.

speaker: Ezio
en: How?

speaker: Uberto
en: The documents you've given me contains evidence of a conspiracy against your family and against the city. I'll present these papers at the hearing in the morning and they'll be released.

speaker: Ezio
en: Thank you, signore.

speaker: Uberto
en: Of course my child. Do you need a place to stay? You're more than welcome here.

speaker: Ezio
en: No grazie. (No thank you.) I'll meet you at the piazza.

speaker: Uberto
en: Don't worry Ezio. Everything is going to be fine.

speaker: Darby
en: Blessings on you, brother.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie. (Thank you.) I wonder if you can help me?

speaker: Darby
en: What do you seek?

speaker: Ezio
en: A monk in black robes who lacks one of his ten fingers.

speaker: Darby
en: Well... Brother Guido has only nine toes. Are you sure it wasn't a toe?

speaker: Ezio
en: Quite sure.

speaker: Darby
en: And then there's brother Domenico, but it's his entire left arm he's lacking.

speaker: Ezio
en: Again, quite sure it was a finger.

speaker: Darby
en: Hmm... Now wait a moment, I do recall a black robed monk with nine fingers. Yes of course, when we had our last 's feast at the abbey.

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes, I know the place. I'll try there. Grazie.

speaker: Darby
en: Go in peace, brother.

speaker: Ezio
en: I always do.

speaker: Ezio
en: Excuse me, brother. I wonder if you can

speaker: Abbot
en: Unholy demon! Get away!

speaker: Ezio
en: What's wrong?

speaker: Abbot
en: You're the one who killed Brother Stefano! Brothers! The killer of the monks has returned!

speaker: Abbot
en: Please, no! I don't want to die!

speaker: Ezio
en: I only kill those who kill others, and your Brother Stefano was a killer. I'm sure you are no such thing. Now, listen to me. I'm looking for a black robed monk who's missing a finger.

speaker: Abbot
en: Missing a finger you say? Do you mean... like Fra' Savonarola?

speaker: Ezio
en: Savonarola?! Who is this? You know him?

speaker: Abbot
en: I did... He was one of us. For a time.

speaker: Ezio
en: And then?

speaker: Abbot
en: We suggested he retire to a hermitage for a good long time.

speaker: Ezio
en: I'm afraid to say his retreat has come to an end. Where would he have gone?

speaker: Abbot
en: Oh dear... Santo Spirito, in Firenze. It's where he studied. Perhaps it's where he would return.

speaker: Ezio
en: I thank you. Go with God, brother.

speaker: Guard
en: Signore. I saw Francesco lead a battalion around the back of the Palazzo della Signoria. I fear he may be seeking another way in.

speaker: Poliziano
en: Go! Before it's too late. Do what you can.

speaker: Francesco
en: You again!? Why aren't you dead? - Men! Slaughter him!

speaker: Francesco
en: Oh! The boy thinks himself a master swordsman. So you've drawn some blood! My men will make short of you! Desisti! (Stop!) You're only delaying your inevitable and painful end! What do you think you are proving? That you're loyal servant of that dog, Lorenzo? Death shall be your reward! I grow tired of this game. Guards, finitelo! (Finish him off!)

speaker: Francesco
en: Guards—! GUARDS!

speaker: Ezio
en: No one's coming... It's just us now.

speaker: Francesco
en: Meledetto! Che il diavolo ti porti! Stammi lontano! (Damn it! Damn you to hell! Get the hell away from me!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Now Firenze will judge you for what you've done.

speaker: Francesco
en: It's over... It's all over...

speaker: Ezio
en: Meglio essere felici in questa vita che aspirare a esserlo nella prossima. (Better to be content in this life, than aspire to it in the next). Requiescat in Pace. (Rest in peace).

speaker: Crowd
en: Libertà! Libertà! Libertà...

speaker: Jacopo
en: Libertà! Libertà! Libertà! Popolo e libertà! (Liberty! Liberty! Liberty! People and liberty!)

speaker: Medici supporters
en: Libertà! (Liberty!)

speaker: Jacopo
en: Francesco...?

speaker: Caterina
en: Ezio, what are you doing here?

speaker: Ezio
en: Paying a visit to the tailor.

speaker: Caterina
en: Rescuing me will provoke Cesare's wrath.

speaker: Ezio
en: Fortunately for us, he is away. Any chance there is a second key?

speaker: Caterina
en: The guard handed his to Lucrezia, so I assume not.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do you know where she is?

speaker: Caterina
en: Her quarters are at the top of the Castello.

speaker: Ezio
en: All right, stay here. That key is as good as mine.

speaker: Caterina
en: I am not going anywhere.

speaker: Pietro
en: I love you so, I want to sing it to the heavens.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Please! You must whisper it only to yourself. If Cesare found out, who knows what he would do.

speaker: Pietro
en: Are you not newly widowed?

speaker: Lucrezia
en: He killed my husband.

speaker: Pietro
en: Oh.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Cesare has always been jealous of my attentions, but that should not deter us.

speaker: Pietro
en: No?

speaker: Lucrezia
en: I will keep our secret.

speaker: Pietro
en: Lucrezia. Your lips call to me.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: What was that?

speaker: Pietro
en: I am late for rehearsal. Farewell, my love.

speaker: Guard
en: I heard the entire exchange, mia Signora (My Lady), and can vouch for it.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Good. Tell Cesare. We shall see how it feels when the shoe is on the other foot.

speaker: Guard
en: Yes, Signora (My Lady).

speaker: Ezio
en: Please. Continue. I did not mean to interrupt.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Ezio Auditore da Firenze? How nice to finally meet after hearing so much. A pity Cesare is no longer here. He would have enjoyed this.

speaker: Ezio
en: My fight is not with you, Lucrezia. Free Caterina and I will stand down.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Impossible.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then you leave me no choice.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Guards!

speaker: Ezio
en: I cannot leave you out here to cause trouble, so you're coming with me. Scream, however, and I will be forced to take your tongue.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Rescuing princesses from castles now? I bet you think you're doing great things, charging around killing whomever you wish. Do you know what became of the Pazzi once your hunt was finished? Your dear friend Lorenzo stripped them of everything and threw them into prison. Even those who played no part in the conspiracy. The women were forbidden to marry and the family tombstones were erased. Wiped from the history books. Poof. Just like that. You ignored the consequences of your actions, content to set events into motion but unwilling to see them through. Cesare will finish what he started and bring peace to Italia. He kills for a higher purpose, unlike you!

speaker: Ezio
en: The ignorant make easy targets.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Whatever. My words are wasted here, ipocrita (hypocrite).

speaker: Christoffa
en: What is the meaning of this delay? The Spaniard promised me an hour of his time.

speaker: Guard
en: Apologies, Master Christoffa, but the Spaniard's plans have changed. All he requires is proof of your death.

speaker: Christoffa
en: Ah! Fortune favors me. Unless you mean me harm as well.

speaker: Ezio
en: A friend of yours sent me to guard you.

speaker: Christoffa
en: Luis Santángel... he cautioned me against this meeting, but I wouldn't listen.

speaker: Ezio
en: How did you find the Spaniard? He isn't one to make many public appearances.

speaker: Christoffa
en: It was he who found me actually. He caught wind of my planned expedition West, and expressed a desire to fund it. This meeting was to be out first of many. But as you can see, it went rather askew.

speaker: Soldiers
en: There he is! Get him!

speaker: Ezio
en: Run! I will draw them away.

speaker: Isabella
en: Santángel, who is our guest?

speaker: Ezio
en: I am Ezio Auditore, a Florentine by birth, and a wayfarer by trade.

speaker: Luis
en: He is a friend, Queen Isabella. It was Ezio who brokered King Muhammad's surrender.

speaker: Isabella
en: Ezio Auditore... it seems the whole of España (Spain) owes you a great debt.

speaker: Ezio
en: I wonder if Christoffa Corombo might profit a little from my royal largess.

speaker: Isabella
en: I wish I could vivify his withering dream, but our funds are still scarce. Take comfort knowing that the King of France has made him a recent offer.

speaker: Luis
en: He cannot be serious!

speaker: Isabella
en: Well he certainly thought it was genuine. He left for Paris this morning.

speaker: Luis
en: Oh, that fool! Ezio... he is still in great danger.

speaker: Ezio
en: I will find him.

speaker: Luis
en: Bring him back here. And tell him... tell him the Queen has had a change of heart.

speaker: Ezio
en: Christoffa, halt! You're in great danger.

speaker: Christoffa
en: Do not interfere, Ezio! I've had quite enough counseling from your quarter!

speaker: Christoffa
en: Help!

speaker: Christoffa
en: Has the world gone so mad that a simple adventurer cannot go but a few weeks without being attacked in the street!

speaker: Ezio
en: Christoffa, you are no simple adventurer.

speaker: Christoffa
en: Unfortunately only you and the King of France recognize this.

speaker: Ezio
en: King Charles hasn't the mettle to back you... this is a Templar trick.

speaker: Christoffa
en: Have you any proof of your outrageous claim?

speaker: Ezio
en: I don't need any. Santángel has assured me that Isabella has had a change of heart.

speaker: Christoffa
en: Good God, how I loathe these games! Lead the way, Ezio...

speaker: Isabella
en: A fascinating proposal, Luis. And one I would gladly accept were Christoffa to return.

speaker: Christoffa
en: And return he has! What's the good news?

speaker: Luis
en: Inspiring words and a few bags of coin have changed the Queen's mind. Prepare to set sail, Christoffa.

speaker: Ezio
en: How many bags of coin did it require?

speaker: Isabella
en: Your friends have agreed to cover half of the total costs, Christoffa.

speaker: Christoffa
en: Praise you Luis, you fine and gracious man.

speaker: Sánchez
en: Soon we will be praising you, my friend. For all the wonders you will find and report to the world.

speaker: Luis
en: But let all rejoicing wait until we have seen your crosstrees dip below the horizon.

speaker: Christoffa
en: Yes, Santángel. Caution! Yours has saved me from myself more times than I should admit. Come gentlemen. Let us celebrate!

speaker: Ezio
en: The atlas... no mistaking that for anything else.

speaker: Captain
en: I found him!

speaker: Guard
en: I must apologize, Boabdil, for putting your beautiful city through such hardship.

speaker: Muhammad XII
en: I am King Muhammad of Nasrid, usurper. Untie me!

speaker: Guard
en: I will regret the destruction of Alhambra palace. Unfortunately, the Spanish siege must continue until Granada is dust, and the Queen is penniless.

speaker: Muhammad XII
en: My dislike of Isabella pales in comparison to the hatred I feel for you and your Templar stooges.

speaker: Guard
en: Hold on to that anger. It may comfort you in your final hours.

speaker: Muhammad XII
en: Peace be upon you, sir. For whom do you work?

speaker: Ezio
en: Luis Santángel sent me to find you. He assumed you were dead, or had gone mad.

speaker: Muhammad XII
en: I am happy to admit to neither. The Assassins and I haven't always seen eye to eye, but I have been grateful for their aid over the years.

speaker: Ezio
en: We need to end this war. As much as it may pain you, your time in España (Spain) is at its end.

speaker: Muhammad XII
en: Too many missteps and misunderstandings to repair... yes, I agree. What shall we do?

speaker: Ezio
en: I will cross the city and open the gates, carrying word of your abdication. Stay here until the city has fallen silent.

speaker: Sánchez
en: Seek out the Inquisitor's Calificador, Pedro Llorente. His tribunal meets in a building on the far side of town.

speaker: Ezio
en: You're not coming?

speaker: Sánchez
en: Oh, no. I'm too well known here. If a tragedy should befall Pedro, I'll need an alibi.

speaker: Pedro
en: Tomás Torquemada! An unexpected but welcome visit.

speaker: Tomás
en: I require neither your blessing nor your permission to enter here, Pedro. How is our prisoner?

speaker: Pedro
en: A staunch one. He refuses to convert or confess.

speaker: Tomás
en: Most who are brought here feel they have God's protection, no matter what their faith... and yet they always tremble with fright. But you... You dismiss the idea of God altogether, and yet you show no fear. Remarkable... Rodrigo Borgia was right to have me arrest you and your cohorts... your lack of faith is a disease. Let the heretic bleed.

speaker: Ezio
en: Already dead... so it was The Spaniard himself who had these men arrested and branded heretics. I won't allow the remaining five to share this man's fate.

speaker: Ezio
en: Antonio gave me the names of two contacts. One of them should be able to provide me with information.

speaker: Contact 1
en: Find the tallest building in town. There's a secret door on the roof.

speaker: Contact 2
en: Yes there's a thieves' guild nearby. Somewhere in the center of town.

speaker: Ezio
en: Empty, as I feared. Now my only recourse is with the Inquisitors themselves.

speaker: Guard
en: Halt! These premises are the property of the church!

speaker: Man
en: Get down! He is still out there!

speaker: Ezio
en: Who?

speaker: Man
en: One of Borgia's dogs! We tried to build a resistenza (resistance). He came to our house and began firing his arquebuse! My poor little Anna, she's... I've got to get back!

speaker: Ezio
en: Just one shooter? He will be easy to overtake. He cannot be very accurate

speaker: Ezio
en: Merda! (Shit!)

speaker: Man
en: He will kill us if we stay here! Listen. I will run to the next pillar to draw his fire. Try to flank him!

speaker: Ezio
en: Adesso basta! (Enough of this!)

speaker: Gaspar
en: I don't scare easily! Merde, merde, merde!

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in pace.

speaker: Annetta
en: Ser Ezio, thank God! I've been looking everywhere for you.

speaker: Ezio
en: I... I couldn't stop them Annetta. I tried, I swear! But there were so many guards...

speaker: Annetta
en: Please. Come with me. We need to get you off the streets.

speaker: Ezio
en: What of my mother and sister?

speaker: Annetta
en: They're safe. I'll bring you to them.

speaker: Ezio
en: No! It's too dangerous for us to travel together. Tell me where to go and I'll meet you there.

speaker: Annetta
en: My sister's house, just north of the Duomo.

speaker: Ezio
en: I'm on my way.

speaker: Ezio
en: I think we have the wrong building...

speaker: Annetta
en: No, no. This is it.

speaker: Paola
en: It is a pleasure to make your acquaintance, Messer Ezio... Annetta speaks quite highly of you. I can see why.

speaker: Ezio
en: I appreciate the kind words Madonna...?

speaker: Paola
en: Ti prego (Please), call me Paola.

speaker: Ezio
en: Thank you for offering your home to my family, Paola.

speaker: Paola
en: It was the least I could do. You must be tired. Perhaps you'd li

speaker: Ezio
en: No, grazie. (No thank you.) I can't stay.

speaker: Paola
en: Why? Where are you going?

speaker: Ezio
en: To kill Uberto Alberti.

speaker: Paola
en: I understand your desire for vengeance, but the is a powerful man. You're not a killer, Ezio

speaker: Ezio
en: Spare me the lecture.

speaker: Paola
en: But I can make you one.

speaker: Ezio
en: And why are you going to teach me how to kill?

speaker: Paola
en: I'm not. I'm going to teach you how to survive. Come.

speaker: Paola
en: Discretion is a paramount in my profession. We must walk the streets freely: seen, but unseen. You too must learn to blend like us and become one with the city's crowds. My girls will show you how...

speaker: Paola
en: Come a little bit closer, Ezio...

speaker: Courtesan
en: We'll take good care of you...

speaker: Paola
en: Bene! (Good!) Now that you've learned to blend. I'll show you how you can use it for more than just moving around. Let's teach you how to steal.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Thief! Thief!

speaker: Paola
en: Once you've stolen from someone Ezio, You mustn't linger.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Help! Somebody stop him!

speaker: Paola
en: Pay attention! You must leave once you've picked their pocket.

speaker: Flee Market
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: ...If Piero had only a tenth of his father's talent, we'd still have someplace to call home...

speaker: Civilian 2
en: ...Never should have welcomed that mad monk into the city. Look at all the misery he's wrought...

speaker: Civilian 3
en: ...Don't understand why they'd be so willing to accept his oppression...

speaker: Monk
en: ...Just threw us out! Said all we owned belonged to the (Church of San Marco) now...

speaker: Civilian 4
en: ...Even Botticelli sides with that monster. It's sorcery! How else to explain it...

speaker: Civilian 5
en: ...Book burnings, arrests, incessant sermonizing. Firenze was meant to stand as a beacon against such ignorance, and yet here we are, mired in it once more...

speaker: Civilian 6
en: Sometimes I wish the Assassino (Assassin) would return to Firenze, that we might be free of this tyranny.

speaker: Civilian 7
en: It's just a myth! A story parents tell their children.

speaker: Civilian 6
en: No, my father saw him years ago- San Gimignano.

speaker: Civilian 7
en: Sure. Sure. Se lo dici tu (If you say so.)

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Salve (Hello) Ezio. You picked a fine time for a homecoming.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then it's true? Savonarola has taken control over Firenze?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Yes. No doubt aided by that treacherous artifact.

speaker: Ezio
en: We should get to work on retrieving it.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: That may be more complicated than you think.

speaker: Ezio
en: Hah! When isn't it? Why don't you fill me in on things?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Walk with me.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: It all started a few weeks ago. The man everyone once reviled was suddenly the one they worshiped.

speaker: Ezio
en: Ah, the Apple?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Only in part. It's not the city he's enthralled, but its leaders: men possessed of influence and power. They, in turn, oppress the citizens and ensure his will is done.

speaker: Ezio
en: The people act as if they have no say in the matter.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Rare is the man who is willing to oppose the status quo. And so it falls to us to help them see the truth.

speaker: Ezio
en: These bodies bear the emblem of the Borgia...

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Yes. The Spaniard keeps sending his soldiers into Firenze, and Firenze keeps sending them back – usually in pieces.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then he knows the Apple is here as well... An unfortunate complication.

speaker: Ezio
en: A direct assault would be dangerous. Especially with the Apple in his possession.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: True. But what other option is there?

speaker: Ezio
en: Aside from the city's leaders, the people's minds are their own, correct?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Sì.

speaker: Ezio
en: And they follow Savonarola not by choice, but force and fear?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Sì.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then I propose we use this to our advantage. If we can silence his lieutenants and stir up discontent, he will be distracted and I will have a chance to strike.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Clever. I'll speak with La Volpe and Paola. They can help to organize the uprising as you free districts.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then it's settled. I'll take care of his abettors.

speaker: Thief
en: I can outrun anyone in this distretto. I hear you're the best. Prove it!

speaker: Ezio
en: Give me the plans.

speaker: Engineer
en: No. I will not.

speaker: Engineer
en: Stop! Stop!

speaker: Ezio
en: Where are the plans?

speaker: Engineer
en: Past the guards. In my house. It is the last one.

speaker: Ezio
en: And the machine?

speaker: Engineer
en: In the tower on top of the fortress.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie. (Thank you.)

speaker: Guard
en: The first designs were defective. Everyone who piloted one died, several even exploded. But we know this one works.

speaker: Ezio
en: They intend to craft more weapons. Leonardo, you will help me stop them.

speaker: Borgia Captain
en: Cesare must know of this!

speaker: Ezio
en: Addio, amico mio! (Goodbye, my friend!)

speaker: Egidio
en: I cannot believe you would just do this.

speaker: Ezio
en: There is a condition.

speaker: Egidio
en: I knew it.

speaker: Ezio
en: Keep an eye on the politics of the city. I want you to report back to Maria at the Rosa in Fiore (Blooming Rose) about targets who are helping the Borgia.

speaker: Egidio
en: And what, you'll...make them disappear? The pezzo di merda (piece of shit) may hate me, but he's still family. Va bene (okay), we go.

speaker: Ezio
en: I will follow you to the Banker.

speaker: Guard
en: Egidio. It seems you are ready to die like a gentleman.

speaker: Egidio
en: I have the money.

speaker: Guard
en: Oh. That's different then. The Banker will be pleased. You came alone?

speaker: Egidio
en: Do you see anyone else here?

speaker: Guard
en: Follow me, furbacchione (wise-ass).

speaker: Egidio
en: Have you heard anything about my brother, Francesco?

speaker: Guard
en: Cesare is dealing with him.

speaker: Egidio
en: I hope he's all right. So what are you going to do with my money?

speaker: Guard
en: The Banker likes to treat his friends well.

speaker: Egidio
en: How generous he is.

speaker: Guard
en: What did you say?

speaker: Egidio
en: Nothing.

speaker: Guard
en: Egidio brought the money.

speaker: Luigi Torcelli
en: Well, well. The Banker has a special evening planned. I will be delivering your payment. Give it here.

speaker: Luigi
en: Hold him until I get back!

speaker: Ezio
en: I better not lose sight of the money.

speaker: Egidio
en: Why not release me? I have paid.

speaker: Guard
en: He is counting the money. Until it is counted you cannot leave.

speaker: Egidio
en: What is taking him so long? Oh.

speaker: Guard
en: He has to count the money from all the Banker's clients.

speaker: Egidio
en: Did he not do that already?

speaker: Guard
en: He must not have written it down.

speaker: Luigi
en: Now to go kill that Senator.

speaker: Thief
en: You! Please, would you grace an admirer with a performance? You have been an inspiration for many of us.

speaker: Guard 1
en: What did you find? Another key?

speaker: Guard 2
en: A door of some kind. Bricked up with hard stone.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Ah, promising! The first key was found behind a similar door.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Ti mou les? (Is that so?) And how did they open that door?

speaker: Guard 1
en: They didn't. The earthquake did.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Ypérocha. (Wonderful.) All we have are a few barrels of gunpowder.

speaker: Guard 1
en: This should do. And if it does not, we get more.

speaker: Ezio
en: Diavolo! (Damn!)

speaker: Guard 1
en: The Assassin! Go! Go!

speaker: Guard
en: You will not leave here alive! Show yourself! He's there! Dilé! (Coward!) Edó íne! (He is here!) Ton petichame! (We got him!) No, no. He is here somewhere. Assassin! He's behind us. Rixte tou! (Shoot him!) Steady! Assassin! Show yourself! Skotóste ton bástardo! (Kill that bastard!) Show yourself! We have gunpowder, we should use it! Stand back! Give me some room! Never underestimate this madman. Na pári! (Dammit!)

speaker: Lorenzo
en: When I was six years old I fell into the Arno. I soon found myself drifting down, and into darkness, certain my life was at an end. Instead I woke to the sound of my mother weeping, at her side stood a stranger, soaking and smiling at me. My mother explained that he had saved me. And so began a long and prosperous relationship between two families; yours and mine. I am sorry I could not save your father and brothers.

speaker: Ezio
en: You have nothing to apologize for. I believe Jacopo de' Pazzi played a part in their deaths. The attack on you as well. I need to find him.

speaker: Lorenzo
en: That coward fled before we could arrest him!

speaker: Ezio
en: Have you any leads?

speaker: Lorenzo
en: No. They've hidden themselves well.

speaker: Ezio
en: They?

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Jacopo was not the only conspirator to escape.

speaker: Ezio
en: If they work with Jacopo, they were surely involved in the plot against my family as well. Give me their names.

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Antonio Maffei, Archbishop Francesco Salviati, Stefano da Bagnone, and Bernardo Baroncelli.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene. (Good) I will go and see my uncle. He has men stationed in the countryside.

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Wait...before you go...

speaker: Ezio
en: A Codex page!

speaker: Lorenzo
en: I took it from the files of Francesco de' Pazzi, seeing as he clearly no longer needs it. I've always had an interest of things of antiquity. As did your father.

speaker: Ezio
en: It is meaningful to me as well.

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Then consider it a gift! Che il Signore ci protegga. (God save us all)

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Duccio
en: Mia cara! (My darling!) The strings of fate have drawn us together. Two italiani (Italians), lost and alone in the Orient. Do you not feel the magnetismo (magnetism)?

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Sofia
en: I feel many things, messere. (sir.) Nausea above all.

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Ezio
en: Is this man bothering you, Sofia?

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Duccio
en: Excuse me, messere (sir), but the lady and I are–

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Duccio
en: Ah! Il diavolo in persona! (The Devil himself!) Stay back!

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Ezio
en: Duccio. A pleasure.

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Duccio
en: Run buona donna (dear lady!) Run for your life!

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Sofia
en: Who was that?

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Ezio
en: Un cane. (A dog.) He was engaged to my sister many years ago.

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Sofia
en: And what happened?

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Ezio
en: His cazzo (dick) was engaged to six others. Chiedo venia. (Excuse me.) So what brings you to these docks?

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Sofia
en: I took a break from my work to retrieve a package, but here they claim the captain's papers are not in order. So, I wait. Che seccatura. (Such a bother.) I could be here all day.

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Ezio
en: Let me see what I can do. I know a few ways to bend the rules.

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Sofia
en: Do you now?

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Ezio
en: Sì. (Yes.) I will meet you back at your shop.

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Ezio
en: Sofia Sartor. Perfetto. (Perfect.)

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Sofia
en: Salute, Ezio. Any luck?

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Ezio
en: Madamigella (Miss) Sofia Sartor, libraia, (book monger,) Costantinopoli.

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Sofia
en: Oh no! Look at the damage. Did they use this to fight off pirates? Well, so far, so good.

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Sofia
en: Ah! Beautiful, no? This is a print of map by Martin Waldseemüller. See here? The new lands described by messer (mister) Amerigo Vespucci.

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Ezio
en: Poor Cristoforo Colombo. History has a strange way of unfolding.

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Sofia
en: What do you make of this body of water here?

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Ezio
en: A new ocean, perhaps? Most of the scholars I know claim the size of the globe has been underestimated.

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Sofia
en: Incredibile. (Incredible.) The more we learn about the world, the less we seem to know.

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Sofia
en: Well, you honored your promise, here is mine fulfilled. If we are correct, this should show you the location of the first book. I must admit, my head is swimming with the prospect of seeing these books. This is knowledge the world lost, and must have again. Perhaps I could print a few copies to distribute myself. A small run of fifty or so, that should be enough...

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Sofia
en: Perché ridi? (Why are you laughing?)

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Ezio
en: Forgive me. It is a joy to see someone with a passion so personal and noble. It is... inspiring.

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Sofia
en: Goodness. Where's this coming from?

scene: The Fourth Part of the World
speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie (Thank you), Sofia. I will return.

speaker: Ezio
en: What!? My pouch-- my money!

speaker: Corradin
en: Oh... your money... I don't have your money!

speaker: Ezio
en: Get back here!

speaker: Corradin
en: Make me.

speaker: Ezio
en: You're making a big mistake, my friend! Enough of this!

speaker: Corradin
en: Enough indeed! Why don't you give up?

speaker: Ezio
en: Return what you've stolen!

speaker: Corradin
en: Would if I could, but I can't.

speaker: Ezio
en: I swear, I'll run you through when I catch you!

speaker: Corradin
en: Ohoho! Now where's the fun in that?

speaker: Ezio
en: I really have no interest in hurting you. So give me back my money and we'll call it even.

speaker: Volpe
en: Not so fast.

speaker: Ezio
en: What do you want? Who are you?

speaker: Volpe
en: They call me many things: Murderer. Tagliagole (Cutthroat). Thief. But you may call me La Volpe. At your service, Messer Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: How do you know my name?

speaker: Volpe
en: It is my business to know everything in this city. Isn't that why you're here?

speaker: Ezio
en: Indeed. I need to find someone; to know where he'll be before even he does.

speaker: Volpe
en: Who?

speaker: Ezio
en: Francesco de' Pazzi.

speaker: Volpe
en: There's word on the street of a caravan just arrived from Roma. A secret meeting, to be held at sunset tonight. You can learn something of Francesco's whereabouts there.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do you know where it is to be held?

speaker: Volpe
en: Ma certo. (Yes.) Let me know when you're ready and we'll go. Oh, yes. Here's your money.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: So, you have a plan?

speaker: Ezio
en: Once inside, your men can overpower the camp's patrols, correct?

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Yes, but...

speaker: Ezio
en: Especially if the patrols are taken completely by surprise?

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Ma certo. (Of course.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Then we need to liberate several suits of French armor. At dawn, we are going to walk right in.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Hah! Ezio Auditore you are truly a man after my own heart. Magnifico! (Magnificent!)

speaker: Ezio
en: I will get the armor.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: My troops will gather it from the dead. We will then depart from the north, so as not to arouse suspicion. And Ezio. Make sure to kill them without a fight. The armor has to stay clean.

speaker: Maria
en: Buon giorno (Hello), Ezio!

speaker: Ezio
en: Buon giorno a voi, madre. Come state? (Hello mother. How are you?)

speaker: Maria
en: Sto bene! (I'm good!) And you? Still recovering from last night?

speaker: Ezio
en: I have no idea what you're talking about.

speaker: Maria
en: Of course not. Anyway, I have an errand to run. I'd like you to join me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Con piacere. (With pleasure.)

speaker: Maria
en: Come. It's not far from here.

speaker: Maria
en: I know about your fight with Vieri...

speaker: Ezio
en: What fight?

speaker: Maria
en: Per piacere, (Please,) let's not play this game.

speaker: Ezio
en: He spoke ill of us. I could not allow him to continue.

speaker: Maria
en: I'm sure he's having a hard time dealing with the accusations against his father. Francesco de' Pazzi is many things – and none of them good. But even I never suspected he'd be capable of murder.

speaker: Ezio
en: What will happen to him?

speaker: Maria
en: I imagine there will be a trial.

speaker: Ezio
en: Will father speak at it?

speaker: Maria
en: He'll have to. He's the one with the evidence.

speaker: Ezio
en: Still, I wish there was another way.

speaker: Maria
en: You've nothing to fear. Everyone wants justice done. It is an unfortunate state of affairs, but it will pass.

speaker: Maria
en: Here we are.

speaker: Maria
en: Hello Leonardo.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Madonna Maria!

speaker: Maria
en: This is my son, Ezio.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Molto onorato. (It's a pleasure to meet you.)

speaker: Ezio
en: L'onore è mio. (The honor is mine.)

speaker: Leonardo
en: Let me go and fetch the paintings. I'll be right back.

speaker: Maria
en: He's very talented.

speaker: Ezio
en: Immagino. (I guess.)

speaker: Maria
en: Self expression is vital to understanding and enjoying life. You should find an outlet.

speaker: Ezio
en: I have plenty of outlets.

speaker: Maria
en: I meant besides vaginas.

speaker: Ezio
en: Mother!

speaker: Leonardo
en: Back to your house, then?

speaker: Maria
en: Sì. Sì. (Yes. Yes.) Ezio, help Leonardo, will you?

speaker: Leonardo
en: So, Ezio, what do you do?

speaker: Maria
en: He's been working for his father.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Ah! You're to be a banker?

speaker: Ezio
en: For now. And you? Art, was it?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Truth be told, it's been difficult for me to settle. Painting is nice, but I often feel like my work lacks... I don't know... purpose. Does that make sense? I'd rather contribute more practically. More directly, Architecture, perhaps. Or anatomy. I'm not content to merely to capture the world. I want to change it.

speaker: Maria
en: Oh, Leonardo! I have no doubt you'll go on to do great things!

speaker: Leonardo
en: Vi ringrazio, Madonna. (I thank you.) That's kind of you.

speaker: Maria
en: Thank you for the help, son. Don't let me keep you from your other duties.

speaker: Leonardo
en: It was nice to meet you, Ezio. I hope our paths cross again.

speaker: Ezio
en: Anch'io. (Me too.)

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Who goes there?

speaker: Ezio
en: Salve (Hello) to you too.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Ezio! I was expecting my wife.

speaker: Ezio
en: Somehow, that does not surprise me.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: The French puttane (whores) have us under pressure.

speaker: Ezio
en: Tell me about their general, this Baron de Valois.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Cesare persuaded King Louis to lend him an entire army to defeat me. I'm flattered.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where can I find him?

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: It's only a matter of time before I have Valois by the throat. We have them in retreat.

speaker: Ezio
en: They seem to be getting closer.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: The situation is under control–

speaker: Mercenary
en: Close the gates!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Bene. (Good.) So maybe I could use a little help.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Ezio, shut the gates!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: They're coming from the other side! Defend the other entrance!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: The other entrance! The gates!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Secure the Barracks!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: They come again. Bianca thirsts for French blood. We are surrounded!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Ezio, shut the gates!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: They're coming from the other side! Defend the other entrance!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: The other entrance!

speaker: Mercenary
en: The Baron de Valois signals from the field!

speaker: Octavian
en: Bonjour, général d'Alviano. Êtes-vous prêt à vous rendre? (Are you ready to surrender?)

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Why don't you come closer and say that?

speaker: Octavian
en: You must learn how to speak French. It would mask your barbaric sensibilities.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Perhaps you could teach me, and I would instruct you in fighting, since you seem to do so little of it!

speaker: Octavian
en: As amusing as this parley has been, I'd like your unconditional surrender before sunrise.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Hah! My lady Bianca will whisper it in your ear.

speaker: Octavian
en: I believe another lady might object to that.

speaker: Pantasilea
en: Mio marito vi ammazzerà tutti! (My husband is going to murder all of you!)

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: I'll kill you, fottuto francese! (you French fuck!)

speaker: Octavian
en: Calm down, for your wife's sake. You know my terms: Enter my camp unarmed at dawn.

speaker: Octavian
en: And practice your French. Soon all of Italie will be speaking it.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: I will get you pezzo di merda figlio di puttana! (you piece of shit son of a bitch!)

speaker: Ezio
en: This is their camp?!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: You steal a man's wife and then go hide inside a fortress?

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Nothing hangs between your thighs. In fact, there is a hole there so deep it reaches into the maledetto inferno! (fucking underworld!)

speaker: Ezio
en: What good are you to her dead? We will regroup and fight through the gates as we did at the Arsenale.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: The entrance is thicker with Frenchmen than the streets of Paris.

speaker: Ezio
en: So we will climb the battlements.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: They cannot be scaled. Pantasilea would know what to do. Maybe this is the end. I enter at dawn bearing gifts and hope that coward spares her life.

speaker: Ezio
en: Perché non ci ho pensato prima? (Why didn't I think of it before?)

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: What did I say?

speaker: Ezio
en: Call your men back to the barracks. I will explain there.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: You better have something good.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Fall back!

speaker: Courtesan
en: Ezio! News of our work has reached the Pope. As we speak, he prepares a courier to Romagna. If Cesare suspects his allegiances are slipping, he will fill the city with troops. Take the Pope's letter from the courier without his knowledge. Bring it to me and I will prepare a forgery. We will make sure Cesare receives his report.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Bene (Good). I can work with this. Give me a moment.

speaker: Ezio
en: My name is Ezio Auditore da Firenze... It has been fifteen years since the Spaniard, Rodrigo Borgia, murdered my family and drove me into exile... Since that time I have suffered greatly but learned a great deal more... I am an Assassin... as my father and grandfathers were before me. Compelled by duty to my order, I have set aside my search for the Spaniard to recover an ancient artifact recently stolen from us. My thirst for vengeance is strong... but my responsibility to the Assassins is stronger still.

speaker: Contact
en: Antonio's been asking for you, Ezio... You should talk to him.

speaker: Antonio
en: Ezio! I have been singing your praises to this gentleman. He has a proposition for you.

speaker: Luis
en: I represent a man who has come to Venezia on a foolish errand. I fear his life is in danger, but he refuses to listen to my counsel.

speaker: Ezio
en: And you want me to protect him?

speaker: Luis
en: It would ease my mind. Antonio claims you are the deadliest man in Italia.

speaker: Ezio
en: That's true, But I am not a hired blade.

speaker: Antonio
en: Ezio, let the man round out his request...

speaker: Luis
en: The gentleman I represent has organized a meeting with someone called The Spaniard...

speaker: Antonio
en: You see, Ezio... the Spaniard has come to us!

speaker: Ezio
en: All right, I will protect your friend, but not his business.

speaker: Luis
en: If that is what it takes to keep Christoffa from harm, so be it.

speaker: Checco
en: Caterina! Caterina Sforza! I know you're in there. I have something you may want back. Are you missing any children?

speaker: Checco
en: And Ezio Auditore...! What a pleasant surprise.

speaker: Ezio
en: I take it you would be the Orsi brothers.

speaker: Ludovico
en: Ludovico

speaker: Checco
en: And Checco.

speaker: Orsi brothers
en: At your service.

speaker: Caterina
en: Basta! (Enough!) Where are my children? Let them go!

speaker: Ludovico
en: Of course Signora. We'll happily give them back—for something of yours. A certain map?

speaker: Checco
en: And a certain Apple, brother.

speaker: Ludovico
en: Sì (Yes), a certain Apple indeed. Or shall I slice your babies' necks ear to ear?

speaker: Caterina
en: Bastardi! (Bastards!) You think you can threaten me? I'll give you NOTHING! You want my children? Take them! I have the instrument to make more!

speaker: Checco
en: When you change your mind, they'll be in the village outside the city—You have one hour.

speaker: Ezio
en: Caterina, no... I can't ask you to sacrifice your children.

speaker: Caterina
en: Nobody's sacrificing anything. Go get them back for me Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì, you have my word. The Apple needs to remain in the citadel. Keep this safe.

speaker: Bianca
en: Is this all the men you have to hold me? Stolti. (Fools.) It won't be enough. My mamma is fierce. We Sforza women are no wilting flowers. We may look pretty to the eye, but the eyes deceive. Just ask babbo (father.) I hope you don't really imagine I'm scared of you. You'd be very mistaken. My mamma would never let you hurt me. And if you touch one hair on my little brother's head, she will hunt you down and eat you for breakfast. Capito? This is absurd, you know? You'll never survive this. I'll be home in an hour. So you're basically just wasting your time and mine. I'm getting bored. Don't you have anything to do, while I wait for you to die?

speaker: Bianca
en: Grazie! Grazie Messere! But my brother–! They are holding Ottaviano at the lighthouse.

speaker: Ludovico
en: You want to see your boy walk again, Caterina? Give us what we want or I'll throw him off the edge!

speaker: Ottaviano
en: Mamma! Help me! I don't want to be here anymore.

speaker: Ludovico
en: Zitto, marmocchio. (Shut up, kid.) Let's go Caterina! Show yourself! The Apple and the map or your kid's a cripple.

speaker: Ottaviano
en: I have to pee. Please Messere. I need to go to the bathroom. Just let me go pee.

speaker: Ludovico
en: Oh, per Dio, chiudi il bocca. (For God's sake kid, shut the hell up.)

speaker: Ludovico
en: Stop acting like a baby. Where are your balls?

speaker: Ottaviano
en: I'm hungry. Can I have something to eat. Please, Messere, I'm hungry.

speaker: Ludovico
en: Basta, basta. (Enough, enough.) You're giving me a headache. This is your last chance, Caterina! The Apple, now! Or I break the boy's legs!

speaker: Ludovico
en: Caterina was a fool to send you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Or are you the fool, dying for a handful of change? Was it worth it?

speaker: Ludovico
en: More than you know... the Maestro gains his prize, because of me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Muori col tuo orgoglio, per quanto vale... (Die with your pride, for all it's worth...) Requiescat in pace. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Ottaviano
en: Grazie Signore!

speaker: Graduation
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Caterina
en: Hurry, Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: Ride across the bridge. I will cover you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Go to Isola Tiberina (Tiber Island). Find Machiavelli there. He will be waiting for me.

speaker: Caterina
en: What about you?

speaker: Ezio
en: Someone has to stay here and distract the guards.

speaker: Caterina
en: Get back in one piece, or I will never forgive myself.

speaker: Ezio
en: Go!

speaker: Ezio
en: What was that?

speaker: Guard
en: Quick! Back to the Castello!

speaker: Ezio
en: Buon giorno. (Good day). How have you taken to your new post?

speaker: Apprentice
en: I do my best, Ezio, but it is no easy task to oversee a district in constant peril.

speaker: Ezio
en: Peril? What has happened?

speaker: Apprentice
en: Despite our presence, the influence of Templar money is strong. Most of the merchants here are still taking bribes.

speaker: Ezio
en: Damnazione. (Damn.) We should talk to the people, and get a feeling for their mood. Vieni. (Come.)

speaker: Apprentice
en: Most of the merchants who have sold their allegiance are Greek, and I am not ashamed to say that I understand why.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then you are a better citizen than most, efendim (my friend). We cannot expect men to find any comfort in having been conquered. But just as they have a right to demand dignity from the Ottomans, the Byzantines have an obligation to keep the innocents safe from harm. This requires a careful balancing act, and we should not be surprised if we stumble from time to time.

speaker: Odai
en: May the Father of Understanding guide and keep you.

speaker: Ezio
en: This is an impressive take for a single day.

speaker: Merchant
en: What business is it of yours how quickly I make my money? I take care of my neighbours, and they take care of me.

speaker: Ezio
en: How did you come across this incredible sum of money?

speaker: Merchant 2
en: Where did you learn your manners, Italyani (Italian)? In the court of the Borgia? Clear away from my shop!

speaker: Merchant 3
en: Bless you, brother! May God shine his radiance upon you.

speaker: Ezio
en: A large sum for him as well.

speaker: Ezio
en: Salute, amico (To your health, friend.) Forgive me for asking, but the insignia on this chest... what does it mean?

speaker: Merchant
en: That? It is the seal of Theodorus Komnenos.

speaker: Ezio
en: And he is your benefactor?

speaker: Merchant
en: Benefactor? Ohi! (No!) He is my friend, my countryman. And one of the wealthiest men in this district, despite our new masters.

speaker: Ezio
en: Of course. Grazie. (Thank you.)

speaker: Ezio
en: What do you think? Shall we pay Theodorus a visit?

speaker: Apprentice
en: I do not want to start a fight we cannot justify, Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: Nor do I, and if we can find a way to avoid bloodshed, we will. But if the Templars are behind this, that will give us few options.

speaker: Theodorus
en: What! Ten thousand Akçe is not enough? Did he actually say that? Is he mad? Does he think I piss money? Far be it for me to question how these Templars work, but I have been hemorrhaging money ever since I came into their company. Find me a quill, quickly! I believe I will write these men a sternly worded missive, packed with subtle barbs and tawdry insinuations. If that does not get their attention, I don't know what will.

speaker: Ezio
en: Theodorus. Buon giorno. (Good day.)

speaker: Theodorus
en: Ah! W-who are you?

speaker: Ezio
en: You have been quite free with your money lately, and the Assassins would like to know what your generosity purchased.

speaker: Theodorus
en: Assassins. You? Both of you?

speaker: Apprentice
en: Calm, efendi (sir). We mean no harm.

speaker: Theodorus
en: I don't want to die! Please! Spare my troubled soul! The Templars have corrupted me. I am a good man at heart.

speaker: Ezio
en: Keep watch over this one. When he has regained his sanity, we will talk.

speaker: Theodorus
en: Please, you must understand! I did not go to the Templars. They came to me! Threatening me with violence if I did not comply with their demands.

speaker: Ezio
en: Which are what, exactly?

speaker: Apprentice
en: He pays money to the merchants in Assassin districts to keep prices artificially high, hoping this will turn public opinions against us.

speaker: Ezio
en: So what do we do with you, Theodorus Komnenos? Are you any use to us at all?

speaker: Theodorus
en: I can take you to the Templar enforcer. He is an African named Dunqas. He is the man in charge of running this racket.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene. (Good.) Lead us there, and we will do all we can to keep you safe.

speaker: Ezio
en: The Templars' coffers are deep. We have always had a difficult time competing on that score.

speaker: Apprentice
en: When you champion the poor and powerless, you take on certain risks.

speaker: Ezio
en: Better to be poor than wrong, is that it?

speaker: Theodorus
en: A fine day, don't you think?

speaker: Guard
en: Bearable.

speaker: Theodorus
en: Are we late? I fear we are. I mean, it's no bother. We can meet tomorrow.

speaker: Guard
en: We are right on time.

speaker: Theodorus
en: Ah. Wonderful. Suddenly I... I don't feel very well. I may be coming down with a... a touch of something.

speaker: Guard
en: This will not take long. You give us the money, we give you access. The Guardian will explain all.

speaker: Theodorus
en: Ah yes, the African gentleman. Y-yes.

speaker: Odai
en: Theodorus Komnenos. You have been a friend to the Templars, and a generous partner. What would you say to a permanent appointment with our man in Alexandria? We could use man of your... means.

speaker: Theodorus
en: What would I say? Well I... ah... Assassins! They followed me! Look! They are here!

speaker: Ezio
en: Lazy fool!

speaker: Theodorus
en: Ah!

speaker: Odai
en: Our business here is done.

speaker: Ezio
en: You follow the Guardian. I can catch up.

speaker: Odai
en: So it comes to this, does it?

speaker: Odai
en: Wealth, power, ambition... such things I have seen in my short time on earth, and reveled in them. Such things are the wonders of man. You may believe you have ended my life, but the truth is, you have completed it. To perish in this age-old struggle is an honor befitting a king.

speaker: Guild Contracts
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Ezio
en: Now I can get back up here.

speaker: Ezio
en: That could help if I fall.

speaker: Ezio
en: Perfect! A route up if I fall.

speaker: Ezio
en: Claudia, my dearest sister. I have been in Acre a week now, safe and in high spirits, but prepared for the worst. The men and women who have fed and sheltered me here also give me warning that the road to Masyaf is overrun by mercenaries and bandits not native to this land. What this could mean, I dread to guess. When I first set out from Roma ten months ago, I did so with a single purpose: to discover what our father did not. In a letter written the year before my birth, he makes mention of a library hidden beneath the stones of Masyaf castle. A sanctum full of invaluable wisdom. So what will I find when I arrive there? Who will greet me? A host of eager Templars, as I fear most strongly? Or nothing but the whistling of a cold and lonely wind? Masyaf has not been home to the Assassins for almost three hundred years now. Can we still claim it for our own? Are we welcome there? Ah, I am weary of this fight, Claudia. Not because I am tired, but because our struggle seems to move in one direction only... towards chaos. Today I have more questions than answers. This is why I have come so far: To find clarity. To find the wisdom left behind by the great Altaïr, so that I may better understand the purpose of our fight. And my place in it. Should anything happen to me, Claudia... should my skills fail me, or my ambition lead me astray, do not seek retribution or revenge in my memory, but fight to continue the search for truth, so that all may benefit. My story is one of many thousands, and the world will not suffer if it ends too soon.

speaker: Guard 1
en: He's behind us! There! You see him?

speaker: Leandros
en: What are you doing? Faster!

speaker: Ezio
en: Damn! Just a scratch! Alright, I felt that! Argh, merda (shit)! This will not hold for long!

speaker: Leandros
en: Die you bastard! Hiya! Move! Faster! Run, you stupid brute! Take this! Move! Where are you, bastard!

speaker: Leandros
en: Closer! Get closer! Closer!

speaker: Leandros
en: Move!

speaker: Guard 2
en: Wait!

speaker: Leandros
en: Go to hell!

speaker: Leandros
en: You again!

speaker: Guard 3
en: I have him.

speaker: Leandros
en: Take this! Die, you bastard! Stop him! STOP HIM!

speaker: Teodora
en: I'm sorry, Ezio. We could not have known Silvio would cheat as he did.

speaker: Antonio
en: You should have.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Sister! You told us to let you know if we saw that rottinculo (cocksucker) who stole the Golden Mask? He's on his way to the Doge's party!

speaker: Ezio
en: I will go! I can catch him before he arrives and take back the mask.

speaker: Antonio
en: How? By killing the poor stronzo (fucker)?

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes. You know what's at stake.

speaker: Antonio
en: No! If you kill him, they'll cancel the party and Marco will retreat back into his palazzo. We'll have wasted our time again! Steal the mask instead... quietly.

speaker: Teodora
en: My girls can help. They're already on their way to the party, all along the route. They can help you distract him while you acquire the mask.

speaker: Ezio
en: Va bene (Alright). I can do that.

speaker: Guard
en: Buona sera, signore. (Good evening, sir.)

speaker: Teodora
