en: You made it! Marco is on a boat, just off shore. He's set to make a speech in a few minutes. Use my girls until then. Move with them to stay out of sight.

speaker: Dante
en: Find him.

speaker: Agostino
en: Honestly, my brother embarasses himself with this display.

speaker: Guest
en: You have no right to speak of him that way - He's the Doge.

speaker: Agostino
en: He is Doge in name only, and it's Venetian money he spends. There are larger things at stake and you know it.

speaker: Guest
en: Marco was the one chosen to lead. Your father may have thought he'd never amount to much, may have foisted his political ambitions on you - but it doesn't matter now, does it, given where things stand.

speaker: Agostino
en: I never wanted to be Doge

speaker: Guest
en: Then it seems you have succeeded wildly!

speaker: Agostino
en: Power is more than wealth. Does my brother truly believe he was chosen for any reason other than his riches?

speaker: Guest
en: He was chosen for his wisdom and leadership.

speaker: Agostino
en: And this is what he does with such wisdom? Offer a light show? He hides away in the Palazzo while the city comes apart at the seams, and then he thinks some expensive explosions will make people forget all their problems.

speaker: Guest
en: The people love spectacle. It's human nature. You'll see...

speaker: Announcer
en: Signore e Signori (Ladies and gentlemen)! I present you, the beloved Doge of Venezia!

speaker: Marco
en: Benvenuti (Welcome)! Welcome, my friends, to the grandest social event of the season! At peace or at war, in times of prosperity or paucity, Venezia will always have Carnevale!

speaker: Ezio
en: Merda (Shit), he's not leaving the boat. I will have to swim out there...

speaker: Teodora
en: I wouldn't try it. You'd be spotted right away.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then I'll fight my way out there–

speaker: Teodora
en: Wait!

speaker: Marco
en: Tonight we celebrate what makes us great! How bright our lights shine over the world!

speaker: Teodora
en: That's it! Your pistola (pistol); the one you stopped the murderer with. It's as loud as those explosions. Time it right and you'll walk out of here unnoticed.

speaker: Ezio
en: I like the way you think, Sister.

speaker: Teodora
en: I'll be waiting for you back at the brothel, my son.

speaker: Marco
en: We all know we have come through troubled times, but we have come through them together! And Venezia stands a stronger city for it. Transitions of power are difficult for all, but we have weathered the shift with grace and tranquility. It is no easy thing to lose a Doge in the prime of his life. And to the cruelty of an Assassin who still hides in our midst! Indeed, we all loved Mocenigo dearly. He was a friend to us all, and he shall be missed, but did any of us truly love his policies? Did we feel safer under his watchful gaze? Did we believe in the road he was guiding us down? Or were you beginning to be afraid, like I was? Afraid that Mocenigo could not see clearly; that he was not prepared for what was to come? Well, my friends, I'm here to tell you: I CAN see down that road! I KNOW where we're going! It's a beautiful place, and we're going there together! The future I see for Venezia is a future of strength, a future of wealth! We shall build our fleet so strong, our enemies shall fear us like never before! We will expand our trade routes across the sea, bringing home spices and treasures like we've never dreamed! And I say to those who stand against us: be careful of what side of the line you choose, because either you're with us, or you're on the side of evil! And we will harbor no enemies among our friends. We WILL hunt you down, we will root you out, we will DESTROY you! And Venezia will always stand the brightest jewel in all of civilization!

speaker: Marco
en: No... it's too soon... I'm not ready.

speaker: Ezio
en: We rarely are. Che la morte non sia crudele (Death not be unkind). Requiescat in pace (Rest in peace).

speaker: Courtesan 1
en: Beautifully done!

speaker: Courtesan 2
en: Che spettacolo! Che spettacolo! (What a show! What a show!)

speaker: Courtesan 3
en: A true hero!

speaker: Teodora
en: You must be exhausted. Come, relax.

speaker: Antonio
en: Ah, the savior of Venezia! What can I say? Perhaps it was wrong of me to doubt you so readily. Now we'll see where all the pieces fall.

speaker: Teodora
en: Enough of that now. You've worked hard, my son. I feel your tired body in need of comfort and succor.

speaker: Ezio
en: But I have such aches and pains, Sister. I may need a great deal of comfort and succor.

speaker: Teodora
en: Oh, that can be arranged. Girls!

speaker: Bodyguard
en: The invention is under guard and I caged the spies.

speaker: Engineer
en: Those who attempted to steal from Cesare must be punished.

speaker: Engineer
en: What do you want?

speaker: Ezio
en: Where are the plans for the weapon?

speaker: Engineer
en: On a table, at the opposite end of the fortress.

speaker: Ezio
en: And the device itself?

speaker: Engineer
en: I am not sure. But you need three people to work it.

speaker: Ezio
en: Come with me then.

speaker: Engineer
en: No! We... we captured three soldiers, they are in a cell across from the plans. They will help you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene (Good).

speaker: Ezio
en: Where is da Vinci's machine?

speaker: Cannoneer
en: Follow us. They have hidden the path, but we discovered the entrance.

speaker: Captain
en: Cesare intends it as the centerpiece of his forces. His army prepares for a surprise assault on Sicilia (Sicily).

speaker: Ezio
en: We will stop the attack.

speaker: Cannoneer
en: We need to open that gate.

speaker: Ezio
en: I will find a way.

speaker: Cannoneer
en: There you are, finally.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do not test me.

speaker: Ezio
en: I will lower the bridge.

speaker: Ezio
en: Leonardo expects me to maneuver this? No instructions. Of course.

speaker: Guard
en: Don't protect it anymore, fire at it!

speaker: Ezio
en: If ours can be injured, so can theirs.

speaker: Captain
en: Just a few more shots!

speaker: Captain
en: You are crippling Cesare's army!

speaker: Ezio
en: I wish I could keep you.

speaker: Ezio
en: No evidence of an army here. And no signs of Tarik's men.

speaker: Dilara
en: Not so close adi herif (pig)!

speaker: Ezio
en: Easy now. Tarik sent me.

speaker: Dilara
en: Only you? Why not more?

speaker: Ezio
en: I am enough. Where are your men?

speaker: Dilara
en: Captured by Byzantines over a week ago. I was dressed to look like a slave, and managed to escape. But the others... Are you a capable fighter?

speaker: Ezio
en: I like to think so.

speaker: Dilara
en: Well when you are certain, come find me.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Welcome to the Rosa in Fiore (Blooming Rose), stranger.

speaker: Ezio
en: Salve (Hello). Would you be kind enough to call the owner for me?

speaker: Courtesan
en: Madonna Solari is not in.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do you know where she is?

speaker: Courtesan
en: I

speaker: Lucia
en: Aiuto! Aiuto! (Help! Help!) Madonna Solari

speaker: Courtesan
en: Lucia. We thought you were gone for good!

speaker: Lucia
en: The men took us on a ship. They released me, but she

speaker: Ezio
en: Who took you on a ship?

speaker: Lucia
en: Slave traders Messere (Mister). Near Isola Tiberina (Tiber Island). They want coin in exchange for her life.

speaker: Ezio
en: I will get her back.

speaker: Slave trader
en: Are you here for the whore?

speaker: Solari
en: Aiutatemi! (Help me!)

speaker: Ezio
en: I have your money. Let her go.

speaker: Slave trader
en: No, take it up with Cesare.

speaker: Ezio
en: Mother? Sister?

speaker: Maria
en: Ezio. Ser (Sir) Machiavelli said that you might be here.

speaker: Ezio
en: What are you doing in Roma? Has Firenze been attacked?

speaker: Ezio
en: Why?

speaker: Claudia
en: Ezio, we want to help.

speaker: Ezio
en: I was trying to help you by sending you to Firenze.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Where is Madonna Solari?

speaker: Ezio
en: She's dead.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Merda. (Shit.)

speaker: Lucia
en: What now? Will we have to close?

speaker: Ezio
en: You cannot close. I need your help.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Messere (Mister), without someone who can run things, we are finished.

speaker: Claudia
en: I'll do it.

speaker: Ezio
en: You do not belong here, Claudia.

speaker: Claudia
en: I know how to run a business. I ran Uncle Mario's for years.

speaker: Ezio
en: This is different.

speaker: Maria
en: What alternative do you have, Ezio?

speaker: Ezio
en: You do this Claudia and you are on your own.

speaker: Claudia
en: I've been on my own for twenty years.

speaker: Ezio
en: Fine. I intend to repair the brothel. This place is a real mess. And I want your courtesans to find Caterina Sforza.

speaker: Claudia
en: You can count on us.

speaker: Claudia
en: Welcome to the Rosa in Fiore (Blooming Rose), as you can see, the most popular brothel in Roma.

speaker: Ezio
en: My money went well invested.

speaker: Claudia
en: Here I keep a list of the skills taught to my girls.

speaker: Ezio
en: You are not teaching them much.

speaker: Claudia
en: Think you can do better?

speaker: Ezio
en: Nessun problema. (No problem.)

speaker: Maria
en: Ezio, the Borgia make it difficult for Claudia's girls. There are several things you can do to that would aid them...

speaker: Ezio
en: I will keep that in mind. Anything else?

speaker: Claudia
en: No. Ezio

speaker: Ezio
en: Did you find Caterina?

speaker: Claudia
en: We are working on it.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene. (Good.) Come to see me at Isola Tiberina (Tiber Island) with her location.

speaker: Farmer
en: Your orders are simple—keep watch over these fields and ensure no harm comes to the bundles of fieno (hay). It may seem a mundane task, but it's critical nonetheless!

speaker: Farmer
en: Without this most basic resource, they'll lose the means to resist. They will be forced to stand down. Already, many have fallen into line. They require clothing. Food. Shelter. Warmth. And all these things are born of fieno. I hear you grumbling. You think this post is a waste of time. But you must understand—our very existence depends on keeping all of this secure! You don't believe me do you? Let me explain... The fieno feeds our horses. They, in turn, pull our carts - which transport our goods to other cities—where trade is conducted. In this way, our economy is made to thrive! Then there is the livestock. Cattle and sheep require fieno for substance. And as you know, they provide us with all manner of things: wool, meat, and milk to name a few. Do you see, then? Why the fieno must not fall into enemy hands? So do not dismiss the work you do here. It is vital to our continued success.

speaker: Ezio
en: You would have let your own people starve! And for what?

speaker: Farmer
en: Too long I suffered their insults. They called me simple and low-class... I wanted their respect.

speaker: Ezio
en: I'm afraid you do not have mine. Per quanto sia penoso il trapasso, lieto sarà il tuo sonno. Requiescat in pace. (Though the passing may be painful, it will be a gentle sleep. Rest in peace.)

speaker: Caterina
en: Bambini! But where are Bianca and Ottaviano!?

speaker: Nezetta
en: Forgive me Signora. They were playing outside when the attack began... I don't know where they are...

speaker: Guard
en: Reinforcements from the mountains! They are breaching the citadel!

speaker: Caterina
en: Ezio, don't let those bastardi (bastards) get in here!

speaker: Machiavelli
en: With me!

speaker: Ezio
en: What happened here? Signor Lorenzo?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Lorenzo's currently indisposed. Hey! You're the one who killed Francesco de' Pazzi. Get him!

speaker: Guard 2
en: With pleasure!

speaker: Guard 4
en: I know I heard a noise down there. It's time to earn your Florins. I want half of you to search the courtyard, the other half come with me to check the Chapel.

speaker: Guard 5
en: Si, Capitano! (Yes, Captain!)

speaker: Guard 4
en: Then we check the secret passageways.

speaker: Guard 6
en: What about Lorenzo?

speaker: Guard 4
en: By now, Lorenzo is already dead.

speaker: Guard 7
en: Lorenzo! Porca vacca! (God damn it!) Someone find a way to get inside there.

speaker: Guard 8
en: You heard him! You two, get a ladder!

speaker: Guard 9
en: What are we doing with the ladder?

speaker: Guard 10
en: Lorenzo isn't coming out.

speaker: Guard 8
en: What's taking them so long? If you both weren't so loud, he wouldn't have heard us coming.

speaker: Guard 10
en: Merda, (shit) you were the loud one.

speaker: Guard 11
en: All of you, mind your own business and keep watch.

speaker: Guard 10
en: It opened.

speaker: Guard 8
en: Did you hear that? It came from the bedroom.

speaker: Guard 10
en: Whoever opened it must be in there.

speaker: Guard 7
en: There's an intruder in the bedroom. Go kill him!

speaker: Guard 9
en: S-si, Capitano! (Y-Yes, Captain!)

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Get back!

speaker: Ezio
en: Lower your sword. It's me.

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Ezio! Again, you save me. First, they enter my church, now my home.

speaker: Ezio
en: I'll hunt them down. They won't come near you again.

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Look around you. This is one of my treasure rooms. You are entitled to take anything you wish from it, in thanks for what you've done. I trust my apartments are safe now?

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes, Signore. Thank you for this most gracious gift. I must go, but I will come to you again when all the Pazzi are dead.

speaker: Lorenzo
en: I will not forget what you have done for me. Buona fortuna (Good luck).

speaker: Ezio
en: ...and then Minerva talked about the sun. She told of a disaster that occurred long ago and another that is coming.

speaker: Mario
en: Sometime far in future, vero (right)? Then we need not worry about it.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì (Yes). Perhaps our work is finished.

speaker: Mario
en: Would that be so bad?

speaker: Mario
en: We upgraded the arsenal while you were away.

speaker: Ezio
en: Ah. And it is now customary for you to fire cannon balls at visitors?

speaker: Mario
en: My apologies. We only installed them a few days ago. My men are still being trained in their use.

speaker: Woman
en: Welcome back, Ezio!

speaker: Ezio
en: Madonna (Ma'am).

speaker: Boy
en: Ezio! Look it is Ezio! Let me see!

speaker: Ezio
en: Buon giorno (Good day). It is good to be home.

speaker: Man
en: Felice anno nuovo (Happy New Year)!

speaker: Ezio
en: This place just keeps getting better.

speaker: Mario
en: Thanks to you.

speaker: Claudia
en: Brother!

speaker: Ezio
en: Claudia, it is good to be home. How is mother?

speaker: Claudia
en: She's fine. I heard you were returning, but I am glad to see it with my own eyes. The Contessa (Countess) of Forlì is here to welcome you. I had no idea you were so famous!

speaker: Ezio
en: Caterina? Here?

speaker: Claudia
en: Is it finished, then? Is the Spaniard truly dead?

speaker: Ezio
en: Gather the others in Mario's study tonight. I'll explain everything there.

speaker: Mario
en: Steel yourself, Ezio. They will have many questions.

speaker: Ezio
en: Claudia, tell the Contessa (the Countess) I look forward to seeing her this evening.

speaker: Sofia
en: Such a climb! É così bello qui. (It is so beautiful here.) This is where your Order began?

speaker: Ezio
en: It began thousands of years ago, but here it was reborn.

speaker: Sofia
en: By the man you mentioned? Altaïr?

speaker: Ezio
en: Altaïr Ibn-La'Ahad. He built us up, then set us free. He saw the folly of keeping a castle like this. It had become a symbol of arrogance, and a beacon for all our enemies.

speaker: Sofia
en: And the mandate for menacing hoods... was that his idea as well?

speaker: Sofia
en: You mentioned a Creed before. What is it?

speaker: Ezio
en: Nothing is true, everything is permitted.

speaker: Sofia
en: That is rather cynical.

speaker: Ezio
en: It would be if it were doctrine. But it is merely an observation of the nature of reality. To say that nothing is true, is to realize that the foundations of society are fragile, and that we must be the shepherds of our own civilization. To say that everything is permitted, is to understand that we are the architects of our actions, and that we must live with their consequences, whether glorious or tragic.

speaker: Sofia
en: Do you regret your decision? To live as an Assassin for so long?

speaker: Ezio
en: I do not remember making that decision. This life, it chose me. For three decades I have served the memory of my father and my brothers, and fought for those who have suffered the pain of injustice. I do not regret those years, but it is time to live for myself, and let them go. To let go of all of this.

speaker: Sofia
en: Then let go. You will not fall far.

speaker: Ezio
en: The end of the road.

speaker: Sofia
en: What do you hope to find behind that door?

speaker: Ezio
en: Knowledge, above all else. Altaïr was a profound man and a prolific writer. He built this place as a repository for all his wisdom. He saw many things in his life, and learned many secrets, both troubling and strange. Knowledge that would drive lesser men to despair.

speaker: Sofia
en: Does that worry you?

speaker: Ezio
en: Sofia, you should know by now. I am not a lesser man.

speaker: Sofia
en: Ezio.

speaker: Sofia
en: You had better come out of there alive.

speaker: Ezio
en: I plan to.

speaker: Ezio
en: No books... no wisdom... Just you, fratello mio (my brother). Requiescat in pace, Altaïr.

speaker: Janissary 1
en: Selim understands our plight. The Byzantines, the Mamluks, the Safavid. Only he has the courage to face these threats.

speaker: Janissary 2
en: Haklisin. (You speak truth.) Selim is a warrior. Like Osman and Mehmet.

speaker: Janissary 1
en: So why has our Sultan chosen a cat over our lion?

speaker: Janissary 2
en: Ahmet shares the Sultan's calm temperament. They are too much alike, I fear.

speaker: Janissary 1
en: Why does Ahmet linger in this city? He knows he is not wanted.

speaker: Janissary 2
en: He is like a moth hovering around an open flame. Waiting for his father to perish so that he may step to the throne.

speaker: Janissary 1
en: Did you hear? He offered Tarik a sum of money in exchange for our loyalty.

speaker: Janissary 2
en: God damn him. What did Tarik do?

speaker: Janissary 1
en: He spent half the money on horse feed and sent the rest to Selim!

speaker: Guard
en: Khardeshlerim! (Brothers!) One of our own was found murdered and stripped of his garments not an hour ago, his body dumped like a mound of rubbish. Keep a close watch on these streets as you move about. Someone is planning to strike in our name. We must be ready.

speaker: Janissary 3
en: Any news from the north?

speaker: Janissary 4
en: Selim's forces have fallen back to Varna. Heavy losses I am told.

speaker: Janissary 3
en: Olacak shey degil, oye degil mi? (Incredible, isn't it?) I pray for a swift conclusion.

speaker: Janissary 4
en: Yes, but in which direction?

speaker: Janissary 3
en: I cannot say. My heart sides with our Sultan, but my head hopes for Selim.

speaker: Janissary 5
en: Have you met Selim's young son, Shehzade (Prince) Suleiman?

speaker: Janissary 6
en: Not personally, but I have seen him. I know he is a remarkable boy.

speaker: Janissary 5
en: Not a boy, but a capable young man. With a magnificent mind.

speaker: Janissary 6
en: Does he take after his father?

speaker: Janissary 5
en: Belki. (Perhaps.) Though I suspect he is another sort of man altogether.

speaker: Janissary 7
en: Sultan Bayezid is a good man, and a kind Sultan... but he has lost the fire that made him great.

speaker: Janissary 8
en: No, no. He is still a fighter. Look at the army he has raised against Selim.

speaker: Janissary 7
en: This is further evidence of his decline. To take up arms against his own son? Shameful.

speaker: Janissary 8
en: Do not bend the truth to match the contours of your passion, efendi (sir). It was Selim who attacked our Sultan.

speaker: Janissary 7
en: Evet, evet. (Yes, yes.) But Selim did so for the glory of the Empire, not himself.

speaker: Janissary
en: Tarik. A message for you.

speaker: Tarik
en: Harikulade. (Perfect.) The rifles have arrived in Cappadocia, where Manuel has garrisoned his army.

speaker: Janissary
en: And our men, are they still with him?

speaker: Tarik
en: Evet. (Yes.) They will contact us when the Byzantines decamp, then we will meet them when they reach Bursa.

speaker: Janissary
en: Everything is falling into place, efendim (my Lord).

speaker: Tarik
en: Evet. (Yes.) For once.

speaker: Tarik
en: Ah, what a bitter irony. Is this the result of Suleiman's investigation?

speaker: Ezio
en: You collude with the Sultan's enemies. What did you expect would come of such treachery?

speaker: Tarik
en: I blame myself. Not for treason, but hubris. I was preparing an ambush. Preparing to strike the Byzantine Templars where they felt safest.

speaker: Ezio
en: What proof do you have of this?

speaker: Tarik
en: See here. This will lead you to the Byzantines in Cappadocia. Destroy them if you can.

speaker: Ezio
en: You have done well, Tarik. Forgive me.

speaker: Tarik
en: Protect my homeland, Assassin. Allah ashkina (In God's name), redeem the honor we have lost in this fight.

speaker: Janissary
en: Murderer! Kill him!

speaker: Ezio
en: I am getting tired of this uniform.

speaker: Honorable Thief
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Ezio
en: Copernico sent me.

speaker: Scholar
en: Grazie. (Thank you.)

speaker: Yusuf
en: Praise the heavens! We feared we had lost our Mentor to the vices of the big city!

speaker: Ezio
en: I am content with my own vices, grazie (thank you).

speaker: Yusuf
en: So, what's on your mind, Ezio?

speaker: Ezio
en: Tell me more about the Templars. You call them Byzantines, yet the Byzantine Empire was overthrown sixty years ago.

speaker: Yusuf
en: These men are remnants of a line loyal to the cause of the last Emperor, Constantine XI. Who leads them now, however, I cannot say.

speaker: Ezio
en: Capisco. (I see.) I suppose it is up to me to find out.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Ezio, where is your hookblade?

speaker: Ezio
en: My hookblade?

speaker: Yusuf
en: You've never seen one? I grew up using these.

speaker: Ezio
en: Hmm, show me how it works.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Follow my lead!

speaker: Yusuf
en: Think of the hookblade as an extension of yourself, Ezio.

speaker: Yusuf
en: You think I can't make this one?

speaker: Yusuf
en: Didn't break a sweat!

speaker: Yusuf
en: Watch and learn, Ezio. We call this a hook-and-run. Sprint at your opponent, and just as you reach him, use the Hookblade to slip by.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Shahane! (Good!) Harika! (Excellent!)

speaker: Civilian
en: Certainly you were impressed this time. That was fast!

speaker: Amelia
en: I could do better. Anyone could!

speaker: Ezio
en: Scusate. (Excuse me.) I'm trying to find a boat to Venezia.

speaker: Amelia
en: You're nearly there, friend. Are you in a hurry?

speaker: Ezio
en: Perhaps not...

speaker: Amelia
en: You can help us settle a dispute. I bet my friend here the first stranger to come along can race the course faster than him.

speaker: Ezio
en: I suppose that would be me. And, if you're right? What do I win?

speaker: Amelia
en: Perhaps, a private riding lesson...?

speaker: Ezio
en: Lend me a horse.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where did the others go?

speaker: Amelia
en: Home with their tails between their legs. They couldn't stand to be beat. Nicely done, Messere...

speaker: Ezio
en: Call me Ezio. I still have some time for that private lesson.

speaker: Amelia
en: It would be my pleasure, Ezio. Call me Amelia...

speaker: Federico
en: Torna qui, maledetto cavallo (Come back here, you goddamned horse)! HEY OHH! I have food for you! Here! Come! Please! Come back!

speaker: Ezio
en: Buongiorno (Hello).

speaker: Federico
en: Ezio. Mario is going to murder me. I have lost his favorite horse.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do not despair. I will bring it back.

speaker: Federico
en: God bless you, Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: Here.

speaker: Federico
en: Grazie (Thank you), Ezio. I can no longer keep up with the horses. Promise me you will enjoy your good health. Do not spend as much time in battle as your Uncle Mario.

speaker: Ezio
en: My battles have already been won.

speaker: Federico
en: That is good news! Arrivederci (Goodbye), Ezio!

speaker: Ezio
en: Bambino (little man), why do you cry?

speaker: Boy
en: They're going to take my mama on a boat ride. They say I will go on the next one.

speaker: Ezio
en: Who?

speaker: Boy
en: A man from the castle came with guards and arrested us. He scared me.

speaker: Ezio
en: They are scary. But you look very brave.

speaker: Boy
en: Will you bring my mama back?

speaker: Ezio
en: Where did they take your mother?

speaker: Boy
en: Down that street.

speaker: Ezio
en: Good. Do you have a place to go for now?

speaker: Boy
en: My uncle's.

speaker: Ezio
en: Go there. Do not stop to talk to anyone!

speaker: Silvestro
en: We must ensure the kidnappings continue.

speaker: Valencia
en: But children, Silvestro.

speaker: Silvestro
en: To secure his reign, Cesare needs to control the populace. Fear keeps them quiet.

speaker: Valencia
en: I can hardly look at you.

speaker: Silvestro
en: Please, Valencia. Soon all this will be behind us.

speaker: Valencia
en: Are you afraid of him?

speaker: Silvestro
en: Who? I am afraid of no one.

speaker: Valencia
en: Did he do that to your hand? ...My apologies, that was out of line.

speaker: Silvestro
en: Please go.

speaker: Valencia
en: I am sorry.

speaker: Silvestro
en: I will have her killed. No, I will kill her myself. The puttana (whore)! How dare she speak of my hand? Ignorant fool, she has never served a higher cause.

speaker: Silvestro
en: Surrender, and you will live. Get in behind him! Careful, this one bites. No!

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in pace. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Hunting the Hunter
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Rosa
en: Salute, bello mio. Come stai? (Hello beautiful. How are you?) You back to see me already?

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Ezio
en: Desolato, mia cara (Sorry, my dear), but I am not here to play. I must speak with Antonio. It's urgent.

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Rosa
en: Antonio! Ezio's here!

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Antonio
en: Ezio! Is everything alright?

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Ezio
en: Carlo Grimaldi and the Barbarigo are in league with the one they call The Spaniard. They're going to murder the Doge and replace him with one of their own. They will have all of Venezia, her entire fleet, in their grasp.

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Antonio
en: And they call ME a criminal!

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Ezio
en: Then you will help me?

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Antonio
en: You have me on your side, brother. And the support of all my men.

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Rosa
en: ...and women.

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie, amici (Thank you, friends).

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Antonio
en: But, Ezio, I must warn you. It's not going to be so easy this time. Palazzo Ducale is the most heavily-guarded building in Venezia.

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Ezio
en: Nothing is impenetrable.

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Rosa
en: This is why we like you, Ezio.

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Antonio
en: Come! Let's go take a look. We'll come up with a plan.

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Antonio
en: This business with the Doge... terrible. Though, treachery like this no longer surprises me. When I was a child, we were taught that the nobles were just and kind. I believed it, too. Though my father was only a cobbler and my mother a scullery maid, I aspired to be much more. I studied hard, I persevered, but the nobles would never have me. If you are not born one of them, acceptance is impossible. So I ask you, Ezio: who are the true nobles of Venezia? Men like Carlo Grimaldi and Marco Barbarigo? No! I say WE are: the thieves, and mercenari and whores. While we work to save this city and its people, the nobles seek to make it their plaything...

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Antonio
en: We need to scout the palazzo carefully; see it from every angle. We just might find a way in. I know of a tall Campanile behind the palazzo. Or we might find a way to climb the back of the Basilica. Do you have any ideas?

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Ezio
en: I assume the front door is out?

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Antonio
en: Va bene, we'll try the front door as well, saputello (wise ass).

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Antonio
en: We're not getting in this way. They'll have time to murder the Doge before we're able to get through all these guards.

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Antonio
en: Look at that. Archers everywhere.

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Ezio
en: And the walls are impossible to climb on this side.

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Antonio
en: Bene! We're in luck. Looks like there's a perfect path up the scaffolding to the roof of the Basilica. Shall we?

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Antonio
en: Ezio, look! Isn't that him? Grimaldi?

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Carlo
en: Don't you understand what I'm offering you, Signore? Listen to me, please! Or this will be your last chance...

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Doge
en: How dare you?!

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Carlo
en: I'm sorry. Mi dispiace (I'm sorry). I meant nothing by it! I'm only looking out for your safety.

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Antonio
en: We're running out of time! There's no way through this fence and there are guards everywhere. Diavolo!

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Antonio
en: It's impossible! There's no way in or out for men. Only birds.

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Ezio
en: Yes... birds...

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Antonio
en: Where are you going now?

scene: If At First You Don't Succeed...
speaker: Ezio
en: To see my friend Leonardo.

speaker: Monk
en: Di grazia (Please), stay away from the artwork on the walls! And when your men paint the dome, take care not to disturb any of the sacred relics in the lanterna on top. They are the most important artifacts in our church.

speaker: Painter
en: Yes, yes Padre (Father). Just make sure to pay us the full sum for our work.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene (good)! Now I have a way back up in case I fall.

speaker: Borgia Seeker
en: Hand me the chest, Luigi. I will bring it to the Banker.

speaker: Borgia Brute
en: You may enter.

speaker: Guard
en: We can't go in?

speaker: Brute
en: You have to patrol by order of Cesare.

speaker: Guard
en: Porca puttana! (Fuck me!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Cesare? He's here?

speaker: Guard
en: Luigi has been killed. We discovered his body at the Pantheon.

speaker: Brute
en: Luigi? We just let him in.

speaker: Ezio
en: Tell Claudia that the Banker is here.

speaker: Guard
en: For the Banker.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Hello there.

speaker: Carrier
en: Hello.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Mind if I walk with you?

speaker: Carrier
en: Ja. (Yes.) I mean, I do not mind.

speaker: Courtesan
en: I've never been to Trastevere before. The old ruins make me nervous.

speaker: Carrier
en: I can protect you.

speaker: Courtesan
en: I bet. That is quite a chest you have there.

speaker: Carrier
en: It's not mine.

speaker: Courtesan
en: But you are holding it in those strong arms of yours.

speaker: Carrier
en: You want to touch them?

speaker: Courtesan
en: What will I tell the Priest in confession?

speaker: Carrier
en: Money for you, Banker.

speaker: Juan
en: I will take that. And that.

speaker: Juan
en: You are dismissed.

speaker: Carrier
en: Where did I put my coin purse?

speaker: Courtesan
en: Onoratissima. (It's an honor.)

speaker: Juan
en: Welcome to my party. I am Juan Borgia.

speaker: Guard
en: Cesare is about to speak in the main room, Eccellenza (Excellence).

speaker: Juan
en: Come.

speaker: Juan
en: Are you having a pleasant evening?

speaker: Courtesan
en: Yes, Eccellenza (Excellence). I am. There is so much to look at.

speaker: Juan
en: Oh good. I spared no expense.

speaker: Courtesan
en: I can tell.

speaker: Juan
en: The finer things in life make power so rewarding. I see an apple, I can pluck that apple. No one will stop me.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Well, it depends whose tree it is.

speaker: Juan
en: You don't seem to understand, my dear. I own all the trees.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Not mine.

speaker: Juan
en: On the contrary. I watched you steal my guard's money, I believe I've earned a free ride as repentance. In fact, I want you here all night long.

speaker: Courtesan
en: For free? I have to make money you know.

speaker: Juan
en: Do you have a sister by any chance?

speaker: Courtesan
en: No, but I have a daughter.

speaker: Juan
en: 300 florins?

speaker: Juan
en: Done! A pleasure doing business with you.

speaker: Cesare
en: Thank you all for coming. We have a long night ahead of us. What better way to celebrate my victories than to join in the brotherhood of man? Soon we will be here once more celebrating a united Italia and then the feasting will last for forty days and forty nights! Cominciamo ora! (Begin now!)

speaker: Rodrigo
en: We did not agree to conquer Italia.

speaker: Cesare
en: If your brilliant Captain General says we can do it, why not rejoice and let it happen?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: You risk upsetting the delicate balance of control we have worked so hard to tighten.

speaker: Cesare
en: I appreciate all that you have done for me, but I have the army, so I am making the decisions. Don't look so glum, enjoy yourself.

speaker: Juan
en: The things I have felt, seen and tasted. I do not regret a moment of it.

speaker: Ezio
en: A man of power must be contemptuous of delicacies.

speaker: Juan
en: But... I gave the people what they wanted.

speaker: Ezio
en: And now you pay for it. Il piacere immeritato si consuma da sé. (Pleasure unearned consumes itself.) Requiescat in pace. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Mario
en: Roma (Rome) beckons, Ezio. Let me know when you are ready to depart.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Assassino! Assassino! (Assassin! Assassin!)

speaker: Guard 2
en: Close the gates! Stop the intruder!

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Credo in unum Deum, Patrem omnipoténtem, factórem cæli et terræ, visibílium ómnium et invisibílium. Et in unum Dóminum, Iesum Christum, Fílium Dei unigénitum, et ex Patre natum ante ómnia sǽcula. Deum de Deo, lumen de lúmine, Deum verum de Deo vero, génitum, non factum, consubstantiálem Patri: per quem ómnia facta sunt. Qui propter nos hómines et propter nostram salútem descéndit de cælis. Et incarnátus est de Spíritu Sancto ex María Vírgine, et homo factus est. Crucifíxus étiam pro nobis sub ; passus et sepúltus est, et resurréxit tértia die, secúndum Scriptúras, et ascéndit in cælum, sedet ad déxteram Patris. Et íterum ventúrus est cum glória, iudicáre vivos et mórtuos, cuius regni non erit finis. Et in Spíritum Sanctum, Dóminum et vivificántem: qui ex Patre Filióque procédit. Qui cum Patre et Fílio simul adorátur et conglorificátur: qui locútus est per prophétas. Et unam, sanctam, cathólicam et apostólicam Ecclésiam. Confíteor unum baptísma in remissiónem peccatórum. Et exspécto resurrectiónem mortuórum, et vitam ventúri sǽculi. Amen. (I believe in one God, the Father almighty, maker of heaven and earth, of all things visible and invisible. I believe in one Lord Jesus Christ, the Only Begotten Son of God, born of the Father before all ages. God from God, Light from Light, true God from true God, begotten, not made, consubstantial with the Father; through him all things were made. For us men and for our salvation he came down from heaven, and by the Holy Spirit was incarnate of the Virgin Mary, and became man. For our sake he was crucified under Pontius Pilate, he suffered death and was buried, and rose again on the third day in accordance with the Scriptures. He ascended into heaven and is seated at the right hand of the Father. He will come again in glory to judge the living and the dead and his kingdom will have no end. I believe in the Holy Spirit, the Lord, the giver of life, who proceeds from the Father and the Son, who with the Father and the Son is adored and glorified, who has spoken through the prophets. I believe in one, holy, catholic and apostolic Church. I confess one Baptism for the forgiveness of sins and I look forward to the resurrection of the dead and the life of the world to come. Amen.)

speaker: Ezio
en: I thought... I thought I was beyond this. But I'm not. I've waited too long... lost too much... Requiescat in pace (Rest in peace), you bastard.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: I don't think so!

speaker: Rodrigo
en: How is it you resist?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: I see... Kind of you to bring me the Apple. Now give it here!

speaker: Ezio
en: Vai a farti fottere. (Go fuck yourself.)

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Ahh, always the fighter. Just like your father. Well—rejoice, my child—for you will see him again SOON! You WILL give it to me!

speaker: Ezio
en: As you wish.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Fascinating! An impressive power, this. But if you think it's going to save you, you've another thing coming!

speaker: Rodrigo
en: How long do you think you can keep this up? A clever trick! But useless! You cannot stop me. You are right to fear me! I'll cut you down, Assassin!

speaker: Rodrigo
en: No! You will not take this from me...

speaker: Ezio
en: It's finished, Rodrigo. Lay down your arms and I'll make sure the end comes swiftly.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Really, Ezio? And would you give up so easily were it the other way around?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Why don't we find out!

speaker: Rodrigo
en: At last!

speaker: Rodrigo
en: And now to deal with you.

speaker: Ezio
en: What is this place...?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Open, damn you! OPEN!

speaker: Ezio
en: It's over, Rodrigo. No more tricks. No more ancient artifacts. No more weapons. Let us see what you are made of, old man.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Alright then, if that's how you want to play it.

speaker: Ezio
en: What do you even want with the Vault, Rodrigo?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Don't you know what lies within? Or do you mean to tell me the great and powerful Assassins didn't figure it out?

speaker: Ezio
en: Figure what out?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: God! It's God that dwells within!

speaker: Ezio
en: You expect me to believe that God lives beneath il Vaticano? (the Vatican?)

speaker: Rodrigo
en: A more logical location than a kingdom on a cloud, don't you think? Surrounded by singing angels and cherubim. Makes for a lovely image—but the TRUTH is far more interesting.

speaker: Ezio
en: Let's say I was to believe you—what do you think he'll do when you open that door?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: I don't care. It's not approval I'm after. Just power.

speaker: Ezio
en: And you think he'll give it up?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Whatever lies beyond that wall won't be able to resist the staff and apple. They were MADE for felling Gods.

speaker: Ezio
en: God is meant to be all knowing. All powerful. You think a couple of ancient relics can harm him?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: You know nothing, boy. You take your image of the creators from —a book, mind you, written by MEN.

speaker: Ezio
en: You are the Pope! And yet you dismiss the central text of your Faith?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Are you so naïve? I became Pope because it gave me ACCESS. It gave me POWER. Do you think I believe a single god-damned word of that ridiculous book? It's all lies and superstition. Just like every OTHER religious tract written over the past ten thousand years.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: You can't! You can't! It's MY destiny! MINE! I am the prophet!

speaker: Ezio
en: You never were...

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Get it over with then.

speaker: Ezio
en: No. Killing you won't bring my family back... I'm done. Nulla è reale, tutto è lecito. Requiescat in pace. (Nothing is true, everything is permitted. Rest in peace.)

speaker: Minerva
en: Greetings prophet. It is good you have come. Let us see it. To give thanks.

speaker: Minerva
en: We must speak.

speaker: Ezio
en: Who are you?

speaker: Minerva
en: Many names. When I died, it was Minerva. Before that Merva and Mera. And on and on. The others, too: Juno, who was before called Uni. Jupiter, who was before called Tinia...

speaker: Ezio
en: You are... gods.

speaker: Minerva
en: No. Not gods. We simply came... before. Even when we walked the world, your kind struggled to understand our existence. We were more... advanced in time. Your minds were not yet ready. Still... not. Maybe never. No matter. You may not comprehend us. But you will comprehend our warning. You must.

speaker: Ezio
en: None of what you are saying makes sense...

speaker: Minerva
en: Our words are not meant for you.

speaker: Ezio
en: What are you talking about? There's no one else here!

speaker: Minerva
en: Enough! I do not wish to speak with you but through you. You are the prophet. You've played your part. You anchor him, but please be silent! That we may commune.

speaker: Minerva
en: Listen: When we were still flesh and our home still whole, your kind betrayed us. We who made you. We, who gave you life! We were strong. But you were many. And both of us craved war. So busy were we with earthly concerns, we failed to notice the heavens. And by the time we did... The world burned until naught remained but ash. It should have ended then and there. But we built you in our own image. We built you to survive. And so we did. Few were our numbers. Your kind and mine. It took sacrifice. Strength. Compassion. But we rebuilt. And as life returned to the world... We endeavored to ensure this tragedy would not be repeated. But now we are dying... And time will work against us. Truth turned into myth and legend. What we built, misunderstood. Let my words preserve the message and make a record of our loss. But let my words also bring hope. You must find the other temples. Built by those who knew to turn away from war. They worked to protect us—to save us from the fire. If you can find them... If their work can be saved... so too might this world. Be quick! For time grows short. And guard against the cross—for there are many who will stand in your way.

speaker: Minerva
en: It is done. The message is delivered. We are gone now from this world. All of us. We can do no more. The rest is up to you, Desmond.

speaker: Ezio
en: What? Who is Desmond? I don't understand... Please, wait! I have so many questions!

speaker: Ezio
en: The city is under siege and everything is locked down... this won't be easy.

speaker: Leonardo
en: It's time. You did it! It's beautiful!

speaker: Antonio
en: Sì (Yes)! Now let's hope your idea works. Because we're nearly out of time.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Listen closely Ezio, you're going to want to fly from fire to fire. The heat of each one you pass over should lift you back up into the air.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene (Good).

speaker: Antonio
en: Be careful! There's archers out on the roofs tonight. Avoid those arrows, or it'll be a short trip.

speaker: Ezio
en: I wish there was some way for me to use my sword while flying this thing.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Well... you do have your feet free. If you get close enough without taking an arrow in the head, maybe you could kick them off the building?

speaker: Ezio
en: Nice.

speaker: Antonio
en: It's now or never, amico mio (My friend).

speaker: Guard
en: Ma cosa (What the)?! Shoot! Shoot the flying demon!

speaker: Mocenigo
en: What was that?!

speaker: Carlo
en: Probably just kids with firecrackers. Come, it's your move.

speaker: Ezio
en: STOP! Signore, don't drink that!

speaker: Carlo
en: You're too late, the Doge is dead.

speaker: Mocenigo
en: What? Carlo...?

speaker: Carlo
en: Apologies Signore, but you should have listened to me when you had the chance. Seems you failed, Assassin.

speaker: Carlo
en: Assassino! Assassino! He's killed the Doge! The Doge is dead!

speaker: Ezio
en: It takes one Assassin to kill another, it seems.

speaker: Carlo
en: We kill thinking it's best for us, do we not, Messer (Sir) Ezio?

speaker: Ezio
en: I do this not for myself. Compio questo sacrificio per il bene superiore. (I make this sacrifice for the greater good.) Requiescat in Pace. (Rest in peace).

speaker: Mocenigo
en: You... You killed me. You killed ME!?

speaker: Ezio
en: This is from Copernico.

speaker: Scholar
en: Thank you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Cut him down.

speaker: Pietro
en: This was not in the rehearsal!

speaker: Ezio
en: Hold off the guards.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Ezio, we are here to help!

speaker: Ezio
en: Stop the guards!

speaker: Pietro
en: Who are you?

speaker: Ezio
en: Your savior.

speaker: Ezio
en: He has been poisoned.

speaker: Brunelleschi
en: That pallor. Cantarella. Drink this.

speaker: Ezio
en: Hurry!

speaker: Brunelleschi
en: Give him a moment.

speaker: Pietro
en: I feel slightly better.

speaker: Brunelleschi
en: Leeches will lead to a full recovery.

speaker: Pietro
en: I cannot thank you enough. I

speaker: Ezio
en: The key to the Castel Sant'Angelo. Now.

speaker: Pietro
en: What are you talking about? I'm simply a poor actor

speaker: Ezio
en: Cesare knows about you and Lucrezia.

speaker: Pietro
en: Here.

speaker: Ezio
en: Un momento! (Hey!) You were at the Villa Auditore during the attack!

speaker: Ezio
en: Why did you run?

speaker: Paganino
en: I

speaker: Ezio
en: You are the traitor, not Machiavelli.

speaker: Paganino
en: Long live the Borgia!

speaker: Ezio
en: Merda! I was right. I have to stop La Volpe before he gets to Machiavelli.

speaker: Ezio
en: I have discovered the traitor.

speaker: La Volpe
en: What?

speaker: Ezio
en: One of our men, he was at the Villa attack. Here, he carried this letter.

speaker: La Volpe
en: My God!

speaker: Machiavelli
en: This is good news.

speaker: Ezio
en: More than you know.

speaker: La Volpe
en: I am once again in your debt, Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: What debt is there amongst friends who trust one another?

speaker: La Volpe
en: Yes. Thank you for relaying the message in time.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Come Niccolò, it has been far too long since we've talked.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: I heard the Colosseum Passion Play took an unexpected turn this evening.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Really?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: It seems Gesù Cristo was resurrected three days early.

speaker: Ahmet
en: That's not a legal move.

speaker: Suleiman
en: It is a European variation. Arrocco. (Castling.)

speaker: Ahmet
en: It's interesting, but not exactly fair when you play by different rules than your opponent.

speaker: Suleiman
en: You may think differently when you are Sultan. Shall I take it back?

speaker: Ahmet
en: Suleiman, I know it has been hard on you, watching your father and me quarrel over Bayezid's throne.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Grandfather has chosen you, and his word is kanun (law). What is there to argue about?

speaker: Ahmet
en: Your father and I were close once, but his cruelty and ambition have made

speaker: Suleiman
en: I have heard the rumors, uncle.

speaker: Ahmet
en: Well, I have a meeting with the viziers soon. Shall we continue another time?

speaker: Suleiman
en: Whenever you like.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: Tarik has been selling guns to a local miser. Manuel Palaiologos.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Palaiologos... that is a sad sound. The last Byzantine Emperor was Constantine Palaiologos. If his heir is arming a militia of some kind, this conflict will escalate.

speaker: Ezio
en: Tarik knows where the rifles are headed. If I find him first, I can follow the weapons straight to the Byzantines.

speaker: Suleiman
en: He will be with his Janissaries in their barracks. So if you want to get close, you will have to be one yourself.

speaker: Ezio
en: Not a problem.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Guzel. (Good.) Get the information you need, then kill him.

speaker: Ezio
en: Are you sure? You told me Tarik and your father were close friends, Suleiman.

speaker: Suleiman
en: This is true. But such naked treason against my grandfather deserves death.

speaker: Ezio
en: Intesi. (Understood.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Father? Federico?

speaker: Annetta
en: Oh! Ser Ezio! (Sir Ezio!) Thank God!

speaker: Ezio
en: What happened? Where is everyone?

speaker: Annetta
en: They took your father and brothers to the Palazzo della Signoria – to prison!

speaker: Ezio
en: And my mother? My sister?

speaker: Claudia
en: Ezio...

speaker: Ezio
en: Claudia! Are you alright?

speaker: Claudia
en: Yes. But mother...

speaker: Annetta
en: She's in shock. They... When she resisted...

speaker: Ezio
en: It's not safe here. Is there a place you can take them?

speaker: Annetta
en: Yes. Yes! To my sister's.

speaker: Ezio
en: Good. Do that. In the meantime I'll go see my father.

speaker: Annetta
en: Be careful Messer Ezio! The guards were looking for you as well.

speaker: Giovanni
en: Ezio!

speaker: Ezio
en: Father! What's happened?

speaker: Giovanni
en: Took a bit of a beating, but I'm alright. What of your mother and sister?

speaker: Ezio
en: Safe now.

speaker: Giovanni
en: Annetta took them?

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes... Wait. You knew this would happen?!

speaker: Giovanni
en: Not the way it did... And not this soon. It doesn't matter now.

speaker: Ezio
en: What do you mean? Explain!

speaker: Giovanni
en: There's no time. Listen closely: Return to the house. In my office is a hidden door. Use your talent to find it. Beyond lies a chest, take EVERYTHING you find inside. Much of it may seem strange to you, but all of it is important. Do you understand?

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes.

speaker: Giovanni
en: Good. Among the contents is a letter – and with it some documents. I need you to take these documents to Messer Uberto. He was with me in the office this morning.

speaker: Ezio
en: The Gonfaloniere. I remember. Now please – tell me what's happening. Are the Pazzi behind this? There was a note at the pigeon coop. It sai–

speaker: Giovanni
en: Go Ezio! Go now!

speaker: Merchant
en: You see this rug. Incredible quality. Your feet will love you more than your wife does.

speaker: Ezio
en: I am not married.

speaker: Merchant
en: Ah, you're better off. Come, feel it!

speaker: Ezio
en: You have sold well today.

speaker: Merchant
en: I have not sold a thing! The Janissaries confiscated most of my rugs just because they were imported.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do you know Tarik Barleti, their captain?

speaker: Merchant
en: Eh, he's around here somewhere. An arrogant man, but–

speaker: Merchant
en: You insult me, sir! I cannot take less than two hundred Akçe (coins) for this! My final offer.

speaker: Ezio
en: When I find him, I will ask about the rugs.

speaker: Merchant
en: You drive a hard bargain, yabanci (stranger). Shall we compromise at one eighty? One eighty Akçe (coins), and we part as friends!

speaker: Ezio
en: There he is.

speaker: Tarik
en: I pray Selim can soon return to the city in good spirits and stronger hands.

speaker: Tarik
en: Of all Mehmet's accomplishments, I am beginning to think this Bazaar was the finest.

speaker: Tarik
en: If you have no business here, you do not belong! Clear the way! No loitering!

speaker: Tarik
en: This is an important meeting... make sure I am not being followed. Ah, when I was a young man, there was a baker who worked right here selling fresh simit all day, every day. And on my free days I would buy two at a time, sometimes three. It is a shame that nothing good ever lasts long. Perhaps your business will do better, eh? This Empire is sick, and Bayezid – it pains me to say – is its cancer. You there! I will be back tomorrow, and if you have not disposed of all this foreign made garbage, I will confiscate it myself, and throw it into the !

speaker: Tarik
en: What news?

speaker: Janissary
en: Manuel has agreed to meet you, Tarik. He's waiting by the arsenal gate.

speaker: Tarik
en: An eager old weasel, isn't he? Come.

speaker: Adad
en: Be merciful! Please! I am a working man, with a family.

speaker: Ezio
en: Doing what kind of work?

speaker: Adad
en: Digging mostly. It took me a year to find this chamber. And for the past three months I have been trying to break through this door.

speaker: Ezio
en: You have not made much progress.

speaker: Adad
en: I have not made a dent! This stone is harder than steel.

speaker: Ezio
en: I doubt you will. This door is guarding objects more valuable than all the gold in the world.

speaker: Adad
en: Ah! Do you mean... gemstones?

speaker: Ezio
en: There are keyholes here. Where are the keys?

speaker: Adad
en: These Templars found one beneath the Ottoman Sultan's palace. As for the others, I suppose their little book will tell them.

speaker: Ezio
en: What book?

speaker: Adad
en: A journal of some kind. That ugly captain, he carries it with him wherever he goes.

speaker: Ezio
en: Go home. Find work with honest men.

speaker: Adad
en: Oh, I would love to leave this place, but these men, they will murder me if I try.

speaker: Ezio
en: Pack your tools.

speaker: Guard
en: The Assassin MUST NOT get his hands on that book. When we reach Leandros, we will escort him out of the village. You stay behind and make sure we are not followed.

speaker: Leandros
en: Fiye apo brosta moul! (Out of my way!) None of you leave until the Assassin is dead. Do you understand?

speaker: Guard
en: Signome, kirie lohayé (Pardon, Captain), but he seems to have found us.

speaker: Leandros
en: Pame! Pame! (Go! Go!)

speaker: Francesco
en: Ezio. Our grudge against Cesare requires action. What is our next step?

speaker: Ezio
en: Cesare's time will come, do not worry. Right now we have no chance of matching his military strength.

speaker: Francesco
en: So what do we do?

speaker: Ezio
en: What do armies require?

speaker: Francesco
en: Soldiers and weapons.

speaker: Ezio
en: True. But you must pay all those soldiers and forge all of those weapons.

speaker: Francesco
en: Of course Cesare has money; he is the one who levies the taxes.

speaker: Ezio
en: Not Cesare personally. His banker, Juan Borgia the Elder.

speaker: Francesco
en: Ah, I see.

speaker: Ezio
en: Have you any clue on his whereabouts?

speaker: Francesco
en: I can't say. I've heard rumor that he is set to throw one of his more colorful parties, but I don't know where.

speaker: Ezio
en: Colorful?

speaker: Francesco
en: I don't know what else to call them. If you come across it, you'll see what I mean.

speaker: Ezio
en: Very well. I will begin my search.

speaker: Juan Borgia
en: What? An Assassin? Cesare will hear of this!

speaker: Ezio
en: Give your cousin a message for me! Tell him that his days are numbered!

speaker: Juan Borgia
en: I would say they number more than you. Guards!

speaker: Ezio
en: It seems it is time to take my leave from this party.

speaker: Juan Borgia
en: The party wasn't that bad, was it?

speaker: Ezio
en: This is not about the party.

speaker: Juan Borgia
en: Oh, good. I was worried I'd offended you in some way.

speaker: Ezio
en: No. I am only doing this to get to Cesare.

speaker: Juan Borgia
en: I see. I'm sure my cousin will have taken notice of this.

speaker: Ezio
en: He will be joining you soon enough.

speaker: Paola
en: You were gone for quite a while.

speaker: Ezio
en: Leonardo likes to talk.

speaker: Paola
en: That he does. But I trust you did more than talk?

speaker: Paola
en: Impressive.

speaker: Ezio
en: I'm rather fond of it myself.

speaker: Paola
en: I've given you the skills, Leonardo's given you the blade. All the remains is the deed.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where can I find Uberto?

speaker: Paola
en: According to my girls, he'll be attending an unveiling tonight of Verrocchio's latest work. It will be held at the Santa Croce cloister.

speaker: Ezio
en: Watch over my mother and sister while I'm away.

speaker: Paola
en: Of course, Ezio. As if they were my own.

speaker: Uberto
en: Again with this?

speaker: Lorenzo
en: You have overstepped your bounds, Uberto.

speaker: Uberto
en: Who are you to speak of bounds. You, who have crowned yourself Lorenzo de' Medici, Principe (Prince) of Firenze.

speaker: Lorenzo
en: I've done no such thing.

speaker: Uberto
en: Of course not. Ever innocent. How convenient. At least now we see how far your reach extends—which is to say—nowhere at all. It has proved a valuable lesson for me and my allies.

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Yes. Your allies, the Pazzi. Is that what this is about?

speaker: Uberto
en: Be careful with your words, Lorenzo. You might attract the wrong sort of attention.

speaker: Guest 1
en: Good evening, .

speaker: Uberto
en: To you as well. I trust you're enjoying yourselves?

speaker: Guest 1
en: Indeed! A nice distraction from that nasty business with the Auditore family.

speaker: Uberto
en: And to think I once thought of Giovanni as a brother...

speaker: Guest 1
en: Don't blame yourself! How could you have known what evils he planned?

speaker: Guest 2
en: I say we strike that traitor's name from the record books. Let history forget he ever even existed.

speaker: Uberto
en: Hmmm. Yes, I should look into that. If you'll excuse me for a moment...

speaker: Beatrice
en: Uberto! A moment of your time?

speaker: Uberto
en: Anything for you, Beatrice.

speaker: Beatrice
en: So! Tell us! How does it feel to be a hero?

speaker: Uberto
en: Please, I am no such thing. As Gonfaloniere it is my duty to ensure that the city of Firenze remains a shining beacon of justice. Corruption and its ilk shall find no purchase here so long as I am in control.

speaker: Beatrice
en: You are a treasure, Uberto! I hope Lorenzo recognizes that!

speaker: Uberto
en: Yes... our great leader, Lorenzo. I'll see you ladies later.

speaker: Guest 3
en: Ah, Uberto! There you are. I was just telling the other about the execution...

speaker: Guest 4
en: I mean no offense, but... what if they did not act alone?

speaker: Uberto
en: You can rest easy, friends. I am confident that this treachery began and ended with the Auditore family.

speaker: Guest 5
en: What of the other son? Ezio, was it?

speaker: Uberto
en: The child poses no danger. Soft hands and an even softer head. He'll be caught and executed before the week is out.

speaker: Guest 3
en: Don't let us keep you, Uberto. We just wanted to say hello.

speaker: Wife
en: Evening to you, Gonfaloniere.

speaker: Uberto
en: Is everything to your satisfaction?

speaker: Wife
en: Do you even need to ask? Of course!

speaker: Husband
en: Accept our thanks—for this evening—and for helping to keep Firenze safe. I always had my doubts about the Auditore. Where did the family even come from? To gain such wealth and ... and prestige in... in a single generation?

speaker: Wife
en: And the children—with their odd names. Always making trouble.

speaker: Husband
en: No surprise, given the company their father kept; whores and thieves, I swear it!

speaker: Uberto
en: Indeed. It is clear now he sought to undermine the city—to overturn all we've worked so hard to build.

speaker: Husband
en: But thanks to you, that's over now.

speaker: Uberto
en: You... Guards! Arrest him!

speaker: Uberto
en: You would have done the same. To save the ones you love.

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes, I would. And I have.

speaker: Ezio
en: The Auditore are not dead. I'm still here. ME! Ezio! Ezio Auditore!

speaker: Woman
en: Assassino!

speaker: Leonardo
en: Ezio! Dio mio (my God)! You're alive! Is it true? They say you killed the Doge.

speaker: Ezio
en: I was trying to save him, Leonardo. But the truth matters little. I failed. And now I'm the most wanted man in Venezia.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Well, perhaps you are in luck! It's Carnevale in Venezia. This is the time when everybody goes without a face!

speaker: Ezio
en: That's why I'm here. Do you have a mask I can wear?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Of course, of course, somewhere in here...

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie, amico mio. (Thanks, my friend.) And I have something for you.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Ohhh! More of the Codex! Aha... This one's quite complex... Hmm... it's a new design, my friend... A mechanism for your wrist, but not a blade... In fact, it seems to be a kind of arma da fuoco (firearm), but as small as a hummingbird!

speaker: Ezio
en: Is it possible?

speaker: Leonardo
en: I have no idea. Let's build it and find out!

speaker: Ezio
en: You've done me good, brother!

speaker: Leonardo
en: Ma certo, (Of course,) but I'm sure your return was not just to play with new toys. Is it about this terrible new Doge they've installed... Marco Barbarigo?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Then you'll want to speak with your friend Antonio. I've seen him quite a bit lately at a, um, mutual friend's. I'd look for him there, in the Dorsoduro district to the south. Ask for Sister Teodora.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sister?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Well, um... In a way. Yes, sister... And Ezio, you can't be carrying weapons out there today.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie, (Thanks,) Leonardo. Now, about that mask...

speaker: Uberto
en: Giovanni Auditore, you and your accomplices stand accused of the crime of treason. Have you any evidence to counter this charge?

speaker: Giovanni
en: Yes. The documents that were delivered to you last night!

speaker: Uberto
en: I'm afraid I know nothing of these documents.

speaker: Ezio
en: He's lying.

speaker: Ezio
en: I need to get closer!

speaker: Uberto
en: In the absence of any compelling evidence to the contrary, I am bound to pronounce you... GUILTY. You and your collaborators are hereby sentenced to death.

speaker: Giovanni
en: You are a traitor, Uberto – and one of them! You may take our lives this day – but we will have yours in return! I swear! We wil–

speaker: Ezio
en: Father!

speaker: Uberto
en: There! Grab the boy! He's one of them!

speaker: Ezio
en: I'll kill you for what you've done!

speaker: Uberto
en: Guards! Arrest him!

speaker: Uberto
en: Abbattetelo! (Put him down!)

speaker: Thief
en: You'd better run, boy. And fast!

speaker: Ezio
en: Buongiorno (Good day). Have you ladies heard of an art viewing somewhere in the city?

speaker: Claudia
en: You have returned to Roma!

speaker: Ezio
en: With just enough time to visit you.

speaker: Claudia
en: Ezio. Do not lie to me.

speaker: Ezio
en: I need to get inside a private showing of Da Vinci paintings.

speaker: Claudia
en: There is a viewing at the Castel Sant'Angelo later today. You will need an invitation. Fortunately, I know where you can procure one. It will give you access to the lower floors. Only cardinals are allowed higher.

speaker: Ezio
en: I knew I could count on you.

speaker: Claudia
en: Sì, sì. (Yes, yes.) Some of my girls will accompany you. Buona fortuna (Good luck) and don't get caught.

speaker: Ezio
en: The invitation is not here.

speaker: Courier
en: I will deliver it to Signore (Sir)!

speaker: Ezio
en: Got it!

speaker: Manuel
en: Ti sto diáolo simvéni? (What the hell is going on?)

speaker: Guard
en: Sabotage, Manuel. You need to take cover.

speaker: Manuel
en: Get out of my way. Citizens! Soldiers! Compose yourselves. Do not give in to fear! We are the true shepherds of Constantinopolis. We are the lords of this land. We are Byzantines. Kouráyo! (Have courage!) Stand fast! Do not let anyone break your

speaker: Manuel
en: Ah, Skatá. (Shit.) Stop that man! Cut him down!

speaker: Manuel
en: Stop and think for a moment! Think about the lives you have disrupted today, the anarchy you have sown here!

speaker: Manuel
en: You! You take advantage of a poor and displaced people, using us to further your own vain quest! But we fight for dignity, Assassin. We fight to restore peace to this troubled land.

speaker: Ezio
en: Templars are always quick to talk of peace, but very slow to concede power.

speaker: Manuel
en: Because power begets peace, vláka (idiot)! It cannot happen in reverse. These people would drown without a firm hand to lift them up, and keep them in line!

speaker: Ezio
en: There he is. The monster I came to kill.

speaker: Manuel
en: I should have been Constantine's successor. I had so many plans.

speaker: Ezio
en: Your dream dies with you, Manuel. Your empire is gone.

speaker: Manuel
en: Ah, but I am not the only one with this vision, Assassin. The dream of our Order is universal. Ottoman, Byzantine... these are only labels. Costumes and facades. Beneath these trappings, all Templars are part of the same family.

speaker: Ezio
en: Enough prattling. I am here for the Masyaf Key.

speaker: Manuel
en: Then take it. Take it and seek your fortune. See if you get within one hundred leagues of that library before one of us finishes you off.

speaker: Ezio
en: Thank you for coming.

speaker: Cristina
en: Of course, of course. Tell me, what can I do?

speaker: Ezio
en: My family's bodies... I can't just leave them hanging from the gallows. I need to give them last rites. Send them on to the next world...

speaker: Cristina
en: Capisco. (I understand.) Lead the way, Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: They've already been cut down!

speaker: Cristina
en: What are we going to do?

speaker: Ezio
en: Hide yourself. I'm going to have a little talk with that guard.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where are the bodies that hung here!?

speaker: Guard
en: They've already been taken!

speaker: Ezio
en: Where? Tell me where they are!

speaker: Guard
en: I don't know! I think they were taking them down to the river to dump them.

speaker: Ezio
en: No... (calling to Cristina) Cristina! Vieni con me! (Come with me!)

speaker: Cristina
en: What will you do?

speaker: Ezio
en: Only one thing to do. Kill them

speaker: Cristina
en: No! Don't do that. They did nothing wrong

speaker: Ezio
en: They follow orders unquestioningly. That makes them

speaker: Cristina
en: Ezio!

speaker: Ezio
en: Va bene. (It's okay.) I'll sneak behind their backs. Get my family, one at a time if I have to, and carry them down to the river.

speaker: Cristina
en: Be careful.

speaker: Ezio
en: I have to leave the city... Cristina, I want you to come with me.

speaker: Cristina
en: I want to... But I can't... My family...

speaker: Ezio
en: So we'll always be together, Cristina.

speaker: Cristina
en: Ezio...

speaker: Priest
en: Omnipotens Deus, Rex regum, et omnium gubernator...

speaker: Priest
en: Omnipotens Deus, Rex regum, et omnium gubernator, cujus potentiæ nulla creatura resistere potest, cui proprium est peccatores punire, et eorum misereri qui vere agunt pænitentiam, serva et libera nos, suppliciter te petimus, a manu inimicorum, reprime eorum superbiam, minue malitiam, dissipa illorum machinationes et astutias, ut nos tuis armis muniti semper servemur ab omnibus periculis, ad glorificandum te, qui es unicus victoriæ largitor: propter merita unigeniti filii tui Domini nostri Jesu Christi. Amen. Pater noster qui es in cælis, Sanctificetur nomen tuum. Adveniat regnum tuum. Fiat voluntas tua, sicut in cælo, et in terra. Panem nostrum quotidianum da nobis hodie. Et dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut et nos dimittimus debitoribus nostris. Et ne nos inducas in tentationem. Sed libera nos e malo. Amen. (O Almighty God, King of all Kings, and governor of all things, whose power no creature is able to resist, to whom it belongeth justly to punish sinners, and to be merciful unto them that truly repent: Save and deliver us, we humbly beseech thee, from the hands of our enemies; abate their pride, assuage their malice, and confound their devices; that we being armed with thy defence may be preserved evermore from all perils to glorify thee, which art the only giver of all victory, through the merits of thy only Son, Jesus Christ, our Lord. Amen. Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so on Earth. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation. But deliver us from evil. Amen.)

speaker: Priest
en: I thought Savonarola preached the word of God.

speaker: Ezio
en: I fear his sermon is a lie.

speaker: Priest
en: I led my flock astray... It's just... I wanted so badly to believe...

speaker: Ezio
en: We all do. Vedrò compiuta l'opera di mio padre (I will see my father's work complete)... Requiescat in pace (Rest in peace).

speaker: Ezio
en: I think it's best if I leave Firenze (Florence).

speaker: Paola
en: Where will you go?

speaker: Ezio
en: My uncle Mario owns a villa near Monteriggioni.

speaker: Paola
en: You're still a wanted man, Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: What would you have me do, then?

speaker: Paola
en: I've seen posters all across the district. Tearing them down will help the city forget your face. No doubt the heralds also incite the public. Bribe them and they'll speak of other things. Or you can hunt those who bear false witness against you. They traded dignity for coin. Their loss would not be mourned. Do any of these and you should be free to leave.

speaker: Leader of the Pack
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus 2.0.

speaker: Leader 1
en: We have recruited many new men to our cause.

speaker: Leader 2
en: I merely speak the name "Romulus" and they obey.

speaker: Captain
en: Bene. (Good.) Our prophecies move them, as predicted. Together, we will create a new religious harmony.

speaker: Captain
en: Assassino! (Assassin!) Mobilize your followers!

speaker: Leader 2
en: We must kill the Assassin! Romulus demands it!

speaker: Captain
en: Show him the strength of our faith! The evil of the Assassins must be silenced! Do not let him get the upper hand! Deliver him to Romulus! His death will purify our lair! Feel the spirit of Romulus enter you! Use it to guide your swords! Kill him and Romulus will return to bless all of us!

speaker: Captain
en: Spill his blood!

speaker: Leader 2
en: Wait for me!

speaker: Captain
en: Save yourself.

speaker: Captain
en: Your end is at hand, Assassin!

speaker: Captain
en: Appease Romulus! Kill him! Only Romulus can grant you peace. The Assassin! Kill him! A place in heaven awaits those who serve the wolf! Kill him and I will raise you up and teach you to speak to Romulus! Teach the unbeliever the truth! Romulus will punish those who do not fight!

speaker: Ezio
en: Did you learn all those lies from your Borgia masters?

speaker: Captain
en: I speak the truth, it is you who tell the people lies.

speaker: Ezio
en: Give me the code sheet.

speaker: Captain
en: All I will give you is death!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Bianca! Bianca!

speaker: Ezio
en: Is everything alright?

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: What do you think?! Look at this place! And poor Bianca... if something's happened to her...

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Ah-ha! Oh, my darling. Thank God you're alright. Ezio, meet Bianca. Bianca, Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: Charmed...

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: So, I know your name, but not why you are here.

speaker: Ezio
en: I have... business with Silvio Barbarigo. I was told you could help.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Ah! It would be my honor!

speaker: Ezio
en: But it's going to require more than just the two – er, three of us to weaken his forces. How do you suggest we proceed?

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: I'll go and ready my men for battle. While I do this, I'd like you to rescue those who were captured during Silvio's assault. I cannot, in good conscience, leave them behind.

speaker: Ezio
en: Intesi (Understood). I will attend to it at once.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Good luck out there, Ezio.

speaker: Guard 1
en: What to do with this lot?

speaker: Guard 2
en: Flood the cage, I say. Drown them all and be done with it!

speaker: Guard 3
en: Silvio wants them alive. Thinks he can turn them to our cause.

speaker: Guard 2
en: I wouldn't count on it. They're as loyal as they are stupid.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Many thanks for the aid, friend! We'd like to fight with you - if you'll have us?

speaker: Guard 4
en: Your master's in chains and your company broken. Come tomorrow, you'll all be hanged!

speaker: Mercenary
en: So be it! We are prepared to die with honor!

speaker: Guard 4
en: Hah! The only things you'll be dying with are soiled breeches and broken necks!

speaker: Mercenary
en: We are with you friend! Only lead the way!

speaker: Guard 5
en: Poor bastard. I heard Marco made him the way he is.

speaker: Guard 6
en: And now he's been passed to Silvio. Like a dog.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Let us join you! Together we will crush the Barbarigo!

speaker: Worker
en: How long do you expect us to work with such petty wages?

speaker: Papal Guard
en: When the aqueduct is restored, we use it to take the treasure out of the quarry. Then, you will be paid well for your efforts.

speaker: Worker
en: Enough with the same lies! I say we get back what belongs to us! Who's with me?!

speaker: Papal Guard
en: This is what happens to rebels. Let it serve as a warning to all of you. Now get back to work!

speaker: Ezio
en: I wonder what that mechanism does. Maybe I can shoot it from here?

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene. (Good.) Now, I hope it will not snap under my weight.

speaker: Ezio
en: That could help if I fall.

speaker: Ezio
en: Now... how to get water to this wheel? I must find another vantage point.

speaker: Ezio
en: That one is set. Now to align the other one. Seems I need to redirect the flow from the cistern.

speaker: Ezio
en: Done.

speaker: Ezio
en: Merda! (Shit!) Perhaps this device can help me get up?

speaker: Ezio
en: There is a waterwheel back there, but this brake locks it in place.

speaker: Ezio
en: Done. I'm sure Leonardo would be impressed.

speaker: Papal Guard
en: What is wrong with you Italians?

speaker: Papal Guard
en: The Assassin! Protect me!

speaker: Ezio
en: Why not come down and fight, coward?

speaker: Papal Guard
en: Twice this sum goes to the man who kills him!

speaker: Papal Guard
en: Money makes the world go round, eh, Assassin?

speaker: Papal Guard
en: You kill guards, but will you kill innocent workers?

speaker: Papal Guard
en: That machine is useless!

speaker: Papal Guard
en: More of my men are on their way. Surrender now and I let you live.

speaker: Papal Guard
en: Scheisse! (Shit!)

speaker: Papal Guard
en: Ha! You missed.

speaker: Papal Guard
en: Wait, stop! What have you done?!

speaker: Papal Guard
en: I have to get out of here!

speaker: Papal Guard
en: Forget the treasure. I will be granted riches beyond belief when I bring Cesare your head!

speaker: Ezio
en: Perhaps I will send him yours.

speaker: Papal Guard
en: Nein! Nein! Nein! (No! No! No!)

speaker: Sofia
en: Enjoying the poem?

speaker: Ezio
en: Who were these men he condemned to hell?

speaker: Sofia
en: Political opponents, men who wronged him. Alighieri's quill cuts deeply, no?

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì. (Yes.) It is a subtle way to seek revenge.

speaker: Sofia
en: Ezio. I plan to make a trip to Adrianopoli in a few weeks to visit a new printing press there.

speaker: Ezio
en: That should be fun.

speaker: Sofia
en: It is a five or six day ride from here, and I will need an escort...

speaker: Ezio
en: Prego? (Pardon?)

speaker: Sofia
en: I'm sorry. You are a busy man.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sofia, I would love to accompany you, but my time is running short.

speaker: Sofia
en: That is true for all of us. Well, I can try to solve this last code now, but I need to run an errand before sundown. Can you wait a day?

speaker: Ezio
en: What do you need?

speaker: Sofia
en: It is silly but... a bouquet of fresh flowers. White tulips, specifically.

speaker: Ezio
en: I can get you the flowers. Nessun problema. (No problem.)

speaker: Sofia
en: Are you sure?

speaker: Ezio
en: It will be a nice change of pace.

speaker: Sofia
en: Bene. (Okay.) Meet me in the park east of Ayasofya (Hagia Sophia) and we will trade. Flowers for information.

speaker: Merchant
en: You look like a man with money to spend. What do you need, dostum (my friend)?

speaker: Ezio
en: Tulips. White, if you have them.

speaker: Merchant
en: Ah, tulips! Forgive me, but I am fresh out. Something else, perhaps?

speaker: Ezio
en: It is not my call, unfortunately.

speaker: Merchant
en: All right, listen. I may know where to get fresh tulips. You wait here and I will return. One hour. Two at most...

speaker: Ezio
en: I am not waiting an hour.

speaker: Ezio
en: What is this?

speaker: Sofia
en: A gift. Sit.

speaker: Sofia
en: Che belli, grazie. (These are nice, thank you.) I wanted to thank you for letting me play a small role in your adventure.

speaker: Ezio
en: A small role is enough for this adventure, believe me.

speaker: Sofia
en: You are a mystery, Ezio Auditore.

speaker: Ezio
en: Mi dispiace. (I'm sorry.) I do not mean to be.

speaker: Sofia
en: It is fine. È affascinante. (It's attractive.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Sembra squisito. (Looks delicious.)

speaker: Sofia
en: Why, thank you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Any luck with the final code?

speaker: Sofia
en: Ah, the code. Sì. (Yes.) I solved it many hours ago. You will get it soon enough.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Ezio, I will lead you to three ambassadors. They are here to meet with the Pope, but will answer to God much sooner than they expect. Allow me to lure them out before you strike.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Hans! You asked me if I had any friends you could play with! I have invited one!

speaker: Ambassador 1
en: Who? Where is she?

speaker: Courtesan
en: Wait right there! (To Ezio) Follow.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Salve, amore (Hello, lover).

speaker: Ambassador 2
en: This is inappropriate.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Not compared to what I plan to do to you.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Oh, there you are! Follow me, I have something to show you.

speaker: Brute
en: If he won't go, I will.

speaker: Ambassador 3
en: No, I will take care of this.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Here we are.

speaker: Ambassador 3
en: What are you planning, woman?

speaker: Courtesan
en: Patience. Wait here.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Addio (Goodbye), Ezio. Stay safe.

speaker: Guard Captain
en: Tell your comrades that only Eduardo may examine the invention up close to make the final adjustments.

speaker: Guard
en: Yes, Capitano. (Captain.)

speaker: Guard Captain
en: He travels by boat to see the mechanism now.

speaker: Ezio
en: Give me the plans.

speaker: Eduardo
en: You are the Assassin, am I right? You must stop Cesare. I will help you. Let me take you to them.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie. (Thank you.)

speaker: Eduardo
en: Join the papal army, she said. Easy work. Good pay. Now look at me... Capitano di questa barca di merda! (Captain of the shit boat!)

speaker: Eduardo
en: How will I ever get used to the smell? Fantastic! A new stench! As if the old one was not foul enough. Could Cesare find a worse task for me?

speaker: Gatekeeper
en: Oh puzza (stink), smell that? Eduardo has arrived. Open the gate!

speaker: Guard
en: Is the cannon ready for testing?

speaker: Eduardo
en: We are working day and night. My men cannot go any faster.

speaker: Guard
en: I asked, is it ready?

speaker: Eduardo
en: Nearly ready.

speaker: Guard
