en: Then you should stay tonight as well.

speaker: Ezio
en: Let us see if you can bite your master's hand, shall we?

speaker: Ezio
en: Perdonatemi (Forgive me), Leonardo.

speaker: Ezio
en: Arkadeshim (My friend), you look distracted.

speaker: Thief
en: Quite. I have a lot on my mind. Someone in this district is funding a campaign to get us arrested.

speaker: Ezio
en: How so?

speaker: Thief
en: Well-placed bribes to Ottoman guards, tipping them off to our actions. We do not want a conflict with our hosts, but we are not keen to surrender to them either.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do you have an idea where this money is coming from?

speaker: Thief
en: I hope to find out today. Would you care to aid me? I will make it worth your while.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì. (Yes.) How can I help?

speaker: Thief
en: We know that the Ottomans were paid a large bribe today. We are going to steal it. Once that happens, someone is sure to send an urgent message back to the money's source. Follow the messenger, and we will have our man.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where is HE going...?

speaker: Halim
en: What are you doing here! I told you to keep an eye on those soldiers!

speaker: Snitch
en: Forgive me, Halim Bey (Lord Halim), but thieves have stolen the bribe.

speaker: Halim
en: What!? How did they know?

speaker: Snitch
en: I am not sure.

speaker: Halim
en: If our contacts in the Ottoman ranks do not get their money, we do not keep our special relationship intact.

speaker: Snitch
en: B-but... what could I do?

speaker: Halim
en: Nothing, obviously. You're just a worm. Now get out of my face.

speaker: Halim
en: It is an insult that I should pay so much to gain so little. Keep your eyes open for those sneaky thieves. They may be coming for us next. Perhaps my informant is not so crooked as he needs to be. We will not be using him again. What is my next move? Think, damn you, think! I should move to Bursa. This city is too diverse. Too messy.

speaker: Ezio
en: You got away with the money?

speaker: Thief
en: Evet (Yes), about half of it. The rest we distributed to the people. It keeps them... honest.

speaker: Ezio
en: Just make sure you do not turn into the criminals you are fighting.

speaker: Thief
en: Point taken. Why don't you stick around and keep us in line.

speaker: Ezio
en: I will call on you when I need a favor. You can count on that.

speaker: Altaïr
en: You have seen to my books?

speaker: Darim
en: Yes. Some we sent with the Polos. The rest will go with me to Alexandria.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Good. Very good.

speaker: Darim
en: Father, I do not understand... Why did you build a library if you did not intend to keep your books

speaker: Altaïr
en: You should go. When the Mongols return, Masyaf must be empty.

speaker: Darim
en: I see. This is not a library at all. It is a vault.

speaker: Altaïr
en: It must stay hidden, Darim. Far from eager hands. At least until it has passed on the secret it contains.

speaker: Darim
en: What secret?

speaker: Altaïr
en: Go, son. Go be with your family, and live well.

speaker: Darim
en: All that is good in me, began with you, father.

speaker: Al Mualim
en: In much wisdom, is much grief. And he that increaseth knowledge, increaseth sorrow.

speaker: Maria
en: What does it tell you? What do you see?

speaker: Altaïr
en: Strange visions and messages. Of ones who came before, of their rise, and their fall...

speaker: Maria
en: But what happens to us, Altaïr? To our family! What does the Apple say?

speaker: Altaïr
en: Who were the ones who came before? What brought them here? How long ago?

speaker: Maria
en: Get rid of that thing!

speaker: Altaïr
en: This is my duty, Maria! Maria? Where... where are you? Where is she!

speaker: Darim
en: Gone, father. You do not remember? She's gone!

speaker: Altaïr
en: If you are asked, say I sent the Apple away. Tell them I sent it to Cyprus, or Cipango, or that I dropped it into the sea. Tell them anything to keep men away from this place. This Apple must not be found, not until the time is right.

speaker: Thief
en: Ezio, you must help my brother, Aldo! Those banditi (bandits) took him, please! He only picks pockets, he's never harmed anyone.

speaker: Captain
en: Kill him!

speaker: Aldo
en: Grazie a Dio! Grazie a Dio! (Thank God! Thank God!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Manfredo!? What happened!?

speaker: Manfredo
en: Men... Savonarola's men... They came through, destroying everything.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where is Cristina!? Manfredo! WHERE IS SHE!

speaker: Manfredo
en: She ran... They went after her!

speaker: Guard 1
en: Whore! Where are your riches now?

speaker: Guard 2
en: Your fancy house, your expensive dress! They are sins against the Lord!

speaker: Cristina
en: Leave me alone! Get away! I did nothing to you!

speaker: Guard 2
en: Savonarola will see all you sinners burn!

speaker: Guard 1
en: You should have submitted to Savonarola when you were told to!

speaker: Cristina
en: Help me! Someone, help! Ezio–!?

speaker: Ezio
en: Cristina! RUN!

speaker: Ezio
en: Cristina... Hold on! I'll get you to a doctor... You're going to be all right.

speaker: Cristina
en: No... Ezio... I don't think I am...

speaker: Ezio
en: No! Don't... Don't go... Stay with me, Cristina.

speaker: Cristina
en: Ezio... Don't you know...? I've always been with you.

speaker: Cristina
en: I wish we... could have had... a second chance.

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in pace (Rest in peace) my love.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Ezio, my sister has been poisoned. A larger dose of the drug they used on me. We know who sells it. A street doctor named Tommaso. He has the antidote, but not for sale. You must find another way! Hurry, Flora's time grows short!

speaker: Courtesan
en: Ezio, you saved my sister's life. Grazie (Thank you)!

speaker: Ezio
en: All letters are delivered.

speaker: Copernicus
en: While you were gone, I determined the most likely source of these strange attacks. The Master of the Sacred Palace.

speaker: Ezio
en: Who is that?

speaker: Copernicus
en: A Dominican appointed by the Pope who ensures that Roman religious philosophy remains pure. He never liked my studies to begin with, now that I have crossed the Templars he has clearly retaliated.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where can I find him?

speaker: Copernicus
en: Cardinals typically congregate nearby. Follow one of them. The Master likes to greet each one. Perhaps you will hear more conclusive evidence.

speaker: Giuliano
en: Master.

speaker: Cardinal
en: Giuliano. Any news of Copernico and the others?

speaker: Giuliano
en: Nothing.

speaker: Cardinal
en: Those fools, inundating the people with their theories. We can barely contain the populace as it is. I have dispatched my best guards to deal with them. I trust they will make quick work of it.

speaker: Ezio
en: I must stop them.

speaker: Caterina
en: Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where is Machiavelli?

speaker: Caterina
en: I could not find him.

speaker: La Volpe
en: I brought the Contessa (Countess) here.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Caterina.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Care to tell us where you have been?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Looking for Ezio. What of Cesare and Rodrigo?

speaker: Ezio
en: Cesare rode off before I could get close to him and Rodrigo was somewhere else entirely.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: That is odd. Rodrigo is usually at the Castello.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Very odd indeed.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: What a waste. No offense.

speaker: Caterina
en: None taken.

speaker: Ezio
en: With Cesare gone to Urbino, we must build our forces.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: I thought we intended to strike now?

speaker: Caterina
en: Impossible. Cesare commands a massive army in Romagna. You would never reach him.

speaker: Ezio
en: I say we work here. In Roma. Erode the Borgia's influence while restoring our own. And in fact, I want to begin right now. Volpe, bring Claudia and Bartolomeo here. Machiavelli, meet me outside.

speaker: Ezio
en: Take care of her.

speaker: Ezio
en: Look. The Borgia rob everything from the people to maintain power.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: What do you intend to do?

speaker: Ezio
en: We will recruit them to our cause.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: You can not be serious.

speaker: Ezio
en: To win this war, Machiavelli, we need loyal soldiers. By recruiting enemies of the state, we arm those who have been disarmed by the Borgia.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Go then. Recruit our first novices.

speaker: Man
en: Assassin!

speaker: Ezio
en: The Liberation of Roma has begun. If you choose to flee, do so now, but if you choose to fight, stand with me against the Borgia.

speaker: Man
en: I am tired of hiding in the shadows. I will join you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then seek Niccolò Machiavelli on Isola Tiberina (Tiber Island) and we will make you one of us. Their lies will no longer mask your truth.

speaker: Mark and Execute
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Minerva
en: It is done. The message is delivered. We are gone now from this world. All of us. We can do no more. The rest is up to you... Desmond.

speaker: Ezio
en: What? Who is Desmond? I don't understand! Please, wait! I have so many questions!

speaker: Mario
en: Better in the hands of the earth than in the hands of man.

speaker: Ezio
en: Uncle?

speaker: Mario
en: What can I say? We sent a single man against an entire army! I was worried! Quick, climb up. We have to get out of here.

speaker: Ezio
en: You would not believe the things I have seen, Mario.

speaker: Mario
en: Then be sure to stay alive that I might hear of them.

speaker: Ezio
en: I expect opposition.

speaker: Mario
en: And I expect the Borgia to mourn the loss of many lives tonight.

speaker: Priest 1
en: Che cosa fate qui (What are you doing here)?

speaker: Priest 2
en: Assassini (Assassins)! God will see you pay for your crimes!

speaker: Priest 3
en: You have desecrated the sanctity of this holy place!

speaker: Ezio
en: You condemn what you do not understand!

speaker: Mario
en: We must go, Ezio. Now!

speaker: Priest 4
en: His is the voice of the devil!

speaker: Priest 5
en: Turn away from them!

speaker: Mario
en: Did Rodrigo manage to hurt you?

speaker: Ezio
en: Barely. My armor blunted his attack.

speaker: Cardinal
en: For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places. Wherefore take unto you the whole armor of God, and the shield of faith, wherewith you shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked.

speaker: Mario
en: Be ready to fight.

speaker: Ezio
en: What are you doing?!

speaker: Mario
en: Saving you, from the looks of things.

speaker: Ezio
en: Not bad for an old man.

speaker: Mario
en: Agreed! You still have some skill.

speaker: Ezio
en: Buona questa (Good one).

speaker: Mario
en: Excellent! Good one! Impressive!

speaker: Mario
en: This decision is yours alone to make. Only do so quickly. Give it to me. You can do with it as you will later.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene (Good).

speaker: Mario
en: Jump!

speaker: Luis
en: Ezio, thank you for all you have done.

speaker: Ezio
en: I'm glad to see you safe, Christoffa, but I am not here to further your interests. I have questions of my own.

speaker: Christoffa
en: I won't have many answers. Borgia was merely a financial opportunity. I didn't know him personally.

speaker: Luis
en: But you may have another chance to find him. Tell him, Christoffa...

speaker: Christoffa
en: The Spaniard discovered our lodgings. Our hostel is crawling with his soldiers. They are searching for an atlas of significant worth, containing maps charting a Western route to the Orient.

speaker: Luis
en: We are prepared to leave Italia for good, but not without that Atlas. In the wrong hands, it could cause great harm.

speaker: Ezio
en: Va bene. But this will be my final favor.

speaker: Luis
en: Thank you Ezio. We will wait for your return in the harbor district.

speaker: Meeting Adjourned
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Patrizio
en: You are here for the painting?

speaker: Marco
en: Yes, Patrizio.

speaker: Patrizio
en: That puttana (whore) sent it to me as a present. I want it out of my house.

speaker: Marco
en: We will be glad to add it to our collection. As agreed, the Master waits at your palazzo to take it off your hands.

speaker: Patrizio
en: She thought I would be pleased with such a gift? After she married another man?

speaker: Marco
en: The ways of men and women are strange, but Hermes teaches us that through careful study, both may be brought to harmony.

speaker: Patrizio
en: Doubtless, one such as Lucrezia has never crossed your path.

speaker: Patrizio
en: What is it? What's going on?

speaker: Marco
en: Damned peasants!

speaker: Patrizio
en: Come with me.

speaker: Ercole
en: You will complete the sale?

speaker: Patrizio
en: Of course. That woman used false passion to seduce me. The error lies in her Spanish blood, I know it.

speaker: Ercole
en: Such untruths you so carefully utter, based on little more than a name. These countries, these groups, make such easy targets for the lazy and ignorant.

speaker: Patrizio
en: You should tell her that, the high and mighty Duchessa (Duchess). Puttana! (Whore!) I have changed my mind. That painting does not deserve to belong to anyone.

speaker: Ercole
en: Take the painting and examine it for clues. Be careful. Human hands aided by a fierce intelligence made that. Treat it with respect. Go!

speaker: Altaïr
en: Are you hurt?

speaker: Faisal
en: Broken foot.

speaker: Faisal
en: What is your name, brother?

speaker: Altaïr
en: Altaïr. Son of Umar.

speaker: Faisal
en: Umar... ah yes. He was a fine man who lived as he died. With honor.

speaker: Abbas
en: Altaïr! We have been betrayed. The enemy has overrun the castle!

speaker: Altaïr
en: You'll live.

speaker: Altaïr
en: And Al Mualim? Where is he?

speaker: Abbas
en: He was inside when the crusaders broke through. We can do nothing for him now. Altaïr! We must fall back!

speaker: Altaïr
en: When I close the castle gate, flank the crusaders in the village and drive them into the canyon.

speaker: Abbas
en: You don't stand a chance!

speaker: Altaïr
en: Abbas. No mistakes.

speaker: Haras
en: Another step and your Mentor dies.

speaker: Altaïr
en: You will not leave this place alive, traitor.

speaker: Haras
en: No. You misunderstand. I am no traitor... for I cannot betray those I never truly loved.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Then you are doubly wretched, for you have been living a lie.

speaker: Haras
en: Now you call on your lapdog to protect you? You disappoint me. Why not share what you have learned with everyone, like a proper Assassin? Why not share with your brothers the true extent of your ambition? Where is your sense of fraternity?

speaker: Haras
en: Another good man dies, and still you say nothing! I am surprised. You taught me many things Al Mualim, but patience was not one of them. Speak now, or I will cut out your tongue that you may speak no more! Your time is running out, old man. Tell me what you know of the artifact! Tell me where you are searching for it. It is a small price to pay to preserve what you have built here, no? Even if you found the artifact, what good would it do you, eh? You have neither the skill nor the breeding to wield its full powers. In your hands it would be a seductive and powerful weapon, yes... but nothing more.

speaker: Haras
en: There now! Three men dead because you refuse to talk. Your silence will be the death of you too, Assassin. My Master wants answers. And if he does not get them, he will gladly take your head!

speaker: Haras
en: You put too much faith in the hearts of men, Altaïr. The Templars know the truth. Humans are weak, base, and petty.

speaker: Altaïr
en: No. Our Creed is evidence to the contrary.

speaker: Haras
en: Ah... perhaps I am not wise enough to understand, but I suspect the opposite. That I am too wise to believe such rubbish.

speaker: Al Mualim
en: You offered him a chance to salvage his dignity. Why?

speaker: Altaïr
en: No man should pass from this world without knowing some kindness.

speaker: Al Mualim
en: But he shunned your graces.

speaker: Altaïr
en: As was his right.

speaker: Al Mualim
en: Altaïr, I have watched you grow from a boy to a man in so short a time, it fills me with as much sadness as pride. You fit your father's shoes as if they had been tailored to your feet.

speaker: Altaïr
en: I did not know him well as a father. He was an Assassin above all.

speaker: Al Mualim
en: You too were born into this Order. Do you regret it?

speaker: Altaïr
en: How can I regret the only life I have ever known?

speaker: Al Mualim
en: You may find a way, in time. And it will be up to you to choose the path you prefer. Come, my boy... and ready your blade. This battle is not yet won.

speaker: Cemal
en: They say he screams in his sleep, calling out for his father.

speaker: Assassin
en: Abbas. What a miserable man.

speaker: Tazim
en: It is not our place to judge.

speaker: Cemal
en: It certainly is. If our master has gone mad, I would like to know.

speaker: Teragani
en: Hush... Good evening.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Water.

speaker: Cemal
en: Of course. Sit.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Many thanks.

speaker: Assassin
en: What brings you here, old man?

speaker: Altaïr
en: Pity Abbas, do not mock him. He has lived as an orphan for most of his life, shamed by his family's legacy. He is desperate for power because he is powerless.

speaker: Tazim
en: He is our Mentor! And unlike Al Mualim or Altaïr, he never betrayed us!

speaker: Teragani
en: Nonsense! Altaïr was no traitor. He was driven out. Unjustly.

speaker: Teragani
en: Is it... is it you? I heard rumors, but I did not believe them.

speaker: Altaïr
en: I wonder if I might speak with Abbas myself. It has been a long time.

speaker: Cemal
en: Impossible. Abbas uses rogue Fedayeen to keep us from the castle.

speaker: Assassin
en: Fewer than half the fighters here are true Assassins.

speaker: Altaïr
en: So where do I begin?

speaker: Cemal
en: With us.

speaker: Altaïr
en: You say these men are cruel. Has anyone raised his blade against an innocent?

speaker: Cemal
en: Alas, yes. Brutality seems to be their sole joy.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Then they will die, for they have compromised the Order. But those who still live by the Creed must be spared.

speaker: Assassin
en: You can trust in us.

speaker: Loyal Assassin 1
en: Mentor!

speaker: Altaïr
en: Welcome.

speaker: Loyal Assassin 2
en: Hush! We do not want to get him killed!

speaker: Altaïr
en: You could have been spared, friend.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Follow me to the castle. And spill no blood if you can help it.

speaker: Loyal Captain
en: Altaïr, two decades have passed since we last saw you within these walls. We could use your wisdom, now more than ever.

speaker: Abbas
en: Kill him! Kill him now! What are you waiting for! You fools! He has bewitched you!

speaker: Assassin
en: Our mentor has returned!

speaker: Altaïr
en: Tell your men to stand down.

speaker: Abbas
en: No! I am defending Masyaf! Would you not do the same?

speaker: Altaïr
en: You corrupted everything we stand for, and lost everything we gained. All of it, sacrificed on the altar of your own spite.

speaker: Abbas
en: And you, you have wasted your life staring into that Apple, dreaming of your own glory!

speaker: Altaïr
en: That is true, Abbas. I learned many things from the Apple. Of life and death, of the past and the future. Let me show you...

speaker: Abbas
en: I can never forgive you Altaïr. The lies you told about my family, my father. The humiliation I suffered.

speaker: Altaïr
en: They were not lies, Abbas. I was ten years old when your father came to see me. He was in tears, begging to be forgiven for betraying my family. Then he cut his own throat. I watched his life ebb away at my feet. I will never forget that image.

speaker: Abbas
en: No.

speaker: Altaïr
en: But he was not a coward, Abbas. He reclaimed his honor.

speaker: Abbas
en: I hope there is another life after this one. Then I will see him, and know the truth of his final days... And when it is your time, we will find you, and then there will be no doubts.

speaker: Assassin
en: Is it truly over? Is that sorcerer dead?

speaker: Altaïr
en: He was no sorcerer. Just an ordinary man in command of illusions. Have you prepared the pyre?

speaker: Assassin
en: I have, but... Altaïr... some of the men, will not stand for such a thing.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Let me handle it.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Are you fit to travel?

speaker: Assassin
en: Well enough, yes.

speaker: Altaïr
en: I asked Malik to ride to Jerusalem with the news of Al Mualim's death. Would you ride to Acre and do the same?

speaker: Assassin
en: Of course.

speaker: Abbas
en: What has happened here?

speaker: Altaïr
en: Our Mentor deceived us all. The Templars corrupted him.

speaker: Abbas
en: Where is your proof?

speaker: Altaïr
en: Walk with me, Abbas, and I will explain.

speaker: Abbas
en: And if I find your answers wanting?

speaker: Altaïr
en: I will talk until you are satisfied. Do you remember the artifact we recovered from Robert de Sablé in Solomon's Temple?

speaker: Abbas
en: The artifact you were sent to retrieve, but others delivered?

speaker: Altaïr
en: Yes. It is a Templar tool, the Apple of Eden. It can conjure illusions and control men's minds. A deadly weapon.

speaker: Abbas
en: And you believe Al Mualim fell under its spell?

speaker: Altaïr
en: I do. Today he used the Apple to enslave Masyaf. You saw that for yourself.

speaker: Abbas
en: I do not know what I saw.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Listen, Abbas. The Apple is safe in Al Mualim's study. When I am finished here, I will show you all I know.

speaker: Abbas
en: Altaïr! No!

speaker: Altaïr
en: I must know that he cannot return.

speaker: Abbas
en: But this is not ! To burn a man's body is !

speaker: Citizen
en: Defiler!

speaker: Altaïr
en: Hear me out! This body could be another one of Al Mualim's phantoms! I must be certain!

speaker: Abbas
en: Lies! All your life you have made a mockery of our Creed! You bend the rules to suit your whims, while belittling and humiliating those around you!

speaker: Citizen
en: Restrain him!

speaker: Assassin
en: Did you not hear him? Al Mualim is bewitched!

speaker: Abbas
en: What did I tell you, Altaïr?

speaker: Altaïr
en: Abbas! Stop!

speaker: Abbas
en: What did you think would happen when you murdered our beloved Mentor?

speaker: Altaïr
en: You loved Al Mualim less than anyone! You blamed him for all your misfortune, even your father's suicide!

speaker: Abbas
en: My father was a hero!

speaker: Altaïr
en: This is not the time to quarrel over the past. We must decide what to do with that weapon!

speaker: Abbas
en: Whatever this artifact is capable of, you are not worthy to wield it.

speaker: Altaïr
en: No man is!

speaker: Abbas
en: Ahhh, it IS beautiful, is it not?

speaker: Abbas
en: Ah...

speaker: Assassin
en: What was that? Are they dead?

speaker: Abbas
en: F-forgive me... I did not know...

speaker: Altaïr
en: Have you anything to teach us? Or will you lead us all to ruin?

speaker: The Merchant of Rome
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Ezio
en: Another artifact? No. You will stay here. I have seen enough for one life.

speaker: Ezio
en: Desmond?

speaker: Desmond
en: He's talking to me?

speaker: Ezio
en: I heard your name once before, Desmond, a long time ago. And now it lingers in my mind like an image from an old dream. I do not know where you are, or by what means you can hear me. But I know you are listening.

speaker: Ezio
en: I have lived my life as best I could, not knowing its purpose, but drawn forward like a moth to a distant moon. And here, at last, I discover a strange truth. That I am only a conduit for a message that eludes my understanding. Who are we, who have been so blessed to share our stories like this? To speak across centuries? Maybe you will answer all the questions I have asked. Maybe you will be the one to make all this suffering worth something in the end.

speaker: Ezio
en: Now... listen...

speaker: Jupiter
en: Do you hear me, cipher? Can you see me?

speaker: Jupiter
en: Ah. There you are. Good. A strange place, this nexus of time. I am not used to the... calculations. That has always been Minerva's domain. I see you still have many questions. Who were we? What became of us? What do we desire of you? You will have your answers. Only listen and I will tell you how.

speaker: Jupiter
en: Both before the end and after, we sought to save the world. We built vaults within which to work, each dedicated to a different method of salvation. They were placed underground to avoid the war which raged above, and also as a precaution, should we fail in our efforts. Each vault's knowledge was transmitted into a single place

speaker: Jupiter
en: It was our duty... mine, Minerva's and Juno's—to sort and sample all that was collected. We chose those solutions which held the most promise, and devoted ourselves to testing their merits. Six we tried in succession, each more encouraging than the last. But none worked. And then the world ended...

speaker: Jupiter
en: The earth shook for days. The fires burned for weeks. And when the ash had settled, less than ten thousand of your kind still lived... and far fewer of ours. But we carried on, together. To rebuild. To renew.

speaker: Jupiter
en: Listen. You must go there. To the place where we labored... labored and lost. Take my words. Pass them from your head into your hands. That is how you will open the way. But be warned: much still remains in flux. And I do not know how things will end—either in my time or yours.

speaker: Andrea
en: Could you deliver this for me? It must be done quickly, but there is a reward.

speaker: Farmer
en: Vattene! Via del mio terreno! (Go away! Get off my land!)

speaker: Savonarola
en: God bears witness to this sacrilege! That you would handle his prophet this way! Blasphemers! Heretics! You'll burn for this. DO YOU HEAR ME? You'll BURN!

speaker: Savonarola
en: O Lord, show mercy... Deliver me from evil's embrace... Surrounded as I am by sin, I cry out to you for salvation.

speaker: Ezio
en: No one deserves to die in such pain.

speaker: Savonarola
en: Infelix ego, omnium auxillio destitutus, qui coelum terramque offendi: quo ibo? Quo me vertem? Ad quem confugiam? Quis mei miserebitur? Ad coelum levare oculos non audeo. Quia ei graviter peccavi. In terra refugium non invenio. Quia si scandalum... (Unhappy me, devoid of any help, I who offended heaven and earth: where will I go? Where shall I turn? Should I flee, and where? Who will take pity on me? I do not dare to lift my eyes to heaven. Because I grievously sinned against it. On earth, I find no refuge. Because if the offense...)

speaker: Savonarola
en: It's you. I knew this day would come. Please, show mercy!

speaker: Ezio
en: I have. Va' ora – che sia il tuo Dio a giudicarti. Requiescat in pace. (Go now – that you may be judged by your God. Rest in peace.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Silenzio. Silenzio. (Silence. Silence.) Twenty-two years ago, I stood where I stand now – and watched my loved ones die, betrayed by those I had called friends. Vengeance clouded my mind. It would have consumed me, were it not for the wisdom of a few strangers, who taught me to look past my instincts. They never preached answers, but guided me to learn from myself. We don't need anyone to tell us what to do; not Savonarola, not the Medici. We are free to follow our own path. There are those who will take that freedom from us, and too many of you gladly give it. But it is our ability to choose – whatever you think is true – that makes us human... There is no book or teacher to give you the answers, to show you the path. Choose your own way! Do not follow me, or anyone else.

speaker: Ezio
en: Salute, Rosa (Hello, Rosa). You seem to be healing well.

speaker: Rosa
en: How are you finding Venezia?

speaker: Ezio
en: It has its charms. But how do you deal with the smell? Che schifo (How disgusting)!

speaker: Rosa
en: So, what brings you to me?

speaker: Ezio
en: I was hoping you could help me with something.

speaker: Rosa
en: And that would be...?

speaker: Ezio
en: I want to learn to climb the way you do.

speaker: Rosa
en: Oh. Va bene (Alright.) I can do that. Well, I can't, but Franco can. Franco! Muovi il culo (move your ass)! Show Ezio how to reach the top of that scaffolding.

speaker: Rosa
en: Begin in a hanging position then jump to the ledge above you. As you reach it, grab it with your hand and pull yourself up. There. See how it works?

speaker: Ezio
en: I think so...

speaker: Rosa
en: Only one way to find out. Try it yourself. Jump, Ezio! Grab the ledge at the height of your jump!

speaker: Ezio
en: So? How did I do?

speaker: Rosa
en: I've seen better.

speaker: Ezio
en: Ah! You wound me with your cruel, cruel words!

speaker: Rosa
en: Alright, smargiasso (show off), let's put your skills to the test.

speaker: Ezio
en: I'm all ears!

speaker: Rosa
en: Meet me in front of the Frari!

speaker: Ezio
en: Seraphina has a head start, but she does not know these tunnels like I do.

speaker: Ezio
en: An old note. The paper is faded. It seems to be a list of prisoners, from when these tunnels were used as a jail. Some names I recognize. Others I do not.

speaker: Seraphina
en: Should we not have ensured Ezio was dead? We do not need him on our scent like a dog.

speaker: Civilian
en: Signore (Sir) Ezio rests with his ancestors.

speaker: Seraphina
en: I hope you are right.

speaker: Civilian
en: Fear not. My men have been exploring these tunnels for weeks. There are more than enough of them to stop him, should he have survived.

speaker: Ezio
en: I can still move when I need to.

speaker: Ezio
en: Ah! This is too far even for me to jump. There must be another way across... Or some way to bridge the gap.

speaker: Ezio
en: These tunnels are old. It is a pity they have been overlooked for so long.

speaker: Ezio
en: This one is unaware of me. A fine target for my blade.

speaker: Matteo
en: I'm not going back to Rizzo empty handed. If there's anything valuable down here, I'm taking it with me. "It could be dangerous, Matteo." Pah–tell it to someone else. I want to be rich.

speaker: Civilian
en: Come on, we must keep moving.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: We're right behind you.

speaker: Ezio
en: A note from a servant. The paper is old, almost falling apart. "Three crates of apples, two wheels of cheese"... It's just a shopping list. Times were easier back then–but maybe it always feels that way.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Matteo wouldn't listen. He wanted to search for "treasure".

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: What we already took from the Villa wasn't enough?

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Not for him.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Then good luck to him. Seraphina says the Assassin could be right behind us.

speaker: Civilian
en: Calm yourself, codardo (coward). He is just one man–

speaker: Seraphina
en: –who just happens to be a Master Assassin.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Please, Seraphina. You have the treasure you need to find the Kerukeion in Venice. You say eternal life shall be ours. Until then, trust me to handle our escape.

speaker: Seraphina
en: You better, or these tunnels will be our doom.

speaker: Ezio
en: This will help with rebuilding Monteriggioni, but for now there are more pressing matters at hand.

speaker: Seraphina
en: We can't stay here.

speaker: Civilian
en: Why not? You still think Ezio is alive?

speaker: Seraphina
en: I'm sure of it.

speaker: Civilian
en: Come now. He was tired, outnumbered, and his best years are behind him. The men I sent to meet him were killers, every one of them. He cannot have survived.

speaker: Seraphina
en: The Assassins are unlike any enemy you've faced before. I expected your men to delay Ezio, and give us time to escape. Let us not delude ourselves bu hoping for more.

speaker: Civilian
en: I hope you're wrong, but Rizzo won't pay us if we perish in these tunnels, will he?

speaker: Seraphina
en: Exactly. We are to return to Venice with the treasure. Nothing else matters.

speaker: Civilian
en: Then what do we do about Alberto?

speaker: Alberto
en: Yes, what about me?

speaker: Seraphina
en: Another distraction for Ezio. Leave him.

speaker: Alberto
en: Leave me? Comandante (Commander), no, get me out of here!

speaker: Seraphina
en: What we took from the Vault is worth more than all our lives.

speaker: Civilian
en: So you say. Alberto, how did you get in there in the first place?

speaker: Alberto
en: I got lost when we fled into the tunnels. I just... followed them and ended up here.

speaker: Seraphina
en: And now he's trapped.

speaker: Civilian
en: It's true. Those bars are too strong to bend.

speaker: Alberto
en: Perhaps with a lever, you could force them apart? Or maybe there's a loose brick in the wall?

speaker: Seraphina
en: Enough. We're wasting time. Ezio could be here at any moment.

speaker: Civilian
en: We don't know that.

speaker: Seraphina
en: But it is not a risk we can take.

speaker: Alberto
en: Don't listen to her, Comandante (Commander)!

speaker: Civilian
en: Quiet! Let me think.

speaker: Seraphina
en: Then do it quickly. We're running out of time.

speaker: Ezio
en: You're mine, bastardi (bastards)!

speaker: Seraphina
en: Run! Run!

speaker: Ezio
en: Your end is at hand! You will not get away from me!

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: He's catching up!

speaker: Ezio
en: I have you now!

speaker: Ezio
en: Do not think this will save you from my justice.

speaker: Seraphina
en: My father and brother deserve justice! Those of us on the right side of knowledge have squared ourselves against you.

speaker: Civilian
en: Seraphina! Come, we must go, our escape is at hand!

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Fear not. We will not fail you.

speaker: Civilian
en: You better not. The city above waits like a flesh feast ready to be devoured.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: We are hungry for riches, sir.

speaker: Civilian
en: Then let Ezio serve as the primo (entrée). Our victory is at hand. My men have prepared a carriage to take you to Venice... and your ascension.

speaker: Seraphina
en: Excellent. Take what you want from the city to appease Rizzo and meet me at our rendezvous. Hermes shall rise again.

speaker: Civilian
en: Hermes shall rise again.

speaker: Ezio
en: Not if I have anything to do with it.

speaker: Ezio
en: "What are we to do with these tiny knives? They are scarcely fit for slicing a salami. If we are to take this town we need swords, not these trickster's tools."

speaker: Ezio
en: Now these, I can use.

speaker: Mercenary 3
en: Curses! Will this lock never open? I can almost smell the treasure behind this door. If only there were a key...

speaker: Ezio
en: That is the problem with these old tunnels. There are all sorts of accidents waiting to happen down here.

speaker: Mercenary 4
en: I'm reporting you for insubordination!

speaker: Mercenary 5
en: Ah, the hell with you.

speaker: Mercenary 4
en: Did you hear what I said?

speaker: Mercenary 5
en: Yes, and I don't care.

speaker: Mercenary 4
en: The commander certainly will.

speaker: Mercenary 5
en: The commander can go to hell with you.

speaker: Ezio
en: "Though we are bound to different masters, we share the same goal, and the same enemy. Obey her as you would me." It is signed 'R'.

speaker: Ezio
en: There has to be some device that will open this gate.

speaker: Civilian
en: You. Stay here while we make our escape. Lock the door behind us.

speaker: Civilian
en: Too late, Assassin! You want Seraphina, you'll have to go through me.

speaker: Ezio
en: That, I can do.

speaker: Ezio
en: She escaped. But the trail is not yet cold.

speaker: Ezio
en: Oh, Monteriggioni. I failed to protect you once before. On my honor, and the memory of my uncle Mario, I shall not fail you again.

speaker: Claudia
en: The city burns. Seraphina and her bandits have done their work well. How could I have been so blind?

speaker: Ezio
en: The fault is mine, dear sister. I have failed you and Monteriggioni.

speaker: Claudia
en: This desecration of our home cries out for revenge.

speaker: Ezio
en: That, I will not fail at. I heard Seraphina and her men talk of Venice and their patron there, Francesco Rizzo. It is there that they have taken our stolen family treasures.

speaker: Claudia
en: Then why do you waste your time here with me? Let Antonio know you are coming, and then on the road to Venice with you. Bring back what is ours and show our foes the Auditores are not to be trifled with.

speaker: Ezio
en: You will see to Monteriggioni?

speaker: Claudia
en: This will not be my first time rebuilding the city, brother. Go, and may the spirit of vengeance go with you.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Ezio, I entertained Bavarese (Bavarian) ambassadors last night. They must have...poisoned me. How? We drank from the same cup! I don't remember what happened next. Come. We must find them.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Him! He was there!

speaker: Ambassador 1
en: What are you pointing at, puttana (whore?)

speaker: Courtesan
en: Wait...was it him? He looks familiar...but...not matter. Come. I will find another.

speaker: Courtesan
en: You! You poisoned me!

speaker: Ambassador 2
en: What?

speaker: Courtesan
en: I remember his name. Gisbert. Or is it George? Follow me.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Him! Get him!

speaker: Ambassador 3
en: What is this?

speaker: Courtesan
en: Grazie (Thank you) Ezio, I'm sure at least two of them were there last night.

speaker: Ezio
en: Buona fortuna (Good luck), and stay out of wine, Madonna (Madame.)

speaker: Leandros
en: Get him, you fools! Kill that bastard! Look everywhere, top to bottom! I want him dead! Ezio! I'm going to dig your heart out with a shovel and feed it to you! Damn this blizzard, he could be anywhere! What the hell are you standing around for? Make yourselves useful!

speaker: Needle in a Haystack
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Ezio, what a surprise to see you here.

speaker: Ezio
en: I thought you had sent for me?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Never. News of the Villa attack has spread across the city. We were certain that you were dead.

speaker: Ezio
en: Not yet. I am still very much alive.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: The Borgia must not discover that you escaped them. Follow me. Take care not to draw any undue attention.

speaker: Ezio
en: When do I ever?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: You would be wise to purchase missing equipment. You will not live long in Roma without supplies.

speaker: Ezio
en: I have my blade.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: And the guards have their guns, courtesy of the Borgia. Fortunately, I can help you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie (Thank you.)

speaker: Machiavelli
en: While you are in my debt, perhaps you will listen to reason.

speaker: Ezio
en: As soon as I hear some, I will let you know.

speaker: Blacksmith
en: That should do I hope... and please come back often!

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Bene. (Okay.) Now you can survive the journey back to Firenze.

speaker: Ezio
en: Perhaps. But I am not going to Firenze.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Oh?

speaker: Ezio
en: There will be no peace until we rise up against the entire Borgia family and the Templars who serve them.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: I do not recall such brave talk at Monteriggioni.

speaker: Ezio
en: How could I have known that they would find me so quickly? That they would kill Mario?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Rodrigo surrounds himself with snakes and murderers. Even his daughter Lucrezia has been sharpened into one of his most artful weapons. But she pales in comparison to the man behind the Villa attack. He is ambitious, ruthless and cruel beyond imagining, the laws of men mean nothing to him. He murdered his own brother to take power. He knows neither danger nor fatigue. Those who do not fall by his sword clamor to join his ranks. The powerful Orsini and families have been brought to kneel at his feet and the King of France stands at his side.

speaker: Ezio
en: Give me his name.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Cesare, head of the Papal armies. What does he intend to do with this power? What drives the man? That I still do not know. But, Ezio, Cesare has set his sights on all of Italia, and at this rate he will have it.

speaker: Ezio
en: Is that admiration I hear in your voice?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: He knows how to exercise his will. A rare virtue in the world today.

speaker: Ezio
en: Should we not travel by horse? Roma is quite large.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: As Cesare's conquests in Romagna continue to succeed and the Borgia grow in power they have taken desirable areas of the city for themselves. We cannot use the stables here.

speaker: Ezio
en: Oh, the will of the Borgia is law now?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: What are you implying Ezio?

speaker: Ezio
en: Do not play dumb with me, Machiavelli.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Do you have some kind of a plan?

speaker: Ezio
en: I am improvising.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Just because you kill a few guards does not mean the people will grant access to the stables.

speaker: Ezio
en: You are right. We need to send a signal. Wait here.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: It seems the stable is now available for purchase.

speaker: Ezio
en: After you.

speaker: Altaïr
en: The Templars have retaken their archive on Cyprus. Abbas sent no reinforcements. It was a massacre.

speaker: Maria
en: Oh my God...

speaker: Altaïr
en: Maria, when we left Masyaf ten years ago, this Order was strong. But all our progress has been undone.

speaker: Maria
en: Abbas must answer for this.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Answer to whom? The Assassins obey only his command now.

speaker: Maria
en: Resist your desire for revenge, Altaïr. Speak truth and they will see their error.

speaker: Altaïr
en: He executed our youngest son, Maria! He deserves to die!

speaker: Maria
en: Perhaps. But if you cannot win back the Order by honorable means, its foundation will crumble.

speaker: Altaïr
en: You are right. Thirty years ago I let passion overtake my reason. And it caused a rift that has never fully healed.

speaker: Maria
en: Speak reasonably, and reasonable men will listen.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Some will, but not Abbas. I should have expelled him thirty years ago when he tried to steal the Apple.

speaker: Maria
en: But you earned the respect of the other Assassins because you let him stay.

speaker: Altaïr
en: How do you know this? You were not there.

speaker: Maria
en: I married a masterful storyteller.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Look at this place. Masyaf is a shadow of its former self.

speaker: Maria
en: We have been away for a long time.

speaker: Altaïr
en: But not in hiding. The Mongol threat demanded our attention, and we rode to meet it. What man here can say the same?

speaker: Maria
en: Where is our eldest son? Does Darim know his brother is dead?

speaker: Altaïr
en: I sent him a message four days ago. With luck it has reached him already. Abbas... I almost pity him. He wears his grudge like a cloak.

speaker: Maria
en: His wound is deep. It will help him to hear the truth.

speaker: Altaïr
en: As I walk these streets, I sense a great fear in the people, not love.

speaker: Maria
en: Abbas has dismantled this place, and robbed it of all joy.

speaker: Altaïr
en: We may be walking to our doom, Maria.

speaker: Maria
en: We may. But we walk together.

speaker: Abbas
en: Let them speak.

speaker: Altaïr
en: We seek the truth about our son's death. Why was Sef killed?

speaker: Abbas
en: Is it the truth you want, or an excuse for revenge?

speaker: Maria
en: If the truth gives us an excuse, we will act on it.

speaker: Abbas
en: Surrender the Apple, Altaïr, and I will tell you why your son was put to death.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Ah, the truth is out already! Abbas wants the Apple for himself. Not to open your minds, but to control them!

speaker: Abbas
en: You have held that artifact for thirty years, Altaïr, reveling in its power and hoarding its secrets. It has corrupted you.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Very well, Abbas. Take it.

speaker: Maria
en: What?

speaker: Swami
en: Before I executed your son, I told him you ordered it yourself. He died believing you had betrayed him.

speaker: Swami
en: Ah!

speaker: Maria
en: Altaïr! Altaïr, no!

speaker: Maria
en: Strength, Altaïr.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Maria...

speaker: Abbas
en: He is possessed! Kill him! Take the Apple! Now!

speaker: Darim
en: Father! I got your message. What has happened?

speaker: Altaïr
en: Darim! Turn back!

speaker: Darim
en: Have they all gone mad?

speaker: Altaïr
en: We have to go. Abbas must not get his hands on the Apple.

speaker: Darim
en: If you need more knives, take them.

speaker: Darim
en: Where is mother?

speaker: Altaïr
en: She is gone, Darim. I'm sorry...

speaker: Darim
en: What? How?!

speaker: Altaïr
en: Later. First we fight.

speaker: Darim
en: Brothers! We need not fight.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Forget reason, Darim. They have been poisoned by lies.

speaker: Darim
en: Was it Abbas who killed my brother?

speaker: Altaïr
en: He killed your brother, Malik, and countless others.

speaker: Darim
en: He is a madman.

speaker: Altaïr
en: A madman with an army.

speaker: Darim
en: He will die. One day he will pay.

speaker: Altaïr
en: It is time to go!

speaker: Abbas
en: I will have the Apple, Altaïr! And I will have your head for all the dishonor you brought upon my family! You cannot run forever! Not from us, and not from your lies!

speaker: Altaïr
en: Maria. My love...

speaker: Federico
en: Alright. Enough of that. We really should head home. Let's go.

speaker: Ezio
en: Wait.

speaker: Federico
en: What...?

speaker: Federico
en: Ezio! Let Cristina sleep.

speaker: Ezio
en: There will be time enough for that – later.

speaker: Ezio
en: Cazzo, (Fuck) it's Vieri, I'd better hide.

speaker: Vieri
en: Keep looking! He couldn't have gotten far...

speaker: Ezio
en: Cristina... Cristina!

speaker: Cristina
en: Who's there?

speaker: Ezio
en: Me!

speaker: Cristina
en: Ezio! I should have known.

speaker: Ezio
en: May I come in?

speaker: Cristina
en: Fine. But only for a minute.

speaker: Ezio
en: A minute is all I need.

speaker: Cristina
en: Indeed.

speaker: Ezio
en: Wait... that came out wrong.

speaker: Ezio
en: Come here.

speaker: Cristina
en: Oh, Ezio...

speaker: Cristina
en: Oh, Ezio...

speaker: Antonio
en: Cristina! Cristina! Sveglia! (Wake up!) Your tutor will be here soon! Come, my daughter... Is it really so terrible tha– Figlio d'un cane! (Son of a bitch!) What is this?!

speaker: Ezio
en: Perdonate, Messere! Chiedo venia! (Forgive me, sir! I beg your pardon!)

speaker: Antonio
en: I'll kill you!

speaker: Ezio
en: Now, now! That's not necessary...

speaker: Antonio
en: Guards! Guards! Voglio la sua testa! (Bring me his head!)

speaker: Ezio
en: There's really no need for violence... You have me confused with someone else... She needed some help... with... some things... I'm mostly innocent!

speaker: No Camping
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: No Laughing Matter
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Ezio
en: I need your help, Leonardo. Does it work?

speaker: Leonardo
en: What? What are you asking?

speaker: Ezio
en: Does it work, Leonardo? Can it really fly?

speaker: Leonardo
en: I don't know. It's only a prototype, an idea. It's not ready yet.

speaker: Ezio
en: Have you tried it?

speaker: Leonardo
en: No! It's too dangerous. To test it, you'd have to leap off a tower. Who would be mad enough to do a thing like that?

speaker: Ezio
en: Leonardo, I think you just found your madman.

speaker: Ezio
en: So, how does she work?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Have you ever watched a bird in flight? It's not about being lighter than air, it's about grace and balance. You must use your body's own weight to control your elevation and direction. Good luck, Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: Ugh! Why am I crashing?! This is ridiculous! The palazzo is too far away! Diavolo (Damn) I give up! I'm going to end up killing myself before I ever kill another Templar.

speaker: Leonardo
en: I can't believe it! It really worked! You flew, Ezio! You flew!

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì, (Yes) but not very far.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Well, what were you expecting? The machine wasn't designed for distance. Alright, look, let me go over my plans here. Maybe I can find some way to extend the duration of the flight.

speaker: Antonio
en: Ezio! My men tell me Carlo has the poison! We must hurry!

speaker: Ezio
en: Antonio, this is Leonardo, the master inventor who built this... this... pezzo di merda (piece of shit).

speaker: Leonardo
en: Hey! It's not the machine's fault, it's mine. I've checked and rechecked my blueprints. It's just impossible! I don't know how to extend the flight! Ah, che idea del cazzo (crazy fucking idea)!

speaker: Leonardo
en: Eureka! Of course! Genio! (Genius!)

speaker: Antonio
en: What is he doing now?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Heat rises... it needs fire. Heated air under its wings will lift the machine.

speaker: Ezio
en: Leonardo, what good is one fire going to do?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Not one fire, Ezio. A dozen, built all across the city. Enough to carry you from here to the Palazzo Ducale!

speaker: Antonio
en: How? Oh, capisco (I understand)! My men could do that, but you're forgetting about the guards.

speaker: Ezio
en: Don't worry, I will take care of them.

speaker: Antonio
en: I'll give the order to have my men move in behind you and hold the locations. They'll light them all up the second the sun goes down over San Marco.

speaker: Ilario
en: How longer do we have to stand here, Saverio? It's cold.

speaker: Saverio
en: What do you want Ilario? Messer Pazzi is paying us good money to watch the entrance, and the dead won't try to murder us. I can't wait to go home to Elena and tell her how much gold we made tonight!

speaker: Saverio
en: Merda (Shit)! The door! Keep watch while I go look. This was supposed to be an easy job!

speaker: Ilario
en: I told you we shouldn't have come here. If I hear anything, I'm running to the other guard post, so help me God.

speaker: Ilario
en: Saverio! I'll be back with the other guards!

speaker: Ilario
en: Have to find a way out. Before he kills me! Must run faster! Leave me alone!

speaker: Ilario
en: Yes, yes. He can't come here.

speaker: Ilario
en: We are under attack! Guards!

speaker: Ilario
en: Kill the assassin!

speaker: Stefano
en: Et benedictio Dei omnipotentis, Patris et Filii et Spiritus Sancti descendat super vos et maneat semper. (And may the blessing of Almighty God, the Father and of the Son and Holy Spirit descend upon you, and remain with you always.)

speaker: Francesco
en: Grazie, padre. (Thank you, father.) Bernardo?

speaker: Bernardo
en: It's all here, Swords, staves, axes, armor, bows. Our men will want for nothing.

speaker: Stefano
en: I take this gift to mean the Pope consents?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: He gave his blessing to the operation... as long as nobody is killed.

speaker: Francesco
en: We are all set for the Duomo in the morning, Signore. The bait's been laid, but it wasn't easy. His fool brother keeps changing his plans...

speaker: Bernardo
en: Sì! (Yes!) We'll need to be on hand to make sure Giuliano even gets out of bed for church tomorrow!

speaker: Rodrigo
en: What is it, Jacopo? Do you think they suspect something?

speaker: Francesco
en: Impossible! The Medici are too arrogant or too stupid to even notice. Likely a bit of both.

speaker: Jacopo
en: Do not underestimate our enemies, Francesco! Or have you already forgotten how your son was murdered?

speaker: Francesco
en: We'll suffer no such surprises this time, Maestro. You have my word.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Molto bene. (Very well.) I should be off. I've some other business to attend to before I return to Rome. Gentlemen. Tomorrow, a new sun rises over Firenze. May the Father of Understanding guide us.

speaker: Templars
en: May the Father of Understanding guide us.

speaker: Ezio
en: I know where Francesco will be and when, But...

speaker: Volpe
en: What is it?

speaker: Ezio
en: I overheard something... They have weapons, enough for a battalion. Even the Pope has given support!

speaker: Volpe
en: Typical of Sixtus, but... What the hell are they planning?

speaker: Ezio
en: I couldn't understand the specifics. But it involves the Medici. And it begins tomorrow morning at the Duomo.

speaker: Volpe
en: The Medici will all be there for Sunday service... Along with the rest of Firenze. They are going to do it right in the middle of High Mass...

speaker: Ezio
en: But it's also a chance for me to blend with the crowd, get close, and stop this madness.

speaker: Volpe
en: If they succeed.. If we lose Lorenzo, and Firenze falls to the Pazzi...

speaker: Ezio
en: It will not come to that. I promise.

speaker: Volpe
en: I hope you're right...

speaker: Teodora
en: You have our gratitude, Ezio.

speaker: Antonio
en: Why is it wherever you go, trouble follows?

speaker: Ezio
en: Antonio, I trust you know why I'm here.

speaker: Antonio
en: I imagine to rid Venice of Marco Barbarigo? But really, Ezio, we did this once already! And this new Templar Doge is a bigger culo (ass) than the last. Never mind that he never leaves the palazzo!

speaker: Teodora
en: Yes, except... for tonight. Marco wouldn't dare miss Carnevale.

speaker: Ezio
en: How do you know this?

speaker: Teodora
en: In fact, he's throwing the biggest party of them all, but getting in won't be so simple. You'll need a golden mask for entry. And before you think of forging one, keep in mind, each mask is numbered. Fortunately for you, I have an idea. Let's see if we can't win you a mask.

speaker: Teodora
en: What is it, my son? You want to ask me something?

speaker: Ezio
en: I do. Forgive me, but why is it you wear a nun's habit if you aren't one?

speaker: Teodora
en: Well whoever said I wasn't? Indeed, I am married to the Lord.

speaker: Ezio
en: And yet you are also a courtesan? You run a bordello.

speaker: Teodora
en: So? I see no contradiction. How I choose to practice my faith; what I choose to do with my body, these are my choices to make. Like many young women I was drawn to the church, but grew disillusioned by the "believers" of this city. Men hold God only as an idea in their heads, not in the depths of their hearts and bodies. Men must know how to love in order to reach salvation. My girls and I provide that to our congregation. No church would agree with me, I realized, so I created my own. It may not be traditional, but men's hearts grow firmer in my care.

speaker: Ezio
en: Among other things, I'm sure.

speaker: Announcer
en: Signore e Signori (Ladies and gentlemen), come one, come all! The Games of Carnevale are about to begin! Do you have the coraggio (courage) to compete for as grand a prize as this?

speaker: Announcer
en: This year, like every year, the Golden Mask will provide entry for one, e uno solo (and only one), to our most beloved Doge's personal ball! Who would not desire such an exceptional reward? Come! Compete! Whoever proves themselves champion in each of four games today, shall be the Doge's personal guest tonight!

speaker: Teodora
en: You'd best get to it, Ezio!

speaker: Courtesan
en: Buongiorno (Hello), Ezio. We are taught to seduce Roma's most powerful men, but not all of us have been able to resist their charms. Follow Giuletta. I suspect she will lead you to her benefactor.

speaker: Giuletta
en: I did not know the bastardo (bastard) was a traitor!

speaker: Ezio
en: You are no longer welcome at the Rosa in Fiore (The Blooming Rose).

speaker: Yusuf
en: Ezio! Come meet my new friends!

speaker: Yusuf
en: You fight like a man late for his own wedding.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì (Yes), by about twenty-five years.

speaker: Yusuf
en: I was too late to save the Bazaar den, unfortunately. But now that my army has doubled in size, we'll take it back together. This way.

speaker: Yusuf
en: When the Templars take control of a district, they flaunt their presence, hanging banners, extorting the merchants. It's a constant battle to keep them at bay, and they rub our noses in every victory.

speaker: Ezio
en: They are quite bold. Why does the Sultan tolerate this?

speaker: Yusuf
en: Sultan Bayezid is far away, Ezio. Warring with his son Selim many fersah (leagues) northwest of the city. He has been away for years, at least since the earthquake, and maybe even before. He is blind to all this turmoil.

speaker: Ezio
en: Ah, but your eyes are open, sì (yes)?

speaker: Yusuf
en: Hem de fal tashi gibi. (Like two full moons.) Believe it.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Too many to engage directly.

speaker: Ezio
en: Hmm, I am not confident a smoke bomb will help us here.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Smoke bomb? Ezio, it's time you Italians joined the sixteenth century. These do not obscure, they distract.

speaker: Yusuf
en: You see? They can't resist. Let's move.

speaker: Ezio
en: You are full of surprises today.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Crafting explosives is a new hobby, one we borrowed from the Chinese and have taken to with great passion.

speaker: Ezio
en: You will have to teach me.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Who is the Mentor here, Ezio? I'm beginning to wonder.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Your turn. Make me proud.

speaker: Yusuf
en: There they go. Hurry. We're nearly there.

speaker: Yusuf
en: This is another of our many dens. Taken by Templars, as you can see. Somewhere among this rabble is a Templar captain. Kill him, then climb the tower and light our signal fire. This warns the Templars that it is time to pack up and go.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene. (Good.) You create a distraction. I will send them home.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Whenever the Templars commandeer one of our dens, they leave a Captain in charge. Search the area carefully, and you might see him strutting about like a peacock. Use those legendary senses of yours, Ezio, and scan the streets. You'll find our target.

speaker: Dogan
en: Bu ne büyük sheref usta. (Mentor, it is an honor.) Is Yusuf with you?

speaker: Ezio
en: An attack in the city demands his attention. What is our situation?

speaker: Dogan
en: We beat back the vanguard, but they are sure to send more troops.

speaker: Ezio
en: Are your men ready for another fight?

speaker: Dogan
en: They are now.

speaker: Ezio
en: Send word if the Templars regroup. I will be with Yusuf at the Grand Bazaar den.

speaker: Dogan
en: Take a ferry across the Haliç (Golden Horn). It's the fastest way to the peninsula.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Did you have an enjoyable ride, Duchessa (Duchess)?

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Hardly. I raced across the grounds at breakneck speed for fear of a knife in my back.

speaker: Guard 1
en: I do not understand, Duchessa (Duchess). Who is trying to kill you?

speaker: Lucrezia
en: My father kept them at bay. Kept me safe. Now they chase after me. They want my head.

speaker: Guard 1
en: But, Signora–

speaker: Lucrezia
en: The countryside was supposed to be serene. Death follows me, even here. Increase the patrols and warn me of any intruders. No one is allowed in the palazzo but my husband's private guard.

speaker: Guard 1
en: You heard the Duchessa (Duchess)! Sound the alarm if an intruder is spotted. Poor Alfonso, his wife has gone mad.

speaker: Servant
en: What is the meaning of this? I am supposed to shine the Duchessa's (Duchess') shoes.

speaker: Guard 2
en: No one is allowed in the palazzo.

speaker: Servant
en: Is she going to shine her own shoes then?

speaker: Guard 2
en: What the Duchessa (Duchess) does or does not do is of no concern to us.

speaker: Servant
en: What a life this is, let me tell you.

speaker: Guard 2
en: I would rather you did not.

speaker: Servant
en: I will complain to the Duca (Duke)!

speaker: Guard 2
en: As long as you are stuck on that side, no one will hear you.

speaker: Servant
en: I have had enough.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Stay where you are.

speaker: Servant
en: Let me through!

speaker: Guard 2
en: You must wait until the Duchessa (Duchess) allows you to pass.

speaker: Guard 3
en: I heard the Duca (Duke) has borrowed guards from the Pope himself to watch over his palazzo.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Julius has lent Alfonso several of his guards in return for siding with the Pope against Ravenna.

speaker: Guard 5
en: We shall see how long that alliance lasts.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Come to kill me at last, Assassino (Assassin)?

speaker: Ezio
en: Buongiorno (Good day), Lucrezia. Or should I say Duchessa (Duchess).

speaker: Lucrezia
en: A borrowed title bestowed by my husband, ill-fitting and barely concealing the truth.

speaker: Ezio
en: You can keep your life. I am here for the art on your walls.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Redecorating, are we?

speaker: Ezio
en: I count five Leonardo da Vinci paintings you have stolen, and I want them returned.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: If only it were that easy. My birthplace, my family, have been taken from me. You think Ferrara loves me? I am a stranger, a castaway. An orphan. Your paintings are gone, Assassino (Assassin).

speaker: Ezio
en: I do not believe you.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Frightening, is it not? To have lost so much. Perhaps we can comfort each other.

speaker: Ezio
en: Perhaps. Where are the paintings?

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Sold to Francesco Colonna... and one to someone who was special to me, Patrizio. He spends his time near Il Vaticano. I kept one for myself.

speaker: Ezio
en: Give it to me.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Guards! Place Da Vinci's Annunciation in a cart. Leave it outside the walls.

speaker: Ezio
en: Molto bene. (Very good.) Now, close your eyes.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: My husband will soon arrive with his guards, so it is best if you hurry.

speaker: Ezio
en: Forgive me, Duchessa (Duchess).

speaker: Lucrezia
en: What for?

speaker: Ezio
en: No man can heal your pain. You must do so on your own. Say hello to the Duca (Duke) for me.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Guards! Guards!

speaker: Ezio
en: Perfect! A route up if I fall.

speaker: Open the Palace Gates
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus 2.0.

speaker: Copernicus
en: Who are you that defends without cause?

speaker: Ezio
en: One who believes in freedom. Ezio Auditore da Firenze.

speaker: Copernicus
en: Ezio. They call me Niccolò Copernico. I have heard your name spoken at the Borgia court, but now I have proof that you truly exist.

speaker: Ezio
en: Il Vaticano (the Vatican) welcomes you, yet you are under attack by its guards?

speaker: Copernicus
en: You think me one of them? Truthfully, you would be right. Yesterday, I was a Templar.

speaker: Ezio
en: And today?

speaker: Copernicus
en: The Templars wanted me to keep the findings of my experiments hidden, and that I cannot do.

speaker: Ezio
en: The Borgia hunt for you and your friends.

speaker: Copernicus
en: My fellow scholars? The logic of such a purge escapes me.

speaker: Guard
en: Find Copernico!

speaker: Copernicus
en: But we will discuss reasoning later.

speaker: Ezio
en: Follow me.

speaker: Ezio
en: You will be safe here.

speaker: Copernicus
en: What of the other scholars?

speaker: Ezio
en: How do I know I can trust you?

speaker: Copernicus
en: How do you know anything? Knowledge gathering is a dangerous enterprise. Easier to stay in place, learning nothing, than to risk in order to truly know.

speaker: Ezio
en: All right. Enlighten me.

speaker: Copernicus
en: Take these letters to the scholars. They must be informed of the threat to their safety.

speaker: Guard
en: Watch the weapon carefully. We must be ready to take it to safety should anything happen.

speaker: Ezio
en: Madre di Dio! (Mother of God!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Not very smart, are they?

speaker: Guard
en: He's stealing the weapon!

speaker: Ezio
en: How many of you are there? Nice try. Go home! If you do not, all of you will die!

speaker: Ezio
en: Il mondo è migliore senza di te! (The world is better without you!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene (good)! Now I have a way back up in case I fall.

speaker: Francesco
en: Welcome, Mentor.

speaker: Ezio
en: Hello, Francesco. How has Rome fared in my absence?

speaker: Francesco
en: We have seen better days, Mentor. The Papal Army fills the streets as if Rome is theirs alone.

speaker: Ezio
en: And they will continue so long as Cesare is in power.

speaker: Francesco
en: So we must deal with him as soon as possible!

speaker: Ezio
en: Not yet. To strike at the heart of the Borgia would only invite retribution from the whole of the Papal Army. We must weaken his forces and his power first.

speaker: Francesco
en: What do we do?

speaker: Ezio
en: Have you been tracking their patrols like I asked you to?

speaker: Francesco
en: Yes, Mentor.

speaker: Ezio
en: Good. Then I simply need to find an isolated group, and strike.

speaker: Francesco
en: At guardsmen? They can be replaced.

speaker: Ezio
en: True. But the Papal Guards that head these patrols cannot be replaced so easily.

speaker: Francesco
en: I see.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do not fret, Francesco. Cesare's time will come, I promise. For now, we must do what we can.

speaker: Francesco
en: I don't understand. What went wrong?

speaker: Ezio
en: Calm yourself, Francesco. You cannot expect every mission to go perfectly as planned.

speaker: Francesco
en: So what do we do?

speaker: Ezio
en: We wait for another opportunity, and we try again.

speaker: Francesco
en: I hope that this is just the start of our efforts.

speaker: Ezio
en: Patience, Francesco. This is just the first step of many. There is still much to do.

speaker: Francesco
en: I know. I am eager to get on with it.

speaker: Ezio
en: The time will come. For now, continue to track the movements of Cesare's army. When I have a task for you, I shall return.

speaker: Francesco
en: I will, Mentor.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where are Claudia and Maria?

speaker: Courtesan
en: We came back with the money. They followed us home.

speaker: Claudia
en: What?

speaker: Ezio
en: My sister knows how to wield a knife.

speaker: Claudia
en: And I am ready to do it again.

speaker: Ezio
en: Spoken like a true Auditore.

speaker: Maria
en: Finally, you two came to your senses. It's about time.

speaker: Ezio
en: Good morning, father.

speaker: Giovanni
en: Come with me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Is something wrong?

speaker: Giovanni
en: Do you think me blind and deaf, son? I know all about your fight with Vieri de' Pazzi last night. And then this little visit to Cristina! Your behavior is unacceptable! It... it...

speaker: Giovanni
en: It reminds me of myself when I was your age! I assume these misadventures won't interfere with your work today?

speaker: Ezio
en: No, padre. Avete la mia parola. (No, father. You have my word.)

speaker: Giovanni
en: I've prepared some documents here for Lorenzo de' Medici to review. I need them delivered to him.

speaker: Ezio
en: With haste, father.

speaker: Giovanni
en: Return to me when it's done.

speaker: Boetio
en: Ah! Ezio! Ben trovato! (Well met!) How are you?

speaker: Ezio
en: Come sempre. (Same as ever.) I have a letter for Messer Lorenzo.

speaker: Boetio
en: I'll see that he receives it when he returns.

speaker: Ezio
en: Returns?

speaker: Boetio
en: They've gone to , I'm afraid. And not expected back for at least another day.

speaker: Ezio
en: I'll let my father know.

speaker: Federico
en: Keep up the good work!

speaker: Ezio
en: Bischero! (Penis!)

speaker: Uberto
en: ...You worry too much, Giovanni. Francesco de' Pazzi is in prison. The threat is ended.

speaker: Giovanni
en: Ah! Hello son. You remember my friend Uberto?

speaker: Ezio
en: Good morning, Gonfaloniere Alberti.

speaker: Uberto
en: To you as well, young man.

speaker: Giovanni
en: I trust you delivered the message?

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì, padre. (Yes, father.) But it seems Lorenzo is out of town.

speaker: Giovanni
en: Hmmm. I did not anticipate this...

speaker: Uberto
en: What does it matter. So you wait another day or two.

speaker: Giovanni
en: Listen, your mother and sister have been looking for you. I'll need you again in a little while, but for now – see if you can't help them.

speaker: Ezio
en: Are you sure?

speaker: Giovanni
en: Yes. Now, if you'll excuse us...?

speaker: Uberto
en: Good to see you, Ezio.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Niccolò Polo... Our time together was brief, I know. But I have faith this Codex will answer the many questions you have yet to ask.

speaker: Niccolò
en: Altaïr, this gift is... invaluable. Grazie. (Thank you.)

speaker: Altaïr
en: So, where will you go next?

speaker: Niccolò
en: Back to Costantinopoli for a time. We will establish a guild there before returning to Venezia.

speaker: Altaïr
en: Your son Marco will be eager to hear his father's wild stories.

speaker: Niccolò
en: He is a little young for such tales. But one day soon, sì (yes).

speaker: Altaïr
en: Niccolò, your cargo and provisions are waiting for you by the village gates. We will escort you there.

speaker: Niccolò
en: Thank you, Mentor.

speaker: Altaïr
en: : Ready the catapults, and watch for my signal. (To Niccolò) Stay close.

speaker: Darim
en: Father... are you hurt?

speaker: Altaïr
en: Give me a moment. Ah. The end of an era... When I was very young, I was foolish enough to believe that our Creed would bring an end to all these conflicts. If only I had possessed the humility to say to myself, I have seen enough for one life. I have done my part. Then again, there is no greater glory than fighting to find the truth.

speaker: Niccolò
en: We are ready.

speaker: Altaïr
en: A last favor, Niccolò. Take these with you and guard them well. Hide them if you must.

speaker: Niccolò
en: Artifacts?

speaker: Altaïr
en: Of a kind. They are keys, each one imbued with a message.

speaker: Niccolò
en: A message for whom?

speaker: Altaïr
en: I wish I knew.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Buongiorno (Hello), Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: It is time to pay a visit to Lucrezia's lover, Pietro.

speaker: La Volpe
en: I have sent my men out to find him.

speaker: Ezio
en: Molto bene. (Very good.)

speaker: La Volpe
en: Ezio. If I may...

speaker: Ezio
en: What is it?

speaker: La Volpe
en: Someone warned Rodrigo to stay away from the Castello.

speaker: Ezio
en: Machiavelli? Do you have proof?

speaker: La Volpe
en: No.

speaker: Ezio
en: We must not split apart by mere suspicion.

speaker: Thief
en: The Borgia know the location of our spies!

speaker: La Volpe
en: Who told them?

speaker: Thief
en: Maestro (Master) Machiavelli asked about our search for Pietro earlier today.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Ezio?

speaker: Ezio
en: I still do not believe Machiavelli has turned traitor.

speaker: La Volpe
en: First the Villa attack, then the Castello and now this. He is behind it all.

speaker: La Volpe
en: What were you able to find out?

speaker: Spy
en: Pietro is to be assassinated this evening. Cesare sent his butcher.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Micheletto. The best killer in Roma. No one escapes him.

speaker: Ezio
en: Until tonight. Come on.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Did you uncover information about Pietro?

speaker: Spy
en: The man is an actor and he is performing in a play stanotte (tonight).

speaker: La Volpe
en: What did you find out about Pietro?

speaker: Spy
en: He is to be suspended from a cross. Micheletto will come for him with a spear.

speaker: Cesare
en: How did you find me?!

speaker: Ezio
en: The Apple you stole from Mario Auditore led me here!

speaker: Cesare
en: Kill him! Kill the Assassin! Tear the maldito bastardo (old fucker) to pieces!

speaker: Ezio
en: I need munitions.

speaker: Civilian
en: Help yourself! There's more than enough to go around.

speaker: Ezio
en: Faster to travel by horse.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Por favor. My legs. I am not able to stop the bleeding.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: I have done all I can, now you must trust in God.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: I'm afraid. Mis piernas. (My legs.) Mis piernas. (My legs.)

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Shhh. Think of all the coin you will be paid come the end of this battle.

speaker: Seeker
en: I heard Cesare Borgia commands the Navarrese.

speaker: Brute
en: ¿Quién? (Who?)

speaker: Seeker
en: He once ruled all of Roma.

speaker: Brute
en: What happened?

speaker: Seeker
en: I heard an assassin killed his supporters. Great rulers rise and fall like leaves in the wind.

speaker: Brute
en: I will give you wind.

speaker: Woman
en: Ayúdenme. Mi hijo. Mi hijo está herido. (Help me. My son. My son is wounded.)

speaker: Woman
en: ¡Déjame en paz! (Leave me alone!)

speaker: Soldier
en: I will not hurt you.

speaker: Civilian
en: That is my house! Por favor! (Please!) No!

speaker: Priest
en: You brought this upon yourselves through sin. This is how the Lord punishes you. Ours is a just God, and this is justice. Praise the Lord! Thank you God for teaching us to be humble. To see our punishment for what it is, a call to spirituality. The Lord he giveth and the Lord he taketh away. So the truth is written. Amen!

speaker: Civilian
en: Run! Run!

speaker: Ezio
en: Cesare! The walls surround you. There is nowhere to run.

speaker: Cesare
en: Come then, Ezio!

speaker: Cesare
en: I cannot die. Fortuna (Fortune) will not fail me. I am the best fighter who ever lived. Stay back! Defeat will never taint me! An Auditore will never best me. Roma, Italia, España. They will all be mine. Take that! No matter what you do I will conquer all. DIIIIIIIIIEEE! Give up Auditore, you are no match for me. I will hunt and kill all those you hold dear.

speaker: Cesare
en: The throne was mine!

speaker: Ezio
en: Wanting something does not make it your right.

speaker: Cesare
en: What do you know?

speaker: Ezio
en: That a true leader empowers the people he rules.

speaker: Cesare
en: I will lead mankind into a new world!

speaker: Ezio
en: Che nessuno ricordi il tuo nome. (May no one remember your name.) Requiescat in pace. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Cesare
en: You cannot kill me! No man can murder me!

speaker: Ezio
en: Then I leave you in the hands of Fate!

speaker: Paying Respects
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Peacekeeper
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus 2.0.

speaker: Contact
en: Thief! Get that bastard!

speaker: Contact
en: Well done. I knew I could count on you!

speaker: Leonardo
en: Ezio! I was hoping to see you tonight.

speaker: Ezio
en: I don't have much time. The Doge's party starts very soon.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Nevertheless, I have news. I hear Cristina Vespucci is in Venezia for Carnevale. Weren't the two of you close?

speaker: Ezio
en: Once...

speaker: Leonardo
en: Perhaps it would not have been better not to tell you. She's with her husband. She may not be too happy to see you.

speaker: Ezio
en: No... It's wonderful. It's Carnevale! With this mask, she need not even know it's me! I know just the way to draw her attention... Grazie, amico.

speaker: Ezio
en: There... Now to await her at the rendezvous.

speaker: Ezio
en: Cristina...

speaker: Cristina
en: Manfredo! When did you get so romantic

speaker: Ezio
en: Sshhh...

speaker: Cristina
en: Ezio...? What the hell are you doing here!? How dare you—?

speaker: Ezio
en: Cristina... It's alright.

speaker: Cristina
en: Alright!? I haven't seen you in eight years!

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì... (Yes...) I was afraid you wouldn't come if I... just asked.

speaker: Cristina
en: You're right. I wouldn't have! Ezio... The last time I saw you, you kissed me in the alley— and then left me behind to get married!

speaker: Ezio
en: It was the right thing to do. He loved you.

speaker: Cristina
en: Who cares what he wanted? — I loved YOU. You had your second chance... Please, Ezio... Don't ever find me again.

speaker: Petruccio
en: Ehi Ezio! (Hey Ezio!)

speaker: Ezio
en: What are you doing out here, Petruccio? You should be in bed.

speaker: Petruccio
en: I want those feathers.

speaker: Ezio
en: What for?

speaker: Petruccio
en: It's a secret.

speaker: Ezio
en: If I get them for you, will you go back inside?

speaker: Petruccio
en: Yes, I promise.

speaker: Ezio
en: Here. As promised.

speaker: Petruccio
en: Grazie (Thank you), brother!

speaker: Ezio
en: You still haven't told me why you want these.

speaker: Petruccio
en: I will. In time.

speaker: Wife
en: After eight years of marriage that figlio di puttana is back with his old woman! Teach him to respect his vows, please!

speaker: Husband
en: Of course! What was I thinking?! My wife! I do love her!

speaker: Ezio
en: Try not to spend all of that money in one place.

speaker: Pickpocket
en: What money would that be?

speaker: Ezio
en: Signora (Lady), I know a pickpocket when I see one. Your technique is good, but not flawless.

speaker: Pickpocket
en: Not so. Until today, I had never been caught or called out.

speaker: Ezio
en: Let me show you a few tricks.

speaker: Pickpocket
en: I need no instruction. And I can prove it. Give me one minute, and I will steal more than you could in a day.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene. (Good). Begin.

speaker: Pickpocket
en: Curse these misers! None of them are carrying any Akçe today!

speaker: Ezio
en: Well, my take was quite good. Are you having an off-day?

speaker: Pickpocket
en: Do not patronize me. I am a skilled thief. You saw it yourself.

speaker: Ezio
en: I did. And I would be grateful if you joined the Assassins to put those talents to better use.

speaker: Pickpocket
en: Hmm, I suppose I should, evet (yes)? I cannot live off the fruits of others forever.

speaker: Piri
en: Try this Ezio. A caltrop bomb. A non-lethal method of stopping pursuers.

speaker: Ezio
en: I like the sound of that.

speaker: Piri
en: When I first sailed with my uncle Kemal more than two decades ago, we had quite a lot of fun with these in many rowdy ports. In Rodos (Rhodes), for instance, it was so easy to lure the Hospitaliers from their palace posts, right into a patch of caltrops. And to see them dancing in the street in a full suit of armor. Nothing is more undignified. Try it. You'll see.

speaker: Piri
en: Did you know that the early Christians used to place East at the top of their maps? They assumed that heaven lay in that direction, beyond Cathay, because that is where the sun appeared every morning. What convenient simplicity, no? With heaven on earth, glass spheres in the sky, and the earth at the center of the universe. Ha! What a load of horse piss. Ah, but you are not here to philosophize. What are you looking at?

speaker: Ezio
en: I need a simple but effective means of distraction.

speaker: Piri
en: Then this is the bomb for you. It gives a nice loud burst, luring all soldiers within earshot right to the source. Have fun.

speaker: Piri
