en: Kopekoglu! (Son of a dog!) I need to reconcile these ancient Greek maps with data from Admiral Columbus, but this is like comparing maps of the moon and the earth. What a mess. Ah, Ezio! Cheer me up. Let me teach you something.

speaker: Ezio
en: What about these poison bombs? How lethal are they?

speaker: Piri
en: Quite lethal, dostum (my friend). We distill our poison from the datura plant. A pretty little flower with a deadly secret. This one kills... slowly but surely. Be very careful, for your sake and for others'.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie. (Thank you).

speaker: Piri
en: For ten months I have been working on a new map for Bayezid. But he is old, and I am a perfectionist... Perhaps the next Sultan will appreciate my efforts. Well, how can I help you, Ezio?

speaker: Ezio
en: Smoke signal bombs. How do they work?

speaker: Piri
en: You must know the old saying, where there is smoke there is fire? These bombs play off that idea, creating a thick plume of smoke to trick city guards into believing a fire has started. These bombs are quiet, however, so only those who see the smoke will be lured away.

speaker: Ezio
en: Subtle. I will give it a try.

speaker: Piri
en: Ah! Turkish smoke bombs. Are you curious to try a few?

speaker: Ezio
en: Should I? I have used smoke bombs before, with varying results.

speaker: Piri
en: But not like ours. We have a special recipe for deep, dark clouds. Throw one of these and your eyes are useless. You must rely on your hearing, and... any other senses you may have cultivated.

speaker: Ezio
en: Other senses? What could that mean?

speaker: Piri
en: Word gets around, Ezio. That you are a special sort of man, with strange gifts.

speaker: Ezio
en: Keep it to yourself.

speaker: Ezio
en: Tell me about your special bomb casings.

speaker: Piri
en: Well, I have some sticky resin bags. My uncle Kemal had a wild fondness for them. During Bayezid's conflict with Venezia (Venice), he was a captain in the Ottoman navy. He liked resin bombs because they stuck to almost any surface... the hulls of large ships, for instance.

speaker: Ezio
en: I lost many friends in that conflict.

speaker: Piri
en: We all did, Ezio. And that war is why I became an Assassin. I hate the artificial boundaries our leaders have built between people.

speaker: Ezio
en: We fight to end the fighting. It is a sad irony.

speaker: Piri
en: It will always be an irony, evet (yes). But perhaps one day it will not be so sad. Use this wisely.

speaker: Piri
en: I used my first bomb when I was in my late teens. I was sailing the Mediterranean under an unrecognized flag, calling myself a privateer.

speaker: Ezio
en: The Francesi (French) would say Corsair (pirate).

speaker: Piri
en: No, they would say, Mort aux hérétiques! (Death to the heretics!) I do miss the days of rough ocean travel, the sea spray and the rolling waves. One day soon I will take to the sea again. But until then, I am here for my Assassins. Here is your bomb. Use it with great care.

speaker: Ezio
en: This one has a strange look. What do you call it?

speaker: Piri
en: A trip-wire bomb. One of the more subtle methods we have of removing your opponent's feet. You see these filaments in the side? This bomb will not detonate unless one of these many wires is disturbed. Very useful in narrow alleys.

speaker: Ezio
en: Or under the seat cushion of someone's horse carriage.

speaker: Piri
en: Oh ho! Ezio Auditore! You are one devious hayvan (animal)! I should keep my distance, lest you corrupt my delicate sensibilities.

speaker: Ezio
en: Oh, I think you will live.

speaker: Piri
en: Of course. Don't blow your hands off, eh?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Where have you been?

speaker: Ezio
en: We all have our secrets.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: I took the liberty of setting up a means of communication with your recruits. We send orders via carrier pigeon.

speaker: Ezio
en: Thank you, Machiavelli.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Bartolomeo sends his apologies. The French have doubled their assault.

speaker: Ezio
en: Claudia.

speaker: Claudia
en: Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: Alright. I have a plan to deal with the Borgia.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: We can either go after supplies or Cesare's followers.

speaker: Ezio
en: My plan is to attack both. If we cut off his funds, Cesare will lose his army and return without his men. So, I ask you, where does he get his money? Volpe?

speaker: La Volpe
en: Agostino Chigi is the Pope's money-lender, but Cesare does business with someone else. As of now, all we know is that he is called The Banker.

speaker: Claudia
en: I know someone who owes The Banker money. Senator Egidio Troche comes in all the time and complains.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene. (Good.) I will follow up on that lead.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: French soldiers are guarding the road back into the Castello. Once Cesare arrives, you will never get to him.

speaker: Ezio
en: I intend to kill the French general. With him dead, Bartolomeo will have the Frenchmen on the defensive and they will abandon their posts on the bridge.

speaker: Caterina
en: Even with those troops gone, the Papal Guard will continue to protect the inner gate.

speaker: La Volpe
en: There is a side entrance. Lucrezia's latest plaything, Pietro, has a key.

speaker: Ezio
en: He was at the Castello.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Come see me later. I will have my thieves ascertain his location.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where are you going?

speaker: Caterina
en: I am of no use to anyone without Forlì. I leave to be with my children and await the restoration of my lands.

speaker: Ezio
en: I wish you would stay.

speaker: Caterina
en: You are the leader of the Assassins now. Unite them, Ezio Auditore and take back Roma.

speaker: Caterina
en: Vittoria agli Assassini! (Victory to the Assassins!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Vittoria agli Assassini. (Victory to the Assassins.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes, sir?

speaker: Guard
en: This is a moment of great importance. Stay in formation. Make this right.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Do you really have it? You were not followed?

speaker: Guard
en: Absolutely. Everything went perfectly. We have followed your orders exactly as specified. The mission to Cyprus was more difficult than expected. There were complications, but we have returned with the artifact. And have carefully transported it to you, as instructed. We look forward to be generously compensated, as I am sure you've already considered... AHEM... what are you waiting for, Courier?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Ezio. It's been some time.

speaker: Ezio
en: Rodrigo. So, where is he?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Hmmm? Who?

speaker: Ezio
en: Your prophet!? Doesn't seem like anybody showed up, Rodrigo! How many people have died for this? For what's in this box?! And look—There's NOBODY here!

speaker: Rodrigo
en: You claim not to be a believer. And yet, here you are... Don't you see him? The Prophet is already here...I AM the Prophet. Now give me the Apple.

speaker: Ezio
en: Come and take it from me.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Is this all you have? Where's the rest of your people?

speaker: Ezio
en: What people?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: You really have no idea, do you? Guards!

speaker: Ezio
en: Uncle?

speaker: Mario
en: Don't worry, nipote (nephew)! You are not alone.

speaker: Ezio
en: Volpe! What are you doing here?

speaker: Volpe
en: We could very well ask you the same thing!

speaker: Ezio
en: We?

speaker: Antonio
en: Save your questions, brother. Don't let Borgia leave with that box!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Avanti! (Forward!)

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Now, you all shall die.

speaker: Antonio
en: Take him down, Ezio. We are right behind you.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Come at me, codardi (cowards)! All of you! My Bianca hungers for more skulls to crush!

speaker: Rodrigo
en: This is pathetic. You cannot stop what is written. What lies in the vault shall be mine!

speaker: Volpe
en: Look, my friends. Our Ezio has become quite a guerriero (warrior).

speaker: Volpe
en: A cuccia, tu (Down, boy.) You mess with the fox, you get the sword.

speaker: Mario
en: What FUN! We should do this more often!

speaker: Rodrigo
en: This is a losing battle for you, hombrecito (boy). You will die by my hand, just like your father... This war has been going on far longer than either of us have played a role.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Isn't this magnifico (wonderful), Ezio?! All of us smashing these Templar heads together!

speaker: Mario
en: Notevole, nipote! (Impressive, nephew!) You have improved since the last time we fought together.

speaker: Antonio
en: Ah, bravissimo. We should do this more often.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Your brothers didn't need to die, I just killed them to make a point. There is no mercy when you cross the Templars.

speaker: Ezio
en: This is for my father you

speaker: Ezio
en: Paola?!

speaker: Paola
en: He's gone, but we have what we came for...

speaker: Ezio
en: No! I need to go after him

speaker: Teodora
en: Do you really, now? Or are you here for another reason, my son?

speaker: Ezio
en: Teodora—? What—?! What are you all doing here?!

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Perhaps the same thing you are, Ezio. Hoping to see the Prophet appear.

speaker: Ezio
en: I came here to kill the Spaniard. I couldn't care less about your prophet.—He never showed up!

speaker: Machiavelli
en: No...? But, you did.

speaker: Ezio
en: What?!

speaker: Machiavelli
en: A prophet's arrival was foretold...And, unbeknownst to us—here you are. Perhaps all along, you were the one we sought.

speaker: Ezio
en: Cosa? (What?) Who are you?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Niccolò di Bernardo dei Machiavelli. I am an Assassin—trained in the ancient ways to safeguard mankind's evolution. Just like you, and each one of us here.

speaker: Ezio
en: You are all Assassins? Paola...? Volpe...?

speaker: Mario
en: It's true, nipote (nephew). We have all been guiding you, for years, teaching you the skills you need to join our ranks... I think it's time...

speaker: Antonio
en: We have our prize, but there is much to be done. Come meet us here at sunset.

speaker: Mario
en: Laa shay'a waqi'un moutlaq bale kouloun moumkine. (Nothing is true, everything is permitted.) These are the words spoken by our ancestors—that lay at the heart of our Creed.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Where other men blindly follow the truth, remember...

speaker: Ezio
en: ...Nothing is true.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Where other men are limited, by morality or law, remember...

speaker: Ezio
en: ...Everything is permitted.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: We work in the dark to serve the light. We are Assassins.

speaker: Assassins
en: Nothing is true. Everything is permitted.

speaker: Mario
en: It is time Ezio... In this modern age, we may not be as literal as our ancestors. But our seal is no less permanent. Are you ready to join us?

speaker: Ezio
en: I am.

speaker: Antonio
en: This only hurts for a while, brother. Like so many things.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Benvenuto (Welcome), Ezio. You are one of us now. Come! We have much to do!

speaker: Leonardo
en: Fascinating! Absolutely fascinating!

speaker: Ezio
en: What is it, Leonardo? What does it do?

speaker: Leonardo
en: I could no more explain this than explain to you why the Earth goes the Sun.

speaker: Mario
en: You mean the Sun the Earth.

speaker: Leonardo
en: It's fabricated with materials that shouldn't exist and yet this is clearly a very ancient artifact.

speaker: Mario
en: The Codex refers to it as a Piece of Eden.

speaker: Ezio
en: The Spaniard. He called it the Apple.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Like Eve's apple of forbidden knowledge. Are you then suggesting that this thing...

speaker: Leonardo
en: This must never fall into the wrong hands. It would drive weaker minds insane.

speaker: Ezio
en: No doubt the Spaniard will be relentless in his desire to gain it back.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Ezio. You must protect this with all the skills we have taught you.

speaker: Mario
en: Take it to Forlì. The citadel's walls are protected by cannons and our ally controls it.

speaker: Ezio
en: Who is this ally?

speaker: Mario
en: Her name is Caterina Sforza.

speaker: Ezio
en: You don't say. I think I may enjoy this mission.

speaker: Ezio
en: Thank you for everything, my oldest friend.

speaker: Mario
en: Leonardo! Ezio tells me that you travel often to Milano. I have a grand villa in Tuscana. You must come visit me there.

speaker: Thief
en: The Cento Occhi have employed a town scribe, Vincenzo. Despite his eloquence, he often fights with a Borgia guard named Galvano. We now have a chance to damage relations between our two enemies, find Galvano, kill him, take something personal from his body, plant it on Vincenzo, my brothers and I will ensure the Borgia hear what they want to hear.

speaker: Borgia captain
en: Vincenzo, Galvano's been murdered.

speaker: Vincenzo
en: What business is that of mine?

speaker: Borgia captain
en: You two were on bad terms, I have to search you.

speaker: Vincenzo
en: Fine, if you must, it will only serve to exonerate me.

speaker: Vincenzo
en: What is that?

speaker: Borgia captain
en: Come with me.

speaker: Political Suicide
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: The Polo Symbols: Church I
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Merchant
en: Secure those crates! We can ill afford to let their contents fall into the wrong hands.

speaker: Merchant
en: We'll see just how tough the holdouts are when they're forced to go without food. If they want to eat, they'll accept Savonarola as their leader. How the Medici family can still hold any sway in this city is beyond me... To think, I once considered them my patrons. But that was before the prophet opened my eyes. Then I saw the evils of commerce and the division it creates. Savonarola will lead us into a new era. One of fraternity, equality, and justice. All that remains is for us to cast off the shackles of our troubled past - and accept the Lord as our saviour and true leader.

speaker: Merchant
en: What... What have I done...

speaker: Ezio
en: You tried to force devotion.

speaker: Merchant
en: Sometimes the people must be told what to think.

speaker: Ezio
en: No good has ever come of that. Benché il mio cuore sia turbato, la mia mente è lucida (Though my heart may be tormented, my head is clear)... Requiescat in pace (Rest in peace).

speaker: Sofia
en: Salute. (Hello.) I'm closing in on two more books – one near Topkapı and the other in the Bayezid district.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bayezid first. Topkapı will be a dead end.

speaker: Sofia
en: Ah, si. (yes.)

speaker: Ezio
en: What do you make of this?

speaker: Sofia
en: Oh Ezio, è incredibile! (This is incredible!) Early coptic bindings, still in good shape. Amazing. This must be a 3rd century transcription of the original.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sofia, what happened here?

speaker: Sofia
en: Oh, that happens once or twice a year. People break in, thinking they will find money. I do not keep much here, but this time they made off with a portrait of some value. It is a shame.

speaker: Ezio
en: You keep working. I will find your painting.

speaker: Sofia
en: Ezio, the thief could be anywhere by now.

speaker: Ezio
en: If the thief came for money, but took a painting, he should be close by, eager to get rid of it.

speaker: Sofia
en: Well, if you happen to find it within the next few hours, meet me by the aqueduct. I will be running errands.

speaker: Ezio
en: There is a man with a suspicious look

speaker: Ezio
en: Where is it, ladro (thief)? Confess!

speaker: Thief
en: I have done nothing! You cannot prove a damn thing!

speaker: Ezio
en: I do not need to. I will just keep hitting you until you talk.

speaker: Thief
en: I found that painting, I mean, someone gave it to me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Get your story straight before you lie to my face.

speaker: Thief
en: God help me!

speaker: Ezio
en: He has much better things to do than answer your prayers.

speaker: Ezio
en: I do not care how you got the painting. Just tell me where it is.

speaker: Thief
en: I sold it to a merchant in the Bazaar. How else will I feed myself?

speaker: Ezio
en: Next time, find a nicer way to be an canaglia (asshole).

speaker: Merchant
en: I have a painting for sale, if you are curious. A luminous portrait. You see how lifelike she looks. Her beauty shines through!

speaker: Sofia
en: It is a good likeness, don't you think?

speaker: Ezio
en: I prefer the original.

speaker: Sofia
en: Buffone. (You jester.) This was a gift from my father for my twenty-eight birthday. I had to sit for messer (Mister) Albrecht Dürer for a full week. Can you imagine? Me sitting still for seven days? Doing nothing?

speaker: Ezio
en: I cannot.

speaker: Sofia
en: Una tortura! (Torture!) So, I found you another book location. And it is not far from here actually.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie. (Thank you.)

speaker: Sofia
en: Ezio, what is this all about? You are not a scholar, that much is clear. Do you work for the church?

speaker: Ezio
en: Not the church, no. But I am a teacher... of a kind. I will explain one day, Sofia. When I can.

speaker: Paola
en: You've done well, Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: What happens now?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Watch.

speaker: Savonarola
en: Silence! I demand silence! Why are you here?! Why do you disturb me?! You should be cleansing your homes. Cleansing your SELVES! There are bonfires to feed! Prayers to be said! Penance to be done!

speaker: Savonarola
en: You will do as I command! You will SUBMIT!

speaker: Savonarola
en: NO!

speaker: La Volpe
en: Find the Apple, Ezio! It can't be far.

speaker: Ezio
en: Salute (Hello), uncle. I did as you asked.

speaker: Mario
en: And quickly too. Ben fatto! (Well done!) Now let's teach you how to fight.

speaker: Ezio
en: No. As I said, we are leaving.

speaker: Mario
en: Ezio! You barely held your own against Vieri. You won't survive a week on the road. If you want to leave—so be it. But at least do so armed with the skills and knowledge necessary to defend yourself. If not for me, for your mother and sister.

speaker: Ezio
en: Fine.

speaker: Mario
en: Ottimo! (Very good!)

speaker: Mario
en: You can swing a sword, to be sure. But offence alone will not carry a battle. You must survive long enough to strike. I will teach you how to dodge.

speaker: Ezio
en: You said my father was more than just a banker?

speaker: Mario
en: No use dancing around it, I suppose. Your father was an Assassin, Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: I told you before: my father was a paper pusher.

speaker: Mario
en: No. He was born and bred to kill.

speaker: Ezio
en: I find this difficult to believe.

speaker: Mario
en: What of the list you carry? Do you think it's merely a catalog of debts? It holds the name of those responsible for your father's murder.

speaker: Mario
en: Bene (Good), I've taught you how to avoid your enemy's attacks. Now you'll learn how to turn them to your advantage!

speaker: Ezio
en: All this talk of Assassins and Templars. It reeks of fantasy.

speaker: Mario
en: Like something from an old parchment covered in arcane writing, perhaps?

speaker: Ezio
en: How did you know...?

speaker: Mario
en: You have your father's blade. I figured you'd have the Codex page he was holding as well.

speaker: Ezio
en: Codex?

speaker: Mario
en: Sì. (Yes.) A guide to the inner workings of our order—its origin, purpose and techniques. Our creed, if you will. Your father believed the Codex contained a powerful secret. Something that would change the world. Perhaps it's why they came for him...

speaker: Ezio
en: Assassins, Templars, Codex pages... This is a lot to take in.

speaker: Mario
en: You need to open your mind, Ezio. Always remember: Nothing is true, Everything is permitted.

speaker: Mario
en: You're making fine progress, Ezio! Today I'm going to teach you how to position yourself in battle. Where you stand and how you move make all the difference. Don't think I haven't seen you picking apart my library. I trust you believe me now?

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes. My father was an Assassin. But why the need for such secrecy?

speaker: Mario
en: Are you familiar with the Templars? One of several Knightly orders formed during the Crusades. History teaches they were disbanded nearly 200 years ago in France. Only they weren't. Merely pushed underground where they continued their nefarious work.

speaker: Ezio
en: What work?

speaker: Mario
en: The Templars seek dominion over man. And we, the Assassins, are sworn to stand against them.

speaker: Ezio
en: Was Uberto one of them?

speaker: Mario
en: Yes.

speaker: Ezio
en: And the other names on my father's list?

speaker: Mario
en: Templars as well.

speaker: Ezio
en: That means Vieri...

speaker: Mario
en: Just like his father, Francesco. Likely the entire Pazzi family.

speaker: Ezio
en: It would explain many things...

speaker: Mario
en: Well done nipote (nephew)! You've really come into your own.

speaker: Ezio
en: Thank you, uncle, for all you have given me.

speaker: Mario
en: You're family! Such is my duty and my desire!

speaker: Ezio
en: I'm glad you had me stay.

speaker: Mario
en: Good! You've reconsidered leaving!

speaker: Ezio
en: We sail for Spain in three days...

speaker: Mario
en: But, nipote (nephew), I have given you these skills that you might be better prepared to strike against our enemies...

speaker: Ezio
en: And if they find me, I will.

speaker: Mario
en: You want to leave, Ezio? To throw away everything your father fought and died for? To deny your heritage? Fine! Come vuoi. Arrivederci e buona fortuna. (So be it. Goodbye and good luck.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Uncle, wait!

speaker: Ezio
en: Why is he so upset?

speaker: Orazio
en: How can he not be? Vieri has been harassing us since you first arrived. To be expected, I suppose. Given his heritage...

speaker: Ezio
en: Uncle! Where is everyone?

speaker: Mercenary
en: They ride for San Gimignano to slay that snake, Vieri.

speaker: Ezio
en: I wish to join them.

speaker: Mercenary
en: You'll find what you need at the stables.

speaker: Claudia
en: Ezio, look at her. I still can't get her to talk! She spends all day and night in front of those feathers Petruccio used to collect. She can't let him go. I don't know what to do.

speaker: Ezio
en: Don't worry. She'll come back to us, I know it.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Ezio...? You are still alive!

speaker: Ezio
en: Look at this place! The past two years have been kind to you.

speaker: Leonardo
en: But you are not the same at all, are you...?

speaker: Ezio
en: I was hoping you might be able to help me with something.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Anything for you, my friend!

speaker: Leonardo
en: Aha! You've found another! How exciting!

speaker: Leonardo
en: Hmmm. This one is tricky to break... Clever in it's use of ancient languages. Maybe if I just... Oh... Oh! It seems to be a manual of sort for different assassination techniques.

speaker: Ezio
en: May I see it?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Wait! What's that?! It's not so much a design this time... Just a series of sketches. Hmmmm. What to make of all this... Hoho! Of course! And why not! What an inspired idea!

speaker: Ezio
en: Can you make it for me while I try what's in that manual fragment?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Take it, I'll have my assistant set up some dummies for you to practice with. Eh, Vincenzo!

speaker: Leonardo
en: I've done it! Come quickly! Look! Take it-- try it!

speaker: Ezio
en: Thank you, Leonardo.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Non c'è di che! (No problem!)

speaker: Ezio
en: There's someone I need to "see" while I'm here. I cannot approach him publicly... Would you know a way

speaker: Leonardo
en: La Volpe.

speaker: Ezio
en: The Fox...?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Sshhhhh!!

speaker: Ezio
en: Capisco... (I understand) But do you know where a fox might roam...?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Perhaps, near the Mercato (market) where the thieves dwell... Sta attento, amico! (Be safe, friend!)

speaker: Yusuf
en: A pleasant surprise, Ezio. We should trade stories if I am not dead by this time tomorrow.

speaker: Ezio
en: Is there a chance of that?

speaker: Yusuf
en: We learned that the Byzantines are planning to infiltrate Topkapı Palace now that Prince Suleiman has returned from his hajj (pilgrimage). If they do strike, it will be tonight at the cultural exposition the Prince has organized.

speaker: Ezio
en: So what is our plan?

speaker: Yusuf
en: Kardeshim (Brother), this is not your fight. No need to snare yourself into the Ottoman affairs.

speaker: Ezio
en: The Byzantines found a key beneath Topkapı Palace, and I would like to know how.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Ezio, we want to protect our Shehzade (Prince) not interrogate him.

speaker: Ezio
en: Trust me, Yusuf. Just tell me where to go.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Topkapı's main gate. We plan to dress as entertainers and walk right in.

speaker: Ezio
en: I will find a disguise and meet you there.

speaker: Ezio
en: Minstrels from Italia? I am going to enjoy this.

speaker: Yusuf
en: I look ridiculous. I feel ridiculous.

speaker: Ezio
en: My blade is too conspicuous in this outfit. Are you armed?

speaker: Yusuf
en: You know how to play that thing?

speaker: Ezio
en: I learned a few chords when I was young.

speaker: Yusuf
en: When were you ever young?

speaker: Guard
en: This courtyard is closed to the public. Turn around and start walking.

speaker: Ezio
en: Perdonate, buon signore. (Forgive me, kind sir.) We are this evening's entertainment.

speaker: Guard
en: Any old gerzek (fool) can carry an instrument around. Get lost.

speaker: Guard
en: You sound like a dying cat. What is this? Berbatsin! (You are terrible!) What are you doing? Pekala! (All right!) Go in and bother the guests with that noise.

speaker: Ezio
en: This courtyard is clear.

speaker: Yusuf
en: But I do not see Prince Suleiman. Follow me.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Now this is a celebration. Suleiman. The Sultan's grandson, and governor of Kefe. And he's only seventeen.

speaker: Ezio
en: We met on the ship. He told me he was a student. And who is that?

speaker: Yusuf
en: His uncle, Shehzade (Prince) Ahmet. The Sultan's favored son. He is grooming himself for the Sultanate as we speak.

speaker: Ahmet
en: Serefe! (To life!) Sagliginiza! (To health!)

speaker: Yusuf
en: Come, we have more Byzantines to find.

speaker: Janissary
en: Suikastchi! Suikastchi! (Assassin! Assassin!) Clear the courtyard! Shehzade (Prince) Suleiman, take cover! Follow them!

speaker: Yusuf
en: Ezio!

speaker: Suleiman
en: It is a relief to see you again, mio bel menestrello. (my handsome minstrel.) Did I say that right?

speaker: Ezio
en: Well enough. I hear you are a governor too. Is there anything you do not do?

speaker: Suleiman
en: I do not talk to strangers. I am Suleiman.

speaker: Ezio
en: Ezio Auditore...

speaker: Janissary
en: Shehzadem! (Prince!) Are you injured?

speaker: Suleiman
en: Who is your captain, soldier?

speaker: Janissary
en: Tarik Barleti. He is away on an errand.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Clear this body and send the guests home. Then summon Tarik to the Divan.

speaker: Janissary
en: Bashustane, shehzadem. (Yes, my Prince.)

speaker: Suleiman
en: Tarik Barleti is a captain in the Janissary corps, the Sultan's elite soldiery.

speaker: Ezio
en: They guard the Sultan, but not his family?

speaker: Suleiman
en: Not very well, evidently. Ezio, do you have time to spare? I would like your opinion on something.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Guzel (Good). Meet me when you are ready.

speaker: Ezio
en: How did we do?

speaker: Yusuf
en: We have won today and recovered our den. But we lost a few friends in this fight.

speaker: Ezio
en: So much death for so little gain.

speaker: Yusuf
en: You have some experience recruiting new Assassins, do you not?

speaker: Ezio
en: More than a little.

speaker: Yusuf
en: The people here are quite sick of these Templar attacks. Can you turn on your charms and find us a few more recruits?

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì. (Yes.) But THIS den will not do for training. Not this soon.

speaker: Yusuf
en: A good point. Speak with one of my men in Galata after you have finished. He can help you begin their training.

speaker: Civilian
en: Are you a compassionate man, efendim (sir)? Can you help me? That I stole fruit from a vendor, I will not deny. But only because my hunger has trumped my honesty. Bring me the key to these chains, and I will repay you tenfold.

speaker: Ezio
en: Wait right here.

speaker: Civilian
en: Obviously...

speaker: Civilian
en: You humble me, efendim (sir). I will return to the merchant I robbed and show him the same kindness.

speaker: Ezio
en: After you have cleared your conscience, amico (friend), consider joining our cause. To be an honest man, one needs honest work.

speaker: Civilian
en: I would be honored. Sagolun. (Thank you).

speaker: Wife
en: It is said you often help the common folk... could I ask you to beat some sense into my rotten, adulterous, joke of a husband?

speaker: Husband
en: All right! You know what, she's right. I am a pezzo di merda (piece of shit). I'll go home now.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Ezio! Since Madonna Solari's death, her brother Santino claims ownership of us. He struggles to gain Borgia favor and must prove himself leader of the courtesans. Humiliate him in public and he loses the support of the Borgia. We will not hear from him again.

speaker: Ezio
en: This man is a worthless liar, the courtesans of Roma will never answer to him!

speaker: Ezio
en: How are you holding up, Luis?

speaker: Luis
en: My patience is thin. Torquemada has already dispatched an Inquisitor to round up heretics for trial in Granada.

speaker: Ezio
en: Torquemada should be arrested for the abuses! Surely the Queen would side with you if the truth were exposed.

speaker: Luis
en: No, she would never believe such charges. Torquemada has been Isabella's confessor since she was a young woman.

speaker: Sánchez
en: Besides, it would be unwise to allow such turmoil to disrupt our plans for Christoffa.

speaker: Ezio
en: Hold fast, gentlemen. I will try to calm this chaos.

speaker: Ezio
en: Inquisitor soldiers are out in full force, meting out blind punishments for invisible offences.

speaker: Sánchez
en: Ezio, find the Inquisitor in charge of this operation. Eliminate him when he is alone, in secret, otherwise the violence will redouble and we will lose our advantage.

speaker: Yerman
en: Assassin!

speaker: Yerman
en: You have nothing to fear, efendi (friend)! Your identity is safe with me!

speaker: Ezio
en: Oh, thank heavens for that.

speaker: Yerman
en: Forgive my brash introduction, but I am an Assassin in training myself. I am strong, fast and... quite a hit with the ladies.

speaker: Ezio
en: That is a start.

speaker: Yerman
en: How about a race, eh? I will prove to you my skill. Say... to that spot there?

speaker: Ezio
en: Well, I could spare a few moments.

speaker: Yerman
en: All right, go!

speaker: Yerman
en: I told you I was good! Hahahaha! Here we go! Did you see that? Nice!

speaker: Yerman
en: You are good, old man!

speaker: Ezio
en: You have some natural talent yourself.

speaker: Ela
en: Yerman? Who is this?

speaker: Yerman
en: Ah! Ela! Come! Meet my new Mentor. I told you I was an Assassin, my love. And to think you ever doubted me.

speaker: Ela
en: Merhaba, efendim. (Hello, sir.)

speaker: Yerman
en: We were just taking the air, Ela, and... discussing tactics and such, no?

speaker: Ezio
en: No. We were discussing when your training would begin. Sunrise, every day, Galata tower. Understood?

speaker: Yerman
en: Ah... evet (yes). Of course, Mentor.

speaker: Sofia
en: Salve (Hello), Ezio. That took some time. What did you find?

speaker: Ezio
en: Something that may interest you.

speaker: Sofia
en: Mio Dio, che meraviglia! (My God, it's beautiful!) And here is my shop.

speaker: Ezio
en: Look at the margins.

speaker: Sofia
en: Strange symbols. And these are titles of books. Rare books! A few of these have not been seen for more than a millennium.

speaker: Ezio
en: Niccolò Polo hid these books around the city. This map should tell us where.

speaker: Sofia
en: Hmm. You are beginning to interest me. Vaguely.

speaker: Ezio
en: From what I can tell, I need these three books first. They may contain clues to locate the rest of these...

speaker: Sofia
en: Molto curioso. (Very curious.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Another was found beneath Topkapı Palace, but there is still time to reach the others.

speaker: Sofia
en: Found by whom?

speaker: Ezio
en: Men who do not read. Sofia, can you decipher this map? Help me find these books?

speaker: Sofia
en: Can I borrow them when you are finished?

speaker: Ezio
en: We will work something out.

speaker: Ezio
en: Yusuf. Salute. (Hello.)

speaker: Yusuf
en: Piri told me I might see you here. Did you find what you were looking for?

speaker: Ezio
en: I believe so. This is one of Altaïr's five keys. A strange artifact.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Ah... it is like nothing I have ever seen. You should keep it somewhere safe.

speaker: Ezio
en: At our headquarters, sì (yes). I will. What brings you this way?

speaker: Yusuf
en: I am coordinating with our allies today: The Thieves in the Bazaar, the Mercenaries near the Arsenal and the Romanies in the Constantine District.

speaker: Ezio
en: You are spread a bit thin, Yusuf. Let me speak with the Romanies myself. I have had so little contact with them in the past.

speaker: Yusuf
en: That would ease my mind. If you are in a hurry, you may travel by our network of tunnels. The air down there is a little foul, but the rats are no bigger than dogs. Have fun.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie. (Thank you.)

speaker: Angelina
en: The men in this town are no better than little girls. An army should be helping me, and look... no one! Cazzo (Fuck)! This box is heavy. I always get stuck with this.

speaker: Ezio
en: Need some help?

speaker: Angelina
en: Salve (Hello).

speaker: Ezio
en: So many flowers. Your husband must be very lucky.

speaker: Angelina
en: I am the lucky one. I have you here to aid me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Let me see what I can do.

speaker: Angelina
en: Back there, I may have given you the wrong impression.

speaker: Ezio
en: Oh?

speaker: Angelina
en: I have no husband. The flowers are for a party.

speaker: Ezio
en: Am I invited?

speaker: Angelina
en: To Claudia Auditore's birthday party in the Villa? If you are willing to help me again, I need someone with class to accompany me.

speaker: Ezio
en: What makes you think I have class?

speaker: Angelina
en: I could tell the moment I saw you. No one in this town walks with such bearing. I am certain Ezio Auditore himself would be impressed.

speaker: Ezio
en: Oh? What do you know of Ezio?

speaker: Angelina
en: Claudia thinks the world of him, but he rarely visits her. From what I gather, he's distant.

speaker: Ezio
en: She's right. I have been.

speaker: Angelina
en: Oh no. You? The party was intended to be a surprise. Promise you will not tell Claudia.

speaker: Ezio
en: What will you do to keep me quiet?

speaker: Angelina
en: I am sure I can think of several things.

speaker: Ezio
en: I'll be waiting to hear them when we get there.

speaker: Ezio
en: Now, about earning my silence.

speaker: Angelina
en: I have something in mind. There is one condition.

speaker: Ezio
en: Anything.

speaker: Angelina
en: You must wait until tomorrow.

speaker: Ezio
en: If it pleases you, I will not stand in your way.

speaker: Angelina
en: It will be worth the wait, Ezio. Trust me.

speaker: Helene
en: Ah, mon petit (my little) Assassin! Are you following me? Or am I following you? The heat seems to have affected my memory.

speaker: Raphael
en: And evaporated your manners. Who are you?

speaker: Ezio
en: Ignore her, Sanchez. She's harmless.

speaker: Helene
en: I wish I could stick around to suffer more insults, gentlemen, but I've got a date with a rather wealthy man named The Cygnet.

speaker: Helene
en: Well, not a date... more like an ambush. Au revoir! (Goodbye!)

speaker: Raphael
en: Follow her, Ezio. The Cygnet is a Templar financier. It would be helpful to know his face. But do not let him come to any harm. The last thing we need is to alert this agent to our presence.

speaker: Helene
en: You're spoiling all my fun, stranger.

speaker: Ezio
en: By the look of it, you were trained by the Assassins like me. Is that right?

speaker: Helene
en: Yes, well... It's a pity to let so much talent go to waste.

speaker: Ezio
en: Attacking that man would have cast suspicion on us, M'lady. Live how you like, but do not agitate the Templars at the expense of our safety. This war is no joke.

speaker: Helene
en: You don't think so?

speaker: Ezio
en: I wish I could convince you otherwise; your skills are impressive.

speaker: Helene
en: ...And open to the highest bidder. Perhaps the Templars will come to their senses before you do.

speaker: Reap What You Sow
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Red Letter Day
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Man
en: Please, don't call the guards. She would have wanted her burial here.

speaker: Ezio
en: Your wife?

speaker: Man
en: She was to be my wife...

speaker: Ezio
en: What happened?

speaker: Man
en: In the Colonna, she had a shop. The Borgia moved into the district and my wife refused to close. They found Monica with two thrown knives in her back.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do you know the killer?

speaker: Man
en: I heard of a woman who takes contracts for Cesare located near the antique baths.

speaker: Ezio
en: Leave before you are seen here.

speaker: Lia
en: Figlio di troia! Who sent you? Stop chasing me! Vattene via!

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in Pace (Rest in peace).

speaker: Ezio
en: You do not co-operate very well.

speaker: Dilara
en: I am here to rescue my men, not make friends. Right there.

speaker: Ezio
en: That armor is too thick for bullets. I will have to get in close.

speaker: Dilara
en: Janos. We have to help him.

speaker: Ezio
en: Men who make a fetish out of murder, deserve no pity.

speaker: Janos
en: Sen chok yasha, Dilara. (Bless you, Dilara.)

speaker: Dilara
en: Can you walk?

speaker: Janos
en: Evet. (Yes.)

speaker: Ezio
en: The rifles you brought. They should be destroyed.

speaker: Dilara
en: Most of them don't actually work. But the gunpowder is real. We could not fake that.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene. (Good.) Keep out of sight until you hear the explosions. Then, you run.

speaker: Dilara
en: Explosions? If you do that, all hell will break loose. You will panic the entire city.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì. (Yes.) I am counting on it.

speaker: Dilara
en: And then what?

speaker: Ezio
en: Then I find Manuel Palaiologos.

speaker: Luis
en: Our Assassin returns... did you find the spy?

speaker: Ezio
en: I did... I overheard him talking about keeping España (Spain) embroiled in this war deliberately.

speaker: Luis
en: Interesting... first they seek Christoffa's map, then they come to España to exacerbate a war that does not concern them.

speaker: Sanchez
en: We have suspected for some time that the Templars were planning their own expedition west. This may be their way of delaying Christoffa's journey.

speaker: Ezio
en: That atlas must contain wonders to inspire such broad schemes.

speaker: Luis
en: Indeed. But we will not know how true they are until Christoffa has set sail. And that won't happen until this war is over.

speaker: Sanchez
en: I fear something terrible has happened to King Muhammad. He was once an ally to the Assassins... but we have not heard from him in many months. Find him if you can, if the Templars haven't already.

speaker: Ezio
en: I'll enter through the catacombs. The Templar Spy preferred that route.

speaker: Cesare
en: I want to see the Pope!

speaker: Guard
en: His holiness waits for you at the top of the Castel, in his apartments.

speaker: Cesare
en: Get out of my way!

speaker: Lucrezia
en: I don't understand. I ordered a fresh batch of la cantarella last night.

speaker: Toffana
en: I am terribly sorry, mia Signora (My Lady), but the Pope has taken it all.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Where is the Pope?

speaker: Toffana
en: He meets with Cesare.

speaker: Lucrezia
en: Strange. He did not tell me Cesare has returned.

speaker: Toffana
en: That woman gives me so much trouble. Why didn't I stay in the stables? What a family this Pope has.

speaker: Sánchez
en: Ah... you have a knack for timing. One minute more and I'd have been dead, or worse... We riled up the Templars and now they're openly sending Inquisitors to imprison us.

speaker: Ezio
en: Revenge by proxy. It's time to find Torquemada and end this.

speaker: Sánchez
en: Before you do anything rash, make him talk. Find out how close to the Templars he really is.

speaker: Ezio
en: Steady now. Are you all right?

speaker: Assassin
en: I will be once I leave this place.

speaker: Sánchez
en: There he is! Our man of action. Thank you for your help.

speaker: Ezio
en: We cut it close, Raphael. And may yet have more work. Look here. I found a troubling list.

speaker: Sánchez
en: I know these men. But they are not local. They live in Zaragoza, in the kingdom of Aragon.

speaker: Ezio
en: The Inquisitor carried this.

speaker: Sánchez
en: Then it is safe to assume these men are also targets.

speaker: Ezio
en: Zaragoza will be my next stop. Will you come?

speaker: Sánchez
en: I will. Although my skills as a fighter are dwindling, I know the town well and could serve as your guide.

speaker: Assassin
en: Stay safe gentlemen.

speaker: Assassin
en: Many thanks, brother.

speaker: Assassin
en: You have my thanks.

speaker: Assassin
en: You have my thanks.

speaker: Assassin
en: Many thanks, brother.

speaker: Pedro
en: What in God's name is going on here! Four escaped heretics?

speaker: Guard
en: We did not anticipate such an organized resistance, Your Holiness.

speaker: Pedro
en: You assumed the people of Zaragoza would shrug off the random imprisonment of six eminent men?

speaker: Guard
en: We accused them of countless heresies, Pedro. Publicly!

speaker: Pedro
en: Your duties do not end with their imprisonment! They begin there! Whoever freed those four men will certainly be looking for the last. Guard our prisoner at all costs, or Torquemada will personally supervise your disemboweling.

speaker: Assassin
en: My most heartfelt thanks, stranger.

speaker: Ezio
en: Nothing strange about me, friend. We're one and the same.

speaker: Ezio
en: Ah, Monteriggioni... It has been far too long.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: What? Can it truly be? Master Ezio?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Master Ezio?

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Master Ezio!

speaker: Civilian 3
en: Welcome home, Master Ezio!

speaker: Seraphina
en: Master Ezio. I am Seraphina. Your sister sent me to meet you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Oh, my wounded pride. My only sister is so busy she must send a servant to greet me?

speaker: Seraphina
en: Master Ezio, Mistress Claudia did wish to escort you, but–

speaker: Ezio
en: Do not worry, Seraphina. I spoke in jest. It is a pleasure to meet you.

speaker: Seraphina
en: The pleasure is all mine. Your reputation precedes you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Ha! You are too kind, Seraphina.

speaker: Seraphina
en: Shall I escort you to Villa Auditore?

speaker: Ezio
en: No, I know the way. I may wish to see the city a bit before I head home.

speaker: Seraphina
en: As you wish. Mistress Claudia is eager for your arrival.

speaker: Herald
en: Look! Everyone! It's Master Ezio!

speaker: Ezio
en: And it seems she is not the only one.

speaker: Seraphina
en: I will let her know you are on your way.

speaker: Herald
en: Hey hey hey! It's master Ezio! He's back, everyone! He's back!

speaker: Ezio
en: The town has changed, but my feet know where to go. Down the via principale (main street) to the villa.

speaker: Civilian 4
en: You would think with all these workers, Monteriggioni would be in better shape.

speaker: Civilian 5
en: I trust Claudia has hired them for a reason. Hopefully, it's to rebuild the city. We shall see.

speaker: Civilian 6
en: Do my eyes deceive me? It's Ezio!

speaker: Ezio
en: "Dearest Giulia. Things go well in Venice. Marco and I have a lease on a workshop in . We cannot compete with the big merchants, but in time our efforts will bear fruit, I am sure of it. Until then, I have your love to keep me going."

speaker: Civilian 7
en: Workers? Bah! Pigro barbones! (Lazy asses!)

speaker: Civilian 8
en: They are here to help, no?

speaker: Civilian 7
en: All they seem to do is lay about.

speaker: Civilian 9
en: It's been a while since I've seen you.

speaker: Civilian 10
en: I've been traveling.

speaker: Civilian 9
en: I see. When did you get back into town?

speaker: Civilian 10
en: Just the other day.

speaker: Civilian 9
en: Going to stay here for a while?

speaker: Civilian 10
en: No, I'm leaving again in two days. Farewell!

speaker: Civilian 11
en: ...our friends at the Villa have found some "promising" work.

speaker: Civilian 12
en: Late last night, I saw some more workers coming into town.

speaker: Civilian 13
en: So? The speed they're going, they need as many hands as they can get.

speaker: Civilian 12
en: These workers had swords. Why would they need weapons?

speaker: Civilian 13
en: Maybe there were bandits on the road here?

speaker: Civilian 12
en: Perhaps... all I know is, I don't like it.

speaker: Civilian 14
en: I remember this city's glory days.

speaker: Civilian 15
en: Do you think they have passed us by?

speaker: Civilian 14
en: Look around. We are in degraded times.

speaker: Civilian 15
en: Perhaps you are right. But there is still hope.

speaker: Civilian 14
en: Hope for what?

speaker: Civilian 15
en: Hope that this city will rise again.

speaker: Ezio
en: A letter from Lucchese the carpenter, complaining about how lazy the new workers are. The fault of the younger generation, as it always is.

speaker: Ezio
en: The front door is blocked. I'll have to find another way in.

speaker: Civilian 16
en: Are you having a good day?

speaker: Civilian 17
en: I'm working. It's a day like any other.

speaker: Civilian 16
en: Surely some days are better than others.

speaker: Civilian 17
en: You couldn't tell by me.

speaker: Civilian 16
en: Try to look for the good things in life.

speaker: Civilian 17
en: If I find any, I will let you know.

speaker: Civilian 18
en: At this point, honest work would be better than this laying about.

speaker: Civilian 19
en: If the rumours are true, there will be plenty of money soon enough.

speaker: Ezio
en: The servant's entrance. I always preferred this way.

speaker: Civilian 20
en: It seems there are still areas of the villa that are off limits to us.

speaker: Civilian 21
en: For now, perhaps, but the damage to the villa is extensive. Every part of it will need our attention eventually.

speaker: Civilian 20
en: And if one of those parts were to, say, collapse unexpectedly?

speaker: Civilian 21
en: Then Mistress Claudia would have to send us to where our skills are needed, wouldn't she?

speaker: Ezio
en: Orders for the workers to reinforce the cavity in the wall of the weapons room in case of collapse. I hope this work has already been done. After two hundred years, I would hate for the Villa to fall down with me in it.

speaker: Ezio
en: Are these workers doing anything?

speaker: Civilian 22
en: –but Mistress, if you could only allow us into the attic, we could–

speaker: Claudia
en: No, I have grown tired of repeating myself. You will work where I tell you to work.

speaker: Civilian 22
en: Yes, Mistress.

speaker: Ezio
en: I see you still have a way with handsome young men, Claudia.

speaker: Claudia
en: Brother! Much like you, Ezio, that man was neither young nor handsome.

speaker: Ezio
en: Oh, you wound me.

speaker: Claudia
en: Oh, please, your pride is more resilient than armor. What took you so long to find the Villa?

speaker: Ezio
en: I got lost in the past while wondering the city.

speaker: Claudia
en: It is easy to do.

speaker: Claudia
en: I am glad you are here now, in the present. As is Monteriggioni.

speaker: Ezio
en: Monteriggioni has never recovered from the siege, has she?

speaker: Claudia
en: No. I hired some workers to do repairs on the Villa weeks ago. Since then, they've been coming to the city like ants on the scent of sugar. It seems that they just lounge about town waiting for work that I can not pay them for. Do me a kindness, dear brother.

speaker: Claudia
en: Take that model of the watch tower and place it on the map.

speaker: Ezio
en: My pleasure, dear sister.

speaker: Claudia
en: I know you love a good puzzle, brother.

speaker: Claudia
en: Up in the attic there is a music box. If you can figure out the way to get it to play you will get a wonderful surprise.

speaker: Claudia
en: Here is the key to your old room. Happy hunting, brother.

speaker: Civilian 23
en: I'm tired of waiting.

speaker: Civilian 24
en: But our orders are to wait.

speaker: Civilian 23
en: And which speaks louder, orders or empty pockets?

speaker: Civilian 24
en: They won't be empty for long. Just be patient.

speaker: Seraphina
en: Calm yourself. We knew this was a possibility.

speaker: Civilian 25
en: He wasn't supposed to be here for a few more days.

speaker: Ezio
en: Seraphina, and one of the workers. What do they have to talk about?

speaker: Seraphina
en: Shh. Mistress Claudia will accept no more excuses. I suggest you get back to work.

speaker: Ezio
en: My mother's box of feathers. The lid is closed. The collection complete. But you are forever in my heart, Petruccio.

speaker: Ezio
en: An unfinished letter. But I know Claudia's hand. "Ezio. I hope you find everything here, if not quite as you would wish it, at least to your satisfaction. Like us, Monteriggioni now has its scars, but these we can try to heal. I am glad you are home."

speaker: Ezio
en: Ah. The music box Claudia spoke of. If I am not mistaken, I recognize Leonardo's handiwork. I expect there will be more to this than it seems.

speaker: Ezio
en: Something I can use must be nearby.

speaker: Ezio
en: Something's not yet right.

speaker: Ezio
en: A letter from Leonardo. "Ezio, I hope this brings you some joy. Alas, painting is but a poor substitute for friendship. God willing, I will see you again soon." Maybe so, old friend.

speaker: Ezio
en: It is as if he plucked her from heaven, and gave her new life. Grazie (Thank you), Leonardo. I shall treasure this until my last day.

speaker: Civilian 25
en: Hurry! Bring it down!

speaker: Ezio
en: Dio Mio... (My God...) What's happening?

speaker: Ezio
en: Ugh! (cough)

speaker: Seraphina
en: I have not found what I seek! You sprang the trap too soon!

speaker: Civilian 25
en: Then I suggest you hurry. We have no way of knowing if he survived the collapse or not.

speaker: Seraphina
en: Very well. I had hoped to be the one to end his miserable life, but fate had other desires. Addio (Farewell) Master Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: So, these "workers" have shown their true faces. Unfortunately for them, I still live.

speaker: Ezio
en: It seems my enemies have met some resistance.

speaker: Ezio
en: Claudia?

speaker: Claudia
en: Enough napping, brother. We have vermin to exterminate.

speaker: Ezio
en: Your present was a gift of fate, then.

speaker: Claudia
en: Indeed. I will clear the bastards from this wing. To keep them from sneaking up behind you. Meet me in the workshop.

speaker: Ezio
en: I shall rid the Villa of the rest of these rattos (rats).

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: You look like you're getting a little pudgy around the middle.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: I am not!

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Sure you are. Who's been a greedy little pig?

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: You take that back!

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Or what? You'll bump me with your belly?

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: I'm warning you, don't say things like that or I'll do for you.

speaker: Claudia
en: Ezio! In here!

speaker: Claudia
en: Here brother! Seraphina and the leader of the bandits escaped into the Sanctuary. I will get rid of the rest that may be lurking on the grounds. Stop the thieves from defiling our home any longer.

speaker: Ezio
en: With pleasure, Claudia. Buona caccia! (Happy hunting!)

speaker: Civilian 25
en: Time for us to go.

speaker: Seraphina
en: By all means, before Ezio arrives.

speaker: Mercenary 3
en: No escape for you now, eh, old man?

speaker: Ezio
en: Oh, you fools, now you shall see what this "old man" can still do.

speaker: Mercenary 3
en: Once we get rid of you, Monteriggioni will be ours for the taking.

speaker: Ezio
en: Seraphina and the leader of these bandits have escaped into the secret passage behind the statue of Altaïr! I must follow quickly if I wish to stop them from escaping.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie (Thank you) Leonius.

speaker: Ezio
en: The Sanctuary gate looks different. I'm gone but for a moment and my sister starts changing things...

speaker: Ezio
en: Perhaps we shall meet in the next life, though in yours or mine, I cannot say.

speaker: Ezio
en: The thieves have entered the tunnels through the crypts. I must hurry. They cannot be far ahead.

speaker: Ezio
en: Pedro is dead, but I have neither seen nor heard any sign of Torquemada.

speaker: Sánchez
en: I guessed you wouldn't. It's a pity the Queen failed to mention to me that her dear Grand Inquisitor was in town.

speaker: Ezio
en: You have spoken with Queen Isabella?

speaker: Sánchez
en: I work for her, Ezio. As her treasurer. While you were out freeing our brothers, I was attending a finance meeting.

speaker: Ezio
en: An Assassin embedded in the monarchy's highest ranks... fascinating.

speaker: Sánchez
en: We have one of her ears, and it may be that the Templars have the other. Naturally, Isabella and King Ferdinand are ignorant of our infiltration. Come, I will tell you more on the road to Granada.

speaker: Ezio
en: I have freed those I came to rescue. I should be returning to Italia.

speaker: Sánchez
en: Ezio, I beg you to stay and help me. We are on the fringe of a grand Templar scheme. Come... I will explain.

speaker: Ezio
en: That shook them. I should be safe. As for Christoffa's safety... perhaps I should check back with Antonio.

speaker: Ezio
en: The meeting was a trap.

speaker: Antonio
en: Hm... Santángel's intuition proved correct.

speaker: Ezio
en: It seems so. Where is he?

speaker: Antonio
en: He asked that you meet him in the Gardens District, should anything go wrong.

speaker: Ezio
en: I'll go, but with caution.

speaker: Ezio
en: Antonio, who are these two men?

speaker: Antonio
en: I don't know. Santángel contacted the thieves' guild from España. When we met, he explained his plight and that's when I contacted you.

speaker: Ezio
en: I'm flattered, but let's not turn this into a habit.

speaker: Caterina
en: Buongiorno (Good day) Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: Caterina. To what do I owe the pleasure of your presence here?

speaker: Caterina
en: I desire...an allegiance. The papal armies have resumed their march on ﻿Forlì. Your mercenaries would be a great asset to my cause.

speaker: Ezio
en: It is likely that I can give you what you seek. But we will talk later.

speaker: Ezio
en: Mother.

speaker: Ezio
en: Machiavelli. It is done. Though not, I think, as any of us expected. I entered il Vaticano (The Vatican) and faced Rodrigo. He used the power of the Papal Staff against me, but I defeated him. Combining the Staff and Apple, I gained access to the Vault. There, a moving painting of the goddess Minerva spoke. She told of a terrible tragedy to befall mankind in the future, but gave hope of lost temples that will provide aid to humanity. And then she called out to a phantom, Desmond, as if he were there, standing beside me. After her warning, she vanished.

speaker: Caterina
en: Amazing!

speaker: Claudia
en: I cannot imagine such wonders!

speaker: Machiavelli
en: The Vault did not house the terrible weapon we feared. This is good news!

speaker: Claudia
en: What of this goddess, this Minerva? Did she appear human?

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes, but her words proved otherwise. All of her kind died many years ago. I wish I could show you the magic she performed.

speaker: Mario
en: Who is Desmond and where are these temples Minerva spoke of?

speaker: Ezio
en: I do not know.

speaker: Mario
en: Perhaps we must search for them.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Tell me how it ended with Borgia. Did Rodrigo beg forgiveness? Make excuses? Promise power in return?

speaker: Ezio
en: No. None of those things.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Interesting. I'm surprised he remained so composed.

speaker: Ezio
en: I let him live.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: The Spaniard lives?! Once our enemies are dead we can speak of vaults and gods and ancient places. You should have killed him. We're sure to suffer for it.

speaker: Ezio
en: I am not here to debate the past. Together, we should discuss the future.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: No. I am leaving immediately for Roma (Rome).

speaker: Mario
en: Ezio, I do not know why you spared him, but I trust your judgment. Machiavelli will come around.

speaker: Caterina
en: Welcome home.

speaker: Host
en: Welcome, Gentlemen. Whether you win or lose, this will certainly be your favorite game of the day! Ladies?! Here's how the game is played: all the ladies in the district have ribbons. Your job is to obtain them. Whoever has the most before my hourglass runs out is one step closer to winning the golden mask!

speaker: Ezio
en: Have anything for me, belle mie? (my beauties?) Could I trouble you for a ribbon? You're all looking lovely this evening. Hello, Ladies. Mind if I join you?

speaker: Host
en: We have a winner! You have more ribbons than any man here! You've proved yourself a favorite of the ladies! And are now one step closer to the greatest prize of all time!

speaker: Luis
en: I just received word... Christoffa has set sail from Palos with three ships and his precious atlas.

speaker: Ezio
en: I am honored to have helped you all, and wish I could be here to welcome him home, but conflicts of my own now draw me back to Italia (Italy).

speaker: Luis
en: Of course. The search for your stolen artifact continues.

speaker: Civilian
en: Luis! You must hide! Torquemada has dispatched guards to arrest you.

speaker: Luis
en: Contemptible man! He already forced a conversion from me... now I suspect the Templars are feeding him orders.

speaker: Ezio
en: Revenge for spoiling their war, I suppose. Stay here, Luis. I'll handle this.

speaker: Luis
en: This was no arrest. They intended to murder me! I'm certain they will be after Sánchez in due course.

speaker: Ezio
en: I won't let that happen.

speaker: Luis
en: Once Sanchéz is safe, find Torquemada and bring him to justice.

speaker: Ezio
en: Is that wise? You said yourself that Torquemada was off limits.

speaker: Luis
en: Just choose your best judgment...and let no one see you.

speaker: Ezio
en: This was your stand?

speaker: Rocco
en: Sì. Everything has been broken.

speaker: Ezio
en: Who did this?

speaker: Rocco
en: Donato Mancini. I rode against his horse in the races and made the mistake of winning. You though, everyone is talking about you. How you fight against the Borgia's men. Donato has demanded I meet him alone. I fear he intends to kill me.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where can I find him?

speaker: Rocco
en: Grazie a dio (Thank god). He is waiting at the Circo Massimo. That's where they hold their private races.

speaker: Donato
en: Where is Rocco? No one keeps me waiting! You are dead Rocco, you hear me!

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in Pace (Rest in peace).

speaker: Ezio
en: The Pazzi are dead. Every one of them.

speaker: Lorenzo
en: I must admit, I've never before believed I could desire the death of others so badly.

speaker: Ezio
en: Nor I...

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Ezio, thank you for the role you've played in keeping this dream of mine alive a little longer.

speaker: Ezio
en: L'onore è mio (It is my honor).

speaker: Lorenzo
en: What will you do now figliolo (my boy)?

speaker: Ezio
en: There are still others I must hunt, Signore. They're already digging their claws into the heart of Venezia.

speaker: Lorenzo
en: This cape identifies you as a friend of the Medici. As long as you wear it, the city guards will be more tolerant of your actions. But be warned, it will not grant you immunity from the law.

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Che la fortuna favorisca la tua lama (May fortune favor your blade).

speaker: Ezio
en: Leonardo!? Leonardo!

speaker: Civilian
en: Mi dispiace, Messere (I am sorry, sir), but he is gone. Maestro Leonardo was commissioned by a Venetian noble to paint some portraits. He paid for the Maestro to move his entire workshop to Venezia. It's quite an opportunity!

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie mile (Thanks a lot), friend.

speaker: Ezio
en: We should be close

speaker: Claudia
en: Grazie a Dio (Thank God).

speaker: Vieri
en: Buongiorno (Good day), Ezio! How could you leave Firenze without saying a proper goodbye?

speaker: Claudia
en: Ezio!

speaker: Ezio
en: What do you want, Vieri?

speaker: Vieri
en: So many things. A larger palazzo, two new steeds, a prettier bride... oh and yes... your life.

speaker: Vieri
en: My condolences for the loss of your father and brothers. What will happen now that there's no one left to help you? I have such wonderful things in store for your mother and sister.

speaker: Vieri
en: I grow tired of this game. Finish him! And do not spare the women!

speaker: Vieri
en: What sorcery is this?!

speaker: Mario
en: Not sorcery, boy. Skill!

speaker: Vieri
en: Show yourself!

speaker: Mario
en: As you wish.

speaker: Mario
en: Here. Use this!

speaker: Vieri
en: Kill them! Kill them all!

speaker: Ezio
en: You have my thanks.

speaker: Mario
en: Keep the sword, Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do I know you from somewhere?

speaker: Mario
en: Don't you recognize me? It's-a-me, Mario!

speaker: Ezio
en: Uncle Mario?

speaker: Mario
en: It's been too long, nipote! (nephew) Far too long! I heard what happened in Firenze. Terrible. Come, let's get you all away from here.

speaker: Ezio
en: Leonardo!

speaker: Leonardo
en: Ezio? What luck! I... er, have run into a bit of trouble.

speaker: Ezio
en: Let me see if I can help.

speaker: Leonardo
en: I know how to fix it, but lack the means to do so. If you could just lift the wagon?

speaker: Ezio
en: What is this thing?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Eh?

speaker: Ezio
en: It looks like a giant bat.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Oh, nothing, just an idea I've been working on.

speaker: Leonardo
en: I could not leave it behind.

speaker: Ezio
en: What is it for?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Well, I shouldn't really talk about it... al diavolo (To hell with it), I can't hold it in any more! Ezio, I think I have figured out how to make a man fly!

speaker: Ezio
en: Come on, I'll drive.

speaker: Leonardo
en: But I haven't even told you where I'm going?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Venezia (Venice), such a beautiful city. So many sources of inspiration! Ponte de Rialto, Piazzo San Marco, L'Arsenale–

speaker: Leonardo
en: What's wrong?

speaker: Ezio
en: We're not alone.

speaker: Leonardo
en: What's happening? Who are they?

speaker: Ezio
en: Rodrigo Borgia's men.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Why? What do they want with us?

speaker: Ezio
en: I think they want us dead. Leonardo, hide!

speaker: Leonardo
en: They're trying to climb on board! Knock them off! Ezio, someone's on top! Do sharp turns to make the carriage roll! Ezio! Watch out behind you! Do something! Watch out, don't let the carriage roll over.

speaker: Ezio
en: Hold on tight! This is going to be a little rough!

speaker: Leonardo
en: Hold on, Ezio! We're almost there! Be more careful, or we won't be able to fix it next time!

speaker: Ezio
en: Go, Leonardo! They're here for me, not you! I'll catch up with you later!

speaker: Thief
en: This is my turf. I can outrun any man I know here, but a little bird told me you're quite good. Care to prove it?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: The Followers of Romulus. This band of false-pagans has been terrorizing the city for months and driving the people into the arms of the Church.

speaker: Ezio
en: Quite convenient.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Exactly! I believe the Borgia are supporting them, but proof remains scarce. That is why the letter is so important.

speaker: Ezio
en: Here it is. I hope you can break a cipher.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Cazzo (Fuck), another encryption! This one was supposed to be legible. They are transmitting them using a code sheet. Without it, we have nothing.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sometimes logic is not the only way to win a war. Andiamo! (Come on!) You said we had allies in this city, bring me to them.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Follow me.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: We recently began travelling through the tunnels to avoid the guards, but many of the entrances in the city are broken. By using them, we can get to our destination rapidly without encountering resistance.

speaker: Fabio
en: Ben trovato (Hello), Niccolò! Ah! Ser (Sir) Ezio, a pleasure. Fabio Orsini, at your service. I've heard a great deal about you from my cousin—Bartolomeo d'Alviano.

speaker: Ezio
en: A fine warrior.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Fabio has lent us an unused storeroom on Isola Tiberina (Tiber Island).

speaker: Fabio
en: I know you were used to better accommodations in Toscana

speaker: Ezio
en: It is perfect.

speaker: Fabio
en: Bene (Good). Then, I am off to begin preparations for Romagna. Today, Cesare commands my men, but soon, I hope, we will be free.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Now, I propose we begin planning our assault on the Borgia.

speaker: Ezio
en: Oh, you think we are ready for such an attack?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Sì. (Yes.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Do you know, for instance, where the Borgia troops took Caterina Sforza?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: What?

speaker: Ezio
en: Are you also unaware that the Borgia have captured the Apple of Eden?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: How could we have lost the Apple?

speaker: Ezio
en: So, you do not know what goes on with our enemies. Do we at least have an underground here to work with?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Hardly. Our mercenaries are ensnared in a losing battle with Cesare's French allies. We have girls working for us in a brothel frequented by cardinals and other important Romans, but the Madame there is lazy and would rather attend parties than further our cause.

speaker: Ezio
en: What about the city's thieves? Do they have a guild?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Sì (Yes), but they refuse to talk to us. I don't know why.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: What are you going to do?

speaker: Ezio
en: Make some friends.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Ezio, you banished that spy Giuletta from the brothel, but she continues to give secrets to our enemies. A Spanish ambassador this time, her lover. We know he sells secrets to the church. Giuletta fears you now. Use that. Send her right to the arms of her Spaniard and kill him.

speaker: Ezio
en: Giuletta, I know of your treachery.

speaker: Giuletta
en: No! Please! Ezio! I can explain!

speaker: Giuletta
en: Help me!

speaker: Giuletta
en: Somebody! Stop him!

speaker: Giuletta
en: Please....I had no choice!

speaker: Ezio
en: Leave Roma. I don't want to see you here again.

speaker: Thief
en: I can beat any man in these parts when it comes to speed. They say you might be a real test for me.

speaker: Thief
en: I'm the best racer in this distretto. They say you're pretty good. I say prove it!

speaker: Sánchez
en: We have quelled the worst violence, but pockets of resistance remain. Bands of lawless soldiers are harassing civilians. We cannot let this city descend into anarchy. When you are certain the civilians are safe, meet me in the chapel at the center of the village.

speaker: Civilian
en: Soldiers kidnapped my wife and child. Follow me, sir! Quickly!

speaker: La Volpe
en: Follow me. But we must move fast! Think you can keep up?

speaker: Ezio
en: Nessun problema. (Not a problem.)

speaker: La Volpe
en: What are you doing back there? I said to keep up with me!

speaker: La Volpe
en: Here we are! Francesco de' Pazzi is meeting his people inside that church.

speaker: Ezio
en: How do I join them?

speaker: La Volpe
en: There are catacombs that run under the city. They'll lead you to a place where you can eavesdrop on the meeting. Grip that stone handle, turn it, then slide it down.

speaker: Ezio
en: Thank you for all your help, Volpe.

speaker: La Volpe
en: Buona Fortuna. (Good luck.)

speaker: Claudia
en: A cardinal revealed under... stress that Cesare plans to meet with Templar loyalists in the countryside. The cardinal departs for the meeting tonight.

speaker: Ezio
en: I will follow him.

speaker: Cesare
en: Join me and I will take back Roma!

speaker: Georges
en: We have decided to elect Della Rovere to the papacy. We are sorry.

speaker: Cesare
en: I paid for your appointment.

speaker: Georges
en: Roma is not the same as it once was. Borgia money has become tainted.

speaker: Cesare
en: You will regret this decision.

speaker: Georges
en: Assassino! Run!

speaker: Ezio
en: Hired men promise you their blood, but as soon as you need help, they turn against you.

speaker: Cesare
en: Guards!

speaker: Apprentice
en: Mentor, we have a problem. A great many Assassins have disappeared in recent months, and I believe I know why.

speaker: Ezio
en: Disappeared? Do you mean they have been killed?

speaker: Apprentice
en: I fear so. But there is no time to explain. Hide in the park west of here, and wait for me to arrive. You shall see for yourself.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sharpen your senses. There is a danger here I do not fully understand. You keep watch, and I will have a look around.

speaker: Ezio
en: I do not like the look of this.

speaker: Ezio
en: Follow that man! Only a guilty man runs with such speed.

speaker: Vali
en: And only a fool stops to fight!

speaker: Ezio
en: Are you injured?

speaker: Apprentice
en: My pride is wounded, and now my heart is heavy. That man, his name is Vali. He was an Assassin once.

speaker: Ezio
en: He has obvious skill. And a score to settle.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Evet. (Yes.) Until that man is caught or killed, I fear none of us will be safe in this city.

speaker: Ezio
en: And until you are properly trained, I will not let you go head-to-head with a killer as deadly as this man. Let us focus on further honing your skills first.

speaker: Ezio
en: Any news of the traitor, Vali? Have you found him?

speaker: Apprentice
en: He found us, Mentor. Two of our brothers were kidnapped from this den earlier today. Now Vali is demanding that we hand over our property to the Templars.

speaker: Ezio
en: No. We do not negotiate with men who use hostages as leverage. We hunt them down, and we eliminate them.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Then we should split up and search Galata now. We have little time to waste.

speaker: Ezio
en: Was it Vali who did this to you?

speaker: Assassin
en: Mentor, forget me. You have fallen for a ruse. He captured me to draw the Assassins away from our headquarters. He will be on his way there now!

speaker: Vali
en: You are a canny soldier, Ezio! But you alone are not enough to save this city.

speaker: Apprentice
en: I will follow from the rooftops.

speaker: Vali
en: Once your Creed was as vital to me as air and water... but when the Turks marched into Wallachia, and you Assassins did nothing to stop it, how could I continue to believe? If a man's philosophy does not let him protect his people, his home, and his family... what good can it do for the world?

speaker: Apprentice
en: Peace be with you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Who did this?

speaker: Courtesan
en: That monster, Malfatto!

speaker: Ezio
en: Did you see him?

speaker: Courtesan
en: That way!

speaker: Courtesan
en: Oh, Mina. I told you not to come out here...

speaker: Ezio
en: Animale! (Animal!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in pace (Rest in peace).

speaker: Yusuf
en: Sayin (Mister) Auditore! Word around the city is you're leaving us.

speaker: Ezio
en: Is nothing I do a secret?

speaker: Yusuf
en: Not to worry, brother. The captain of your ship is a friend. But neither of you are going anywhere just yet. The Janissaries have raised the chain across the mouth of the Haliç (Golden Horn) and ordered a full blockade until you are caught.

speaker: Ezio
en: They raised the chain for me?

speaker: Yusuf
en: We will celebrate later. Here, I have something for you.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Careful. This has fifty times the kick of our usual bombs.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene. (Good.) I know what to do.

speaker: Yusuf
en: The suspense is palpable.

speaker: Ezio
en: Yusuf, wait. Un favore. (A favor.)

speaker: Yusuf
en: Yes?

speaker: Ezio
en: There is a woman running a bookshop at the old Polo trading post... Sofia. Look out for her. She is a remarkable lady.

speaker: Yusuf
en: You have my word.

speaker: Ezio
en: Gather your men. This will attract some attention.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Those ships are armed. They're waiting to stop your boat. You take care of them. We will clear the docks.

speaker: Piri Reis
en: Yours is not a subtle approach.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì. (Yes.) Sorry for the delay.

speaker: Worker
en: So kill me then. At least I will have my honor, unlike the son of a pig farmer standing in front of me!

speaker: Brute
en: He should have kept an eye on his men. Trying to break into the treasury is a serious offense.

speaker: Agile
en: We needed him to build the ships! Now I'll have to go find another shipbuilder. Next time, inform the watch when you question an intruder instead of dealing with it yourself! Asino (donkey).

speaker: Agile
en: Cazzo (fuck)! Assassino (Assassin)!

speaker: Agile
en: I'm outpacing him! Leave me alone! He's not going to get me! Have to find a way out before he kills me! Kill the Assassin!

speaker: Agile
en: What is it, Capitano (Captain)?

speaker: Captain
en: Shh. Speak softly. I am about to make you rich. I just purchased a key from a man in the market that opens the Torre delle Milizie.

speaker: Agile
en: How does that make me rich?

speaker: Captain
en: The man claims there is a treasure in the topmost room. The stairs have partially collapsed. I need your help getting up–

speaker: Agile
en: We are no longer alone.

speaker: Captain
en: So you will bring the ladder to my wife?

speaker: Agile
en: Yes. Of course I will.

speaker: Captain
en: You are such a good friend to my family. I owe you a reward for your assistance.

speaker: Agile
en: I look forward to such a gift, Capitano.

speaker: Captain
en: Be ready with the ladder tonight.

speaker: Agile
en: What about my reward?

speaker: Captain
en: Assassino (Assassin)!

speaker: Guard
en: Go! We will stop him!

speaker: Agile
en: Cazzo (Fuck)! Stay away from me Assassino!

speaker: Showtime
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Federico
en: Quite a night!

speaker: Ezio
en: Indeed. I only wish they were all as much fun... Oh, wait! They are!

speaker: Federico
en: We should head home, Ezio. Father's sure to be wondering where we've gone.

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes. And I'd rather avoid a lecture.

speaker: Federico
en: Up for a little race, then?

speaker: Ezio
en: To where?

speaker: Federico
en: Uhh-Roof of that church. On the count of three. Uno. Due. Tre!

speaker: Federico
en: Baby brother still has much to learn! Come on, tartaruga!

speaker: Ezio
en: I almost feel bad about this! No shame in failure, brother!

speaker: Federico
en: Come on, then. This way.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where you going?

speaker: Federico
en: You'll see!

speaker: Federico
en: It is a good life we lead, brother.

speaker: Ezio
en: The best. May it never change.

speaker: Federico
en: And may it never change us.

speaker: Signs and Symbols, Part I
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus 2.03.

speaker: Signs and Symbols, Part II
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus 2.03.

speaker: Signs and Symbols, Part III
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus 2.03.

speaker: Sitting Ducks
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Ezio
en: Now I can get back up here.

speaker: Ezio
en: If I fall, that will aid me.

speaker: Ezio
en: That could help if I fall.

speaker: Ezio
en: Magnifico. (Magnificent.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Perfect! A route up if I fall.

speaker: Ezio
en: Amen.

speaker: Wife
en: A delicate matter... but important to me. Could you persuade the idiot I married to come home to me, and stay home? I implore you!

speaker: Husband
en: You win! Tell her I'll be a good, faithful husband!

speaker: Giovanni
en: Ezio! Come in, son. I need these packages delivered to associates of mine in the city. I also need you to retrieve a message for me from a pigeon coop not too far from here.

speaker: Ezio
en: Va bene. (Okay.) I'll get it done.

speaker: Giovanni
en: Come back here when you're finished. There are some things we need to discuss. And please, my son, stay out of trouble, hmm?

speaker: Thief
en: You Giovanni's kid?

speaker: Courtesan
en: No, idiota (idiot). He just happens to look EXACTLY like the man.

speaker: Thief
en: Give it here.

speaker: Thief
en: Don't worry boy, we're not contagious.

speaker: Thief
en: Least I'm not...

speaker: Mercenary
en: Here. Over here!

speaker: Ezio
en: I have a delivery from

speaker: Mercenary
en: Giovanni Auditore?

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Were you followed?

speaker: Ezio
en: No... Why would I be followed?

speaker: Mercenary
en: Give me the package.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Tell your father that they're moving tonight. He should as well.

speaker: Ezio
en: Who's moving? What's going on here?

speaker: Ezio
en: Wait! Come back! Explain yourself!

speaker: Contact
en: Please get this delivered on time and I'll repay you handsomely!

speaker: Luca
en: Molte grazie. (Thank you very much.)

speaker: Vicente
en: Eh grazie. (Thank you.)

speaker: Ludovico
en: Ahh grazie. (Thank you.)

speaker: Guard 1
en: Did you happen to see that? We caught another of the Sultan's spies lurking about. A woman this time, disguised as a harlot of low birth.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Sending his harem girls now, eh? It seems the Sultan is running out of skilled fighters. Where did you take her?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Inside. Into the prisons. But she won't last long. Not with Shahkulu in charge.

speaker: Manuel
en: How soon before my soldiers are trained to use those guns?

speaker: Shahkulu
en: A few weeks at most.

speaker: Manuel
en: The Janissaries will know I have betrayed them by now. But do they have the resources for retribution?

speaker: Shahkulu
en: Doubtful. The Sultan's battle with Selim commands most of their attention.

speaker: Manuel
en: Ah! What the hell is that smell?

speaker: Shahkulu
en: Apologies, Manuel. Some of these Ottoman prisoners are so... fragile.

speaker: Manuel
