en: Shahkulu, try to moderate your anger. I know the Sultan humiliated your people. But there is no need to spit on men who are beneath us.

speaker: Shahkulu
en: Hmm. You. Take the woman from the prison and bring her to the chapel.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Shahkulu, I don't have the key.

speaker: Shahkulu
en: Find it!

speaker: Guard 1
en: Who has the key? You?

speaker: Guard 2
en: I think Nikolos has it. He's on leave in the market.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Hristé mou! (Christ!) I'd like to run that man through with a spear.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Hey hey. Keep that to yourself, Entáxi (Okay)?

speaker: Dilara
en: You took your time.

speaker: Ezio
en: You are welcome.

speaker: Dilara
en: Aman Allahim! (Good God!) What is that?

speaker: Ezio
en: Not everyone was taken prisoner.

speaker: Dilara
en: Poor men. Allah sizi kutsasin. (God keep you.) That Turkmen renegade did this. Shahkulu. I'll kill him!

speaker: Ezio
en: Wait!

speaker: Artist
en: Reject the base and material! Seek salvation in the flames! The brush, the pen, the sculptor's clay! These are the Devil's tools, and what wretched things they birth! So today I call upon you to cast off these abominations; and consign them to the flames that you may be cleansed, that you may be FREE! Give them up – or my guards will do it for you! When I first became a painter, I did so as a means to express my devotion to God. Here, there was an opportunity to grow closer to him. For, if divinity was perfection, then surely capturing it would be divine? It seemed a righteous work. A form of prayer – of worship. And if others might gaze upon my creations and see something of the Lord within – well, would they not be also brought closer to Him? And so I thought myself an altruist. A speaker. A preacher. A guide to those who had lost their faith. But in truth, I was deceived. The Devil is a crafty sort, his manipulations, many. I thought my works were windows, but in truth, they were doors. Doors that allowed his corrupting influence to enter into our world. My art did not comfort people – but poisoned them instead! Made them lustful and base and immoral when before they were not. I had been deceived! But now I have a chance to make amends. To undo the damage I have wrought. I pray that you will join me! Free yourselves of deception and corruption! Give up your blasphemous works! Ink and canvas evoke desire, which in turn, births jealousy and rage. Destroy them! Suppress such emotions for they are dangerous! Dedicate yourselves wholly unto our Lord and his prophet, Savonarola! Give up those things that would tempt you from the righteous path!

speaker: Artist
en: What have I done... What have I done...

speaker: Ezio
en: Your actions were not your own.

speaker: Artist
en: But they were! My own self-doubt let him hold me as he did. I am sorry.

speaker: Ezio
en: As am I. Non è una scelta che compio a cuor leggero. Requiescat in pace. (This is not a choice I make lightly. Rest in peace).

speaker: Helene
en: It's a lovely night for a stroll, don't you think.

speaker: Ezio
en: You HAVE been following me. And now you're spying.

speaker: Helene
en: I go where the adventure goes. And right now it seems to be following you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Well, you're too late this time. The war is over.

speaker: Helene
en: I see. Then the rumors I have heard—about the planned assassination of Queen Isabella—I can just ignore those?

speaker: Ezio
en: That had better be a poor attempt at humor.

speaker: Helene
en: I wouldn't come all the way from Zaragoza to tell you a bad joke, Assassin. Rumor has it that a gang of Templars plan to ambush the queen during King Muhammad's abdication ceremony.

speaker: Ezio
en: That's happening now!

speaker: Helene
en: I don't suppose there will be a reward for saving the Queen's neck, hm?

speaker: Helene
en: Bravo, Ezio! Perhaps the life of an Assassin is not as dull as I had come to believe.

speaker: Ezio
en: You know my name?

speaker: Helene
en: Ezio Auditore da Firenze, yes. And may I say, the legend is not half as amusing as the truth. My name is Helene Dufranc. I was born into a family of Assassins like yourself... but unlike you, I had no patience for the duties of the Order.

speaker: Ezio
en: I am new to all of this myself.

speaker: Helene
en: I know your purpose is a grand one, Ezio. I hope it has been worth all the effort and pain.

speaker: Ezio
en: Thank you for your help, Helene. Will you join us in Italia (Italy) some day?

speaker: Helene
en: And trade one family of Assassins for another? I'm flattered, Ezio, but I prefer the life of a rogue.

speaker: Ezio
en: If that is your calling, I wish you the best of luck... but as far from me as possible.

speaker: Helene
en: Ah, this never gets old...

scene: Stop the Burning of the City
speaker: Sánchez
en: War is ended, and a conciliatory King Muhammad is in a meeting with the Queen to discuss terms.

scene: Stop the Burning of the City
speaker: Christoffa
en: Oh, I have been waiting for this moment, Luis! Do you feel it, the tide shifting beneath us?

scene: Stop the Burning of the City
speaker: Luis
en: Patience, Christoffa. It will take some time for Isabella to entertain thoughts of spending money on you.

scene: Stop the Burning of the City
speaker: Christoffa
en: I have been waiting SIX YEARS for an answer from the Queen. If she cannot indulge me now, I will indulge other offers!

scene: Stop the Burning of the City
speaker: Luis
en: Christoffa, don't be foolish. We're close!

scene: Stop the Burning of the City
speaker: Christoffa
en: We've been close for too long, Luis. It's now or never.

scene: Stop the Burning of the City
speaker: Luis
en: Damn him. It's too soon to go begging for money from a war weary monarch.

scene: Stop the Burning of the City
speaker: Civilian
en: Help! We need soldiers! Mobs are trying to burn the city down!

scene: Stop the Burning of the City
speaker: Sánchez
en: Ezio, this is more Templar meddling.

scene: Stop the Burning of the City
speaker: Sánchez
en: Wars never end abruptly, do they?

scene: Stop the Burning of the City
speaker: Ezio
en: They never end at all, Sánchez. It just appears that way when the body count is low.

scene: Stop the Burning of the City
speaker: Sánchez
en: You have given us an advantage. And when we secure a mandate for , you will have given us hope as well.

scene: Stop the Burning of the City
speaker: Ezio
en: My understanding is still cloudy. Hope for what exactly?

scene: Stop the Burning of the City
speaker: Sánchez
en: Most men stoke their imagination of what lies beyond the ocean sea with stories of quick routes to Cipango and Cathay... But Christoffa's maps tell another tale, one the Templars know quite well... legends of an intermediate land as large as our own.

scene: Stop the Burning of the City
speaker: Ezio
en: Another continent?

scene: Stop the Burning of the City
speaker: Sánchez
en: A new world, Ezio...

speaker: Supply in Demand
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Doctor
en: It's quite simple, amici (my friends). If you desire care, you'll submit yourselves fully to our new ruler. The choice is yours to make. Continue to support the Medici—who—as you know, have long since fled Firenze—or accept Savonarola. Why fight it? Why refuse? He is a good man, strong of character and morals. He seeks to save us from ourselves. And saving is what we need. Before Savonarola came to us, we were mired in sin: gluttony, lust, pride, avarice... Need I go on? We cared over much for earthly things and pleasures of the flesh. We shied from the face of God. And why wouldn't we, shamed as we were at our actions? This is why you ache and take ill. It is divine retribution! But fear not! If you wish to be healed—if you wish to be SAVED—only pledge yourself to Savonarola. Do this, and I will admit you. Within these walls you will be granted the finest care Firenze has to offer. Free of charge. For I am a being of compassion and mercy—just as the Lord made me.

speaker: Doctor
en: You have spilled the blood of a healer.

speaker: Ezio Auditore
en: No. I have spilled the blood of a tyrant.

speaker: Doctor
en: To command such power over the body, between this world and the next. It seems, I grew intoxicated.

speaker: Ezio Auditore
en: And now you grow still. La tua morte non sarà inutile... Requiescat in pace. (Your death will serve a purpose... Rest in peace.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Luis Santángel? This is an unusual coincidence.

speaker: Luis
en: Not a coincidence at all, Ezio. Sánchez sent word that you might be joining us. We Assassins run in close circles, after all.

speaker: Sánchez
en: The world is not so large as it feels, is it?

speaker: Luis
en: Wherever you go, you are bound to find one of us working in secret... in the court of a monarch, for instance.

speaker: Ezio
en: Both of you work for Isabella and Ferdinand?

speaker: Sánchez
en: It has taken many years and reluctant conversions to gain their confidence. But it has been necessary. The King and Queen are easily swayed by pious blather.

speaker: Luis
en: There will be time later to explain our purpose in greater detail, but we have need of your skills now. A Templar Spy is passing false information to King Muhammad inside the city, encouraging him to continue the fight. Find the secret passage the spy is using before killing him.

speaker: Sánchez
en: If this war does not end swiftly, the Templars will continue to use the chaos to their advantage.

speaker: Tactical Correction
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Ezio
en: So, these are the new cannons?

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Yes, Signor (Mr.) Ezio.

speaker: Ezio
en: May I try one?

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Yes, but...

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Go on. Tell him.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: We cannot seem to make them work properly and the fool who mounted them is nowhere to be found.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then it is up to me to find him.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: We do not want to waste your time.

speaker: Ezio
en: It is not any trouble. I have all the time in the world now.

speaker: Ezio
en: Salve, Messere (Hello, Mister). We need you to fix the cannons on the battlements.

speaker: Engineer
en: Leave me be. I do not begin repairs before noon.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do you know what time it is?

speaker: Engineer
en: I make cannons, not clocks.

speaker: Ezio
en: If you are busy, someone else will fix them.

speaker: Engineer
en: Uno momento (One moment). No one else will touch my cannons.

speaker: Engineer
en: Soldiers have no respect for artillery. They expect a gun to work like magic. You need to feel her out, give her a little encouragement. We are only equipped with simple cannons now, but I got hold of a design from Francia (France), a hand cannon, something called a . Imagine, firing a cannon... from your hands. That is the future.

speaker: Engineer
en: What have you done?

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: We used them.

speaker: Engineer
en: They were not ready for firing! You could have gotten us all killed. Let me see.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: His breath is more fatal than our cannons.

speaker: Engineer
en: Only when you two fools are shooting them. There. Try it. Aim at something to test the alignment.

speaker: Engineer
en: Perfetto (Perfect). At least someone here knows how to shoot. Now for the other one.

speaker: Ezio
en: I must go.

speaker: Engineer
en: Too bad it will not do you any good.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Very funny. Now, fix the second cannon.

speaker: Templar Raid at Ginestra Florita
en: was a genetic memory.

speaker: Known Owners
en: Unknown Current Status: Unknown The Memory Seal is an obscure Precursor relic, apparently capable of storing recorded memories. The small, circular object seems made of wrought metal and stone, resembling ancient Phaistos Disks, featuring symbols, stylized icons, and geometrical shapes.For more information about Precursor Relics, see page 186 of the Assassin's Creed - Animus Handbook.

speaker: Ercole
en: Leonardo, I still cannot comprehend why you have turned against the ideals we always held dear!

speaker: Leonardo
en: Trust is a terrible thing.

speaker: Ercole
en: You are betraying mine!

speaker: Ercole
en: Tell me where the entrance is.

speaker: Leonardo
en: How naïve of me... To have thought you sought knowledge as I did.

speaker: Ercole
en: Why seek knowledge without putting it to use? We have the chance to fashion a better world, one in which we have the freedom to shape our own destiny.

speaker: Leonardo
en: And what if we choose not to be a part of your vision?

speaker: Ercole
en: That is foolish. Do you not see? We can banish ignorance. Free people from their social classes and kingdoms, from their animal emotions. Every one will have the truth at their grasp.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Beating me down here in the dark enlightens the people of Italia?

speaker: Ercole
en: The Pythagorean unifier is in that temple. We both know it. That number is coupled to all nature, all things. It is the source. With it, we can open the minds and souls of men. We can fill them with knowledge.

speaker: Ercole
en: That is the Hermetic vow. Together, we will make mankind into Gods. Now, show me the entrance.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Why? Do you not know where it is?

speaker: Ercole
en: How could I?

speaker: Leonardo
en: You know mankind's wants and needs, I assumed discovering the location of a simple hidden entrance would be an easy feat.

speaker: Ercole
en: You– Where is it?!

speaker: Leonardo
en: Guess.

speaker: Ercole
en: I am finished with your obstinacy. Procedete! (Do it!)

speaker: Leonardo
en: My body may feel pain, but my mind will remain unharmed.

speaker: Ercole
en: Impressive. Do it again. Again.

speaker: Ezio
en: Stop.

speaker: Ercole
en: Ezio Auditore! You who arrested Cesare Borgia, who stopped the spread of Roman ignorance, convince our friend Leonardo to open the temple and usher in the golden age of mankind.

speaker: Ezio
en: Should I persuade "our friend" by kicking him? Or would you rather I used my knife?

speaker: Ercole
en: On the contrary, there is nothing I would like more than an amiable solution. Help Leonardo see reason. With the Pythagorean unifier, we will remake humanity together.

speaker: Ezio
en: Not under my creed.

speaker: Ercole
en: Then the revolution will begin without you. Ucciderlo! (Kill him!)

speaker: Ercole
en: Leonardo, I must know. Please, for the future of mankind. Tell me! We are running out of time!

speaker: Ercole
en: Go! Stop him!

speaker: Ezio
en: Very foolish.

speaker: Ercole
en: Stay away from me, Assassino. (Assassin.) We are all the same underneath, yet these people persist in their witch hunts! You intend to banish us back to our primitive origins? Firenze against Venezia, Venezia against Roma. Ignorant group against ignorant group forever, is that what you want?

speaker: Ercole
en: You... an Assassin... the enemy of knowledge?

speaker: Ezio
en: One must choose to search for truth. Forcing it on others accomplishes little.

speaker: Ercole
en: These lost people... warring kingdoms... I would have ended their suffering.

speaker: Ezio
en: Che tu possa conoscere la verità nella morte. (May you know the truth in death.) Requiescat in pace. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Come. Let us leave this place.

speaker: Leonardo
en: We cannot, Ezio. Not without reaching the final room of the temple.

speaker: Ezio
en: You are hurt.

speaker: Leonardo
en: I will be fine. If that number is left intact, we risk another madman discovering it.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Coming?

speaker: Ezio
en: Take that torch. I will lead the way.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Thank goodness I sent Massimo to look for my paintings, it delayed their progress significantly.

speaker: Leonardo
en: The Pythagoreans believed that the soul moved through cracks in the earth, like a beam of light. It ignites fire, which symbolizes knowledge.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Perhaps you could move the mirrors to concentrate the light on that rope.

speaker: Ezio
en: Now I can get back up here.

speaker: Leonardo
en: You are almost there!

speaker: Ezio
en: Easy for you to say.

speaker: Leonardo
en: We must continue onward!

speaker: Leonardo
en: I suppose Salaì is out having fun spending my hard-earned florins?

speaker: Ezio
en: He is safe at home.

speaker: Leonardo
en: I am relieved... about the florins of course.

speaker: Ezio
en: You do not need to lie to me. Salaì fits you. I approve.

speaker: Ezio
en: Leonardo da Vinci at a loss for words? That is a first.

speaker: Leonardo
en: This room could use some light.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Do you hear that? The sound of wind.

speaker: Leonardo
en: The Pythagoreans believed all the forces of nature could be whittled down to numbers. Mathematica can then act on nature, allowing man to harness nature's power.

speaker: Ezio
en: Now I can get back up here.

speaker: Leonardo
en: The wheel is turning. You are channeling the air, keep going!

speaker: Ezio
en: Perfect, a route up if I fall.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Only one final room before we reach the center!

speaker: Leonardo
en: How unexpected! Delightful.

speaker: Ezio
en: The fire of knowledge.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Correct! Harmony was achieved for the Pythagorean when multiplicity became unity. When many thoughts combine to form one original idea.

speaker: Ezio
en: That could help if I fall.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Yes! How enlightening!

speaker: Ezio
en: Very funny.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Unity is achieved! But the door is not opening.

speaker: Ezio
en: Leonardo, come here. Recognize these symbols?

speaker: Leonardo
en: No... Wait. These are the symbols that were shown to me by the Apple of Eden! They are in the wrong order. Let me just... if I rearrange these... done!

speaker: Ezio
en: I know this architecture.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Those are not Pythagorean symbols. 43 39 19 N 75 27 42 W. Nothing. The Cult of Hermes is wrong. The number is meaningless.

speaker: Leonardo
en: You are leaving?

speaker: Ezio
en: No mere number can repair the world. Come, my friend, help me charter a ship to Navarre. I must finish with Cesare Borgia.

speaker: Ezio
en: It is not intended for us.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Ezio. What are you not telling me?

speaker: Ezio
en: What else are you working on?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Well, I have begun several dissection studies. Then King Louis XII seems interested in hiring me as an engineer. Oh yes, I am thinking of repainting the lost in the Villa fire. Salaì would model for it again, of course. Then, perhaps I will study a woman with child to see how her body changes.

speaker: Ezio
en: Interesting. Tell me more.

speaker: Ezio
en: How best to get inside? I'll scale the wall and....oh that's not good. I'll never make that jump. I need to find another way.

speaker: Rosa
en: I need your help.

speaker: Ezio
en: Hey, I remember you.

speaker: Rosa
en: We need to go!

speaker: Ezio
en: You never did apologize for knocking me over.

speaker: Rosa
en: Now!

speaker: Ezio
en: Va bene, (Okay,) where to?

speaker: Rosa
en: The water.

speaker: Ezio
en: That doesn't exactly narrow it down...

speaker: Rosa
en: I'd be better off on my own! What are you doing?! Hurry up! Goddam archers... Quickly! They're getting closer!

speaker: Rosa
en: Ahh! Cristo, my leg!

speaker: Ezio
en: Can you walk?

speaker: Rosa
en: What do you think?!

speaker: Ezio
en: I never did catch your name.

speaker: Rosa
en: Rosa.

speaker: Ezio
en: Onorato, (Honored to meet you,) Rosa. I'm Ezio.

speaker: Rosa
en: I know.

speaker: Ezio
en: What do you mean "I know"?

speaker: Rosa
en: Non ora. (Not now.) Now is not the time for small talk. Or are you blind? Hey! Hey! Don't forget about me! I hope you weren't planning on leaving me here! Pick me up!

speaker: Rosa
en: Ugo!

speaker: Ugo
en: What's this?!

speaker: Ezio
en: Rosa's been wounded.

speaker: Ugo
en: Pass her here. We'll go the rest of the way in the boat.

speaker: Ezio
en: Careful.

speaker: Ezio
en: Go! I'll deal with the guards!

speaker: Ugo
en: Kill them, Ezio! Quickly!

speaker: Rosa
en: Keep going, Ezio! Clear the way for us!

speaker: Ugo
en: They're all over the rooftops! Do something! Quickly!

speaker: Rosa
en: Figlio di puttana! (Son of a bitch!) Stop them!

speaker: Ugo
en: They're shooting at us!

speaker: Rosa
en: They're still shooting at us!

speaker: Rosa
en: He's dead, idiota! (idiot!) Say a prayer later! I need to see--ugh--I need to see Antonio!

speaker: Ugo
en: Porco demonio! (Goddammit!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Be careful! Let me do it! Go and find Antonio!

speaker: Rosa
en: Oh, cristo, Ugo! Do what he says!

speaker: Ugo
en: Qua l'ultimo arrivato da gli ordini! (I can't believe I'm taking orders from this guy!)

speaker: Rosa
en: So tired...

speaker: Ezio
en: Hey, hey! Wake up!

speaker: Ezio
en: We need help!

speaker: Ugo
en: Where's Antonio?! Make yourselves useful! Clear a space for her! (to Ezio) Put her down, there.

speaker: Rosa
en: Where are we?

speaker: Ezio
en: Home. They've sent for help.

speaker: Rosa
en: Thank you...

speaker: Antonio
en: Rosa! What's happened?

speaker: Rosa
en: Just get this thing out of me!

speaker: Antonio
en: Soon, soon. Let's have a look first. Clean entry and exit through the thigh. That's good.

speaker: Rosa
en: Get. It. Out!

speaker: Antonio
en: Rosa, we must take care not

speaker: Rosa
en: NOW!

speaker: Antonio
en: Come vuoi. (As you wish.) Tenetela (Hold it)!

speaker: Antonio
en: I'm sorry, piccola. (sweetheart.)

speaker: Rosa
en: Sorry?! Ficcatelo nel culo your sorry! (You can shove your "sorry" up your ass!)

speaker: Antonio
en: Go fetch Bianca and be quick! (to Ezio) Help me with this.

speaker: Ezio
en: How?

speaker: Antonio
en: Take a clean piece of linen. When I remove my hand, press the cloth into her wound. Are you ready? Now!

speaker: Rosa
en: Ahh! Porca puttana! (son of a bitch!)

speaker: Antonio
en: Ben fatto. (Well done.) You work well under pressure. She's spirited, this one.

speaker: Rosa
en: Porca puttana!

speaker: Antonio
en: Avanti! (Come on!) Get Rosa inside so that Bianca can close the wound! (to Rosa) You'll be alright. The worst has past.

speaker: Rosa
en: Ti venisse il cancro, brutto bastardo! (I hope you catch plague, you bastard!) ...a te e quella grandissima troia di tua madre! (...you and your whore mother!)

speaker: Antonio
en: Thank you. Rosa is most dear to me. If I had lost her...

speaker: Ezio
en: I've always had a soft spot for women in distress.

speaker: Antonio
en: So I've heard. Don't look so surprised. We know all about you, Ser Ezio. Your work in Firenze and the rest of Tuscany. Good work too, if a little unrefined.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then you know why I'm in Venezia?

speaker: Antonio
en: I can guess. When you have a minute, come see me in my office. There's something we should discuss.

speaker: Ezio
en: Ah, the Hidden Blade. The Assassin's weapon of choice.

speaker: Ezio
en: The staff has been dismissed for the day. There will only be a couple of guards for me to deal with. Good to know.

speaker: Ezio
en: Once again, my path leads back to Venice. Alas, I must deny my friends here the pleasure of my company. I have a sword to retrieve, and a lesson to teach: no-one steals from an Auditore and lives to boast about it.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: I wish we were with the rest of the troop right now instead of being stuck standing guard here.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Why? They're working hard out there in the countryside. All we have to do is watch an empty building and drink wine.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: They'll be getting plenty of chances to line their pockets when the day comes.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: We'll be getting our reward sure enough. Don't be impatient.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: I'm not impatient. I just want my fair share.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: I have no doubt we will all get what we deserve.

speaker: Ezio
en: A map of Monteriggioni... why is this here?

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: When am I done? I really was looking forward to the chance to do a little, shall we say, acquisitions work.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Why are you in such a rush?

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: I have bills to pay. And they won't give me credit down at the wine shop any more.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Ah, so your money was burning a hole in your purse. Now you need more, and you thought the other operation would give you some easy pickings.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: It's not like that, but that doesn't mean it's any less unfair we can't be part of the fun.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Fun? I suppose that's what you'd call it.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Why not? No guards, no real opposition. I'll wager the men who got sent there come back with jewels and coin galore. You've heard the stories of hidden treasure. We all have.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Yes, and they're probably just that—stories. You ask around and every little town supposedly has secret tunnels filled with treasure. I don't believe a word of it.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Shows what you know, then.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Not as if it matters. We're here, and we've got a job to do here. So quit your bellyaching about all the treasure you won't be bringing home, and straighten up and man your post instead.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Fine, fine, whatever you say. But when the lads come home with their purses full, don't say I didn't tell you.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: I'll take that risk.

speaker: Ezio
en: It says here the painting is to be delivered to Francesco Rizzo. I know that name...

speaker: Ezio
en: There's an empty socket above the fireplace.

speaker: Ezio
en: What is this?

speaker: Ezio
en: Two pieces join together. But where do they go? I need to keep looking.

speaker: Ezio
en: A secret passage...

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Quickly, I must leave the city tonight!

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Yes, mistress.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: I should never have been away so long. Is my carriage ready?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Yes, mistress.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Good. Now put your back into it. There is no time to waste.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Yes, mistress.

speaker: Ezio
en: What is this? A treasure room of some kind? My sword could well be here.

speaker: Ezio
en: My sword must be here somewhere.

speaker: Ezio
en: Christ and the Madonna. A popular .

speaker: Ezio
en: A warrior from ancient times. I am glad we dress more sensibly these days.

speaker: Ezio
en: A lion. The symbol of San Marco. Though this one does not have wings.

speaker: Ezio
en: That is quite the treasure. On whose head did it once rest, I wonder?

speaker: Ezio
en: The work of a master, undoubtedly. Though I do not know who.

speaker: Ezio
en: Here it is.

speaker: Ezio
en: A note. "The sword is attractive, but ultimately useless for our purposes. It is not the item we need. We must plan more carefully, and try again." There is no signature.

speaker: Ezio
en: My yataghan. Such an elegant blade.

speaker: Ezio
en: A hidden door... Ah. Time to get out of here.

speaker: Ezio
en: "I have found my father's notebooks, and within them, the key to the power I seek." Huh. The ravings of a lunatic, no doubt.

speaker: Ezio
en: The path ahead is guarded, but there is always a way through.

speaker: Ezio
en: I could use this to distract the guards.

speaker: Ezio
en: The sword is mine again, but my heart is not yet at ease. I will make for Monteriggioni. It is time I went home.

speaker: Maid
en: Spingi! Spingi! (Push! Push!) Di nuovo! (Again!)

speaker: Maid
en: Si! Si! Brava! (Yes! Yes! Good!)

speaker: Maid
en: It is a boy!

speaker: Giovanni
en: Oh, my love! Mi dispiace! (I'm sorry!) I was at the bank when they told me! Did I miss it? Am I too late?

speaker: Giovanni
en: Give him here...

speaker: Maria
en: Giovanni...?

speaker: Giovanni
en: Shhh, my love. It will be alright.

speaker: Giovanni
en: Tu se un Auditore. Sei un combattente. Perciò combatti! (You are an Auditore. You are a fighter. So fight!)

speaker: Giovanni
en: Listen to him! A fine set of lungs!

speaker: Maria
en: And what shall we call him, my love?

speaker: Giovanni
en: Ezio! Ezio Auditore da Firenze!

speaker: The Final Humiliation
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore's genetic memories stored in the Abstergo Cloud and relived by an Assassin hacker in 2023 through the Animus.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Merhaba (Hello) Mentor. In all your wanderings, have you heard the name Lysistrata?

speaker: Ezio
en: The drama by Aristophanes?

speaker: Apprentice
en: Not quite. She is a local actress named for the character in that play.

speaker: Ezio
en: I have not.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Will you walk with me? We have a small problem.

speaker: Apprentice
en: We have been hearing rumors for some time now that paint Lysistrata in a very dangerous light. We fear she is responsible for the disappearance of several eminent men throughout the empire.

speaker: Ezio
en: But you have no proof?

speaker: Apprentice
en: Not yet. But today, we may. There she is. And she has company. I will tail her from the street. You take the rooftops. Take note of anything... suspicious.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene. (Good.)

speaker: Lysistrata
en: Not today!

speaker: Apprentice
en: Mentor! She disappeared!

speaker: Ezio
en: We can find her if we hurry.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Forgive me, Mentor. I attacked too soon, with too much distance between us. I should have stopped that witch.

speaker: Ezio
en: To live is to learn. Take this lesson to heart, and clear your mind. You will have another chance.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Promising news, Mentor. The actress Lysistrata is making a public performance under a stage name.

speaker: Ezio
en: Hmm. She knows it is wiser to stay hidden, but her vanity is getting the better of her.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Follow me. We will get her this time.

speaker: Ezio
en: No mistakes. Take your time, and plan your attack.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Evet (Yes), Mentor. I will wait an entire year if I have to.

speaker: Ezio
en: I hope it does not come to that. I am a busy man.

speaker: Apprentice
en: She is bold. You must admit that.

speaker: Ezio
en: Boldness is often a sign of weakness. A true master never takes unnecessary risks.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Will you wait here, or should we do this together?

speaker: Ezio
en: As I said, no unnecessary risks. We go together. And if you do not get her, I will.

speaker: Lysistrata
en: All the long years when the hopeless war dragged along we, unassuming, forgotten in quiet, endured without question, endured in our loneliness all your incessant childish antics. Our lips were kept tied, aching with silence, though well all the while we knew how wretchedly everything still was progressing. Always you discussed the war and its politics loudly, and we sometimes would ask you, our hearts deep with sorrowing, "What's to be inscribed on the side of the Treaty-stone?" or "What, dear, was said in the Assembly today?" "Mind your own business," you would answer me growlingly "hold your tongue, woman, or else go away."

speaker: Lysistrata
en: You do your duty well, Assassin... but you do it with such coldness that I almost pity you. The lives you fight to protect are dull, weak, and lacking luster. What a bland world it will be if you Assassins get your way.

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in pace.

speaker: Ezio
en: We have attracted some attention. Run!

speaker: Thicker than Water
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Thin the Ranks
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: The Three Amici
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Leader
en: Kill him! Romulus demands his death! The Assassin must suffer as Remus suffered!

speaker: Leader
en: Your death is written, Assassin.

speaker: Ezio
en: By your Borgia masters?

speaker: Leader
en: You know nothing!

speaker: Ezio
en: I know you receive enciphered letters from them. Prove your innocence, tell me where the code sheet is hidden.

speaker: Leader
en: Never!

speaker: Ezio
en: Merda (Shit), which one is he?

speaker: Gambalto
en: Salute Ezio! (Hail!) Antonio Maffei has sought refuge atop the city's tallest structure – spouting scripture and arrows in equal measure. The man has clearly lost his mind. Making matters worse, he's posted archers all around him. You'd do well to clear them out before approaching.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie for the information.

speaker: Antonio
en: Citizens of San Gimignano, heed well my words! You must repent! Repent and seek forgiveness! For your wicked ways have incurred the wrath of a demon! Summoned by your sins, he now walks our world, cloaked in shadow and darkness! And everywhere he treads, DEATH FOLLOWS! Why you ask? Because you have strayed and sacrificed your liberty to that wretch Lorenzo de' Medici. You are puppets, enslaved by purse strings! Won over by poisonous words! You have lost your virtue. You have lost your dignity. You have lost your faith! And this draws the demon in to feed. And feed they will. All whilst you wander lost in ignorance. Know that good men have died protecting you from evils. Men who sought to save these lands, to purify them! Join me in prayer, my children so that together we might stand against this darkness! Give ear, O heaven, and I will speak; and hear, O earth, the words of my mouth. Let my teachings drop as the rain. My speech distill as the dew. As raindrops on the tender herb, and as showers on the grass. For I proclaim the name of the Lord; ascribe greatness to our God. He is the rock, His work is perfect; for all His ways are justice, a God of truth and without injustice; righteous and upright is He. They have corrupted themselves; they are not His children, because of their blemish: a perverse and crooked generation. Do you thus deal with LORD, O foolish and unwise people? Is He not your Father, who bought you? Has He not made you and established you?

speaker: Antonio
en: By the light of the LORD, be cleansed!

speaker: Ezio
en: No grazie! (No thanks!)

speaker: Antonio
en: I will put you on your knees, sinner!

speaker: Ezio
en: You would enjoy that, wouldn't you?

speaker: Antonio
en: Beg forgiveness!

speaker: Ezio
en: I have no need to!

speaker: Antonio
en: Give me strength, O Lord – that I might cast out this demon! It is not too late for you to turn away from evil! Repent, sinner! You may yet be forgiven! I do God's work! And it is good!

speaker: Antonio
en: Away with you, demon!

speaker: Ezio
en: Have some respect for death, my friend.

speaker: Antonio
en: I'll show you respect! –

speaker: Ezio
en: No. I will. Che tu possa alfine trovare riposo nel corpo e nella mente. (May your body and mind at last be still.) Requiescat in Pace. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Ezio
en: All quiet today?

speaker: Apprentice
en: Not remotely. A heated conflict is brewing between two factions of Romanies. One group has banded together against a woman they call Mirela, accusing her of swindling the poor on dozens of occasions. As we speak, they are on their way to exile this trickster, by force if necessary.

speaker: Ezio
en: By your tone, you seem to believe there will be trouble.

speaker: Apprentice
en: I do. Mirela is a frightening woman and her temper is well known. I fear for anyone who crosses her.

speaker: Ezio
en: Then we should give these Romanies our support. No good can come of this fight if it escalates.

speaker: Ezio
en: We can escort the Romanies to the meeting, and provide protection until the impasse is resolved.

speaker: Apprentice
en: A wise plan, but only in secret. If Mirela gets wind that the Assassins are aiding her opposition, there is no telling what she might do. There they are. How should we proceed?

speaker: Ezio
en: You take to the rooftops, and I will wander the streets.

speaker: Romani
en: You crook! You charlatan! How dare you defile our people? How dare you turn the city against us, simply to satisfy your greed.

speaker: Mirela
en: Keep your voice down. You know nothing of my motives.

speaker: Romani
en: I will not be silent! This woman is a trickster! A cheat! She robs the poor of their money by preying on their fears!

speaker: Mirela
en: You will regret taking that tone with me.

speaker: Romani 2
en: What's wrong?

speaker: Guard
en: Ah! Murderers! Surrender yourselves! Stop right there!

speaker: Romani 2
en: We did nothing!

speaker: Ezio
en: Protect the Romanies. But do not harm the guards. This is a grave misunderstanding! Soldiers! In your haste to serve justice, you let the real murderer slip away. These women are innocent.

speaker: Apprentice
en: I will stop her before this gets out of hand. I give you my word, Mentor.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bene (Good). We will speak again soon.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Ezio, good news.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sì? (Yes?)

speaker: Apprentice
en: Mirela was spotted here several moments ago purchasing various reagents and oils.

speaker: Ezio
en: Such as?

speaker: Apprentice
en: What did the man say... walnut oil, cardamom, datura...

speaker: Ezio
en: Datura is a deadly poison, made from a flowering plant. Hm. I may be able to track her.

speaker: Apprentice
en: What is it, Mentor? What do you see?

speaker: Ezio
en: The subtlest evidence of things that have been. A trace here, a wisp there. Signs and scents. My senses are more finely tuned than most. This way.

speaker: Ezio
en: She has been here within the past few minutes.

speaker: Apprentice
en: I will take cover, while you flush her out.

speaker: Ezio
en: Damnazione! (Damnit!)

speaker: Mirela
en: So dies another wretched Romani; is that what you are thinking, Assassin? Maybe your heart is filled with pity for me? Then leave me be, for I despise such charity. I took what was owed me, in spite of oppression, of hatred, of ignorance. I lived my own way, for myself!

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in pace.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Bring me a suit of that perverted armor.

speaker: Ezio
en: You are not wearing one.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: What?

speaker: Ezio
en: It is part of the plan. You surrendered to us. We are bringing you to the Baron.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Ah, yes. Then what?

speaker: Ezio
en: Your men attack on my signal.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Bene (Good). Go change into costume. Dawn approaches.

speaker: Mercenary
en: We must follow the patrol route. We cannot deviate or the Duc's men will know something is wrong.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: The Baron thinks Cesare will allow the French to rule Italy. He's so blinded by the trickle of royalty in his blood, that lazy inbred can't see the battlefield. Whatever the French may think, Cesare intends to be king.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: More troops up ahead!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Your plan is brillante (brilliant), but I don't like using this kind of trick. I believe in fair fighting, may the best man win.

speaker: Ezio
en: Cesare and the Baron seem to have a different style.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: "There will come a day in which men no longer cheat each other. And on that day we will see what mankind is truly capable of."

speaker: Ezio
en: I've heard that before...

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: It is something your father once wrote.

speaker: Ezio
en: I will take care of them.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Stop them before they attack us.

speaker: Gatekeeper
en: Que venez-vous faire ici? (Declare yourself.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Mes soldats conduisent le capitaine italien à Son Excellence le Baron. Il veut se rendre. (My soldiers are taking the Italian captain to His Excellency the Baron. He wants to surrender.)

speaker: Gatekeeper
en: What part of France are you from?

speaker: Ezio
en: Montréal.

speaker: Gatekeeper
en: Open the gates!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: You speak French?

speaker: Ezio
en: There were a couple of French girls in Firenze.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Chien d'Italien. (Italian dog.)

speaker: Guard 2
en: Regardez-le, il a honte de ce qu'il est! (Look at him, he is ashamed of what he is!)

speaker: Octavian
en: Général d'Alviano. It seems that you have seen the light.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Enough of your crap. Release my wife.

speaker: Octavian
en: Such entitlement from a man born with nothing to his name.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Mine is worth its currency. Unlike yours, which is counterfeit.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: You think that commanding an army grants you nobility? Nobility comes from fighting besides your soldiers, not kidnapping a woman to cheat your way out of battle. Why don't you grow a pair and release my wife?

speaker: Octavian
en: You savages never learn.

speaker: Courtesan
en: Ezio, Cesare has captured the great condotierri (mercenaries) Prospero and Fabrizio Colonna. He has brought them to Roma for torture. Once freed, these men will cause significant trouble for the Borgia and their allies. They will be transferred soon, under guard, but I suspect that will not be a problem for you.

speaker: Prospero
en: You have saved us, amico (friend).

speaker: Ezio
en: You are not free yet. Prepare yourselves!

speaker: Prospero
en: There must be a way we can repay your kindness.

speaker: Ezio
en: Continue the fight against the Borgia.

speaker: Prospero
en: That we will. Addio, amico mio (Goodbye, my friend)!

speaker: Fabrizio
en: Addio (Goodbye)!

speaker: Turning the Tables
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Ezio! Here! Over here! Thank you, Ezio! You saved my life!

speaker: Ezio
en: I did what had to be done. You would have done the same.

speaker: Leonardo
en: I doubt it. Bravery is not my strong suit. I owe you a debt, brother.

speaker: Ezio
en: Di niente. (It's nothing.)

speaker: Captain
en: Tutti a bordo! Fra poco si salpa! (All aboard! We're leaving soon!)

speaker: Leonardo
en: That's our traghetto (ferry.) Venezia awaits!

speaker: Captain
en: Where's your pass?

speaker: Ezio
en: What pass?

speaker: Leonardo
en: You don't have a pass?

speaker: Captain
en: You cannot enter Venezia without a pass. Who invited you?

speaker: Ezio
en: Um... Nobody.

speaker: Captain
en: Basta! (Stop!) No pass, no entrance.

speaker: Ezio
en: Don't worry, Leonardo. I'll come up with something.

speaker: Caterina
en: Don't just stand there! I need help!

speaker: Caterina
en: Dio del Cielo! Aiutatemi! (For Christ's sake! Help me!) Qualcuno mi aiuti! Non so nuotare! (Somebody help me! I can't swim!) Aiuto! Qualcuno mi faccia scendere da quest' affare! Aiutatemi! (Help! Someone get me off this thing! Help me!)

speaker: Caterina
en: What the hell is this?!

speaker: Ezio
en: I'm rescuing you.

speaker: Caterina
en: Without a boat? What are you going to do, carry me? Go get the boat!

speaker: Ezio
en: Madonna.

speaker: Caterina
en: Oh, you're good. The ladies must like you.

speaker: Ezio
en: I wasn't looking to impress. Only to help someone in distress.

speaker: Caterina
en: Which is exactly WHY you impress. And you are Messer...?

speaker: Ezio
en: Auditore. But, please, call me Ezio.

speaker: Caterina
en: I'm Caterina. Now, Ezio, we must find you suitable reward... Do you have any suggestions?

speaker: Ezio
en: There is—perhaps—something you could help me with...

speaker: Caterina
en: I'm all ears...

speaker: Captain
en: Yes Signora... Whatever you say Signora...

speaker: Caterina
en: He won't trouble you any more. I... took care of it.

speaker: Ezio
en: Thank you, Caterina.

speaker: Caterina
en: Perhaps we'll see each other again... Should you ever find yourself in the city of Forlì, it would be my pleasure to welcome you...

speaker: Ezio
en: I look forward to enjoying your hospitality.

speaker: Captain
en: Please accept my most humble apologies, Messere. (Sir.) Had I known...

speaker: Ezio
en: It's quite alright, my friend.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Be careful, Ezio. Do you know who that was?

speaker: Ezio
en: My next conquest?

speaker: Leonardo
en: I don't think so, Ezio! That's Caterina Sforza, daughter of the Duca di Milano. Her husband

speaker: Ezio
en: Husband?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Si. (Yes.) Her husband is the Lord of Forlì. That woman is as powerful and dangerous as she is young and beautiful.

speaker: Ezio
en: Sembra come una donna per me. (Sounds like my kind of lady.)

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Ah, there you are! Is it done?

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes. All your men are in place.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Bene, bene (Good, good).

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Take this. I assume you know how it works?

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Find the highest point you can in the district and fire it from there. This signals my men to begin the attack.

speaker: Ezio
en: Alright, then. I will see you on the battlefield.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: That you will.

speaker: Ezio
en: Bartolomeo needs my help.

speaker: Dante
en: Must return to L'Arsenale...

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Salute, Ezio!

speaker: Ezio
en: Care for some company?

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: By all means!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: After him!

speaker: Silvio
en: A fine specimen, isn't he? You should be honored to die by his hand!

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Ciucciami i coglioni, muso da mona (Suck my balls you fucking idiot)! Porca puttana (Son of a bitch)! Come on, Ezio! We need to stop that grassone bastardo (fat bastard)!

speaker: Silvio
en: You think I don't know why you're here, Ezio?! But you're too late! There's nothing you can do to prevent us from obtaining it. Ah! That's right! You still don't know, do you? Though once Dante's done with you it won't matter anymore. Do you miss him, Ezio? Your fool of a father?

speaker: Silvio
en: My greatest regret is that I could not have been the one to pull the lever. To watch him kick and gasp and hang! You'll follow him into the ground! You and that condottiero (mercenary captain) too! And after we'll come for the others! Your uncle. Your mother. Your sweet, sweet sister.

speaker: Silvio
en: Enough of this! We're out of time! Return to me. We must depart.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Ezio! Go now! That brute will no doubt lead you straight to his master. My men and I will remain here and keep the guards from giving chase.

speaker: Silvio
en: Hurry! They're going to leave without us!

speaker: Silvio
en: God damn them all! I've been nothing but loyal! And this – THIS – is how they repay me?

speaker: Dante
en: What trouble, master?

speaker: Silvio
en: Don't you see what's happened?!

speaker: Dante
en: No.

speaker: Silvio
en: Of course not, slow as you are. We've been betrayed! The ship has sailed – without us! And now the Assassin approaches. Perhaps there's still time for us to escape. If not to the island, at least away from here...

speaker: Dante
en: As you command.

speaker: Silvio
en: Yes. Prepare the ship!

speaker: Crew
en: Raise the sails! Pull up the anchor.

speaker: Ezio
en: What's happened here? Why the boats? I thought you sought the Doge's seat?

speaker: Silvio
en: Just a distraction. We were meant to sail...

speaker: Ezio
en: Sail where?

speaker: Silvio
en: I'll never tell.

speaker: Dante
en: Cyprus is their destination. They want... they want...

speaker: Ezio
en: Non temete l'oscurità, accettate il suo abbraccio (Fear not the darkness, but welcome its embrace). Requiescant in pace (Rest in peace).

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Well done, Ezio! Silvio is defeated and the military district returned to us! Perhaps now Venezia might finally enjoy a bit of pace e tranquilità (peace and quiet)! We should celebrate this victory!

speaker: Ezio
en: I am glad for you and your men, Bartolomeo, but I cannot join. I fear my work has just taken a rather strange turn...

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Ezio
en: Silvio wasn't looking to replace Marco as Doge. He was about to leave Venezia, in fact. This whole thing was just a distraction.

speaker: Bartolomeo
en: Why?

speaker: Ezio
en: That is what I need to find out.

speaker: Suleiman
en: I have arranged a meeting with my uncle Ahmet and the Janissary captain, Tarik Barleti. The Janissaries are loyal to my grandfather, but they have lately become angry over his choice of the next Sultan.

speaker: Ezio
en: Your uncle.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Exactly. The Janissaries prefer my father, Selim.

speaker: Ezio
en: You are in a tough spot. But how do the Byzantines fit into this?

speaker: Suleiman
en: I had hoped you might know. Would you be willing to help me find out?

speaker: Ezio
en: I am tracking them myself. I can help you as long as our interests run parallel.

speaker: Suleiman
en: I will take what I can get. There is a hatch at the top of that tower which leads to a secret room. Go there, wait, and watch.

speaker: Ahmet
en: Heed my nephew, Tarik. Your incompetence borders on treason. And to think that today our Janissaries were outshone by an Italian lute player! Preposterous!

speaker: Tarik
en: An inexcusable failing, efendim (your grace). I will conduct a full investigation.

speaker: Suleiman
en: I will conduct the investigation, Tarik. For reasons that should be obvious.

speaker: Tarik
en: Evet, Shehzadem. (Yes, Prince). You have your father's wisdom.

speaker: Suleiman
en: And his impatience.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Uncle, I am relieved to see you safe.

speaker: Ahmet
en: Likewise, Suleiman. Allah's emanet olun. (May God protect you.)

speaker: Ahmet
en: Tarik Bey (Lord Tarik)... a word? What was the purpose of this attack, I wonder? To make me look weak? An ineffective steward of this city? If you had a hand in this mess, Tarik, you have made a grave mistake. My father has chosen me as the next Sultan, not my brother.

speaker: Tarik
en: Ahmet, I am not depraved enough to imagine the conspiracy you accuse me of.

speaker: Ahmet
en: What have I done to earn such contempt from the Janissaries? What has my brother done for you that I have not?

speaker: Tarik
en: May I speak freely?

speaker: Ahmet
en: You'd better.

speaker: Tarik
en: You are weak, Ahmet. Pensive in times of war and restless in times of peace. You lack passion for the traditions of the ghazi (holy warriors), yet you speak of fraternity in the company of infidels. You would make a decent philosopher, Ahmet, but you will be a poor Sultan.

speaker: Ahmet
en: You may show yourself out.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Quite a family, eh?

speaker: Ezio
en: Your uncle lacks sway over the men he will soon command.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Tarik is a hard man, proud and capable but ambitious. And he admires my father greatly.

speaker: Ezio
en: But he failed to secure this palace against a Byzantine invasion. That alone is worth our attention.

speaker: Suleiman
en: Precisely.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where should we begin?

speaker: Suleiman
en: For now, keep an eye on Tarik and his Janissaries. They spend much of their free time in and around the Bazaar.

speaker: Ezio
en: I will start there when I can.

speaker: Voice
en: Pst. Ezio! Over here. Ezio! Come here.

speaker: Ezio
en: Chi è lá? (Who is there?)

speaker: Leonardo
en: Ezio!

speaker: Ezio
en: Leonardo!

speaker: Leonardo
en: I knew you were behind the break-in at Sant'Angelo! It is good to see you, friend.

speaker: Ezio
en: Come here.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Forgive me. The Borgia have commandeered my services. Actually, they would have killed me had I refused.

speaker: Ezio
en: What do they want?

speaker: Leonardo
en: War machines. I have constructed weapons for all the Borgia guards and other terrible monstrosities besides. They are very well designed, Ezio. Here. The names of the Templars overseeing their construction. Cesare intends to supply his army with my creations. You must dismantle them.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie (Thank you). I will take care of the plans and the machines.

speaker: Leonardo
en: There is far graver news, I am afraid. They have the Apple.

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes, I know. I gave the Apple to Mario.

speaker: Leonardo
en: I am sorry, Ezio. Cesare left it in my hands to study, to make it work. Then Rodrigo took it from me, I know not where.

speaker: Ezio
en: I will recover it in time. Leonardo, I have lost all the Codex inventions you once fashioned for me.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Hmm. Remaking them will be easy, I never forget a design. But you must compensate me for the raw material.

speaker: Ezio
en: Really? They are not paying you at il Vaticano (the Vatican)?

speaker: Leonardo
en: Very... very little. If we are to do this, we must appear to not meet at all.

speaker: Ezio
en: A hand pointing?

speaker: Leonardo
en: It's pointing to where you should sit. So, sit!

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes, maestro.

speaker: Leonardo
en: Wait here. I will be back soon. I must return to my workshop. Wait here.

speaker: Ezio
en: I can kill double the guards.

speaker: Ezio
en: Now nothing will be out of my reach.

speaker: Ezio
en: Just a small sting and my enemies will fall.

speaker: Leonardo
en: I will wait nearby for a few more hours in case you change your mind.

speaker: Leonardo
en: What can I get you this time? What would you like me to make for you? Let me guess, you need more designs. What can I bring you this time Ezio?

speaker: Father
en: The bastards! The damn bastards! I will tear off their arms and use them as clubs!

speaker: Ezio
en: Calm, friend. Anger is the enemy of caution.

speaker: Father
en: Those Byzantine thugs kidnapped my son, Ezio! To get at me, they attack an innocent boy!

speaker: Ezio
en: We can get your son back, but only if we coordinate, and act carefully.

speaker: Father
en: Evet. (Yes.) Of course. If you lead, I will follow.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Is he breathing? Does he live?

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: I cannot say. He is as still as a corpse.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: He may yet have a pulse but... I am not trained for such things.

speaker: Ezio
en: His heart is weak, but he lives.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Poison. There is no other explanation.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: If so, there may be a remedy.

speaker: Ezio
en: We will get him to a doctor.

speaker: Ezio
en: Hekim effendi (Doctor, sir), this boy has been poisoned!

speaker: Doctor
en: Give me room.

speaker: Son
en: Trap... it is a trap.

speaker: Ezio
en: Say again?

speaker: Son
en: The Templars, they used me as bait. To flush you out. To kill all of you.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Have we been followed? I would not doubt it.

speaker: Ezio
en: Take positions, and be ready for anything.

speaker: Ezio
en: Keep this boy from harm. Let no one get close. Hold the line! Steady! Keep close! Do not waver.

speaker: Father
en: My boy! How do you feel?

speaker: Son
en: I am fine, father. Stop doting.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Well, if you think saving your life is doting, there may be hope for you yet.

speaker: Son
en: Ah, ow! I need to lay down.

speaker: Ezio
en: Drink water and keep still. Agitation speeds the poison through your body.

speaker: Father
en: Tesekkür ederim (Thank you), Ezio. I owe you a great debt.

speaker: Thief
en: Ezio! Ezio! Ser Antonio wishes to speak with you.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie (Thanks) for the message.

speaker: Antonio
en: Ah, there you are! Come, Ezio. I'd like to introduce you to an associate. This is Agostino Barbarigo, soon to be Doge of Venezia... thanks to you.

speaker: Ezio
en: È un fare la vostra conoscenza, illustrissimo (It is an honor to make your acquaintance, Doge) I am sorry for the loss of your brother.

speaker: Agostino
en: He had it coming. He was bought and paid for by the Borgia, a mistake I have no intention of making.

speaker: Antonio
en: Come, Ezio. We have much to discuss.

speaker: Antonio
en: We've located Silvio Barbarigo for you. He's fled to L'Arsenale.

speaker: Agostino
en: Ha! Fled? You mean occupied... and joined by two hundred mercenari (mercenaries), no less.

speaker: Ezio
en: You're Doge now. Can't you command them to stand down?

speaker: Agostino
en: The has yet to confirm my ascension. And this little stunt of Silvio's has only made things worse. He has an entire army at his command!

speaker: Ezio
en: Then help me to raise my own.

speaker: Antonio
en: I figured you'd say as much. Bartolomeo d'Alviano is the man you seek. He and his men have little love for Silvio. He resides within the military district... southwest of L'Arsenale.

speaker: Ezio
en: Va bene (Okay), I'll go and see him.

speaker: Thief
en: Ezio Auditore? Perdiana! (Wow!) I've heard stories about your speed! Let us see if you can match mine!

speaker: Yusuf
en: Mentor, say hello to your extended family.

speaker: Ezio
en: Salute a voi, Assassini. (Greetings, Assassins.) It is an honor to find such fast friends so far from home.

speaker: Yusuf
en: You see brothers? Our mentor is not afraid to weep openly in front of his pupils.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do not worry. I will not make a habit out of it.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Ezio and I were ambushed on our way here. I'd like some of you to do a sweep of the area. Hemen. (Immediately.)

speaker: Yusuf
en: And you, Ezio. Your weapons and armor are in a pitiful state. Maybe find some money and repair what you can. There is a blacksmith nearby. He's a friend.

speaker: Ezio
en: Buona idea. (Good idea.)

speaker: Nobleman
en: You must not disrupt our work! Firenze is sick! It's our duty to cure her.

speaker: Ezio
en: How? By forcing her people to follow a madman?

speaker: Nobleman
en: It is unwise for you to challenge those in power.

speaker: Ezio
en: Yes. Well, that is about to change.

speaker: Nobleman
en: No! You won't take me! Savonarola will know of your treachery! Guards! Guards!

speaker: Nobleman
en: Savonarola is our savior! Why must you resist this?! Things are better under him! Under us! The people agree, else they would not follow as they do! Savonarola warned of dissent! But I did not expect it would it be violent! Only take a moment to reflect! You'll see that we are right! Let me be! I've done no wrong. Only the prophet's will. Take your fight to Savonarola! I am merely doing what I must.

speaker: Nobleman
en: I was a victim! It's not my fault!

speaker: Ezio
en: No. You made a choice.

speaker: Nobleman
en: He charmed me. With that... thing.

speaker: Ezio
en: Only because you allowed it. Lo faccio per il popolo... (I do this for the people...) Requiescat in pace. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Thief
en: I hear you're pretty fast. I'm bit of a speedster myself... you would honour me by granting a quick race...

speaker: Vertical Slice
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Yusuf
en: The standard Ottoman Hookblade has two parts, you see... the hook and the blade. So you can use one or the other. An elegant design. How about a bigger challenge?

speaker: Ezio
en: Va bene. (Okay.) Let's go.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Having fun? That's right. Let the Hookblade do the work. Iste boyle. (There you go.) Throw yourself into it.

speaker: Yusuf
en: Welcome to Konstantiniyye, Ezio. The crossroads of the world. Many generations of men have ruled this city, but they have never subdued her. She always bounces back.

speaker: Ezio
en: It seems a fine place to call home.

speaker: Yusuf
en: It is. Race you to the bottom?

speaker: Caterina
en: Ready to go again?

speaker: Ezio
en: You don't need to ask.

speaker: Caterina
en: One should always have the freedom to choose.

speaker: Caterina
en: Shhh. What's that?

speaker: Ezio
en: Probably just training exercises.

speaker: Ezio
en: Merda! (Shit!) I have to find Mario and rally the troops.

speaker: Caterina
en: My men are in the courtyard. I aim to lead them around back and flank our attackers.

speaker: Ezio
en: Stay out of sight.

speaker: Mario
en: It's the Borgia.

speaker: Ezio
en: How did we not see this?

speaker: Mario
en: They must have massed to the east during the night. We need to hold them off until the townspeople have escaped.

speaker: Ezio
en: I will take care of it.

speaker: Mario
en: Use the cannons above the ramparts. I intend to lead a frontal assault.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do you have it?

speaker: Mario
en: I am keeping it safe. The Borgia must not be allowed to breach the walls until everyone is safely away. Insieme per la vittoria! (We stand together!)

speaker: Ezio
en: Insieme. (Together.) Uncle... be careful.

speaker: Mario
en: I will.

speaker: Woman 1
en: My children. Where are my children?!

speaker: Man 1
en: Where are we going?

speaker: Child
en: My mother. I can't find my mother.

speaker: Woman 2
en: Aiuto! Aiuto! (Help me! Help me!)

speaker: Man 2
en: Oh God. Where are you, Marcello?!

speaker: Woman 3
en: Run! Run!

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Signor Auditore, thank God! We must hold them back until the villagers escape!

speaker: Ezio
en: Load the cannon.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Aim for the cannons, Signore (Sir)! Destroy their cannons, Signore (Sir)! We have lost everything. Fire at them! Aim carefully, we can't withstand this attack much longer! Please, save us, Signore (Sir). If they breach the walls, all our people will die. My family will die. Nearly half the townspeople have made it out! They're destroying us! Pater Noster, qui es coelies, sanctificeteur nomen tourn– (Our Father, –) Reload. Reload! Aahhh!

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: He's dead, Signore (Sir)!

speaker: Ezio
en: Keep loading the cannon.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Some townspeople still haven't escaped! Keep going! Almost all the townspeople are outside the walls! You have saved them! ...Wait. Soldiers are climbing the walls! Signore (Sir), forget the cannons. You must stop them! Go! I will carry on here!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Show no mercy!

speaker: Soldier 2
en: No one shall be spared! Take this town for the Borgia!

speaker: Man
en: They're breaching the gate!

speaker: Cesare
en: I know you're there, Ezio. The Pope told me about you and your little group of Assassins... and this.

speaker: Cesare
en: Give me the gun his friend fashioned for us. We've had too much bloodshed. I think a cleansing is in order. So, consider this an invitation, from my family... to yours.

speaker: Guard 1
en: There is something moving over there in that haystack.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Sit back down, we're in the middle of playing a .

speaker: Guard 1
en: No no! This time I saw something. I know it.

speaker: Guard 2
en: That's what you say every time!

speaker: Guard 2
en: You were right, there was something in that haystack you femminuccia (sissy)!

speaker: Guard 1
en: I'm tired of your jokes, this isn't funny! I could have been killed!

speaker: Guard 2
en: Leave me alone! Run faster!

speaker: Guard 2
en: Yes. Yes, I think I got away.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Have to find a way out before he kills me...

speaker: Guard 2
en: We're under attack! Guards! Guards, to arms! To arms!

speaker: Apprentice
en: Mentor, I am told you still have the speed and strength of a twenty year-old.

speaker: Ezio
en: I try to keep healthy.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Then how about a race? I could use a bit of exercise.

speaker: Ezio
en: You begin, and I will follow.

speaker: Ezio
en: That Templar is up to something. We should track him.

speaker: Ezio
en: Do not let him escape!

speaker: Apprentice
en: I can handle this, Mentor.

speaker: Apprentice
en: He was holding this, Mentor. It must belong to the Vizier he robbed.

speaker: Ezio
en: You take care of this body. I will return this document.

speaker: Ezio
en: I believe this belongs to you.

speaker: Damat
en: Ah! You have spared me much humiliation before the Sublime Porte. Thank you, efendim (my lord). And is that the young Assassin who aided you today?

speaker: Ezio
en: Enjoy the rest of your day.

speaker: Man
en: Mentor! Mentor! You must hurry! One of your Assassins is in grave danger.

speaker: Ezio
en: Where?

speaker: Man
en: The Grand Bazaar. The Templars have cornered your den master there since morning.

speaker: Ezio
en: Grazie. (Thank you.)

speaker: Ezio
en: Are you safe, friend?

speaker: Apprentice
en: There are Templars everywhere, Mentor. It seems I have a bounty on my head!

speaker: Ezio
en: Then we should turn the tables. Flee here and draw them out into the open.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Evet (Yes), Mentor.

speaker: Damat
en: Find the Assassin and bring that rat to justice!

speaker: Damat
en: You Assassins are a plague on the hope of humanity, putting down every edifice of progress we manage to build up. Given enough time, I could have delivered my people into the arms of the Templars. But no more.

speaker: Apprentice
en: Leave this life in peace.

speaker: Wife
en: My husband carries on with wanton sluts! My reputation... and I'm stuck with the bastard! Please, make him feel my displeasure.

speaker: Husband
en: I'm sorry! I regret it, truly! I am going straight home, I swear!

speaker: War Plans (Bomber)
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus 2.01.

speaker: War Plans (Machine Gun)
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus 2.01.

speaker: War Plans (Naval Cannon)
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus 2.01.

speaker: War Plans (Tank)
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus 2.01.

speaker: Ramondo
en: I need this delivered right away! If you're quick, I'll make it worth your while!

speaker: Vincente
en: Oh grazie. (Thank you.)

speaker: Brute 1
en: This is ridiculous! Vincenzo was supposed to take my shift an hour ago. My wife is going to murder me if I miss dinner again.

speaker: Brute 2
en: E che ti frega? (Why should you give a shit?) Just go. It's not like we're guarding the Doge.

speaker: Brute 1
en: What the hell are we guarding anyway?

speaker: Brute 2
en: A shipment from China. Some kind of colored powder they brought over for a big party - really expensive! You ask me, the way these nobles spend their money...

speaker: Ezio
en: She was beautiful.

speaker: Husband
en: She was...until that porco (pig) defiled her. I wish he'd just killed her. I wish he'd just killed la mia amata (my beloved)! People who saw her grow up cheered when he spat on her! Smiles on their faces when her neck...

speaker: Ezio
en: I understand.

speaker: Husband
en: How can you? My Livia was innocent!

speaker: Ezio
en: I have lost family to the rope...to treachery.

speaker: Husband
en: Il Carnefice watches from his home on the hill above. He threatens to hang me if I cut her rope.

speaker: Ezio
en: When you are ready, take her down. I will deal with Il Carnefice.

speaker: Borgia Soldier
en: Nice work down there.

speaker: Il Carnefice
en: Not my best, but it's hard to make art with poor materials.

speaker: Il Carnefice
en: You didn't think this through! Tell me if you need to rest. Uh, which limb shall I take first, huh? Maybe I will start with that pretty head? Ha! Good! Good! You've tasted blood before!

speaker: Ezio
en: Requiescat in pace. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Wet Work
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ezio Auditore da Firenze's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus 2.0.

speaker: Mario
en: Ezio? What are you doing here?

speaker: Ezio
en: Taking responsibility. Vieri troubles you because of me.

speaker: Mario
en: Vieri troubles us because he is a Templar and we are Assassins.

speaker: Ezio
en: Either way. I wish to help.

speaker: Mario
en: Va bene. (Alright.) Then listen close: First we must find a way inside the city. Though it seems Vieri expects us... He has sealed the gates and sent his men to guard them. Fortunately for us, the city is larger than its host. The southern gate suffers for it. So this is where we will strike. Pronti? (Ready?)

speaker: Mario
en: Alright, Ezio. Here's how it is going to work: My men and I will distract the guards. Once we've engaged them, get yourself over the wall and find a way to open the gate. Take these throwing knives. Use them to dispatch the archers.

speaker: Ezio
en: I'm ready when you are.

speaker: Mario
en: Then let us begin. All'attacco! (Charge!)

speaker: Mario
en: Well done, Ezio! We're in!

speaker: Mario
en: This way, men!

speaker: Mario
en: I want you to distract those guards, and keep them from raising the alarm. Hopefully it will buy me enough time to find and silence Vieri.

speaker: Ezio
en: Va bene. (Alright.)

speaker: Mario
en: Wait, nipote (nephew). Take a few of my men with you... Just to be safe. Come join me once they are dealt with.

speaker: Guard 1
en: What's Vieri up to now?

speaker: Guard 2
en: No one knows. But something has him on edge. How else to explain all the patrols?

speaker: Guard 3
en: We're meant to be soldiers. Instead he's turned us into nursemaids. And why?

speaker: Guard 2
en: Shooting his mouth off again, no doubt. Angering the wrong sorts of people... And so now we pay the price.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Careful. Or do you want us dragged before him like Bernardo was?

speaker: Guard 2
en: Poor bastard... I heard Vieri took his eyes.

speaker: Guard 1
en: I'd like to keep mine. So let's end this conversation.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Ezio! Your uncle's under attack and needs help! Go to him!

speaker: Mario
en: Ah, nipote (nephew)! There you are! It seems my plan has hit something of a snag... Vieri's men ambushed us, and now we've got our hands full. My brothers and I will deal with these guards – I want you to go ahead and root out that snake! Find Vieri! See that justice is served!

speaker: Spaniard
en: It's settled: Vieri, you will remain here to coordinate the mercenari (mercenaries). Francesco will organize our forces in the city and send word when it's time to strike. Jacopo, your job is to calm the citizens once the deed is done.

speaker: Vieri
en: What about that ubriacone (drunkard) Mario? He continues to harass my forces and I fear he'll discover what we intend.

speaker: Francesco
en: He's always been trouble. Just like that bastardo (bastard) brother of his.

speaker: Vieri
en: Then let me reunite them, father!

speaker: Spaniard
en: There will be plenty of time to clean up rifiuti (trash) when we've finished. Now, is there anything else?

speaker: Spaniard
en: Muy bien. (Very well.) May the Father of Understanding guide you!

speaker: Guard
en: Comandante! Comandante! (Commander! Commander!)

speaker: Vieri
en: What?!

speaker: Guard
en: Mario Auditore has invaded the city! He comes for you!

speaker: Vieri
en: Then let's not keep him waiting.

speaker: Vieri
en: Ah! There you are. I've been looking forward to this for a long, long time.

speaker: Ezio
en: What are you and your allies planning? Is this what my father discovered? Is this why he was killed?

speaker: Vieri
en: I'm sorry, were you hoping for a confession?

speaker: Ezio
en: Pezzo di merda! Vorrei solo che avessi sofferto di più! Hai avuto la fine che meritavi! Spero che bru– (Piece of shit! I only wish you'd suffered more! You met the fate you deserved! I hope yo–)

speaker: Mario
en: Enough, Ezio! Show some respect.

speaker: Ezio
en: Respect? After all that's happened? Do you think he would have shown either of us such kindness?

speaker: Mario
en: You are not Vieri. Do not become him.

speaker: Mario
en: Che la morte ti dia la pace che cercavi. (May death provide the peace you sought.) Requiescat in Pace. (Rest in peace.)

speaker: Mario
en: Take this. Read it when you have time. Our work here is finished. Let us return to the villa...

speaker: Guard 1
en: Everything going well in there?

speaker: Guard 2
en: We have to go, Luigi, or we'll be late!

speaker: Guard
en: The count is complete? Va bene. (Okay.) Kill him.

speaker: Ezio
en: No!

speaker: Guard
en: Lucky you. Luigi says he gets to live. Lead the way, boss.

speaker: Guards
en: Now we're going the right way. Soon the party will be all around us. We're on track. Now we are making good time. We are nearly there. I hope they let us go inside. Soon we will be there. Soon this job will be over. Where are we going? I am not questioning your authority... but should we not get going? Signore (Sir), are you all right? The route you are taking is very... interesting. I would not have gone this way, but who am I? Isn't the Banker the other way? Do you think he's forgotten where we're going? Respectfully, Signore (Sir), I am not sure where you are going. He's going in the wrong direction.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Did you liberate your money from our friend?

speaker: Ezio
en: I did.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: A small victory.

speaker: Ezio
en: They add up. And in time, with work, we'll have a few dozen more.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: And in time, Cesare's gaze will return to us and we'll be broken again. Now, where is my contact, Vinicio? He should have already intercepted the letter. Follow me.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Look at these facades masquerading as government. The Pope is very clever to keep this place in business. It fools your friends the people quite easily.

speaker: Ezio
en: When did you become so cynical?

speaker: Machiavelli
en: I merely describe the reality of Roma today. But all may not be lost. The good news is that we have allies in the city. How much longer this will last, however, I cannot say.

speaker: Guard 1
en: He was attempting to steal official Vatican mail.

speaker: Vinicio
en: Perdonatemi, Signore (Pardon me, Sir) You must be mistaken.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Who are you working for, ladro (thief)?

speaker: Vinicio
en: I am working for no one.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Then no one will care what we do to you.

speaker: Vinicio
en: Grazie! (Thank you!)

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Where is it?

speaker: Vinicio
en: The courier still has the letter.

speaker: Machiavelli
en: Ezio, stop him! Find me at the Terme (Baths)!

speaker: Ezio
en: If I can stay my blade long enough to follow him, he'll lead me to his Templar brothers. I'll have more names for my list...

speaker: Ezio
en: What's going on here? Are they late? They haven't seen me, this much I know... What are you and the others planning, Jacopo? Your letter mentioned Venezia... are there Templars there as well? How many men are responsible for my father's death?

speaker: Jacopo
en: I am sorry, Maestro (Master). I did all I could, but the Assassin proved too strong.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Clearly. Else the others would be here with you. To say nothing of that fact that Firenze remains in Medici hands...

speaker: Jacopo
en: It's Francesco's fault! His impatience made him reckless! I tried to be the voice of reason...

speaker: Emilio
en: More like the voice of cowardice.

speaker: Jacopo
en: You're one to talk, Signor Barbarigo. Had you sent us quality weapons instead of this garbage you Venetians call ar–

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Enough! We put our faith in your family and you repay us with inaction and incompetence?! Then when asked to account for your failures, you make excuses and insult us?! How do you expect me to respond?

speaker: Rodrigo
en: It's alright. I do...

speaker: Jacopo
en: No... please... don't...

speaker: Emilio
en: Please don't what?

speaker: Jacopo
en: I can... fix this. Only... spare me...

speaker: Rodrigo
en: No.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: What a mess.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: So sorry to have claimed your prize, Assassin!

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Did you honestly think I wouldn't expect you to follow? That I didn't plan for it? We've been at this a lot longer than you.

speaker: Rodrigo
en: Kill him.

speaker: Ezio
en: I know you're only doing as you're told, so if you release me, I will spare your lives.

speaker: Guard
en: Ha! Listen to this– Ahhhh!

speaker: Ezio
en: Vai, amico, libero da fardelli e paure. (Go forward friend, unburdened and unafraid.) Requiescat in pace. (Rest in peace).

speaker: Ezio
en: I seek those who lead the Followers of Romulus.

speaker: Ezio
en: Perfect! A route up if I fall.

speaker: Follower of Romulus 1
en: Hear us, oh Romulus, what must we do to this trespasser?

speaker: Ezio
en: Do not listen. Only the Borgia speak through him, not your god.

speaker: Follower of Romulus 1
en: Romulus says that the Assassin must die!

speaker: Follower of Romulus 2
en: We cannot follow!

speaker: Follower of Romulus 3
en: Come! One of the other tunnels will lead us to him.

speaker: Ezio
en: There's Lorenzo, and his wife. There's Giuliano, Lorenzo's brother. But where is Francesco...?

speaker: Ezio
en: There he is. Time to strike.

speaker: Bernardo
en: Crepa, traditore! (Here, traitor!)

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Giuliano! No–!

speaker: Giuliano
en: No! In nome di Dio, vi scongiuro! Pietà! (No! In the name of God, I beg you, mercy!)

speaker: Francesco
en: Nessuna pìetà, cane maledetto! Muori! Muori! Muoriii! (No mercy for you, dog! Die! DIE!)

speaker: Francesco
en: Your day is done, Lorenzo! Your entire family dies by my sword!

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Wait... Please. I need help.

speaker: Lorenzo
en: You... saved my life.

speaker: Ezio
en: It's nothing. But the man who did this to you has to pay!

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Not now... I need help first. To my home. People I can trust there... Can you...?

speaker: Lorenzo
en: I'm losing a lot of blood...

speaker: Ezio
en: Hang on, Signore! I'm moving as fast as I can.

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Francesco de' Pazzi! I'll kill him! I'll wipe his entire family from the city! They'll be ERASED!

speaker: Ezio
en: Quietatevi, Signore. (Be still, sir.) Conserve your energy, or I'll be delivering a corpse. We're almost there now...

speaker: Ezio
en: Lorenzo's been wounded! Aprite la porta! (Open the door!)

speaker: Poliziano
en: What's the password?

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Poliziano! Open the maledetta porta!! (fucking door!)

speaker: Poliziano
en: By the Thrice Greatest! Come in. Quickly! The city is at war! Hurry!

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Wait.. I am in your debt. Tell me. Why did you help me?

speaker: Ezio
en: You are not the only one who lost a brother to the Pazzi. My name is Ezio Auditore.

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Ah! You're Giovanni's son... Your father was a good man. He understood honor, loyalty.

speaker: Guard
en: The Pazzi thugs are storming the Palazzo della Signoria! We can't hold them off much longer–

speaker: Poliziano
en: No! If they get inside, they'll murder all our supporters and put their own devils in power!

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Then my survival would mean nothing. I have to...

speaker: Lorenzo
en: Francesco de' Pazzi... Help save our city, Auditore... Kill him.

speaker: Leandros
en: Do not take your eyes off this road for a moment, do you understand me? Nothing gets through!

speaker: Guard
en: Leandros. There. (points at Ezio)

speaker: Leandros
en: Well, well... Look what crawled out of its hole to die!

speaker: Leandros
en: He's at death's door. Finish him off! Bring me his head, or throw yourselves into the canyon!

speaker: Ezio
en: This used to be so easy.

speaker: Leandros
en: Could it be that you are every bit as deadly as the legends say? Or am I in charge of an army of drunks swinging sticks?! Right this way, Ezio. Nowhere left to run now!

speaker: Ezio
en: Not for me, and not for you!

speaker: Leandros
en: Kill that dog! Cut him down!

speaker: Leandros
en: Do your worst, malákas (asshole)!

speaker: Leandros
en: Face me.

speaker: Leandros
